entry.summary: This work proposes Oscillatory Predictive Learning (OPL), a two-stage framework combining Artificial Kuramoto Oscillatory Neurons (AKOrN) with predictive self-supervised pretraining that achieves adversarial robustness in computer vision without adversarial training or test-time purification. The key claim is that robustness can emerge from architectural and representation-learning inductive biases alone, avoiding the heavy computational cost of generating adversarial examples or iterative denoising. If validated, this could significantly change how robust vision models are built.

entry.title: Transformers as In-Context Samplers: From Closed-Form Diffusion to Estimation-Free Sampling

author.name: Arman Adibi, Alireza Jafari, Mohammad Ghavamzadeh, Hadi Daneshmand

entry.summary: Proves that frozen transformers can perform in-context learning for data generation, not just supervised learning: they can simulate iterative generative samplers, including closed-form diffusion samplers, from in-context samples. The theory gives softmax attention a concrete generative role in computing responsibility weights. Extends the theoretical understanding of in-context learning to the generative setting.

entry.title: Beyond Arbitrary Geometry: Topology Generalization In neural PDE Operators

author.name: Peiyao Chen, Zhouyuan Xu, Jianguo Nie, Jiansheng Fan, Chen Wang

entry.summary: This paper rigorously separates geometry generalization from topology generalization in neural PDE operators, using Hodge heat flow and a benchmark (TopoBox-3D) where tunnels and cavities vary Betti numbers. Across six architectures, implicitly topology-aware models degrade out-of-distribution in 37 of 45 model-task cells, with spectral properties (Rayleigh quotient) predicting error. It exposes a blind spot in how neural operators are evaluated and understood.

entry.title: A Theoretical Framework for Masked Pretraining (MPT)

author.name: Qi Zhang, Runyu Zhou, Yifei Wang, Yisen Wang

entry.summary: The paper develops a theoretical framework for masked pretraining, proving that masking implicitly creates semantically similar positive pairs so that reconstruction loss behaves like contrastive learning in pulling them together. This establishes a formal bridge between two major self-supervised paradigms. It helps explain the mechanism behind MPAE/MAE-style methods across domains.

entry.title: Behavioral Cloning Outperforms Entropy-Regularized RL: Critic-Driven Failure of Actor-Critic Methods on Adaptive Tumor Treatment

author.name: Aleksandar Dimitrov, Giacomo Spigler

entry.summary: Studies adaptive tumor dosing on a three-population ODE where optimal-control analysis fixes the structure of a good bang-bang schedule, used as a near-optimal reference. It finds that SAC trained from scratch never achieves cure while behavioral cloning of the reference succeeds, diagnosing critic-driven failure modes of actor-critic methods in clinical control.

entry.title: Online Draft Co-Training for Speculative Decoding in Large-Scale, Long-Context RL Post-Training

author.name: Zili Wang, Zhaopeng Qiu, Yuekai Zhang, Shuang Yu, Junjie Lai

entry.summary: Presents an end-to-end system for co-training speculative decoding drafts with target models during large-scale, long-context RL post-training, where rollout generation dominates cost. It extends context-parallel attention to support branch attention and introduces TapChannel for transporting target features across pipeline-parallel stages.

entry.title: A Theoretical Analysis of Generalization Dynamics in Neural Networks under Gradient Descent with Weight Decay

author.name: Yuqing Wang, Ioannis G. Kevrekidis, Mikhail Belkin

entry.summary: This theory paper proves convergence of gradient descent with weight decay to a neighborhood of global minimizers and decomposes population error into data, optimization, and prediction-variation components with separate bounds. Authored by Mikhail Belkin and colleagues, it advances the theoretical understanding of how data, architecture, and training dynamics jointly determine generalization. Rigorous foundational work for the deep learning theory community.

entry.title: Miles v0.1: Production-Level Post-Training

author.name: RadixArk, :, Tom Chen, Mao Cheng, Shi Dong, Kangrui Du, Yanbin Jiang, Jiajun Li, Yiming Li, Tao Lin, Yusheng Su, Andy Ye, Yueming Yuan, Zhichen Zeng

entry.summary: Miles v0.1 is a full-stack, production-ready system for frontier RL post-training of LLMs, built on the slime codebase with SGLang-based rollout engines, a choice of Megatron-LM or PyTorch FSDP trainer backends, multiple weight-synchronization transports, and support for LoRA RL and on-policy variants. Its design principle is that every loop component be verifiable, clean, and customizable. It matters because accessible, reliable frontier-scale RL infrastructure is currently a bottleneck for both academic labs and enterprises.

entry.title: A Specialized Large Multimodal Model for Interpreting PET/CT in Head and Neck Cancer

author.name: Haengbok Chung, SunGyu Kim, Joo hyun Lee, Sangjin Bae, Min Jeong Cho, Minseok Suh, Jae Sung Lee

entry.summary: Fine-tunes LLaVA-NeXT with a two-level curriculum on a large multi-institutional PET/CT dataset to build a standalone specialized LMM for head and neck cancer interpretation. The work argues generalist LMMs lack domain knowledge and raise privacy concerns, motivating on-premise clinical specialists.

entry.title: Beyond Worst-Case Coreset Bounds for $k$-Clustering via Determinantal Sampling

author.name: Diptarka Chakraborty, Satyaki Mukherjee, Gaurav Vallabhdas Revankar, Hoang-Son Tran

entry.summary: This theoretical work shows that substantially smaller epsilon-coresets for (k,z)-clustering are achievable beyond essentially tight worst-case bounds, under mild natural assumptions on data. The authors use determinantal sampling to construct compact weighted subsets that preserve clustering costs for all center choices. The result bridges theory and practice since worst-case coreset lower bounds are driven by unrepresentative instances.

entry.title: Marigold V2: Revisiting Diffusion Transformers for Monocular Depth Estimation

author.name: Igor Pavlovic, Thiemo Wandel, Anton Obukhov, Luca Bartolomei, Andrey Davydov, Fabio Tosi, Matteo Poggi, Sabine S\"usstrunk, Dengxin Dai

entry.summary: Marigold V2 repurposes modern DiT-based image generation and editing models into state-of-the-art monocular depth estimators, targeting single-step inference from pretrained multi-step flow-matching models with optional quantization. It improves on prior Marigold recipes for out-of-distribution generalization and sharp, detailed depth maps at low inference cost.

entry.title: A Ticket from Marginals to Joints: Coupled-Noise Distillation for One-Step Block Generation in Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Lin Yao

entry.summary: Investigates whether diffusion language models can commit an entire block of tokens in a single forward pass using a noise-conditioned masked denoiser, showing that conventional winner-take-all or importance-weighted training gives the noise field only coarse control (information growing logarithmically with competing fields). It proposes coupled-noise distillation so a sampled field selects one joint mode of the block, enabling one-step block generation.

entry.title: Line-Coupled Language Model

author.name: Shiyuan Li, Shaorong Zhang, Zhaorui Yang, Qian Zhang, Greg Ver Steeg, Bingyao Li

entry.summary: LCLM is an autoregressive model that advances multiple text lines in parallel by predicting the next token for every active line while coupling lines through shared causal context, using line-staggered rotary positions. It retains the standard next-token objective and causal attention, unlike diffusion or insertion decoding which add training token traffic or struggle with dependent tokens. Controlled experiments suggest more useful output per forward pass than standard decoding.

entry.title: NeoHorse-1: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement via Agentic Post-Training with Routing Harness

author.name: NeoHorse Team, Guoliang Cao, Guohao Dai, Tianyu Guo, Kai Han, Hailin Hu, Zihan Jiang, Xiang Kuang, Boxun Li, Yulong Li, Zehua Pei, Yuchuan Tian, Jiamin Wang, Yu Wang, Yunhe Wang, Yihong Wu, Haiyang Xu, Shuo Zhang, Hang Zhou, Siyang Cheng, Jiayu Fan, Wei He, Qingrui Jiao, Hongguang Li, Zhiyuan Li, Runke Liu, Xi Liu, Xinchen Liu, Sinno Jialin Pan, Yi Ren, Liuyang Song, Chenyu Wang, Bei Yu, Quanlu Zhang, Xiangyu Zhang, Mengyu Zheng, Yingjie Zong

entry.summary: Presents NeoHorse-1, a family of agent-native models exploring recursive self-improvement through agentic post-training: a heterogeneous model pool with intelligent routing logs capability demands and interactions, converts them into structurally validated training examples preserving reasoning and tool calls, and organizes supervised fine-tuning via routing signals.

entry.title: Grounded Skill Synthesis from Code at Scale for Agentic Intelligence

author.name: Yongqi Tong, Pan Wang, Hang Wang, Jianshe Li, Xin Zhang, Jiang-Ming Yang, Wei Wu

entry.summary: Code2Skill is a fully automated pipeline that mines source code into implementation-anchored skill records (atomic operations, workflows, recurring patterns) and verifies each record via source-body-blind reconstruction, requiring no prior agent-environment interaction. This bridges the gap between trajectory-based skill synthesis (environment-bound) and document-derived skills (unverifiable). It addresses a core scalability problem for transferable agent competence.

entry.title: Studying Image Tokenizers as Visual Languages in Unified Multimodal Models

author.name: Siting Li, Zhengyang Wang, Simon Shaolei Du, Xi Chen, Yang Liu

entry.summary: This work builds a controlled pure-autoregressive testbed to study how image tokenizers behave when visual tokens are modeled jointly with text, tracking task-specific validation losses across text, image, text-to-image, and image-to-text prediction during multimodal continual pretraining. Findings include that losses must be analyzed per task due to divergent scaling behavior, informing multimodal learnability and tokenizer design.

entry.title: ProtoRAG: Prototype-Based Retrieval Augmentation for Few-Shot Fine-Grained Remote Sensing Object Detection

author.name: Jian Wang, Yuxiang Hong, Chufeng Zhou, Chao Pang, Xiaokang Zhang

entry.summary: ProtoRAG is a retrieval-augmented framework for few-shot fine-grained object detection in remote sensing that decouples coarse localization (via multimodal LLMs) from fine-grained recognition using an external object-level visual memory of learned prototypes. It introduces Discriminative Prototype Space Learning to build reliable visual memory from few support samples. This matters for applying retrieval augmentation ideas to visual recognition with scarce annotations.

entry.title: PASTEL: Panoramic Alignment for Monocular 4D Scene Reconstruction

author.name: Yuankun Yang, Yi Wei, Bo Bai, Wenyang Zhou, Li Zhang

entry.summary: PASTEL introduces a new 4D scene reconstruction paradigm combining visible-region reconstruction from monocular video with generation of invisible regions beyond camera boundaries, using a panoramic scene alignment representation to exploit generative priors. This matters for VR and embodied AI applications where full-scene synthesis from casual captures is desired. It pushes reconstruction toward generative scene completion.

entry.title: 3DHarnessBench: Probing Agentic 3D-to-Code Capabilities of Frontier Vision-Language Models

author.name: Ling Liu, Bingchen Gong, Amal Dev Parakkat, Maks Ovsjanikov

entry.summary: Introduces 3DHarnessBench, a benchmark evaluating frontier VLMs on recovering 3D geometry as Blender Python code across four harness settings of increasing agentic freedom: single-view, multi-view, active visual exploration, and full 3D interaction via Blender MCP function calls. It probes perception, tool calling, and self-correction.

entry.title: Disparity Has a Sign: Stereo Matching Beyond the Zero-Disparity Plane

author.name: Jian Shi, Xinge Yang, Chaoyang Wang, Wolfgang Heidrich, Peter Wonka

entry.summary: The paper exposes a blind spot in modern stereo matching: models fail when disparity crosses zero, with end-point error rising 4.6-37x, because rectified parallel camera geometry makes negative disparities unrepresentable even though cinema 3D and VR content routinely contains objects behind the zero-disparity plane. The authors contribute ZDPShift, a benchmark of 21,495 stereo pairs from seven cinematographer-authored open movies, to measure this failure. The diagnosis cascades through datasets, architectures, and evaluation protocols, suggesting significant rethinking of the standard pipeline.

entry.title: PhysFlow: Physics-Aware Optical Flow for Motion Controllable Video Generation

author.name: Cong Wang, Hanxin Zhu, Yonglin Tian, Jiayi Luo, Ruiqi Song, Boyi Sun, Long Chen, Zhibo Chen

entry.summary: PhysFlow is a two-stage video generation framework that decomposes generation into physics-aware optical flow synthesis (PA-Flow) followed by motion-conditioned appearance synthesis, aiming to improve the physical plausibility of generated videos. By encoding physical regularities in motion patterns, it also enables motion-controllable generation. This addresses a well-recognized weakness of current video diffusion models: visually appealing but physically implausible dynamics.

entry.title: Human-Centric Image Captioning with Subject-Centered Spatial Understanding

author.name: Bozhou Li, Jiahang Zhang, Yue Ding, Yushuo Guan, Bohan Zeng, Yiyan Ji, Xinlong Chen, Yang Shi, Yifan Dai, Yuran Wang, Chengzhuo Tong, Pengfei Wan, Yuanxing Zhang, Wentao Zhang

entry.summary: This paper identifies structural hallucinations in multimodal LLMs for human-centric scenes, particularly failures in subject-centered spatial grounding like egocentric left/right laterality and anatomical-object binding, which existing benchmarks under-detect. The authors build a systematic framework to expose and quantify these localized spatial inversions. This matters because such errors propagate into downstream avatar and human video/image generation and fine-grained action understanding.

entry.title: SignRefine: Adapting Foundational Video Models for Sign Language Generation

author.name: Anton Pelykh, Edward Fish, Ozge Mercanoglu Sincan, Richard Bowden

entry.summary: SignRefine adapts a pretrained video diffusion transformer for sign language video generation from 2D keypoint conditioning, using local adapters with spatial grounding to refine hand and face articulation that generic video models render unintelligibly. The release includes NVSign, a large-scale sign language video dataset to support broader research. This advances accessibility technology for deaf and hard-of-hearing communities.

entry.title: Spheriverse: 3D Scene Understanding from Spherical Observations in the Wild

author.name: Fei Teng, Sheng Wu, Mengfei Duan, Guoqiang Zhao, Junhui Ma, Kai Luo, Siyu Li, Hao Shi, Zhiyong Li, Kailun Yang

entry.summary: Spheriverse is a large-scale dataset of 64,400 temporally aligned spherical image-LiDAR pairs across 644 sequences, spanning diverse scenes, illumination, and weather conditions with fine-grained semantic classes. The authors address the angular-vs-Cartesian representation gap and establish benchmarks for semantic occupancy prediction, semantic mapping, and 3D object detection, evaluating over 30 methods. It matters because omnidirectional perception is central to autonomous driving and surveillance, yet high-quality spherical benchmarks are rare.

entry.title: Privacy Leakage from a Thousand Words: Millipixel Location Recovery from Dot Maps

author.name: Yuntao Du, Tanishq Pauskar, Hao Wang, Jing Su, Ninghui Li

entry.summary: AutoLocate is an automated framework that recovers high-precision individual locations from dot maps by exploiting anti-aliasing artifacts introduced during rendering, which encode sub-pixel information about dot positions. It formulates recovery as black-box optimization over estimated coordinates. The work reveals a previously underappreciated privacy risk in widely used geospatial visualizations of sensitive data.

entry.title: GIF: Agentic Generation of Interactive and Functional Object Compositions for Robot Learning

author.name: Long Xu, Zhiqi Zhang, Mi Yan, Shengliang Deng, Chong Xia, Mingyu Dong, Jiayi Chen, Jiangran Lyu, Fei Gao, Zhizheng Zhang, He Wang

entry.summary: GIF is an agentic framework for generating interactive, functional object compositions in simulation to support scalable evaluation and data generation for robot manipulation foundation models. It recasts scene generation as disentangled reconstruction plus relative pose recovery, combining 2D and 3D generative models with a pose refinement module. This addresses the gap between coarse scene layout generation and the fine-grained functional compositions needed for manipulation training.

entry.title: RefGuard: Identity-Aware Language-Guided Robot Manipulation via Joint Target-Anchor-Frame Grounding

author.name: Lan Wei, Kangyi Lu, Yongchen Wang, Chenmeng Bi, Qi Chen, Hanlin Niu, Yip Fun Yeung, Dandan Zhang

entry.summary: RefGuard addresses identity-switch failures in VLA manipulation, where a robot executes a geometrically valid action on a semantically compatible but unintended object in cluttered scenes. It treats referent resolution as joint inference over target, anchor, and reference frame, and delays commitment to avoid irreversible silent errors. This highlights an underexplored failure class in language-guided manipulation.

entry.title: ContextFlow: In-Context Flow Matching for Robot Manipulation

author.name: Jian Ding, Xianjie Dai, Roei Herzig, Nussair Hroub, Jinjie Mai, Dengxin Dai, Bernard Ghanem, Mohamed Elhoseiny

entry.summary: ContextFlow brings in-context imitation learning to robotics via a conditional flow-matching model that learns continuous action distributions, avoiding the discretization and error accumulation of autoregressive next-token approaches. The method aims to improve generalization to unseen task configurations in robot manipulation. It combines two strong current threads - in-context learning and flow-matching policies - in a way that has been underexplored.

entry.title: PhysReal: Learning Real-World Deformable Object Physics via Hybrid Constitutive Modeling

author.name: Yinan Deng, Jianqiao Song, Yisi Zhang, Yuhan Wang, Jiahui Wang, Yufeng Yue

entry.summary: PhysReal is a video-driven framework that learns and simulates the physics of real deformable objects using a spatially varying hybrid of analytical expert constitutive models and neural residuals, coupled with a differentiable MPM simulator and 3DGS renderer. Expert models give interpretable physical priors while neural components capture heterogeneous material responses beyond predefined formulations. This is relevant to interactive world models and deformable manipulation.

entry.title: Visible-Reachable Workspace for Perception-Aware Humanoid Design

author.name: Boxi Xia, Zijiang Yang, Ryan Shin, Bokuan Li, Eric Wun-Hao Lu, Jacob Lee, Jiaxun Liu, Boyuan Chen

entry.summary: The paper introduces the visible-reachable workspace (VRW), a design-stage measure that conditions camera visibility on feasible reaching configurations, capturing that a kinematically reachable target may not be visible in the required pose. The authors demonstrate the concept by building a 31-DoF humanoid with independently actuated RGB-D cameras. This is a novel co-design contribution linking perception and kinematics in humanoid design.

entry.title: Training on probes: What's going on

author.name: Charlie Steiner

entry.summary: Analyzes what happens when probes are incorporated into training: gradient descent against a probe during continued training teaches the model to evade it, while post-hoc probe training works but does not teach new skills. The key claim is a theorem that RL with a probe term fails to change behavior under naive credit assignment, so recent papers obtaining effects from RL-on-probes are working through collateral credit-assignment damage.

entry.title: Beyond Prompts: Measuring and Optimizing LLM Tool-Agent Harnesses

author.name: Cen (Mia), Zhao, Haibo Ruan, Wenjie Chen, Pei-fen Tu, Usman Abbasi, Joel Hesch

entry.summary: This work studies improving fixed-model tool agents at runtime by optimizing the harness around the model, scoped to prompts and tool-boundary middleware. It proposes an optimizer-agnostic evaluation protocol with metrics including mean and worst-condition lift, repeatability, and a conservative held-out gain estimate RelLift95(B).

entry.title: FACT: A Forensic Agent with Compiled Tool-Use Trajectories for AI-Generated Image Detection

author.name: Jiaoyang Chen, Bin Hu, Jingyu Hu, Kun Zhou, Qin Zhang, Zhengzhe Liu

entry.summary: FACT is an agentic AI-image detector that learns an image-conditioned policy for selecting and sequencing forensic tools, interpreting returned evidence and stopping when sufficient, rather than applying a fixed detector. Its Evolve-Distill-Refine pipeline compiles execution-verified forensic skills into action-observation trajectories, targeting open-world generalization across unseen generator families.

entry.title: Segment Any Motion with Radar: Robust Multimodal Moving-Object Segmentation and Tracking

author.name: Jue Wang, Xuan Wang, Hao Zhou, Ruixiang Zhou, Yixuan Zhou, Tianshuo Yuan, Jieming Ma, Jie Zhang, Fei Luo

entry.summary: This work introduces RGBTR-Motion, a synchronized benchmark pairing RGB, thermal, and radar streams with dense moving-instance masks and temporally consistent identities for surveillance, and leverages radar's direct radial velocity measurement for robust moving-object segmentation. It targets failure of appearance and flow-based methods under poor illumination, weather, and occlusion. Both a resource and a method contribution for all-weather motion perception.

entry.title: Same Values, Different Languages? From Multilingual Probing to Steering LLMs Toward Chinese Social Values

author.name: Yuemei Xu, Kexin Xu, Jian Zhou, Haoyu Lu, Yequan Wang, Aishan Liu

entry.summary: The paper builds C-Voices, a multilingual contrastive probe dataset of 86,400 dilemma-based instances in six languages covering twelve dimensions of Chinese Social Values, to test whether LLM value preferences are consistent across languages, and develops steering methods toward CSV alignment. It moves beyond safety-centric principles to culturally grounded value alignment. Findings inform pluralistic alignment of multilingual LLMs.

entry.title: A Novel Semantic Manifold Alignment Attack against Embedding-to-Embedding Obfuscation in Privacy-Preserving LLMs

author.name: Sicong Li, Lingfeng Yao, Xingke Yang, Ke Tu, Chenhao Wu, Hao Wang, Jiang Liu, Phone Lin, Xin Fu, Miao Pan

entry.summary: This security paper attacks Embedding-to-Embedding Obfuscation (E2EO) schemes for privacy-preserving LLM inference, showing their one-to-one substitution mechanism lacks cryptographic guarantees and can be broken by Proxy Manifold Alignment, which maps obfuscated embeddings back to plaintext semantics. E2EO previously resisted token-frequency and embedding-inversion attacks. The result is a significant caution for deploying embedding-obfuscation privacy defenses.

entry.title: VidaForge: Open Research Infrastructure for Video Pretraining Data Recipes

author.name: Yan Ma, Jiadi Su, Zhulin Hu, Ethan Chern, Linhao Zhang, Tiantian Mi, Pengfei Liu

entry.summary: Presents VidaForge, open infrastructure representing video pretraining data recipes as executable five-stage workflows from raw videos to training datasets, where decisions can be varied to build alternative datasets with full provenance. It demonstrates comparative analysis of data recipes by coverage and quality in early pretraining.

entry.title: SciLitBench: Benchmark and Design Principles for LLM-Powered Systematic Literature Reviews

author.name: Miguel Zabaleta, Baihan Lin

entry.summary: SciLitBench is a multi-stage benchmark for LLM-driven systematic reviews covering title/abstract screening, full-text screening, and schema-guided extraction, with 42,981 records, 1,012 full texts, and annotations for 888 included papers. Evaluating 22 open-weight LLMs from six families, it finds explicit criteria improve abstract screening substantially while data extraction accuracy drops sharply for complex tasks, yielding actionable design principles.

entry.title: When and What to Teach: Budget-Aware Online Adaptation for Web Agents

author.name: Jianwei Zhang, Sihan Cao, Pengcheng Zheng, Ya Wen, Pei Ke, Kuien Liu, Shen Gao, Wei Dong, Yang Yang, Chaoning Zhang

entry.summary: This paper proposes Score-Guided Online Teaching with Budgeted Trajectory Trimming, a framework for cost-efficient online adaptation of lightweight local web agents taught by a stronger teacher model. It identifies that standard trajectory-level preference optimization wastes budget on unresolvable episodes and redundant turns, and systematically prunes which episodes and steps receive teacher feedback.

entry.title: The Normalization of Deviance in AI Development

author.name: Emilio Barkett, Alexander Kimpton, Daniel Graham, Yusuf Kundgol

entry.summary: This paper argues that AI safety analysis has overemphasized capability risk while neglecting organizational failure dynamics, applying the concept of normalization of deviance to institutions building AI systems. Using case studies of the Challenger disaster, Three Mile Island, and the Boeing 737 MAX, it identifies structural mechanisms that predispose organizations to drift toward catastrophic failure regardless of model capability levels.

entry.title: Multimodal Resource-Exhaustion Attacks on Vision-Language Models via Joint Pixel-Prompt Optimization

author.name: Zhaoxiong Ni, Yatie Xiao, Chi-Man Pun, Fei Peng, Qingxiao Guan, Keke Tang

entry.summary: The paper introduces JPPO, a compound adversarial framework that jointly optimizes image perturbations and user-visible prompts to mount resource-exhaustion (availability) attacks on autoregressive vision-language models. Prior work treated only the image branch as an attack surface; elevating the prompt to a first-class adversarial variable expands the threat model for VLM deployments.

entry.title: Substrate-Portable Execution for Production LLM Workflows

author.name: Tarun Gopinath, Atul Kulkarni, Vijay Rajakumar, Shrikar Katti, Parthasarathy Govindarajen

entry.summary: Presents a binding-abstraction approach for making production LLM agent workflows portable across runtimes, motivated by Amazon Rufus, which serves real-time, asynchronous, and batch modes with different SLOs. Decoupling orchestration semantics from a single runtime enables batch inference APIs with roughly 50% cost savings. Matters because it documents hard-won systems engineering from a large-scale production deployment.

entry.title: Elastic Horizon: Discovering the Effective Interaction Frontier in Agentic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Gangyi Zhang, Junjie Meng, Letian Zhang, Wei Wu, Yang Zheng, Dong Wang, Yang Liu, Guanjun Jiang, Chongming Gao

entry.summary: The paper proposes the effective interaction frontier hypothesis: a dynamic boundary beyond which longer agent-environment interaction horizons yield diminishing returns relative to linearly growing cost. Elastic Horizon is a closed-loop controller that tracks this boundary via the 90th percentile of successful trajectory lengths, replacing open-loop curriculum schedules. It improves agentic RL training efficiency on benchmarks like AppWorld for long-horizon LLM agent tasks.

entry.title: AgentIdeaBench: Benchmarking Scientific Ideation in the Agent Era

author.name: Yunxiang Mo, Tianshi Zheng, Yisen Gao, Rui Wang, Newt Nguyen Kim Hue Nam, Kelvin Kiu Wai Tam, Jiaxin Bai, Yangqiu Song, Ginny Wong, Simon See

entry.summary: A multidisciplinary benchmark evaluating scientific ideation under two matched settings - static observation of curated papers versus active exploration via retrieval - across 33 LLMs and 40 scored subfields in five disciplines. It directly addresses the gap between static idea-generation tests and the retrieval-and-reasoning workflows of real AI scientists.

entry.title: Key Path Identification for Resolving Knowledge Conflicts via SAE-based Steering

author.name: Wenbo Zhang, Zhongxiang Sun, Zhiguang Han, Jun Xu

entry.summary: Improves sparse-autoencoder-based steering for knowledge-conflict resolution by identifying a minimal key path of features rather than mass-steering large correlated feature sets, showing that steering a small subset matches or beats existing methods with less noise. The work also accounts for feature interactions neglected by correlation-based selection. This advances interpretability-driven controllability of LLM knowledge behavior.

entry.title: SRPO: Setwise Relative Policy Optimization for Multi-Agent LLMs

author.name: Shengtian Yang, Ziyu Xiong, Yu Li, Yewen Li, Qingpeng Cai, Lei Feng

entry.summary: Proposes SRPO, a reinforcement learning method for multi-agent LLMs that treats the active set of jointly-consumed outputs as one multi-agent action, combining member log-ratios into a cardinality-normalized set ratio with a single relative advantage and clipping. This aligns the RL update unit with the actual action executed by the system and unifies division-of-labor and joint credit assignment.

entry.title: CLAMP: Constrained Decoding for Vision-Language Embodied Planning

author.name: Tianyi Ma, Parisa Kordjamshidi

entry.summary: This paper introduces CLAMP, a framework that converts visual scene evidence and a symbolic action model into decoding-time constraints for a frozen vision-language model used in embodied planning. Hard token masks during decoding prevent the model from referencing unobserved objects, selecting actions without available affordances, or violating syntax, improving plan executability without fine-tuning. It matters because it addresses the gap between fluent-looking plans and actually executable robot actions.

entry.title: Everything in Moderation: Per-Domain Coverage Optima and Alignment-Resistant Domain Gaps in Multi-Domain Mid-Training

author.name: Yunpeng Xu, Kun Zheng

entry.summary: A controlled study of mid-training data composition on Qwen3-8B-Base across five logical-reasoning domains, training 30 simplex allocations at five seeds each. The authors find every domain has an interior coverage optimum in a moderate 10-40% band, and that some domain gaps persist after alignment. The work offers principled guidance for data mixture design in the mid-training stage.

entry.title: TC-Next: Zero-Shot Multimodal Cyclone Forecasting

author.name: Zhe Wang, Sijie Chen, Yiming Luo, Daehyun Kim, Chien-Yi Chang

entry.summary: TC-Next is a multimodal deep learning model that forecasts tropical cyclone track and intensity at 6-24 hour lead times by combining foundation-model atmospheric forecast fields with GridSat infrared satellite imagery. Trained only on GraphCast forecasts over the Western Pacific, it reduces track error by 15-44% and intensity error by 3-6x versus the rule-based TempestExtremes tracker, and generalizes zero-shot to Pangu-Weather and IFS HRES fields without retraining. This demonstrates that learned cyclone tracking can transfer across weather foundation models, which matters for operational hurricane forecasting.

entry.title: Interface-Aware KV Cache Quantization for Dense On-Chip NVM in Long-Context LLM Decoding

author.name: Jiahao Zheng, Yifan Qin, Xiaobo Sharon Hu, Yiyu Shi

entry.summary: This paper examines KV cache quantization when the cache resides in dense on-chip non-volatile memory behind fixed-range converters, showing that GPU-oriented schemes like KIVI and KVQuant impose structures (per-group metadata, sparse outliers) that cost 25% or more in this setting. It designs an interface-matched quantization scheme to reduce off-chip bandwidth pressure in long-context decoding.

entry.title: Geometry-Aware Test-Time Learning for Quantitative Spatial Reasoning

author.name: Gege Zhang, Shuaicheng Niu, Gang Dai, Lei Sun, Shuangping Huang

entry.summary: Introduces TTL-SR, a test-time learning framework for quantitative spatial reasoning in vision-language models that uses geometric consistency constraints and unlabeled test data to adapt predictions. It targets brittleness under distribution shifts caused by the high cost of 3D supervision.

entry.title: SkillSpec: Intent-Masked Specification Reasoning for Agent Skill Correctness

author.name: Yizhuo Zhang, Bo Kang, Yi Yang, Zhiyu Duan, Zhouteng Ye, Shunkun Yang

entry.summary: Proposes SkillSpec, a Hoare-style framework that recasts correctness of reusable agent skill bundles as specification reasoning, converting heterogeneous skill repositories into a unified graph representation to catch semantic failures like intent conflicts that are silently masked by the underlying model.

entry.title: VERPO: Verified Evidence Regularized Policy Optimization

author.name: Haijiang Li, Chengyu Lv, Yi Zhang, Zhibing Zhang, Rui Qian, Yuchen Zhang, Xiaofan Zhang, Mingshan Wang, Xiaofei Jing, Yu Tong, Cangqi Zhou

entry.summary: Introduces VERPO, a post-training framework that treats replayed evidence-conditioned teacher trajectories as proposals for token-level policy correction rather than targets for indiscriminate imitation, separating evidence-free reference restoration from signed corrections and using Fisher Evidence Contrast to attenuate spurious corrections.

entry.title: It is Not Yet Another Tool: Creating and Deploying an Agentic AI Companion in a Security Operations Center

author.name: Kritan Banstola, Faayed Al Faisal, Duy Dao, Ryan Irving, Daniel Lende, Xinming Ou

entry.summary: This is a rare longitudinal field study of an LLM-based agentic AI companion deployed for over a year in a real Security Operations Center, with analyst usage analyzed during a four-month evaluation. Analysts found the companion's outputs reusable in more than 90% of cases, providing empirical evidence of practical value for ticket triage automation. Such deployment-based evidence of agentic AI effectiveness in production security settings is uncommon and valuable.

entry.title: ProcArena: A Multi-Scenario Benchmark for LLMs on Direct and Interactive PL/SQL Development from Natural Language

author.name: Hang Zhang, Chaokun Wang, Yuzhi Pan, Ziyao Zhong, Shuo Cao, Yue Xue, Zeyu Huang, Xingwei Zhou, Fang Niu, Bofan Xie, Guanchen Ge, Leqi Zheng, Ziyang Liu, Xiannian Cao, Pengcheng Ge

entry.summary: ProcArena is an execution-based benchmark evaluating LLMs on natural-language-to-PL/SQL across multiple realistic scenarios: from-scratch generation, modification, debugging, and optimization, in both direct and multi-turn interactive modes and multiple dialects. It fills a gap by covering the full software development lifecycle rather than only one-shot generation.

entry.title: AURA-Eval: Evaluation Framework for Acting Under Risk Awareness in LLM Agent Trajectories

author.name: Ruoxi Shang, Christina-Maria Androna, Orfeas Menis Mastromichalakis, Yu Feng, Aniruddhan Ramesh, Rico Angell, Shang Hong Sim, Chrysoula Zerva, Emmanouil Koukoumidis

entry.summary: This paper introduces AURA-Eval, a benchmark framework for evaluating how LLM agents recognize and respond to safety-critical decision points in tool-use trajectories. It generates controlled variations of 157 sourced trajectories to produce 1,249 evaluation items, distinguishing cases where a safe fulfillment path exists, and evaluates 20 frontier and open-weight models using rubrics for risk detection and action strategy.

entry.title: From Synthetic Priors to Model Behavior: Structural Coverage in Tabular Foundation Models

author.name: He Zhao, Ryan Thompson, Daniel M. Steinberg, Ashfaqur Rahman, Edwin V. Bonilla, Cheng Soon Ong

entry.summary: The paper recovers or reconstructs the synthetic data generators behind four tabular foundation models and measures how well their synthetic pretraining task distributions cover the structural space of real benchmark datasets, using a common set of schema, distribution, and dependence descriptors. This distribution-level attribution approach explains how pretraining priors map to downstream performance.

entry.title: From LLM-Generated Specifications to Learned Quadruped Locomotion

author.name: Merve Atasever, Keyan Azbijari, Cagan Bakirci, Alfredo Reina Corona, Tolga Izdas, Richard Yang, Erdem Biyik, Jyotirmoy V. Deshmukh

entry.summary: This work studies whether LLMs can generate Parametric Signal Temporal Logic specifications from natural-language locomotion goals, which are then used as shaped rewards for quadruped RL policy learning, replacing hand-crafted reward engineering. It bridges formal methods interpretability with LLM automation to lower the expertise barrier for robot reward design. This is a promising direction for scalable, interpretable robot training.

entry.title: FreqBLiMP: Frequency-Controlled Minimal Pairs Reveal Robustness and Fragility of LLMs Under Lexical Rarity

author.name: Tyrone White, Yuki Arase

entry.summary: FreqBLiMP regenerates all 67 BLiMP paradigms under explicit Zipf-frequency regimes while preserving grammatical contrasts, testing whether LMs' grammatical preferences survive rare lexical items. Evaluations across open-weight model families and scales reveal both robustness and fragility patterns tied to lexical frequency. It exposes a systematic confound in minimal-pair evaluation that has been largely ignored.

entry.title: PV-WM: A Heterogeneous Micro-Macro World Model for Articulated Pedestrian-Vehicle Co-Rollout

author.name: Haozhuang Chi, Jingsong Liang, Ziying Song, Lei Yang, Shihao Li, Haoruo Zhang, Chen Lv

entry.summary: PV-WM is a history-only world model for joint pedestrian-vehicle forecasting that recurrently advances pedestrian root motion, 15-joint articulation, and vehicle states in a synchronized heterogeneous representation. It bridges two previously separate lines - road-agent forecasting (which ignores articulation) and pose forecasting (which ignores vehicles) - enabling articulated co-rollout for autonomous driving. Vehicle boxes are reconstructed from predicted center and heading with observation-aware corrections.

entry.title: Efficient Exploration Is Enough

author.name: Mikel Malag\'on, Jon Vadillo, Josu Ceberio, Michael Bowling, Jose A. Lozano

entry.summary: The paper redefines efficient exploration in the absence of extrinsic rewards: efficient explorers prioritize generating generalizable experience that supports predictive models across the environment. Theoretically, such agents naturally schedule trajectories to visit informative regions first; empirically, this produces an automatic curriculum of progressively complex behaviors.

entry.title: Bag of Tricks or Bag of Myths? Reducing Modeling Complexity with Task Knowledge in Explainable Suicide Risk Assessment

author.name: Shlok Shelat, Shrey Salvi, Souvik Roy, Manas Gaur, Amit Sheth

entry.summary: Audits 31 common NLP techniques across roughly 300 controlled experiments on 1,635 clinician-annotated social media posts for suicide risk assessment, testing which gains survive under severe class imbalance and author-disjoint splits. Provides evidence-based guidance for building clinically grounded, explainable risk-assessment systems.

entry.title: AttnCompress: Dynamic Attention-Guided Trajectory Compression for Software Engineering Agents

author.name: Zhengran Zeng, Yixin Li, Rui Xie, Wei Ye, Shikun Zhang

entry.summary: AttnCompress dynamically compresses the lengthy trial-and-error interaction trajectories generated by autonomous software engineering agents, using attention signals to decide what to prune while preserving task-critical evidence. It targets context-window limits and cost without the granularity mismatches of static pruning. This is directly relevant to making coding agents cheaper and longer-running.

entry.title: The Unreliable Progress Bar: Can LLM Agents Reliably Report Task Progress Throughout Execution?

author.name: Boyang Wang, Yunhan Wang, Yalun Wu

entry.summary: The authors systematically study whether LLM agents can accurately report their own task progress at multiple checkpoints, using tau^2-bench and a controlled testbed called StageIF spanning the task lifecycle. They find that reporting reliability varies by task stage, with nearly all deployed models reliable at some stages and unreliable at others, and failure modes differ by position in the task.

entry.title: From Where to How: Continuous 4D Interaction Forecasting from Egocentric Video

author.name: Qiaohui Chu, Haoyu Zhang, Meng Liu, Haoxiang Shi, Dongmei Jiang, Liqiang Nie

entry.summary: This paper introduces Coherent4D, a large-scale egocentric dataset for continuous 4D interaction forecasting, which unifies predicting where future interactions will occur in 3D with how the human body will move to achieve them. It addresses the gap left by prior work that models localization and pose forecasting separately, targeting applications in assistive robotics and human-computer interaction.

entry.title: Silent Revision: Measuring Undisclosed Change in the Safety Frameworks of Frontier AI Developers

author.name: Louis Yiven Zhu

entry.summary: This paper introduces the silent revision rate: the share of material changes to a frontier developer's published safety framework commitments that the developer's own changelog fails to disclose, contextualized by EU and California accountability requirements. The author releases a versioned, hash-pinned corpus covering every public version of safety frameworks from the twelve developers that have published one. This provides a novel, reproducible transparency metric for holding AI labs accountable for how they modify their safety commitments over time.

entry.title: Evaluating and Improving Evidence-Grounded Fact-Checking in LLMs via Multi-Round Evidence Ablation

author.name: Xingyu Deng, Mingzi Cao, Nikolaos Aletras, Xi Wang, Mark Stevenson

entry.summary: Introduces Fact-Ablated Evaluation (FAE), a framework that iteratively removes cited evidence to test whether LLM fact-checkers actually use provided evidence or fall back on parametric knowledge. Finds that off-the-shelf LLMs rely more on internal knowledge, and proposes a fine-tuning approach to improve evidence faithfulness. This matters for the reliability of automated fact-checking and misinformation detection.

entry.title: DeCAL: Towards Physically-Grounded Dexterous Vision-Language-Action Models via Contact-Aware Latent Co-Imagination

author.name: Yankai Fu, Ning Chen, Junkai Zhao, Heng Zhang, Guocai Yao, Pengwei Wang, Zhongyuan Wang, Shanghang Zhang

entry.summary: Presents DeCAL, a dexterous vision-language-action model built on a Mixture-of-Transformers architecture that unifies understanding, imagination, and action generation for contact-rich manipulation, with adaptive tactile integration and explicit physical dynamics modeling. It targets occlusion and contact-dynamics challenges that limit existing VLA models in fine-grained robotic tasks. A substantial architecture contribution in embodied AI.

entry.title: One Rate Is Not Enough: Adaptive Anisotropic Learning Rates for LoRA Fine-Tuning

author.name: Huiyi Wang, Daijiao Liu, Lina Yao, Dong Gong

entry.summary: This paper shows that uniform learning rates across LoRA rank-one components overlook substantial within-module heterogeneity, causing low-velocity modules to underutilize the rank budget. It proposes assigning each rank-one component an online-computed, mean-normalized effective learning rate. Given LoRA ubiquity in LLM fine-tuning, better utilization of adapter rank is broadly relevant.

entry.title: Rethinking the Evaluation of Efficiency Methods for Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Jiamu Zhang, Lingxi Zhang, Pengjun Lu, Qiyue Zhang, Yu-Neng Chuang, Zhengchen Li, Shuai Xu, Vipin Chaudhary, Hanjie Chen

entry.summary: This paper critiques evaluation practices for efficiency methods in LLM-based multi-agent systems, arguing that reported gains are often confounded by method-specific prompts and starting topologies, and frequently appear in settings where a single agent or random pruning suffices. The authors propose a more rigorous evaluation methodology to separate true structural efficiency improvements from artifacts. This is a valuable meta-analysis for a rapidly growing subfield.

entry.title: Are Verifier Errors Independent Within a GRPO Group? Evidence from Qwen2.5 Rollouts

author.name: Esther Xin

entry.summary: Analyzing 24,998 GRPO groups of Qwen2.5-1.5B rollouts on math benchmarks, the paper finds verifier errors are strongly correlated within groups (pooled correlation 0.530), reducing effective sample size of eight-completion groups to about 1.7 under an exchangeable-error model. Dependence varies with answer format, with fractions and symbolic expressions showing stronger clustering. This challenges independence assumptions underlying variance estimates and data-value analyses in RLVR.

entry.title: Not Just Oversmoothing: Detecting the Echo Chamber Effect in Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Asela Hevapathige, Ahad N. Zehmakan, Asiri Wijesinghe, Saman Halgamuge

entry.summary: Identifies the Echo Chamber Effect in GNNs, where representations collapse within communities while inter-community separation persists, a failure mode missed by global oversmoothing diagnostics. It introduces the Echo Chamber Index (ECI), which stratifies pairwise distances by community membership to quantify this heterogeneity.

entry.title: PhysSAE: Mechanistic Interpretability with Sparse Autoencoders

author.name: Nandita N. Patil, Eshwar R. A., Gajanan V. Honnavar

entry.summary: Applies sparse autoencoders to Physics-Informed Neural Networks, training overcomplete SAEs on penultimate-layer activations and causally intervening on dictionary atoms in the frozen hidden state. Across six PDE families, discovered SAE features align with independently defined physical observables, opening a path to interpreting scientific neural networks mechanistically.

entry.title: I Don't Miss You, but I Do: Self-Explanation Faithfulness of Modality Missingness in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Aydin Javadov, Daniel Schoess, Florian von Wangenheim

entry.summary: This paper introduces an interventional protocol for testing whether vision-language models faithfully self-explain how missing input modalities affect their predictions. The authors compare stated claims about modality sufficiency and counterfactual answers against realized behavior under actual modality interventions across eight open-weight VLMs and four tasks. The work matters because faithful self-explanation is a prerequisite for trustworthy deployment of multimodal models in imperfect real-world conditions.

entry.title: Risk-Conditioned Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models

author.name: Zixuan Liu, Fangzheng Wu, Brian Summa, Zizhan zheng

entry.summary: The authors extend Risk-Averse RLHF (which optimizes Conditional Value-at-Risk at fixed risk levels) by training a single LLM policy conditioned on a continuous risk-control input, letting users dial the degree of risk aversion at inference time without retraining or deploying multiple models. Experiments across multiple benchmarks show one risk-conditioned policy adapts to different risk levels. This is relevant to safety-critical LLM deployment where rare harmful generations carry high cost.

entry.title: GPU-Enabled Large-Scale Optimization Using Randomized Linear Algebra

author.name: Pratik Rathore, Zachary Frangella, Parth Nobel, Xuning Hu, Madeleine Udell

entry.summary: Introduces rlaopt, a PyTorch-based library providing GPU-accelerated solvers for large-scale optimization using randomized numerical linear algebra (RandNLA), including NystromPCG for linear systems, NysADMM for constrained convex problems, and SAPPHIRE for stochastic methods. It includes a modeling language so users can specify problems in natural mathematical syntax. This matters because it lowers the practical barrier to applying RandNLA algorithms at scale.

entry.title: Distillation as Probability Transport: Routed On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Tianle Xia, Lingxiang Hu, Yiding Sun, Linfang Shang, Ming Xu, Lan Xu, Ning Zheng, Wei Xu, Jie Jiang

entry.summary: RouteOPD reframes on-policy distillation as teacher-guided probability transport: instead of scalar per-token credit, it decomposes teacher-student disagreement into student-excess and teacher-deficit components, couples them into explicit transport pairs, and optimizes pairwise log-odds toward jointly realizable targets with an adaptive transport budget. This gives a more principled and stable mechanism for transferring teacher knowledge on student-generated trajectories. It matters because on-policy distillation is becoming a core LLM post-training technique, and this clarifies exactly how probability mass should move.

entry.title: The BatchNorm Illusion: Diagnosing Normalization Artifacts in Machine Unlearning Evaluation

author.name: Aaryaman Kalani, Murari Mandal, Dhruv Kumar, Mohan Kankanhalli, Yash Sinha

entry.summary: Identifies a confound in machine unlearning evaluation on BatchNorm architectures: a single weight-preserving forward pass over retain data rewrites normalization statistics and can reverse apparent forgetting metrics. The paper formalizes this as a fixed-point operator and proves such gaps are attributable to BN statistics rather than actual unlearning.

entry.title: SimpleMemVLA: A Simple but Effective Native-Video Memory for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Cheng Yin, Wang Xu, Junpeng Yang, Sikyuen Tam, Hanyu Liu, Yuan Yao, Xiangrui Zeng, Junbo Cui, Yequan Wang, Zhouping Yin, Yankai Lin

entry.summary: Challenges the assumption that minute-scale robot manipulation history is too large to process directly, introducing a VLA model with no dedicated memory module that instead passes intact timestamped video history to a pretrained VLM backbone and reads sub-task hidden states. This simplifies long-horizon partially observable manipulation.

entry.title: Broken on Arrival: Silently Defective LLM Artifacts in Public Model Registries and How to Catch Them

author.name: Aditi Patodiya

entry.summary: Empirically audits 327 quantized GGUF model artifacts from Ollama and HuggingFace using a calibrated smoke suite plus deeper evaluation, second-backend checks, and independent conversions as referees, revealing silently defective local LLM distributions that no pipeline currently tests. Proposes catching mechanisms for broken artifacts before they reach users.

entry.title: GradeTrap: Authority Cues in Images Shift VLM Judgments Despite Explicit Instructions to Ignore Them

author.name: Deep Dessai (The University of Texas at Austin)

entry.summary: GradeTrap is a controlled benchmark testing whether vision-language models defer to authority cues in images: it pits a student answer (sycophancy bait) against conflicting answers attributed to peers, teachers, or official answer keys, while explicitly instructing models to solve independently and ignore such cues. Across 60 synthetic trade-off scenarios, it measures how authority attribution shifts VLM judgments. This matters for deploying VLMs in consequential evaluation and assessment settings where uncritical deference to human authority is a safety and reliability risk.

entry.title: Separating Capability from Confidence: Grounded Dual-State Calibration for GRPO-Trained Medical Vision-Language Models

author.name: Yangyang Xie, Ke Hao, Jiaqi Liu, Yun Gu, Xinglin Zhang

entry.summary: DualRead addresses a flaw in GRPO-trained medical vision-language models where joint optimization of answers and verbalized confidence degrades answer learning and pushes confidence toward near-binary values. The method freezes the GRPO-trained actor and estimates reliability from internal states, combining pre-answer solvability with post-answer assessment, explicitly grounding confidence in visual evidence. This improves trustworthy deployment of medical VLMs where confidence must reflect patient-specific imaging.

entry.title: Towards Bridging the Gap Between Offline and Iterative Alignment via Preference Distillation

author.name: Wenbo Zhang, Wenzhuo Zhou, Hengrui Cai, Zhengling Qi

entry.summary: Investigates why iterative extensions of DPO outperform offline DPO for LLM alignment, finding through controlled experiments that the explicit preference model introduced in iterative procedures is the key factor. It then proposes preference distillation to bring these advantages into a purely offline alignment setting.

entry.title: HoneyRoute: Honeypot-Model Routing for Adversarial LLM Serving

author.name: Han Jin

entry.summary: HoneyRoute is an inference-serving layer that classifies incoming requests as malicious and routes them to a dedicated honeypot model, protecting production LLMs while harvesting attacker interactions for intelligence. The system combines a lightweight streaming router, a dual-implementation honeypot, and a feedback loop that turns trapped interactions into attacker fingerprints for router retraining.

entry.title: The Blindness of Document-Level Translation Evaluation

author.name: Ahrii Kim, Vil\'em Zouhar, Chanjun Park, Seong-heum Kim

entry.summary: This paper tests whether presenting full documents to annotators in machine translation evaluation actually elicits document-level judgments. Using a counterfactual condition (MIX) that mixes segments from different systems within a document, the authors find with 18,420 expert English-to-Korean annotations and 14 automatic metrics that scores and rankings are statistically indistinguishable between coherent and incoherent documents, suggesting current document-level evaluation protocols are effectively blind to cross-segment consistency.

entry.title: DFlow: Enabling Verifier Information Flow in Block Diffusion Speculative Decoding

author.name: Yaojie Zhang, Linfeng Zhang, Bin Cui, Xupeng Miao

entry.summary: Observes that in block diffusion speculative decoding, rejected token positions still carry useful verifier representations that existing methods discard, forcing the drafter to rebuild context from scratch. DFlow channels verifier information from rejected positions into subsequent drafting rounds, improving LLM inference efficiency without changing the acceptance decision logic.

entry.title: CantoneseLLM v2: Reasoning in a Low-Resource Language

author.name: Tsz Chung Cheng, Chung Shing Cheng, Chaak Ming Lau, Cheuk Hei Chong

entry.summary: The authors release CantoneseLLM v2, Qwen3 8B and 30B-A3B based models trained via continued pretraining on 784M Cantonese tokens, chat-vector merging, SFT, DPO, and RLVR. Their stage-by-stage evaluation yields insights: chat-vector merging transfers instruction following but not reasoning language, limited Cantonese SFT erodes reasoning traces, and DPO partially restores reasoning format. This is both a useful low-resource release and a study of which post-training stages preserve reasoning in language adaptation.

entry.title: Probing the Structure and Dynamics of LLM Value Expression through Value Conflicts

author.name: Kaicheng Zhang, Jingyi Xiao, Renjun Hu, Xiaoling Liu, Yunshi Lan, Xuan Zhou

entry.summary: Introduces Conflict-driven Value Probing, a controlled framework that places ten LLMs in value conflicts and applies four intervention types to study how models express and reconfigure values. It identifies recurring patterns including expression duality (idealistic in abstract settings, pragmatic in concrete conflicts) and functional steerability of expressed values. This challenges the view of model values as static and monolithic, with implications for alignment evaluation.

entry.title: From Echo Chambers to Epistemic Monoculture: Large Language Models Present Temporally Contingent Partisan Alignments as Knowledge

author.name: Wend K. Tam

entry.summary: The paper argues that LLMs are not neutral conduits like search engines but political intermediaries whose generated answers embed invisible framing decisions. Using mechanistic analysis of Llama 3.1 8B, it shows partisan identity is encoded as a locatable geometric direction, and examines how temporally contingent partisan alignments get presented as knowledge.

entry.title: Global Divergence, Local Convergence: Representation Geometry in SSMs and Transformers

author.name: Amit Ben-Artzy, Roy Schwartz

entry.summary: Analyzes representation geometry across transformers, SSMs such as Mamba, and hybrids, finding SSMs distribute representational information evenly across dimensions while transformers are dominated by a single principal direction, with hybrids shifting toward transformer-like skew. This connects architectural differences to measurable representational structure.

entry.title: Experience Funnel: A State-Policy Alternating Loop for Self-Evolving Agents

author.name: Wenbo Gao, Zhaomou Song, Zhiyuan Ji, Renxi Liu, Xing Li, Xianzhi Yu, Xiaoguang Li, James Chung-wai Cheung, Weizhe Lin, Yaoyuan Wang

entry.summary: Experience Funnel is a self-evolving LLM agent framework that couples fast textual state adaptation (skills, harnesses) with slower-to-update parametric policies, addressing the tension between rapid adaptation and durable skill consolidation. It alternates between explicit external context and internalized competence to convert task-specific interaction experience into reusable ability. This is relevant to the fast-moving area of self-improving autonomous agents.

entry.title: FrankenReport: Early Exiting in Long-Form Generation Using Expected Value of Computation

author.name: Zhengping Jiang, Gonzalo Ramos, Jina Suh, Shiqian Rachel Ng, Elias Stengel-Eskin, Justin Svegliato, Benjamin Van Durme, Andy Huntington, Sam Thomson

entry.summary: FrankenReport is an interface for long-form report generation that adaptively decides per section whether further computation will meaningfully improve quality, predicting future gains from intermediate drafts to enable early exiting. Simulation studies show up to 4x improvement over random allocation at low budgets, with smooth recovery of full-pipeline quality as budget grows, supported by user studies. It tackles the latency and cost problems of deep research systems with a principled compute-allocation approach.

entry.title: A Survey on Adversarial Attacks and Defenses for Diffusion Models Across Multiple Modalities

author.name: Ozgur Kara, Tarik Can Ozden, Furkan Horoz, Zeqian Long, Haotian Xue, Yipu Chen, Oguzhan Akcin, Yongxin Chen, James Matthew Rehg

entry.summary: This survey provides the first unified review of adversarial attacks and defenses for diffusion models across image, video, and 3D modalities, organized by a task-centric taxonomy with chronological groupings within each generative task. It also consolidates evaluation settings, datasets, and metrics across the literature.

entry.title: Beyond Classification: Structured Supervision Aligns Visual Evidence with Medical Semantics

author.name: Hexiang Bai, Hanyang Xu, Xiaoxue Li, Xiaoliang Wu, Shangde Gao, Hongxia Xu, Ke Liu

entry.summary: This paper investigates pre-training paradigms for Vision Transformers in medical imaging, addressing spatial collapse where classification pre-training leads models to rely on background shortcuts instead of localizing lesions. It evaluates three structured supervision forms: graph-based topological priors, dense segmentation constraints, and image-text cross-modal grounding. The work matters because it offers systematic guidance for building more reliable medical image analysis models.

entry.title: MobileVLA-R1 2.0: RL-Enhanced Reasoning for Mobile Robot Control

author.name: Ting Huang, Yue Huang, Zeyu Zhang, Shuicheng Yan, Hao Tang

entry.summary: MobileVLA-R1 2.0 is a vision-language-action framework that couples structured embodied reasoning with executable mobile robot control, trained through multi-granularity reasoning over trajectories and reinforcement learning enhancement. It targets the gap between high-level semantic reasoning and low-level locomotion/manipulation for long-horizon robot decision making. This aligns with the growing VLA-plus-RL trend in robotics.

entry.title: Scaling 3D Generative Priors to Large-Scale Scene Meshes from Multi-View Images

author.name: SangEun Lee, Wonseok Chae, Hoyoung Yoo, Geunyong Kim, NackWoo Kim, Hyeonjin Kim

entry.summary: Presents a training-free framework for generating large-scale textured scene meshes from multi-view images by tiling pretrained object-centric 3D generative priors across scene regions, with local and global coordination to preserve geometric continuity and appearance consistency.

entry.title: Learning to Use Imagination: Progress-Conditioned Future Utilization for World Action Models

author.name: Yijie Zhu, Zitong Yu, Wei Li, Hui Ma, Wen Li, Rui Shao, Liqiang Nie

entry.summary: Proposes ProWAM, a progress-conditioned World Action Model that adaptively weights the use of imagined future visual latents based on execution progress, addressing inter- and intra-progress non-uniformity in the utility of predicted futures for action generation. It extends vision-language-action models with dynamics-aware control.

entry.title: Ambient @ EgoLongQA 2026: Distilling Long-Video perception into a Sub-2B Model

author.name: Logesh Kumar Umapathi

entry.summary: A first-place ECCV 2026 Wearable-AI Challenge entry (sub-2B division, 0.8279 on held-out test) describing how a single 2B vision-language model answers questions about ten-minute egocentric videos in one forward pass. The approach distills the junior perception module of a tool-using agentic teacher pipeline, filtered to correct traces, recovering 89% of the teacher's accuracy with 1.1% of its parameters and lifting a 27.1% base model to 81.4%.

entry.title: Search-to-World: Evaluation of 3D World Delivery from User Request through Web Search

author.name: Zixiao Gu, Yabo Chen, Xunzhi Xiang, Yu He, Haibin Huang, Chi Zhang, Yunbo Wang, Xuelong Li

entry.summary: This work introduces the first end-to-end benchmark for evaluating whether agentic systems can turn web-retrieved content into a usable 3D world, defining metrics (Observed Retrieval Rate and World Delivery Rate) that separate finding relevant content from delivering a request-aligned 3D result. It also presents WorldSearcher, a harness connecting existing search agents to 3D world delivery pipelines.

entry.title: VI-Bench: Benchmarking Prompt Inversion from AIGC Videos

author.name: Wulin Xie, Rui Zhao, Kecen Li, Xiujin Liu, Bokang Zhang, Zheng Liu, Xinwen Hou, Chen Gong

entry.summary: VI-Bench is a benchmark for prompt inversion from AI-generated videos, built from 16.1 million real-user prompts and 900 human-verified AIGC videos, measuring whether generation-relevant controls (style, camera behavior) can be recovered, not just captions. This is important both for creative reuse/editing and for assessing prompt leakage privacy risks in video generation.

entry.title: Tracking-by-detection in Multi-object Tracking: Survey and Experiments

author.name: Yujin Yang, Kyujin Shim, Kangwook Ko, Changick Kim

entry.summary: This survey examines the tracking-by-detection paradigm in multi-object tracking, addressing a key reproducibility problem: methods are often evaluated under inconsistent protocols with different baselines, hyperparameters, and datasets, obscuring which components truly drive gains. The authors provide a structured survey plus standardized experiments to enable fair component-wise comparison. This is valuable because MOT is central to surveillance, autonomous navigation, and human-computer interaction, and the field lacks rigorous ablation-based evaluation.

entry.title: FIRE3D: Feed-forward Interactive 3D Scene Reconstruction Within A Minute

author.name: Hongchi Xia, Tianhang Cheng, Wei-Chiu Ma, Shenlong Wang

entry.summary: FIRE3D converts a single RGB image or casual video into simulation-ready 3D scene assets in under a minute, predicting per-object 6-DoF pose, bounding box, mesh, and texture via a feed-forward network with no test-time optimization. By modeling scenes as discrete, physically decoupled entities, it produces interactive environments far faster than prior interactive scene reconstruction methods.

entry.title: Prior-free relative 6D pose estimation of multiple object instances

author.name: Behdad Khodabandehloo, Andrea Caraffa, Davide Boscaini, Fabio Poiesi

entry.summary: This paper defines a new, extreme setting for 6D object pose estimation: recovering the relative poses of multiple instances of an unknown object in a single image with no CAD models, templates, or reference images. The proposed method, PROSE, uses training-free coarse correspondences from multimodal foundation model features, then refines them. It removes the last remaining prior assumption in a research line that has progressively reduced object-specific priors.

entry.title: Multi-robot Learning-based Informative Path Planning Using Spatio-Temporal Gaussian Process Kalman Filter

author.name: Muqing Cao, Yunwoo Lee, Junbin Yuan, Lorenzo Schenk, Sebastian Scherer

entry.summary: The paper proposes a grid-based spatio-temporal GP-Kalman filtering framework for learning-based multi-robot informative path planning in persistent target monitoring, replacing per-target GPs with a single latent field over a workspace grid. The recursive update handles arbitrary camera fields of view and avoids centralized belief assumptions of prior methods. This matters for scalable decentralized monitoring with real sensing and communication constraints.

entry.title: A Brain-inspired Hierarchical Framework for Zero-Shot Robot Task Reasoning and Execution

author.name: Guangming Wang, Pengfei Ye, Qizhen Ying, Yixiong Jing, Yuxiang Ma, Haonan Chen, Haibing Wu, Olaf Wysocki, Molong Duan, Brian Sheil

entry.summary: This paper proposes a zero-shot hierarchical framework for robots following open-ended language instructions, functionally inspired by the division of roles in the human brain. It combines visual perception, language grounding, action-sequence generation from a shared atomic action library, cost-based plan selection, and physical verification, addressing limitations of end-to-end VLA policies for long-horizon tasks. The work matters because it offers an explicit structure for decomposition, verification, and recovery that monolithic policies lack.

entry.title: ComVLA: Communication-Aware Split Inference for VLA Models in 6G-Connected Robotics

author.name: Boliang Liu, Wint Yi Poe, Jingyun Di, Riccardo Trivisonno, Giuseppe Caire

entry.summary: ComVLA addresses cloud-offloaded VLA inference for 6G-connected robots by using the dense semantic information in language instructions to select which visual tokens are transmitted over bandwidth-limited wireless links. Unlike semantic codecs requiring channel retraining or channel-agnostic token pruners, it couples the language modality with the communication channel. This makes large VLA models practical on wirelessly connected robots.

entry.title: PGMT: Perceptive General Motion Tracking for Humanoid Robots

author.name: Hongyi Li, Li Peizhuo, Yucheng Tao, Ze Wang, Fangzhou Xu, Jinyi Chen, Yanyan Yuan, Dapeng Jia, Yongbin Jin, Mingfeng Fan, Guillaume Sartoretti, Hongtao Wang

entry.summary: PGMT is a perceptive motion-tracking pipeline for humanoids that learns terrain adaptation by independently selecting motion references and terrains, learning a general tracking and recovery prior first. It adds motion-conditioned terrain glimpses that encode only terrain regions relevant to the current motion, plus terrain-aware tracking relaxation that preserves motion intent while permitting necessary deviations. Zero-shot deployment on a Unitree G1 demonstrates robust terrain-adaptive locomotion.

entry.title: Model Predictive Control of Tensegrity Robots via Contact-Aware Graph Neural Dynamics Model

author.name: Nelson Chen, Patrick Meng, Charles Tang, Angelina Degay, Zachary Brei, Rebecca Kramer-Bottiglio, Kostas E. Bekris, Mridul Aanjaneya

entry.summary: The paper combines an MPPI controller with a learned graph neural network dynamics model extended by a differentiable contact detection module, enabling control of a three-bar tensegrity robot over non-horizontal terrain, obstacles, and self-collisions. A closed data-collection loop iteratively improves both model and controller. This is a strong demonstration of learned dynamics for contact-rich, hard-to-model robot morphologies.

entry.title: Training on probes: Research ideas

author.name: Charlie Steiner

entry.summary: A sequel post laying out research directions for training models against interpretability probes, analogizing probes to hardwired instincts that must be connected to learned world-models, in the spirit of brain-like training stories. It proposes questions such as training probes on weak supervisors that only observe easy-to-detect subsets of bad behavior, and teaching new honest behaviors beyond the training distribution. The post is agenda-setting rather than empirical.

entry.title: Data Scout: Targeted Web Crawling for Domain-Specific Pretraining Corpora

author.name: Chirag Garg, Eelaaf Zahid, Farhan Ahmed, Jay Pankaj Gala, Eric Butler, Heiko Ludwig

entry.summary: Data Scout inverts the standard filter-a-web-archive approach for domain-specific pretraining data: an LLM expands a root topic into a taxonomy and thousands of search queries, and a probe classifier admits subdomains based on small samples, exploiting the finding that relevance has a sharp boundary at the subdomain level (e.g., 21x higher relevance in mathematics). This enables corpora for sparse, specialized domains that popularity-driven crawlers miss.

entry.title: SAFEGuard: Detect Optimization-Based Jailbreak Attacks Through Harmful Semantic Analysis and Fluency Measurement

author.name: Quoc Viet Vo, Trung Le, Damith C. Ranasinghe, Ehsan Abbasnejad

entry.summary: SAFEGuard is a unified detection framework for optimization-based jailbreak prompts that combines a hybrid fluency signal (cross-layer distribution distance plus perplexity) with harmful-semantic analysis, targeting attacks that are either highly fluency-optimized or semantically obfuscated. It aims to outperform existing detectors that fail against the wide range of adversarial search mechanisms.

entry.title: TDDN: Text-aligned Diffused DINO Network for Puzzle Understanding

author.name: Harsha Patnala, Debopriyo Banerjee, Ayush Sunil Munot, Somak Aditya

entry.summary: Fuses DINOv3 and CleanDIFT representations into a text-aligned perception encoder that preserves fine-grained visual detail CLIP lacks, matching CLIP on image-text retrieval with frozen backbones and roughly 590K alignment pairs while more than tripling its dense-prediction accuracy. Targets structured visual reasoning tasks like puzzles that current VLMs struggle with.

entry.title: Noise Adaptive Streaming Audio-Visual Speech Token Enhancement for Robust Full-Duplex Spoken Dialogue Models

author.name: Bella Godiva, Yeonju Kim, Yong Man Ro

entry.summary: AV-STE is a modular streaming front-end that restores corrupted semantic speech tokens from noisy audio and lip video before they reach the speech LLM, keeping the downstream dialogue model frozen and preserving its conversational abilities. This improves full-duplex spoken dialogue robustness under noise and overlapping speech without costly multimodal retraining of the dialogue model. The modular design is practical for real deployments.

entry.title: One Step, One Lead: Mitigating Higher-Order Interference in Multi-Domain Reinforcement Learning via Cross-Step Control

author.name: Zihan Lin, Xiaohan Wang, Jie Cao, Jiajun Chai, Guojun Yin, Wei Lin, Ran He

entry.summary: The paper identifies a sequential form of interference in multi-domain RL for LLM reasoning: gradients that look orthogonal in a single-step view can produce consecutive updates that partially reverse each other in output space. It uses adjacent-checkpoint token log-probability footprints to detect this second-order interaction and proposes cross-step control to mitigate it. Directly relevant to the increasingly common practice of multi-domain RLVR training of LLMs.

entry.title: HyperTransfer: Understanding the Equivalence between Base Optimizer and Hyperball

author.name: Jinghui Yuan, Hongtao Zhang, Jade Zou, Tianyu Li, Wenjie Zhou, Tianyu He, Wei Chen

entry.summary: Proves that Hyperball optimizers, which constrain parameter norms and update only directions, are dynamically equivalent to conventional base optimizers for scale-invariant networks. Builds HyperTransfer to reproduce a target optimizer's dynamics from only its initialization and learning-rate schedule, with an inverse mapping and extension to non-scale-invariant networks.

entry.title: Prevalence calibration as shortcut mitigation

author.name: Mohamed Amine Kina, Eike Petersen

entry.summary: The paper reframes shortcut learning as a calibration problem: unconstrained learning calibrates each shortcut group to its training prevalence, producing systematically over- and under-confident predictions across groups. The authors propose two encoder-agnostic prevalence-equalizing calibration methods that work even with frozen foundation model encoders. A clean conceptual insight with practical, broadly applicable mitigation techniques.

entry.title: Do Reviewers Still Reward Lexical Complexity? A Frozen-Rater Study of Preference Drift in 124K ICLR Reviews

author.name: Jiabin Zheng (School of Computer Science, Peking University)

entry.summary: Using a frozen rater design — over 81,000 machine reviews generated in a single window with one model family — the author separates year-to-year changes in submission composition from changes in human reviewer preferences across ICLR 2018-2025. The study tests whether reviewers still reward lexically elaborate prose now that LLMs have collapsed the cost of such writing.

entry.title: MEMO: Multimodal Evidence Memory Organization for Long-Horizon LLM Agents

author.name: Xian Gao, Jinpeng Wang, Jiacheng Ruan, Guangyu Cao, Ting Liu, Yuzhuo Fu

entry.summary: Tackles the tension between accumulating interaction trajectories and limited context in long-running LLM agents by organizing memory across modalities: text readout preserves fidelity but competes for context at near-uniform cost, while visual readout renders content as document-like images that exploit two-dimensional space for density. MEMO selects necessary evidence under a budget and assigns it an appropriate modality rather than defaulting to text. A creative angle on agent memory that leverages multimodal models as consumers of their own memory.

entry.title: ActReview: Rebuttal-Guided Training Data and Rubric Rewards for Actionable Peer Review Generation

author.name: Yiling Ma, Yilun Zhao, Sihong Wu, Ziyu Chen, Manasi Patwardhan, Arman Cohan

entry.summary: ActReview targets actionable peer review by decomposing it into diagnostic claims and revision suggestions, using author rebuttals from OpenReview as latent supervision for what concrete fixes look like. It builds a 40K-example dataset (ActReview-40K) and applies rubric-based rewards for post-training. This is a clever use of naturally occurring review-rebuttal pairs to improve LLM feedback quality.

entry.title: GenPuzzle: Benchmarking Visual Reasoning in Image Generation Models

author.name: Changpeng Zhao, Yiren Song, Jinpeng Wang

entry.summary: GenPuzzle is a benchmark of 2,005 problems across 12 tracks (Sudoku, mazes, tangrams, nonograms, orthographic projection, mathematical visual proofs, etc.) requiring image-generation models to solve visual puzzles and express solutions faithfully in pixels. It shifts evaluation of image generators from aesthetics and prompt alignment toward reasoning-centric generation.

entry.title: One Model, Two Worlds: Bidirectional Sonar-Optical Translation

author.name: Shengji Jin, Trung Tien Dong, Ahmed Lamidi, Chen Chen, Xiaomin Lin, Yi Sheng

entry.summary: This paper introduces DARB, a direction-asymmetric diffusion bridge that shares a generative trunk for bidirectional sonar-optical image translation while routing direction-specific physical priors through asymmetric pathways (range-aware modulation for sonar-to-optical, polar ray-dependent processing for optical-to-sonar). This avoids duplicating models for the two directions while respecting differing image-formation physics. It matters for underwater perception where each modality has complementary strengths.

entry.title: Selective Knowledge Control for Continual GUI Agent Learning over Application Streams

author.name: Zirui Shang, Xin Shu, Yang Liu, Zhi Gao, Xinxiao Wu, Lifeng Fan

entry.summary: Proposes activation-conditioned selective knowledge control for continual learning in GUI agents, using neuron-level gradient manipulation to protect highly activated MLP neurons carrying historical knowledge while accommodating new applications. It maintains a compact historical knowledge state over application streams.

entry.title: TransNormal-2: Geometry-Grounded Rectified Flow with Edge-Aware Decoding for Precise Normal Estimation

author.name: Mingwei Li, Yi Yang, Hehe Fan

entry.summary: Identifies VAE reconstruction degradation as a shared error source in diffusion-based monocular geometry estimation, quantifying 1.3-8.5 degree mean angular error from encode-decode of ground-truth normals, and proposes TransNormal-2, a FLUX.2-based rectified-flow framework with geometry-aware supervision and edge-aware decoding correction to fix boundary normals.

entry.title: TeMo: Temperature Modulation for Multimodal Contrastive Learning

author.name: Dhimitrios Duka, Bernt Schiele, Hilde Kuehne, Anna Kukleva

entry.summary: TeMo adaptively modulates the contrastive learning temperature hyperparameter per positive-negative pair based on their similarity, replacing fixed or globally learned temperature values. This enables more fine-grained multimodal contrastive training and integrates with both multimodal and unimodal contrastive objectives. Given the outsized role of temperature in CLIP-style training, this could broadly improve multimodal representation learning.

entry.title: CoordFormer: Give Me Any Coordinates and I Will Give You Labels

author.name: Iacopo Curti, Pierluigi Zama Ramirez, Alioscia Petrelli, Luigi Di Stefano

entry.summary: CoordFormer is a coordinate-based semantic segmentation architecture that predicts labels at arbitrary spatial locations via a Coordinate Decoder with localized cross-attention, combining coordinate embeddings and high-resolution patch features with global tokens from a ViT encoder on a downsampled image. This enables flexible inference at arbitrary resolutions with low memory on very-high-resolution imagery. It targets the persistent challenge of segmenting gigapixel or high-resolution images.

entry.title: LANTERN: A Closed-Loop Benchmark for VLM-Based Cooperative Driving with Temporally Grounded Warnings

author.name: Yongshuo Liu, Xu Gao, Morui Zhu, Yongqi Zhu, Qi Chen, Deyuan Qu, Song Fu, Qing Yang
