entry.summary: LANTERN is a closed-loop benchmark for temporally grounded cooperative driving warnings, separating warning onset, hazard onset, termination, and recovery, and evaluating each event under matched warning and no-warning executions to isolate the warning's contribution. It provides 3,272 sequences with over 236k frames and 120 matched route pairs, plus a Cooperative Unified Score. This enables rigorous measurement of whether VLM-generated warnings actually improve driving safety.

entry.title: How Long Until Your Robot Ignores You? A Safety Benchmark for LLM Orchestrators in Human-Humanoid Collaboration

author.name: Aulon Bajrami, Mohamed Elshamouty, Werner Kraus

entry.summary: This paper introduces the first benchmark for evaluating LLM-based robot orchestrators as safety-aware decision makers in human-humanoid collaboration, built on an MCP-based architecture with invariants grounded in ISO 10218-2:2025 protective measures. It defines five testable safety invariants and measures a compliance spectrum from overcompliance to full safety violations. This fills a genuine gap in evaluating natural-language robot safety layers against standards.

entry.title: CAST: Alternating State-Value Targets and Expanded Policy Gradients for Model-Based Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Pietro Noah Crestaz, Mohamed Yassine Kabouri, Nicolas Mansard, Andrea Del Prete

entry.summary: CAST improves model-based RL by learning the value of planner-guided behavior rather than the policy alone, alternating state-value targets to regularize value estimates with the current policy. From the Andrea Del Prete group with Nicolas Mansard, it targets the sample-efficient combination of learned policies with online planning. This is a meaningful algorithmic refinement for planning-augmented MBRL in robotics.

entry.title: When Does Memory Help? A Cost-Aware Evaluation of Long-Term Memory in Tool-Using LLM Agents

author.name: Shweta Mishra, Shashank Mishra

entry.summary: The authors introduce MERIT, a benchmark measuring whether long-term memory actually improves task-executing tool-using agents, rather than just dialogue recall as in LoCoMo or LongMemEval. With 23,440 scored episodes across three domains, it includes verified memory dependence, a difficulty ladder with updated-fact recall, controlled memory corruption, and full token and dollar cost accounting, addressing the open question of when memory is worth its cost.

entry.title: CUSP: Decomposable Collective Uncertainty for Multi-Agent Multimodal Reasoning

author.name: Chung-En Johnny Yu, David Garcia, Brian Jalaian, Nathaniel D. Bastian

entry.summary: CUSP is a training-free framework for system-level uncertainty quantification that maps multiple VLM responses into a shared semantic response space and pools them, reporting collective uncertainty (dispersion) and Jensen-Shannon divergence (conflict). A notable property is the exact decomposition of unnormalized collective entropy into interpretable components.

entry.title: AutoKD: Autonomous Knowledge Discovery

author.name: Qinwen Ge, Bo Ni, Haowei Fu, Ngoc N. Tran, Erik Blasch, Tyler Derr

entry.summary: Presents AutoKD, a six-agent LLM multi-agent framework for autonomous scientific knowledge discovery that is cumulative: validated findings persist in a knowledge base and steer subsequent inquiry, unlike one-shot hypothesis-generation systems. Targets the human-bandwidth bottleneck in data-rich scientific domains. Contributes an architecture for iterative, validated knowledge accumulation.

entry.title: A visual large language foundational model for medical image recognition using clinician-oriented social media

author.name: Lingxuan Hou, Yuhua Xie, Yue Hu, Yan Zhuang, Junqi Li, Chengzhi Xia, Binh Phu Nguyen, Abubakar Siddique, Minh Nguyen, Yao Hou, Yanju Bao, Kexin Liu, Ke Chen, Jianjun Sun, Zeqi Li, Trung Nguyen, Jiangli Lin

entry.summary: Constructs ThoughtMed-1M, a medical VQA dataset of over one million long-form pairs built from de-identified clinician social media images and expert commentary, using an LLM pipeline with clinician-in-the-loop verification to capture structured clinical reasoning and image-text alignment. Trains a medical visual foundation model on this data. Addresses scarcity of clinically grounded multimodal medical data.

entry.title: When and Why LLM Causal Priors Help: Closed-Loop Prior Selection for Amortized Causal Inference

author.name: Haohao Zhou

entry.summary: Investigates whether LLM-generated causal graphs can serve as synthetic training priors for prior-data fitted networks (PFNs) that estimate causal effects in a single forward pass, and proposes a closed-loop procedure for selecting which LLM-distilled priors actually improve estimates. This targets a recognized bottleneck (hand-designed priors) in amortized causal inference tools relevant to medicine, economics, and policy.

entry.title: Human-like moral judgments conceal divergent motive attributions in large language models

author.name: Xiaoyan Wu, Jean-Claude Dreher

entry.summary: Comparing five LLMs with two human samples (N=125 and N=742) on whistleblower moral judgment scenarios, the study finds models reproduce human rankings of moral character but attribute systematically different motives, portraying whistleblowers as more helpful and less self-interested than humans do. Prompt changes meant to elicit human-likeness shifted ratings little. This matters because it challenges the validity of using LLMs as human participants in moral psychology simulation.

entry.title: From Simulated Citizens to Simulated Deliberation: Challenges in Representation and Interaction

author.name: Chaemin Jang, Junsik Min, Jaewoo Choi, Donggyu Lee, Haiin Lee, Junyoung Park, Namhee Kim, Hyunwoo Kim, Jungwon Kim, Juho Kim, Nuri Kim, Jihee Kim

entry.summary: Evaluates LLM-based multi-agent deliberation using census-grounded Korean personas debating real policy questions against national survey benchmarks. Finds persona agents fail to reproduce population opinion patterns - responses are over-concentrated and often reverse demographic differences - though deliberations produce varied, reciprocal arguments and substantial stance movement.

entry.title: Do Dynamic Routers Need Memory? HeRo: History-Aware Routing for Efficient LLM Inference

author.name: Hongjin Lin, Wentao Wan, Keze Wang

entry.summary: Proposes HeRo, a dynamic layer-routing framework for LLM inference that maintains an explicit routing-state memory across model depth using linear attention, rather than making each layer-skip decision independently from the current hidden state. This addresses the path-dependent nature of routing decisions and aims to improve both efficiency and output quality versus stateless routers.

entry.title: CrossModalQA: A Cross-modal and Multi-hop Benchmark for Multimodal Retrieval-augmented Generation

author.name: Jiacheng Cai, Zijin Hong, Zheng Yuan, Huachi Zhou, Qinggang Zhang, Xiao Huang

entry.summary: CrossModalQA is an open-domain benchmark for evaluating multimodal retrieval-augmented generation, targeting cross-modal, multi-hop reasoning over heterogeneous text and image corpora rather than single-hop retrieval over small provided context sets. It addresses fragmented coverage in existing multimodal RAG benchmarks by requiring open-domain evidence discovery across multiple images and documents. This fills a genuine evaluation gap as multimodal RAG systems proliferate.

entry.title: ViT3Flow: A Test-Time Training Transformer MeanFlow for Postoperative Radiograph Synthesis in Scoliosis

author.name: Rui Tang, Sicheng Yang, Moxin Zhao, Hongqiu Wang, Guankun Wang, Lei Zhu, Hongliang Ren, Menglin Cong, Nan Meng

entry.summary: The authors propose ViT3Flow, a single-step conditional MeanFlow transformer that synthesizes postoperative spine radiographs from preoperative images to support scoliosis surgical planning. They also release ScoliSurg, the first paired dataset of 632 pre- and post-operative whole-spine radiographs with morphology annotations. The work frames surgical correction as finite-interval generative transport.

entry.title: Concord: A Video Relational Algebra for Cross-Modal Query Optimization

author.name: Sultan Muratbek, Charisse Ivana Yeung, Chanwut Kittivorawong, Alvin Cheung

entry.summary: Concord is a system for semantic video queries that introduces Video Relational Algebra, a nested algebra over videos, transcripts, frames, and object tracks, plus approximate rewrite rules and cost-based optimizations to avoid naive MLLM execution over hours of footage. This brings classical database query-optimization ideas to multimodal LLM workloads, addressing a real cost and accuracy problem.

entry.title: From Review to Authorization: Key-Isolated Threshold Signing for LLM Agents

author.name: Yu Zheng, Qizhi Zhang

entry.summary: KITA is a review-to-authorization architecture for autonomous LLM agents that keeps the user's signing key and all threshold key shares outside every LLM process, so compromising the proposer and fewer than t reviewer-signer domains cannot forge a valid authorization. This cryptographically separates judgment from execution authority, blocking prompt injections from crossing into effectful actions like payments and permission changes.

entry.title: The Role of Gradient Modification in Heavy-Tailed Nonconvex Stochastic Min-Max Optimization

author.name: Tianxi Zhu, Yi Xu, Xiangyang Ji

entry.summary: Provides a comprehensive theoretical analysis of SGD ascent-descent under heavy-tailed gradient noise with only finite p-th moment, showing that vanilla SGDA can converge without clipping or normalization in both nonconvex-strongly-concave and nonconvex-nonconvex settings. This challenges the common belief that gradient modification is necessary.

entry.title: Diamond Agent: Agentic Control of Federated HPC Resources as a Service

author.name: Haotian Xie, Junlin Chen, Mingkai Zheng, Yifan Zhu, Minu Mathew, Max Burnette, Yadu Babuji, Volodymyr Kindratenko, Shivaram Venkataraman, Kyle Chard, Ian Foster, Zhao Zhang

entry.summary: Diamond Agent is an agentic system that lets LLM-driven agents orchestrate HPC workflows across heterogeneous, independently administered clusters, providing typed skills for cross-site resource discovery, data movement, execution, and result retrieval. It addresses real barriers to agentic use of supercomputing infrastructure, including preserving workflow context and reasoning about site-specific scheduler policies. This is significant as scientific workloads become a major target for AI agents.

entry.title: AutoLexSteer: Automatic Contrast Construction for Lexical Activation Steering

author.name: Shuhe Wang, Lachlan Cowley, Eduard Hovy, Jey Han Lau

entry.summary: The paper introduces Hangman, a steering vector type operating at the level of word senses, and AutoLexSteer, the first fully automated pipeline for constructing steering vectors using related word families from WordNet. The resulting vectors can steer behaviors such as sycophancy with fine lexical precision. This addresses the manual, opaque nature of building activation steering vectors in interpretability and control.

entry.title: Mind the Approximation: Fisher-Weighted SVD Compression for ViTs

author.name: Moritz Thoma, Maximilian Groezinger, Maximilian Forstenh\"ausler, Emad Aghajanzadeh, Ryan Pegoud, Manoj Rohit Vemparala, Pierpaolo Mori, Alexander Frickenstein, Daniel Mueller-Gritschneder, Ulf Schlichtmann

entry.summary: The paper shows that improving Fisher approximation fidelity is a poor predictor of post-compression accuracy for Vision Transformers, then proposes FACTS, a structured Fisher approximation enforcing token-local aggregation while preserving within-token activation-gradient dependencies for Fisher-weighted SVD compression. This is a principled correction to a common assumption in loss-aware compression. It matters for deploying large ViTs under compute constraints.

entry.title: Zero-Shot Sim-to-Real Contact-Rich Assembly via Proprioception-Anchored Cross-Modal Pretraining

author.name: Yuhan Wang, Yurou Chen, Hongye Jiang, Wenzhao Lian

entry.summary: PACE is a cross-modal pretraining scheme that anchors temporal visual and force/torque representations by predicting proprioceptive state transitions, exploiting the fact that proprioception transfers consistently between simulation and hardware. This enables zero-shot sim-to-real transfer for contact-rich assembly tasks requiring submillimeter precision and reliable force interpretation.

entry.title: SAFIRE: Safety-Critical Benchmark for Fine-grained Fire and Smoke Understanding in Multimodal LLMs

author.name: Pengfei Li, Naufal Suryanto, Sicheng Zhang, Mohammad Alsharid, Muzammal Naseer

entry.summary: Introduces SAFIRE, a large-scale benchmark for fire and smoke understanding in multimodal LLMs with 83K captioned images across 20 scenarios and 193K multiple-choice VQA items spanning 10 dimensions from perception to reasoning, verified via a GPT-5.4-assisted pipeline. Evaluations of ten open-source models reveal significant reliability gaps in this safety-critical domain.

entry.title: IPM-FM: A Foundation Model with Consensus Feature Selection for Industrial Process Monitoring

author.name: Liang Cao, Weide Liu, Yan Qin, Jun Cheng, Weisi Lin, Bhushan Gopaluni

entry.summary: IPM-FM adapts the foundation-model paradigm to industrial process monitoring, learning general-purpose representations via self-supervised pretraining on unlabeled process data with consensus feature selection to handle safety-critical decisions and asymmetric sampling between process variables and lab measurements. It replaces the one-task-one-model paradigm that is label-inefficient and drift-prone. This brings transferable, multi-task models to a safety-relevant industrial domain.

entry.title: Do New Attention Mechanisms Actually Fix Attention Sinks at Million-Token Context?

author.name: Sara Rizwan, Samaanah Abdus Salam

entry.summary: SinkProbe is a diagnostic suite measuring sink mass, massive activations, and position-resolved recall at million-token contexts, applied to gated attention and Kimi K3 with Kimi Delta Attention and Attention Residuals. The paper asks whether fixes shown to cut first-token attention at shorter ranges survive an eightfold jump in context length. Kimi K3 is an established model (GA August 2026), so this is analysis of existing mechanisms rather than a new release. Findings matter for long-context reliability claims.

entry.title: Training-Free Task Vectors for LLM Behavioral Control

author.name: Gabriel J. Perin, Lucas Boscaini, Andr\'e Araujo, Nina S. T. Hirata

entry.summary: Introduces TFTVs, a method for computing task-vector-like weight-space directions without fine-tuning by mapping activation steering vectors to rank-one weight edits using only forward-pass statistics. The resulting vectors support arithmetic composition for adding and forgetting behaviors. This reduces the cost of post-training model editing significantly.

entry.title: Online Learning with LLM Experts from Limited Feedback

author.name: Wang Wei, Soumyabrata Pal, Koyel Mukherjee, Franck Dernoncourt, Ryan A. Rossi, Branislav Kveton, Hoda Eldardiry

entry.summary: The paper formulates routing of prompts to multiple LLM experts as a bandit problem with a limited feedback budget, proposing algorithms with regret bounds of order O(dT/sqrt(m)) in the full-information setting and O(dT sqrt(K/m)) in the bandit setting, where m is the feedback budget. Experiments demonstrate efficient learning of routing strategies across diverse LLMs. It addresses the practical problem of cost-efficient model selection when querying multiple LLMs is expensive.

entry.title: On-the-go Forgetting without Explicit Unlearning via ERASE

author.name: Kushal Chakrabarti, Mayank Baranwal

entry.summary: ERASE introduces a machine unlearning alternative that suppresses the observable influence of private data at inference time using structured, class-conditioned input perturbations, without modifying model weights, retraining, or keeping model copies. The authors provide theoretical conditions under which functional forgetting of designated subclasses is provably achieved while preserving other predictions. This sidesteps common unlearning drawbacks like duplicated memory costs and degraded generalization.

entry.title: FMMO: Detecting the Divergence Between Local Attribution and Global Drift

author.name: Muhammad Rehman Zafar, Ali El-Sharif, Naimul Khan

entry.summary: FMMO exposes a critical blind spot in model monitoring: local attribution methods like TreeSHAP can appear stable while model reliability collapses under post-deployment drift, especially where false positive rates spike for subgroups. The framework detects divergence between local explanation stability and global distribution shifts. This has direct implications for algorithmic accountability practice, since many teams rely on attribution-based drift auditing.

entry.title: When Retain Constraints Conflict: Mitigating Forget-Retain Interference in Tabular Data

author.name: Zijie Liu, Jinhao Duan, Bingqi Shang, Xinming An, Sijia Liu, Tianlong Chen

entry.summary: Identifies schema-induced forget-retain overlap as a key challenge for machine unlearning on tabular data, where forget rows sit near retain rows sharing high-signal attributes, causing interference. The paper characterizes this conflict and proposes mitigation for tabular and serialized-record unlearning in high-stakes domains.

entry.title: Stochastically Perturbed Weights: Ensembles from Deterministic Machine-Learning Weather Models

author.name: Simon Adamov, Oliver Fuhrer, Reto Knutti, Sebastian Schemm

entry.summary: The authors propose stochastically perturbing the raw weight tensors of an already-trained deterministic ML weather model at inference time, extracting ensemble-based uncertainty estimates without any retraining, analogous to how physical ensembles perturb parametrization tendencies. Given that many deployed ML weather models are deterministic and uncertainty-free, this offers a cheap route to probabilistic forecasting. It matters because ML weather models now match operational NWP, and calibrated uncertainty is essential for real-world forecasting use.

entry.title: Entropy-Regularized Rank-Masked Policy Optimization for Test-Time Reinforcement Learning in Code Generation

author.name: Jiacheng Xu, Feng Chen, Xiuneng Xu, Bo An

entry.summary: Extends test-time reinforcement learning to code generation by proposing probe-driven TTRL: it builds output-free probe inputs, executes candidate programs on them, and derives a Probe Consensus Reward from behavioral agreement. To counter reward hacking from imperfect probes, it adds entropy regularization and rank-masked policy optimization.

entry.title: Contextual Observer Grounding: Evaluating Situated Spatial Reasoning in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Mimo Shirasaka, Haochen Zhang, Yonatan Bisk

entry.summary: Introduces POVBench, a benchmark of 3D scenes and queries testing whether vision-language models can infer a speaker's viewpoint from contextual cues and interpret situated spatial relations, distinguishing Inferred, Stated, and Given forms of observer grounding. This targets a capability important for language-conditioned robotics.

entry.title: How to Make the Gradient Mapping Small for Constrained Stochastic Min-Max Problems and Beyond

author.name: Ahmet Alacaoglu

entry.summary: This optimization theory paper closes a complexity gap for constrained convex-concave min-max problems and monotone variational inequalities, achieving near-optimal stochastic first-order oracle complexity for the gradient mapping residual. It improves the best-known rate from O(epsilon^-4) toward the optimal O(epsilon^-2) attained in unconstrained settings.

entry.title: Limitations of Automated Simulatability: LLM Simulators Can Bypass Explanations

author.name: Antonin Poch\'e, Fanny Jourdan, Nils Feldhus, Qianli Wang, Jing Yang, Simon Ostermann, Nicholas Asher, Philippe Muller, Vera Schmitt

entry.summary: This work critically examines automated simulatability, where LLM simulators replace human explainees when evaluating explanation quality. The authors replicate and extend the ConSim ranking, identifying two key flaws: simulators can achieve high simulatability by solving the classification task directly, and class anonymization can reward explanations that leak hidden labels.

entry.title: SinoGlyphBench: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Chinese Glyph-Level Obfuscation in Language-Model Moderation

author.name: Yifan Wang, Zimu Wang, Suliu Qin, Changyu Zeng, Tong Chen, Siqi Chen, Yijie Lin, Lingyu Jiang, Jionglong Su, Yushan Pan, Haiyang Zhang, Wei Wang, Qiaoyu Tan

entry.summary: SinoGlyphBench is a diagnostic benchmark measuring how glyph-level obfuscation of Chinese text, which stays human-readable, degrades automated content moderation. Across roughly 177,000 paired evaluations of 12 LLMs and multimodal LLMs in text and image modalities, obfuscation raises harmful false-negative rates by 6.1 points and false-positive rates by 4.7 points, with models retaining only about 75.7 percent of originally correct moderation decisions. The matched-pair design separates corruption of moderation-relevant evidence from surface variation, providing a targeted tool for hardening moderation systems.

entry.title: Don't Lose Entities from Retrieval to Generation: Dual Entity Recovery RAG for multi-hop QA

author.name: Heechang Lee, Dong-Young Lim

entry.summary: This paper identifies a shared failure mode in retrieval-augmented multi-hop QA: entity information is lost both when sub-questions drop entities resolved in earlier hops and when sentence-level chunking strips the context needed to resolve pronouns. The proposed Dual Entity Recovery RAG architecture explicitly restores entity information at both failure points, improving multi-hop QA performance.

entry.title: Cross-Lingual Representation Alignment by Token-Level Optimal Transport in a Language-Agnostic Space

author.name: Taisei Yamamoto, Ryoma Kumon, Danushka Bollegala, Hitomi Yanaka

entry.summary: Proposes CAROT, a cross-lingual alignment method that first identifies language-specific representations in LLM internal states, then aligns language-agnostic representations across languages at the token level using optimal transport while preserving language-specific information. This departs from prior sentence-level alignment that ignores language-specific encodings and can cause input-output language mismatch.

entry.title: Where to Look and What to Use: Retrieve-Localize-Generate for Long-Term Conversational Memory Question Answering

author.name: Yifan Wang, Xinkui Lin, Yongxiu Xu, Shen Gao, Ruochen Yang, Kun Huang, Yubin Wang, Jie Wu, Wei Liu, Jian Luan, Hongbo Xu, Shuo Shang

entry.summary: MemLoc is a Retrieve-Localize-Generate framework for long-term conversational memory QA that decomposes sessions into multi-granularity memory units, routes queries via an inner-memory graph with entropy-based granularity selection, and localizes evidence to counter fragmentation and the lost-in-the-middle effect. It addresses both scattered evidence across distant sessions and noise within retrieved sessions. The approach should improve personal-assistant style QA over conversation histories.

entry.title: Separating Stream Stability from Long-Term Recall in Language Models

author.name: Peipei Cao, Xin Zhang, Jie Tang, Xiao Li, Siying Li, Qing Pei

entry.summary: Argues that streaming language model methods are conflated with long-context and memory capabilities and introduces three explicit horizons: the stability horizon (predictive well-behavedness), the access horizon (causal influence of past content), and the utility horizon (task performance). It shows constructively that stability can be infinite while access and utility remain finite, as with attention sinks. This conceptual clarification matters for honest system claims and evaluation design.

entry.title: LLM Agents as Computational Typologists

author.name: Changbing Yang, Christopher Hammerly, Freda Shi, Jian Zhu

entry.summary: AUTOTYPOLOGIST is an LLM agent that performs evidence-grounded linguistic typology over reference grammars, retrieving grammar sections, analyzing interlinear glossed text, and iterating on typological hypotheses in a ReAct-style workflow. Evaluated against expert annotations and typological universals across 25 open-source grammars, it automates labor-intensive cross-linguistic comparison.

entry.title: Jacap: Robust KV Cache Eviction via Jacobian-Based Nonlinear Information Capacity Preservation

author.name: Jiaming Yang, Chenwei Tang, Liangli Zhen, Chenyang Zhang, Jiancheng Lv

entry.summary: Reframes KV cache eviction through local information geometry, modeling attention as a nonlinear Gaussian channel and deriving a Jacobian Information Capacity objective capturing query relevance, softmax sensitivity, and structural diversity. The resulting Jacap method provides a theoretically grounded alternative to heuristic eviction policies for long-context inference.

entry.title: ToolLoop: Closed-Loop Tool-Use Data Synthesis via Decomposed Generation and Dynamic Self-Feedback

author.name: Min Zeng, Yuzhou Liu, Zhenyu Cao, Hanxiu Chen, Heng Li, Caiquan Liu, Yafei Wen, Xiaoxin Chen

entry.summary: ToolLoop replaces the standard generate-then-filter paradigm for synthetic tool-use training data with a closed loop of sampling function names, backward-deriving user queries, and forward-deriving tool calls, with dynamic self-feedback at each stage. Experiments on the Berkeley Function Calling benchmark indicate improved data quality and feature balance. It matters because tool-use data quality is a key bottleneck for agentic LLM training.

entry.title: Time-Aware Assistive Navigation

author.name: Masaki Kuribayashi, Zhongkai Shangguan, Eshed Ohn-Bar

entry.summary: This paper introduces a large-scale egocentric multimodal benchmark for assistive outdoor navigation for visually impaired users, and identifies a fundamental gap: language agents plan what to say but not when or whether to speak in real time. It frames timing-aware response realization as a distinct machine intelligence challenge for MLLM agents, since poorly timed interventions add cognitive load.

entry.title: Depth-to-Image Synthesis-Driven Generative Unguided Depth Completion

author.name: Jiayi Yuan, Na Zhao, De Wen Soh

entry.summary: GUDC converts unguided depth completion into a semantics-guided task by using ControlNet to synthesize pseudo-RGB images directly from sparse depth, then leveraging these for semantics-aware depth inference without real RGB input. It addresses image-depth misalignment introduced by the synthesis step. This bridges 2D generative models with 3D perception in an RGB-free setting.

entry.title: CAM: Question Answering on Entity-Centric Videos with Continuous Extraction and Adaptive Querying

author.name: Yizhou Tian, Zizhe Chen, Shiyuan Deng, Garry Yang, Zijie Dai, Luohao Pan, Hao Lin, Peiqi Yin, Xiao Yan, James Cheng

entry.summary: Proposes CAM, a memory architecture for long-video QA with multimodal LLMs that stores entities and relations extracted continuously over extended time spans (capturing traits and relations) and uses adaptive querying beyond pure similarity retrieval to surface fine-grained details needed for answering questions.

entry.title: CHILD: Human-in-the-Loop OOD Detection for Safe Clinical Deployment

author.name: Jinlun Ye, Kaiyue Lu, Runhe Lai, Xinhua Lu, Jia-Xin Zhuang, Ruixuan Wang

entry.summary: CHILD is a training-free framework for streaming out-of-distribution detection in medical AI that uses sparse, adaptive, risk-aware human feedback instead of fully automatic test-time adaptation, reconciling safety oversight with clinician resource constraints. It targets safe clinical deployment by escalating only the most decision-relevant samples for physician review.

entry.title: Self-Supervised Multi-View 3D Gaze Target Estimation via Probabilistic Ray Marching

author.name: Keqi Chen, Vinkle Srivastav, Nicolas Padoy

entry.summary: Self-MVGTE is the first method to estimate 3D gaze targets directly in 3D space from multiple calibrated camera views without any ground-truth annotations in the target scene. It leverages noisy pseudo-labels from monocular gaze models and handles their multi-view inconsistency via a probabilistic ray marching framework that models uncertainty. Relevant to applications like surgical scene analysis where annotation is costly.

entry.title: EdMCGS: Event-Driven Markov Chain Gaussian Splatting for Extreme-Low-Frame-Rate Dynamic Scene Reconstruction

author.name: Yuzhong Wang, Wenmin Wang, Xinxing Yu

entry.summary: EdMCGS reconstructs dynamic 3D scenes from very low frame rate RGB video plus event camera streams, modeling scene motion as an event-driven Markov chain where sparse RGB frames anchor states and events drive transitions between them. This enables rendering at arbitrary intermediate timestamps, filling in missing motion evidence that causes artifacts in RGB-only methods. It is relevant to robotics, VR, and any setting with bandwidth-constrained capture.

entry.title: Layer Selection in VLMs for Zero-Shot OOD Detection via Multi-Resolution Entropy Estimation

author.name: Shyam Nandan Rai, Francesco Di Salvo, Sebastian Doerrich, Christian Ledig

entry.summary: This paper shows that the common assumption that final-layer VLM embeddings are optimal for zero-shot out-of-distribution detection fails in medical imaging, where intermediate layers carry complementary OOD signals and the optimal depth varies by image modality. It proposes multi-resolution entropy estimation to exploit this. The work is motivated by safe deployment of medical AI under domain shift across institutions and populations.

entry.title: Task-driven Processing with Coarse-to-Fine Glimpse-based Active Perception

author.name: Oleh Kolner, Thomas Ortner, Stanis{\l}aw Wo\'zniak, Angeliki Pantazi

entry.summary: CF-GAP introduces a task-driven front-end that lets existing instance detectors selectively direct a sequence of limited-view glimpses across high-resolution cluttered scenes, zooming in on task-relevant regions instead of processing resized full images. This coarse-to-fine active perception preserves critical details that are lost when images are downscaled to fit model constraints. It matters for compute-efficient high-resolution vision, especially instance detection in dense scenes.

entry.title: CosmoH2G: A Hand-to-Gripper Transfer Dataset and Baseline Method for Object Manipulation with Complex Spatial Movements

author.name: Hongxiang Zhao, Mutian Xu, Zeyu Jin, Yiming Hao, Shuguang Cui, Xiaoguang Han

entry.summary: CosmoH2G introduces a scalable acquisition pipeline and a large paired dataset of over 6,000 hand-gripper demonstrations collected with a handheld gripper, targeting transfer of human demonstrations to robotic grippers for complex 3D motions like rotations and flips. Prior approaches were confined to simple planar tasks. It also provides a baseline method guided by fine-grained hand-pose motion.

entry.title: Information-Guided Safe Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Gas Source Localization using sUAS

author.name: Sachin Giri, Thomas Zhao, Matthew Huynh, YangQuan Chen

entry.summary: This work introduces an information-guided safe reinforcement learning framework for localizing fugitive gas emissions with small unmanned aircraft, evaluated in a custom GPU-accelerated 3D simulator coupling wind and Lagrangian dispersion models. The authors identify a Gramian bias vulnerability in deterministic information-seeking planners operating on intermittent turbulent concentration fields. The contribution bridges safe RL, information-theoretic planning, and environmental monitoring.

entry.title: GloVLA: Let Geometry Move and Local VLA Interact for Robust Object-Centric Manipulation in Unstructured Environments

author.name: Truong Thanh Nguyen, Huy Hoang Nguyen, Ha Anh Nguyen, Binh Khanh Dinh, Ngo Anh Vien, Duy Nguyen Ho Minh, Minh Nhat Vu, Ngan Le

entry.summary: GloVLA is a hybrid framework that separates object-centric manipulation into a geometric transport regime for long-range end-effector movement and a local VLA regime for contact-rich interaction. This decomposition reduces brittleness from visual shifts, clutter, and occlusions that push single end-to-end policies out of distribution. It offers a pragmatic architecture pattern for deploying VLAs in unstructured environments.

entry.title: Unifying Physics-Based Humanoid Interaction with a Context-Conditioned Interaction Prior

author.name: Jianan Li, Xiao Chen, Tien-Tsin Wong

entry.summary: CHIP is a unified physics-grounded framework for learning reusable humanoid interaction skills spanning locomotion and object manipulation from heterogeneous motion data. It uses a conditional interaction prior over a shared discrete skill space, trained in stages starting from physics-based motion-imitation teacher policies. The work aims to replace task-specific reward engineering with a scalable skill-reuse architecture.

entry.title: Phase-and-First-Arrival VLM Feedback for Sparse-Reward Reinforcement Learning in Surgical Manipulation

author.name: Wanli Liuchen, Fangyuan Wang, Bin Li, Anqing Duan, Yunhui Liu, Peng Zhou, David Navarro-Alarcon

entry.summary: This paper introduces phase-and-first-arrival feedback, where a VLM query per episode identifies the furthest visually verified task phase and its timing, enabling credit assignment and reuse of partial behavior in sparse-reward RL for surgical manipulation. It also releases SurgPhaseBench, a phase-structured benchmark spanning rigid and deformable surgical tasks. The approach extracts much richer learning signal from failed multi-stage attempts than terminal rewards or scalar VLM ratings.

entry.title: Functional-SLAM: Interaction-Aware Mapping with Online Functional Scene Graphs

author.name: Xinggang Hu, Chenyangguang Zhang, Zihan Zhu, Ruida Zhang, Xiangkui Zhang, Xiangyang Ji

entry.summary: Functional-SLAM is claimed to be the first SLAM framework that continuously maintains a functional 3D scene graph as an online state, representing object and interaction-element relations needed for fine-grained robotic manipulation. It combines anchor-keyframe geometry, temporal accumulation of functional edges, and visual loop closure. This moves scene graphs from offline reconstruction toward real-time interactive use.

entry.title: HiBRIDGE: A Hierarchical Bayesian Neural Network Framework for Interpretable Dialogue Management in Group-Robot Interaction

author.name: Massimiliano Nigro, Hatice Gunes, Micol Spitale, Fethiye Irmak Dogan

entry.summary: HiBRIDGE is a hierarchical Bayesian framework enabling robots to decide whom to address and what to say in multi-party conversations, explicitly representing uncertainty over plausible behaviours. The hierarchical structure decomposes decisions into interpretable intermediate steps. This targets a genuine gap in group human-robot interaction where multiple conversational actions are simultaneously plausible.

entry.title: Bias-Corrected Subspace Intersection: Minimax-Optimal Shared Subspace Estimation in Multi-View Data

author.name: Xianwen Song, Yuepeng Yang, Cong Ma

entry.summary: The authors identify a second-order bias in standard plug-in subspace intersection methods like AJIVE, caused by direction-dependent leakage of empirical singular vectors, and propose bias-corrected subspace intersection (BCSI). They prove finite-sample minimax-optimal risk bounds without condition-number assumptions, accommodating unequal dimensions and ranks. A rigorous statistical fix for a widely used multi-view analysis tool.

entry.title: Reasoning-Aware Compression: Identifying and Protecting Vulnerable Reasoning Circuits for Energy-Efficient LLM Deployment

author.name: Leonard Twagirayezu, Prasenjit Mitra

entry.summary: This work benchmarks INT4 quantization across five reasoning benchmarks with hardware-level GPU energy measurement, profiles per-module vulnerability across all layer-projection pairs via perturbation sweeps, and selectively restores the most sensitive reasoning circuits to FP16. Notably, it finds INT4 quantization can paradoxically increase energy consumption by lengthening reasoning chains, despite a 25% power reduction.

entry.title: Inference-Time Graph Engineering for Multi-Agent LLM Workflows

author.name: Katherine Tieu, Dongqi Fu, Yinglong Xia, Hong Li, Hong Yan, Jingrui He

entry.summary: ReActNet is a training-free framework that compiles a query and role-specialized agents into task-conditioned temporal communication graphs, where each snapshot represents a reasoning stage and each edge carries natural-language message instructions. This shifts multi-agent orchestration from optimizing static topologies toward dynamic, inference-time graph synthesis.

entry.title: SAP: State-Guided Data Synthesis with Argument Provenance for Multi-Turn Tool Use

author.name: Zichen Tian, Jinpeng Chen, Cheng Gong, Suiyun Zhang, Rui Liu

entry.summary: SAP is a data synthesis method for multi-turn tool-use training that combines state guidance, tool-argument provenance constraints, and turn-level validation to produce trajectories with long-range dependencies and correctly grounded argument values. Using SAP-generated data, the authors build SAP-4B, a competitive small model for agentic tool use.

entry.title: APPSim-Bench: Bridging Real-world Apps and Reproducible Evaluation for Mobile GUI Agents

author.name: Jintian Feng, Long Chen, Xiao Yu, Jiayi Dai, Chenglong Liu, Haoru Wang, Zizhen Xue, Yuxuan Shi, Ziyang Wang, Yichen Gong

entry.summary: Proposes APPSim-Bench, using controllable simulated mobile apps built via coding-agent-assisted, human-verified workflows that preserve real interaction logic while enabling deterministic evaluation, with 557 tasks across 17 high-frequency Chinese and English apps. It resolves the realism-versus-reproducibility tradeoff in GUI agent benchmarking.

entry.title: Less Is Personal: Learning Minimal Sufficient User Profiles for Personalized Language Models

author.name: Minghang Liu, Qiang Qiu, Yuanzhuo Wang, Huawei Shen, Xueqi Cheng

entry.summary: Studies minimal sufficient personalization for retrieval-augmented LLMs, proposing ENOUGH, a method that adaptively constructs the shortest ordered user profile needed per input by iteratively appending behavioral records or emitting STOP, evaluated with bounded counterfactual search. This avoids the standard practice of prepending a fixed number of history records even when they are redundant or harmful. The result is more efficient and potentially higher-quality personalization.

entry.title: Co-Evolving Harnesses and Models: On-Policy Correction Helps Weaker Models Catch Up Where Imitation Fails

author.name: Zhou Yu, Bin Bi, Shiva Kumar Pentyala, Shubham Mehrotra, Sougata Chaudhuri, Shilpa Bhagavath, Zeyuan Chen, Ran Xu, Phil Mui, James Zhu, Sitaram Asur

entry.summary: This paper studies how automated evolution of agent harnesses (system prompts, tools, scaffolding) should be combined with lightweight fine-tuning of smaller models across seven enterprise agent tasks. A key finding is that naive imitation of expert trajectories under an evolved harness backfires, while on-policy correction enables weaker models to close the gap. The work offers practical guidance for cost-efficient agentic deployments.

entry.title: FedSubMuon: Communication-Efficient Federated LLM Fine-Tuning via Structured Subspace Muon

author.name: Shaolong Chen, Youming Tao, Shuzhen Chen, Falko Dressler, Qingqing Ye, Di Wang

entry.summary: Proposes FedSubMuon, a federated fine-tuning method that applies Muon-style orthogonalized momentum within a structured low-dimensional subspace, avoiding full layer-size transmissions while preserving Muon's matrix-aware update geometry. It improves communication efficiency for cross-device LLM fine-tuning over prior federated Muon variants.

entry.title: Steering Geometry: Validating Human Value Geometry in LLM Steering Space

author.name: Mohammad Mahdi Abootorabi, Armin Saghafian, Ali Bazshoushtari, Hamid Rezaei, EunJeong Hwang, Vered Shwartz, Parvin Mousavi, Purang Abolmaesumi

entry.summary: This work tests whether activation steering vectors in LLMs encode coherent semantic structure rather than behavior-specific shortcuts, using Schwartz's Theory of Basic Human Values and a new 26K-sample benchmark covering 20 values. Connecting steering-space geometry to established human value theory gives alignment research a principled framework for interpreting and validating steering interventions. It matters for making inference-time behavioral control more predictable and safe.

entry.title: SRD-GUARD: A Defense Framework of LLMs via Semantic Rewriting and Joint Multi-Model Scoring for Latent Intent Exposure

author.name: Qi Wang, Chengcheng Wan, Jiangtao Wang

entry.summary: SRD-GUARD is a parameter-free, black-box, inference-time defense against jailbreak attacks: it generates five semantic rewrites of a prompt that strip contextual packaging, then has multiple independent LLM safety scorers jointly assess the original and rewrites to expose concealed harmful intent. It aims to reduce both missed disguised attacks and over-refusal.

entry.title: SpatialBlock: Enhancing Spatial Intelligence in LVLMs via Synthetic Block-Stacking Problem

author.name: Soohyun Ryu, Sohee Kim, Eunho Yang

entry.summary: SpatialBlock proposes training LVLM spatial intelligence on synthetic block-stacking problems, inspired by human cognitive development, avoiding costly and noisy real-scene 3D annotations. The accompanying SpatialBlock-15k dataset provides 15k synthetic examples of foundational spatial manipulation skills. This paradigm could transfer foundational 3D reasoning to real scenes more cheaply than dense geometric labeling.

entry.title: A*-Thought-V2: Efficient Latent Reasoning via Geometric Dynamics of LLM

author.name: Xiaoang Xu, Siyuan Liu, Shuo Wang, Junlan Feng, Fanyu Meng, Zhu Zhang, Jixun Wang, Xiaorong Wang, Zihan Zhou, Xin Li, Chaojun Xiao, Yiming Zhang, Huijia Wu, Liuyu Xiang, Peipei Li, Zhaofeng He

entry.summary: Models chain-of-thought as a hidden-state trajectory in a 3D PCA space, keeping question-aligned steps as explicit text while compressing deviating steps into continuous latent tokens, using an explicit-implicit interleaved architecture. This reduces the computation and context costs of CoT without the information loss of hard pruning.

entry.title: CS-CLIP: Compositional Scene Graph-guided CLIP for Robust Compositional Reasoning

author.name: SeongJun Jeong, Minjoon Jung, Woo Suk Choi, Youwon Jang, Byoung-Tak Zhang

entry.summary: CS-CLIP shows that existing compositionality-aware VLMs have element-specific biases and can underperform vanilla CLIP on certain compositional tests. The method uses scene graphs to identify compositional elements and constructs structured negatives via selective masking, retaining the most contradictory negatives to force reliance on compositional structure. This improves robustness of vision-language alignment on compositional reasoning.

entry.title: TANGO: Humanoid Navigation in Cluttered Environments with a Whole-Body Vision-Language-Action Model

author.name: Anqi Li, Yuxin Chen, Zhaobo Li, Zhuo Cao, Junli Ren, Masayoshi Tomizuka, Dhruv Shah

entry.summary: Presents TANGO, a whole-body vision-language navigation framework that predicts 29-DoF joint-space actions for humanoid traversal of cluttered 3D environments from language instructions and egocentric RGB, trained entirely in simulation with teacher-student distillation. It moves beyond 2D path planning toward coordinated arm, torso, and gait adaptation. Builds on a strong robotics collaboration including UC Berkeley and Tomizuka.

entry.title: Representation Learning for Sample-Efficient CATE Estimation by Leveraging Multiple Outcomes

author.name: Maitreyi Swaroop, Shikha Bhat, Samantha Rodriguez, Tamar Krishnamurti, Bryan Wilder

entry.summary: This paper improves sample efficiency of conditional average treatment effect (CATE) estimation by learning low-dimensional representations from abundant historical multi-outcome data, transferring structure to limited experimental samples. It exploits a supervision source (large observational outcome datasets) that is typically ignored in causal effect estimation. Directly useful for policy and medical intervention targeting where RCT data is scarce.

entry.title: HealthLoopQA: A Context-Aware Question Answering Benchmark for Interpreting Wearable Monitoring Data in Diabetes Care

author.name: Yuchen Niu, Yanan Ma, Srinivasan Nandakumar, Maolin Chen, Viktor Schlegel, Kexin Wei, Ling Cheng, Anna Bird, Anil Anthony Bharath, Siew-Kei Lam

entry.summary: Presents HealthLoopQA, a benchmark evaluating LLM reasoning over longitudinal wearable monitoring data in diabetes care, covering long-term patterns, therapeutic and behavioral context, and system failure detection beyond short-horizon classification. Targets clinically meaningful assessment of LLM analytical rigor.

entry.title: Temporal-Causal Inference for Reinforcement Learning via Automata Learning

author.name: Jan Corazza, Daniil Kaminskyi, Simon Lutz, Patrick Nossol, Hadi Partovi Aria, Zhe Xu, Daniel Neider

entry.summary: Formalizes RL in environments with hidden, irreversible phase transitions as a two-phase non-Markovian decision process and introduces TCIRL, which jointly learns a policy and infers the hidden temporal cause via a hypothesis DFA refined with counterexample-driven SAT-based synthesis. Convergence to the true cause language is proven almost surely.

entry.title: InfluenceField: A Differentiable Field with Interventionally Identifiable Causal Structure for Multimodal World Modeling

author.name: Zihao Yang, Zijia Wang, Zhiqiu Huang

entry.summary: InfluenceField inserts an intervention-aware latent field between the visual encoder and language decoder of multimodal LLMs, propagating directed influence to predict how local visual interventions affect downstream answers, trained with counterfactual rollout supervision and structural regularization. It targets the gap between visual-linguistic correlation and causal intervention prediction in world modeling. Theoretical identifiability results are provided for a nonlinear finite-basis model.

entry.title: Tight Lower Bounds for State Tomography with Limited Entanglement

author.name: Ufuk Keskin, Jason Luo, Mahbod Majid, Matthew Radzihovsky

entry.summary: Proves lower bounds matching prior upper bounds for quantum state tomography where each measurement acts on at most k fresh copies with no inter-block quantum memory, establishing copy complexity of max{d^3/(sqrt(k) eps^2), d^2/eps^2} up to constants. The bounds hold for arbitrary adaptive block measurements and remove earlier restrictions on k.

entry.title: Diagonal Attenuation: A Finite-Sample Correction for PCA

author.name: Qiang Sun

entry.summary: Proposes diagonal attenuation, a simple finite-sample correction to PCA that preserves sample cross-covariances while shrinking coordinatewise sample variances, shown to arise exactly from averaging masked reconstruction losses. The paper derives explicit expected-risk theorems explaining how sample-variance error rotates empirical PCs away from population directions.

entry.title: Fast PAC Global Optimization via Restarted Langevin: Exploration, Exploitation, and Degenerate Cooling

author.name: Ioannis Kontoyiannis, Sean Meyn

entry.summary: This theoretical work analyzes the computational effort needed for global optimization of smooth nonconvex objectives under (epsilon, delta)-PAC guarantees, comparing classical simulated annealing and fixed-temperature Langevin diffusion against newly proposed parallel-restart Langevin and Langevin-gradient hybrid schemes. The analysis characterizes performance in terms of the dominant energy barrier and distinguishes exploration from exploitation phases. Notable authors from information theory and control/systems contribute rigorous continuous-time analysis.

entry.title: SGD in Multiclass Logistic Regression: Sequential Learning and Scaling Laws

author.name: Konstantinos Christopher Tsiolis, Denny Wu, Christos Thrampoulidis, Murat A. Erdogdu

entry.summary: Establishes precise scaling laws for cross-entropy risk during training of multiclass logistic regression on high-dimensional Gaussian mixtures, showing learning proceeds sequentially across classes from most to least frequent with a three-phase risk trajectory under power-law class priors. It also analyzes how model capacity interacts with optimization under fixed compute budgets.

entry.title: FramingQA: Does the Question Shape the Answer? Measuring the Compositional Framing Effect

author.name: Hazel H. Kim, Andrew M. Bean, Guilherme Affonso Ferreira de Camargo, Shanyu Chauhan, Felix Drinkall, Jade Kosch\'e, Chenyang Ma, Glory Nwaugbala, Nabeel Seedat, Bradley Max Segal, Samuel Recht, Hinrich Sch\"utze, Philip H. S. Torr

entry.summary: Introduces FramingQA, a benchmark measuring LLM sensitivity to question framing across law, medicine, finance, and robotic simulations by injecting framing bias at three nested levels, including biased assumptions embedded in questions. It documents that models change responses to subtle rephrasings that imply a stance, which is dangerous in high-stakes domains where users often ask questions with incomplete or misleading assumptions. This speaks directly to robustness and user-safety concerns in deployed assistants.

entry.title: When Metrics Reward the Worst Translations: Internalizing Cultural Reasoning for Social Media Translation Evaluation

author.name: Yiwen Qiu, Linjuan Wu, Dingming Li, Yizhou Liu, Zixuan Wang, Haolei Xu, Ye Guo, Daoxin Zhang, Weiming Lu, Yongliang Shen

entry.summary: Demonstrates that standard translation metrics (COMET, XCOMET, BERTScore) exhibit near-zero or negative correlation with human judgments on culturally loaded social media content, including a severity inversion where scores rise as quality falls. Even a large LLM judge achieves very low agreement, motivating culturally internalized evaluation approaches.

entry.title: Report of the 8th LSVOS Challenge: Complex and Multimodal Video Object Segmentation

author.name: Chang Liu, Henghui Ding, Lingyi Hong, Ning Xu, Linjie Yang, Yuchen Fan, Canyang Wu, Jinrong Zhang, Xusheng He, Ce Bian, Xianjing Han, Jianlong Wu, Mingqi Gao, Sijie Li, Jungong Han, JeongRae Kim, Chaehyun Kim, Changwon Lim, Jungyoon Lee, Gyuil Lim, Doeon Kim, Seong-heum Kim, Pranjal Aggarwal, Sean Welleck, Yiwen Ren, Jianing Liu, Yingxin Wang, Kexin Zhang, Licheng Jiao, Lingling Li, Xu Liu, Jinxing Zhou, Suiyi Zhao, Yanghao Zhou, Ruohao Guo, Liangtao Shi, Jinxia Xie, Xiantao Hu, Ting Liu

entry.summary: This report summarizes the 8th Large-scale Video Object Segmentation Challenge at ECCV 2026, covering semi-supervised VOS on MOSEv2, text-guided referring VOS on MeViSv2-Text, and audio-guided VOS on MeViSv2-Audio. It reviews the top nine solutions, showing trends like foundation models combined with target-aware memory, multimodal reasoning, target-existence verification, and agentic correction. The report maps the state of the art in video segmentation.

entry.title: PLSR: Progressive and Localized Super-Resolution of 3D Objects via Localized Latent Voxel Diffusion

author.name: Yuxin Liu, Minshan Xie, Jiawen Liang, Runsong Zhu, Chi-Wing Fu, Tien-Tsin Wong

entry.summary: Introduces PLSR, a 3D super-resolution framework that takes coarse geometry from pretrained 3D generators and progressively upscales resolution by decomposing global SR into localized sub-tasks via an associative input decomposition and a flow-based localized latent voxel diffusion. It is designed for memory efficiency and detail.

entry.title: AFID: A Unified Open Framework for Automated Fingermark Identification, Quality Assessment and Feature Extraction

author.name: Tim Oblak, Rudolf Haraksim, Peter Peer

entry.summary: AFID is an open-source framework for friction ridge (fingermark) processing covering recognition, quality assessment, and feature extraction with a single shared encoder trained only on public data. It sets a new state of the art in fixed-length fingermark recognition with minimal preprocessing, addressing fragmentation of closed-source forensic tools. This matters for reproducibility and fairness in forensic biometrics.

entry.title: ReactVAU: A Slow-Fast Decoupled Framework for Streaming Video Anomaly Understanding

author.name: Chia-Hui Chen, Shih-Ying Yeh, Fu-En Yang, Min-Hung Chen, Shang-Hong Lai

entry.summary: ReactVAU proposes a slow-fast decoupled framework for real-time streaming video anomaly understanding, combining a lightweight Fast Detection Module with Spatial Grid Filtering, an Anomaly-Aware Persistent Memory that protects transient cues from temporal decay, and selective invocation of heavyweight MLLMs. It addresses the mismatch between offline video models and the causal constraints of live surveillance streams.

entry.title: SciFigure2Code: An AI-Reconstructed Benchmark for Scientific Figure-to-Code

author.name: Wentao Li, Yibo Wu, Yizhe Chen, Ruixuan Chen, Jiangjie Qiu, Yijun Li, Zhao Leyi, Xiaonan Wang

entry.summary: SciFigure2Code is a benchmark for scientific figure-to-code that evaluates presentation recovery: generating editable Python programs preserving how a panel is arranged and read, with role-specialized Codex agents generating, executing, visually refining, and auditing silver-standard presentation programs. It reframes the underdetermined problem of recovering original data/code as recovering visual provenance.

entry.title: CAR-MIL: Counterfactual Attention Regularization for Multiple Instance Learning

author.name: Imane Chraki, Pierre Marza, Stergios Christodoulidis, Maria Vakalopoulou

entry.summary: CAR-MIL introduces counterfactual attention regularization for multiple instance learning, adding a lightweight counterfactual attention branch that produces alternative predictions to keep attention faithful to instance importance and avoid spurious correlations. It is aimed primarily at digital pathology, where fine-grained annotations are costly and MIL is standard. The method builds on standard attention-based MIL architectures.

entry.title: LLM-Aided Design for Manufacturing: A Multi-Agent System for Intent-Preserving Redesign of CAD for Improved Manufacturability

author.name: Kojo Welbeck, Xiangyu Shi, Zahra Sadeghi, Qi Zhu, Ping Guo

entry.summary: This paper presents a multi-agent pipeline where a multimodal LLM-driven DFM Reviewer proposes manufacturability improvements and a CAD Modifier executes them as edits to CadQuery programs, producing redesigns that are easier to manufacture while preserving design intent. It decomposes redesign into individually verified transitions instead of unreliable single-shot generation. This is a notable example of LLM agents applied to engineering design workflows.

entry.title: A Heterogeneous General Model for Neuromorphic-Inspired Computation

author.name: Matteo Mirigliano

entry.summary: This theoretical work proposes a general mathematical model for neuromorphic-inspired computation based on an input-dependent stochastic weight network called a substrate, whose weights evolve via input-triggered stochastic updates governed by a matrix-valued covariance kernel. The aim is to provide missing design guidelines and general models for emerging neuromorphic systems and hardware. A unifying framework of this kind could help standardize how the field reasons about non-von Neumann architectures.

entry.title: mjorbit: A Simulation Framework for Space Robotics

author.name: John Z. Zhang, Joris Verhagen, Fausto Vega, Patrick McKeen, Zachary Manchester

entry.summary: mjorbit is an open framework built on MuJoCo that simulates multi-body space robots with contact, adding spacecraft dynamics, actuators, and sensors for in-space servicing, assembly, and manufacturing. It includes an empirical study of coupling orbit propagation with robotics simulation, plus C++ CPU and GPU backends behind a Python API. Demonstrations cover MPC and RL on realistic on-orbit case studies.

entry.title: FOCI Policy: Focus on Object-Centric Interactions for Relational Manipulation Policies

author.name: Ze Fu, Pinhao Song, Yutong Hu, Renaud Detry

entry.summary: FOCI Policy proposes an interaction-centric manipulation framework that extracts compact interaction segments from demonstrations and represents skills as relative SE(3) object motions. This two-fold temporal and spatial abstraction improves generalization for rigid relational manipulation tasks. From Renaud Detry's group, it offers a principled middle ground between overly simple and overly dense object-centric representations.

entry.title: Adaptive Conformal Inference Under Delayed Feedback: Coverage Guarantees and a Delay-to-Memory Diagnostic

author.name: Lama El Halabi, Adam Brandt

entry.summary: Studies Adaptive Conformal Inference when prediction outcomes arrive with a horizon delay, showing the delayed recursion decomposes into interleaved ACI sequences and deriving finite-sample coverage bounds with explicit delay dependence. It also introduces a delay-to-memory diagnostic to assess when delayed feedback degrades coverage.

entry.title: AutoFyn Technical Report: Non-Parametric Expert Iteration for Long-Horizon Agents

author.name: Adib Hasan, Daniel Schaffield, Akashnil Dutta, Tarik Adnan Moon

entry.summary: AutoFyn adapts the Expert Iteration algorithm to a frozen model by updating persistent non-parametric state (memory files, reports, repository state) from verified reward signals instead of model weights. Each round starts fresh, an orchestrator explores multiple approaches with specialized agents, and a task-grounded verifier provides objective rewards that are distilled into persistent state, effectively updating the policy without weight updates.

entry.title: Causal Attribution for Agentic Decisions: Estimators, Coupling, and a Traceability Specification

author.name: Ajay Pravin Mahale (Hochschule Trier)

entry.summary: Defines estimands and estimators for post-hoc causal attribution of individual steps in agentic AI decisions, distinguishing marginal total effects from common-random-numbers total effects, and shows both fail in characteristic ways, including cases where a causally inert step is indistinguishable from a decisive one. Proposes a traceability specification for high-risk AI record-keeping. Directly relevant to emerging AI liability and auditability requirements.

entry.title: iBrain: A Unified Foundation Model Reading the Brain from Surface to Spikes

author.name: Ying Chen, Tiou Wang, Zhifeng Yue

entry.summary: Introduces iBrain, a neural foundation model that jointly pretrains on intracranial EEG and intracortical spiking activity using signal-specific encoders feeding a shared spatiotemporal Transformer backbone. Unifying heterogeneous invasive recording paradigms could move the field beyond per-paradigm silos toward general brain-decoding models for neuroscience and neurotechnology.

entry.title: Encoded Early, Used Late: Where Transformers Begin to Act on an Inferred Partner's Expertise

author.name: Mika Okamoto, Gabriele Sarti

entry.summary: Using ExpertCollab, a corpus of multi-turn research-planning dialogues between model-played personas at four expertise levels, the authors show that an inferred attribute (partner expertise) is most linearly decodable in early transformer layers and decays to near chance before the network midpoint. Counterfactual patching probes where the model actually acts on this representation, extending encode-early/use-late findings from stated input attributes to socially inferred ones.

entry.title: SAEScientist-Bench: Can AI Agents Conduct Autonomous SAE Interpretability Research?

author.name: Yuqiao Tan, Shizhu He, Jun Zhao, Kang Liu

entry.summary: The paper introduces SAEScientist-Bench, a benchmark evaluating whether AI agents can autonomously conduct mechanistic interpretability research using Sparse Autoencoder tools. Agents design contrastive probes and navigate the Gemma Scope dictionary of 131K+ features in Gemma-2-9B-IT to discover features for target concepts. It connects autonomous research capability to safety-critical model auditing.

entry.title: When Agent Governance Helps

author.name: Michael Ray Johnson, Linda Naimi

entry.summary: The paper synthesizes the GAMPO framework for governed autotelic multi-agent organizations (agents pursuing self-generated goals within guardrails) from a qualitative synthesis of 321 sources, then empirically probes a prompt-layer instantiation on CHI-Bench, a long-horizon healthcare benchmark, across open and frontier models. The key finding is a boundary condition: governance benefits are gated by a model's spare capacity and are domain- and model-specific, with governance overhead potentially harming capacity-constrained open models. This provides rare empirical grounding for when agent governance actually pays off.

entry.title: What if LLMs Ate Their Words: Causal History Effects in Multi-Turn Interaction

author.name: Jinnan Li, Zheren Fu, Yue Wang, Jinzhe Li, Yuan Wu, Yi Chang

entry.summary: This study analyzes how LLM-generated conversation history causally affects later behavior, comparing fully specified single-turn inputs to progressively revealed multi-turn interactions across six task families and five models, including replaying conversations with altered history. It finds degradation is task- and model-dependent, that stronger one-shot performance does not imply interaction robustness, and dissects how assistant turns become self-conditioning context.

entry.title: Structurally Close, Temporally Distant: Measuring Security Exposure in Long-Horizon LLM Agents

author.name: Md Jafrin Hossain, Nur Al Hasan Haldar

entry.summary: This paper argues that temporal remoteness overstates security separation in stateful LLM agents and introduces a provenance-aware execution graph defining influence distance (shortest structural path from untrusted source to sensitive action) versus sequence distance. Because the influence graph contains every sequence edge, influence distance bounds sequence distance, giving a better measure of prompt-injection exposure in long-horizon agents.

entry.title: Second-Order Smooth Planning with Optimal-Transport Bellman Smoothing

author.name: Tuan Dam

entry.summary: This theory paper improves sample complexity for smooth value-based planning: it shows the complexity exponent of SmoothCruiser-type planners is governed by the Taylor remainder order and achieves O(eps^-3) complexity via an optimal-transport-smoothed second-order Bellman backup. This improves on the first-order O(eps^-4) guarantee.

entry.title: Counterfactual Tests for Measuring Chain-of-Thought Faithfulness in Visual Language Models

author.name: Bayar Menzat, Maximilian S\"uss, Ruizhi Wang, Benno Steinegger, Thomas Lukasiewicz, Oana-Maria Camburu

entry.summary: Adapts counterfactual faithfulness tests (CT and CCT) from text to visual inputs, introducing vCT and vCCT, and benchmarks eight open-source vision-language models on two datasets. Findings show CoTs do not reliably track visual evidence influencing predictions, sometimes omitting decisive visual information.

entry.title: Protocol effects on feature-based hardware-Trojan detection across Trust-Hub families

author.name: Hang Xiao, Chuhong Xu, Kainan Zhou, Gangzhen Qian, Lu Yi

entry.summary: This paper measures how train/test protocol choices inflate reported performance in hardware-Trojan detection on Trust-Hub, showing random forest F1 drops from 0.914 with pooled gates to 0.636 when withholding complete netlists or host families due to leakage of seen host logic. It is a careful negative/replication result rather than a new classifier. This has direct implications for the credibility of the hardware security ML literature.

entry.title: Matryoshka Hash Representations for Model-Aware Compact Semantic Retrieval

author.name: Peichun Hua, Yunming Xiao

entry.summary: This work extends Matryoshka-style representation learning to hash-based quantization for RAG dense retrieval, training codes whose short prefixes are directly searchable so deployments can choose efficiency-quality operating points without re-encoding the corpus. Rather than pure reconstruction fidelity (as in product quantization), it optimizes codes for retrieval utility across multiple byte budgets. This addresses the dominant index cost at corpus scale.

entry.title: ObGynLongBench: Revealing the Evidence-to-EHR Gap in Longitudinal EHR Decision-Making

author.name: Jun Xiang, Zhijie Bao, Rong Hu, Kaizhou Qin, Wei Chen, Zhongyu Wei

entry.summary: ObGynLongBench is a rule-grounded long-context benchmark for obstetric and gynecologic decision-making from real longitudinal EHRs, with 1,500 clinical decision-point cases from 976 pregnancy histories and traceable rules. It enables testing across evidence, visit-level, and history-level information boundaries, exposing a gap between LLM performance on static QA and real longitudinal clinical reasoning.

entry.title: Sparse Data Augmentation for Optimization with Provable Guarantees

author.name: Behrooz Tahmasebi, Melanie Weber

entry.summary: Studies whether full group-based data augmentation in geometric machine learning can be approximated by a small fixed sample of transformations, proving that gradient descent on the sparsely augmented objective achieves an epsilon-stationary point with high probability under regularity conditions. Addresses the prohibitive cost of augmenting over large transformation groups.

entry.title: Let It Go or Learn to Self-Correct: Continuous Diffusion for Constrained Discrete Tasks

author.name: Mariia Drozdova, St\'ephane Liem Nguyen, Fran\c{c}ois Fleuret

entry.summary: Studies diffusion sampling for globally constrained discrete tasks like Sudoku and N-queens, showing that standard DDPM samplers preserve early errors. Simply sampling from the model's clean prediction, without retraining, lifts Sudoku validity from 31% to 95% with consistent gains across tasks. A simple, striking result about how diffusion noise schedules can trap constrained discrete generation.

entry.title: Steering Under Compression: Dose-Response, Capability Cost, and Failure Asymmetry in Quantized LLMs

author.name: Saurav Bhandari, Benjamin Wade

entry.summary: This systematic study characterizes how activation steering interacts with post-training quantization (INT8, NF4) across four open 7-9B models, using an iso-effect framework to compare capability costs at matched behavioral effect. Sentiment steering survives quantization, while reasoning-length steering shows failure asymmetries, with careful correction of a GSM8K parser artifact. It fills a real gap as both techniques converge in efficient deployment.

entry.title: Towards Unified Multimodal Graph Foundation Model: A Bridge-Router-Adapter Based Approach

author.name: Sirui Zhang, Yubing Zhou, Xunkai Li, Zekai Chen, Shumeng Li, Wang Luo, Yinlin Zhu, Yujin Gao, Rong-Hua Li

entry.summary: Addresses limitations of multimodal graph foundation models, namely cross-scope context entanglement and scope-ignorant modality routing, via a bridge-router-adapter architecture that preserves scope-specific contexts and routes modalities adaptively across neighborhood ranges. Targets transferable unified representations across graph domains and tasks.

entry.title: Stable-MM-R1: Anchoring Multimodal Reasoning Dynamics via Entropy-Guided Stratification

author.name: Yimeng Ye, Shuang Chen, Wenxuan Huang, Manyuan Zhang, Kaituo Feng, Zhangquan Chen, Jiayu Chen, Yucheng Zhou, Yicheng Xiao, Zhiyuan Feng, Tianyu Shi

entry.summary: Targets training instability and entropy collapse in RL for multimodal reasoning. The framework combines Potential-Aware Query Mining (PAQM), which dynamically selects data in a high-potential Distillation Zone, with Hybrid Stratified Replay (HSR), which restructures batches by stratifying rollouts via a Path Entropy confidence proxy.

entry.title: MLIP Detective: Active Failure Mode Discovery Beyond Benchmark Scores for Machine-Learning Interatomic Potentials

author.name: Ryuhei Okuno, Nontawat Charoenphakdee, Kaoru Hisama, Yuta Tsuboi

entry.summary: MLIP Detective is an agentic framework that actively hunts for hidden failure modes of universal machine-learning interatomic potentials: it generates falsifiable physics-informed hypotheses from benchmark evidence, screens them with cheap simulations, and escalates only the most suspicious cases to human experts with proposed verification protocols. Without issue-specific prompting it identified and characterized real failure modes that static benchmarks missed. This matters because it demonstrates agentic evaluation as a complement to fixed benchmarks in scientific ML.

entry.title: Representation learning of human cortical folding to reveal long lasting neurodevelopmental signatures

author.name: Julien Laval, Robin Guiavarch, Antoine Dufournet, Racim Menasria, Barth\'el\'emy Drabczuk, Cristobal Mendoza, Saeb Tounsi, Chikh Abdelghani Baroud, Merieme Bourenane, Vanessa Troiani, William Snyder, Marisa A Patti, Myl\`ene Moyal, Marion Plaze, Arnaud Cachia, Federica Santacroce, Giorgia Committeri, Claire Cury, Kevin De Matos, Olivier Colliot, Zhong Yi Sun, Clara Fischer, Vincent Frouin, Pietro Gori, Denis Rivi\`ere, Jo\"el Chavas, Jean-Fran\c{c}ois Mangin

entry.summary: Introduces Champollion, a self-supervised framework learning interpretable local representations of cortical folding from structural MRI, outperforming neuroimaging and general-purpose foundation models on folding-related tasks. The learned representations reveal stable neurodevelopmental signatures established shortly after birth.

entry.title: To Adapt or Not to Adapt? Selective Adaptation for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Siru Jiang, Yuwei Liang, Jian Liang, Ran He, Tieniu Tan

entry.summary: The paper identifies two failure modes in test-time adaptation of vision-language models: adaptations that change nothing and, more seriously, adaptations that flip correct predictions to incorrect ones. It introduces selective adaptation, a new problem of deciding per-sample whether to adapt or skip, and proposes methods to make that decision.

entry.title: Generating Adversarial Texts for Machine Translation via GRPO

author.name: Florian Zogaj, Jakob H\"utteneder, Giovanni De Muri, Federico Villa, Aryan Sood, Vil\'em Zouhar

entry.summary: The authors propose a reinforcement-learning approach for automatically generating harder machine translation test sets by fine-tuning an LLM with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) to rewrite source texts into translation-difficult instances. Reward signals balance translation difficulty against semantic similarity, grammaticality, and length constraints, offering a scalable alternative to manual stress-test creation.

entry.title: SLATE: Are AI-Generated Slides Educationally Effective? A Benchmark for Language Teaching Quality and Learner Knowledge Acquisition

author.name: Jingzhuo Wu, Jiajun Zhang, Liu Yi, Leqi Zheng, Yuheng Jing, Xinyuan Zhou, Quan yang

entry.summary: Presents SLATE, the first benchmark evaluating AI-generated language teaching slides on instructional effectiveness and learner knowledge acquisition rather than visual polish. It converts linguistics olympiad puzzles over low-resource languages into 90 standardized instructional units with 1,133 assessable items in a pretest-posttest design with near- and far-transfer tests, neutralizing pretrained-knowledge contamination.

entry.title: RouteRelay: Event-Triggered Cross-Layer Route Reuse for Efficient Dynamic Sparse Attention

author.name: Bin Li, Sisi Liu, Chenyang Hu, Chaoyang Zhang, Wei Li, Hui Song

entry.summary: Introduces RouteRelay, a router-agnostic method that reduces the overhead of dynamic sparse attention by reusing route metadata across Transformer layers instead of rebuilding chunk-to-chunk score matrices at every layer. Anchor layers perform full routing while intermediate layers rescore only the previous top-k routes plus a sentinel set of near-miss and random chunks, rerouting a query only when a sentinel challenges its weakest selected chunk. This targets router cost, a distinct bottleneck from attention kernel cost.

entry.title: From Reading Code to Reading Spec: A Verified Layer for LLM-Driven Codebase Maintenance

author.name: Xinhao Zhang, Jingjie Lu, Kunpeng Liu, Fei Xie

entry.summary: PROOF manages codebases indirectly through structured natural-language specifications, abstracting codebase topology hierarchically and establishing trust by proving semantic equivalence via reconstructing source code solely from the specification. Maintenance requests then operate on the verified spec layer rather than raw code. It responds to the growing maintenance burden of LLM-generated code with a verification-first design.

entry.title: From Scores to Evidence: Auditable Decisions Can Improve Speech Deepfake Detection

author.name: Mengzhe Geng, Yujia Lu, Patrick Littell, Manuela Kunz, Xie Chen

entry.summary: The paper argues that single-scalar outputs from speech deepfake detectors hide useful provenance, and proposes an auditable decision record that carries four aligned evidence cues (including passive and retrieval evidence) into a late calibration step. This preserves interpretability about why a borderline utterance is trusted, deferred, or reviewed while keeping the final decision scalar.

entry.title: MORPHA: Morphology-Constrained Training and the Limits of Cross-Acquisition Transfer in Low-Resource Malaria Microscopy

author.name: Favour Okechukwu Igwezeke, Chikodili Helen Ugwuishiwu, Joseph Uzochukwu Emesiani, Samuel Ifebuche Agada, Ekenechukwu Lilian Anozie, Mary Ofuru Kama, Adaobi Chiazor Emegoakor

entry.summary: MORPHA introduces a morphological consistency constraint for malaria microscopy models, penalizing predictions that deviate from stage-conditional parasite morphology statistics, and studies where such constraints help cross-acquisition transfer on real Ugandan field data. The paper also honestly delineates where generic regularization suffices. This matters for deploying reliable diagnostics in genuine low-resource clinical settings.

entry.title: Object-Aware Background-Controlled Editing via Weighted Velocity Guidance

author.name: Wuji Wang, Yue Wu, Chenhao Yi, Shuhui Wang

entry.summary: OAVC is a training-free image editing framework that introduces object-level control into velocity integration for diffusion and flow-matching models, decoupling where semantic residuals act from how strongly they apply. This prevents background drift and unstable object boundaries caused by prompt-induced residuals leaking outside target objects. It improves the precision of training-free object-centric edits.

entry.title: MARR: Decoupling Policy, Execution, and Calibration for All-in-One Medical Image Restoration

author.name: Haobin Chen, Ao Chang, Heqin Zhu, Rundong Wang, Ting Liu, Shaohua Kevin Zhou

entry.summary: Recasts all-in-one medical image restoration across PET, CT, and MRI as a question of where to place limited adaptation, proposing MARR with degradation-aware policy routing, modality-private residual execution, and image-domain residual calibration in a compact framework. It avoids entangling modality-specific errors while enabling unified deployment.

entry.title: Agentic Visual Generation: From Generative Models to Agentic Control

author.name: Yinming Huang, Shuyuan Tu, Xi Yan, Jiahao Zhan, Zihan Yang, Zhen Xing, Hui Zhang, Tiehua Zhang, Yu-Gang Jiang, Zuxuan Wu

entry.summary: This position/survey paper argues that visual generation is shifting from single-invocation generative models to agentic control processes that plan, select tools, inspect intermediate outputs, revise failures, and reuse experience, with LLMs or VLMs as controllers. It critiques the field for lacking a consistent criterion of agenticity, noting that planning depth, tool use, and multi-role collaboration are often conflated with agentic capability. The proposed organization around what a controller can actually direct offers a useful conceptual framework for a rapidly growing area.

entry.title: Drive by Hindsight and Foresight: Tool-Grounded Synergistic Reasoning over Hierarchical Memory for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Baojie Chen, Zijun Jia, Jing Zhong

entry.summary: This work presents a framework for vision-language model based autonomous driving that couples hierarchical short-term and long-term driving memory with proactive tool invocation in a closed reasoning loop. It targets known VLM failure modes in driving such as hallucination, weak spatio-temporal perception, and poor generalization by letting the agent accumulate experience after each answer. It claims to be the first synergistic combination of hierarchical memory and tool use for driving agents.

entry.title: GSComplete: Gaussian Splat Completion with 2D Diffusion Priors

author.name: Elias Brugger, Philipp Erler, Stefan Ohrhallinger, Paul Guerrero

entry.summary: GSComplete completes missing regions of Gaussian splat 3D objects using only 2D diffusion priors via score distillation sampling, with a novel preservation loss that retains original splats in visible regions and generates new splats only where needed. This avoids the need for scarce 3D training data and preserves input geometry, addressing a practical limitation of existing completion methods. The authors also contribute a new dataset of partially complete splats.

entry.title: LightSplat: Real-Time High-Fidelity 3D Gaussian SLAM with Loop Closure

author.name: Junze Bao, Ye Gao, Yiming Huang, Xiaolong Yu, Chen Dong, Qing Gao, Wei Wang, Jinhu L\"u

entry.summary: LightSplat is a hybrid RGB-D SLAM framework combining sparse-feature tracking with a dual-thread backend building dense Gaussian submaps, and introduces online loop closure via feature-accelerated 3DGS registration with pose graph optimization. It achieves real-time, high-fidelity reconstruction suited to real-world deployment. This addresses the operational performance gaps of current 3DGS-based SLAM systems.

entry.title: OVMAN: A Task and Benchmark for Open-Vocabulary Motion-Aware Navigation

author.name: Dibyendu Ghosh

entry.summary: OVMAN defines a navigation task where an agent tours a scene, returns after a scripted change, and must navigate to a goal specified by the change itself — e.g., go to where the vase used to be. It releases 219 oracle-certified two-visit episodes, including relations requiring reasoning about places where objects have left, and shows existing zero-shot navigators fail as predicted. This exposes a real capability gap in current navigation systems regarding change-aware reasoning.

entry.title: SkillX: Unified Multi-Skill Policy Learning for Humanoid Soccer

author.name: Zhangchen Ye, Enxuan Ruan, Yifei Bao, Runhan Huang, Jiankun Yang, Jiakang Jin, Yixiao Huo, Pengyuan Wang, Yinan Han, Huaxing Huang, Wenhao Cui, Yiming Li, Xiaoyu Tian

entry.summary: SkillX presents a unified reinforcement learning framework for humanoid soccer that learns and composes multiple atomic object-interactive skills through a single command-conditioned policy.
