It combines skill-specific adversarial motion priors, per-skill critics, and an object-aware temporal encoder to handle balance, locomotion, and skill switching over long horizons. Humanoid soccer is a demanding whole-body control testbed, making this a strong demonstration of multi-skill policy composition.

entry.title: DYAD: A Multimodal Dataset of Co-Located Human Assistance

author.name: Akhil Ajikumar, Mahya Qorbani, Sakib Reza, Sean Andrist, Mohsen Moghaddam

entry.summary: DYAD is a synchronized multimodal dataset of human-human co-located assistance during gearbox assembly, linking a helper's verbal and physical interventions to performer requests, task state, assistance triggers, and outcomes across 20 sessions. It fills a gap left by datasets of solo execution or remote verbal instruction. Such data is essential for training embodied assistants that work physically alongside people.

entry.title: DI-Bench: Systematically Generating In-Domain Data Intelligence Benchmarks for Enterprise Agents

author.name: Jiangyun Zhang, Kristen Surrao, Torpong Nitayanont, Yupei Zhang, Roopali Singh, Zhiyu Chen, Julia Huang, Zhou Tang, Shayan Ali Akbar, Omar Alonso, Erwin Cornejo, Yuan Li, Yi Zhang

entry.summary: DI-Bench is a pipeline that automatically generates realistic enterprise data-intelligence benchmarks by building an artifact linkage graph over tables, dimensions, metrics, and documents, forming questions that require both structured computation and business-knowledge retrieval. Ground-truth answers come from query execution, addressing the cost and scarcity of domain-specific agent evaluation.

entry.title: Beyond Top-$k$ Skill Retrieval: Diversity-Aware Skill Routing for LLM Agents

author.name: Wang Wei, Tiankai Yang, Samyadeep Basu, Hongjie Chen, Yue Zhao, Zhengzhong Tu, Xiyang Hu, Franck Dernoncourt, Ryan A. Rossi, Hoda Eldardiry

entry.summary: The paper proposes Diverse Skill Routing (DSR), a reranking framework using a Determinantal Point Process to balance relevance and non-redundancy when routing user requests over large skill registries for LLM agents. It introduces a query-residual diversity kernel that penalizes redundant skill overlap without penalizing shared query relevance. DSR improves recall and full-task success on the SkillRouter benchmark while conserving context budget.

entry.title: DAREBench: Deployment-Aware and Reliable Evaluation of Models as Agents

author.name: Yu Liu, Zhilin Liu, Zhiwei Yang, Shaojie Zhang, Zheyuan Deng, Tingwei Huang, Zhenbo Luo, Lei Jiang, Yanbing Liu, Pei Fu

entry.summary: DAREBench is an agent benchmark with 233 tasks adapted from 22 source benchmarks in a shared OpenClaw execution environment, designed to assess multimodal perception, multi-step execution, tool use, and artifact delivery under workload variation. It aims to make agent evaluation more comparable, interpretable, and reliable for deployment decisions than task-specific existing benchmarks.

entry.title: Improving Proficiency and Efficiency of Android GUI Agents via Self-Generating Tool Actions

author.name: Juyong Lee, Woogyeol Jin, Kimin Lee

entry.summary: Presents DroidTool, a framework enabling Android GUI agents to self-generate tool actions as Python functions over application states via an agentic pipeline of proposal, implementation, test generation/execution, and repair, including relational tests across tools to naturally prepare test preconditions. Reduces the human labor that has limited hybrid GUI-plus-tool action spaces. Strongly aligned with current agentic tool-learning trends.

entry.title: SkillAlign: Aligning Skill Interfaces for LLM-based Agents

author.name: Shuo Ren, Xiaomian Kang, Jiajun Zhang

entry.summary: SkillAlign argues that a skill's utility for LLM agents depends not just on its content but on how its interface is exposed (full instructions, hints, compressed summaries, workflows, or none). It provides a provider-agnostic framework using multi-view procedural cards enabling counterfactual evaluation of exposure choices while holding task, agent, and skill fixed. This reframes skill selection as an interface-alignment problem, an underexplored axis in agent design.

entry.title: What Does an LLM-Agent Leaderboard Rank Actually Compare?

author.name: Wei-Jung Huang

entry.summary: An estimand-aware analysis of what public LLM-agent leaderboard scores actually estimate, showing pairwise superiority conclusions often fail when systems differ in task mixture, label source, or cost rules. It proposes a pairwise procedure with common-support checks, uncertainty rules, and practical margins, applied to SWE-bench and other leaderboards.

entry.title: Mini-Batch Risk-Averse Deep Q-Learning: A Robot Navigation Case Study

author.name: Aayush Patel, Andrzej Ruszczy\'nski

entry.summary: Addresses the obstacle that dynamic, time-consistent Markov risk measures depend nonlinearly on the transition kernel and thus cannot be estimated from single transitions, by introducing mini-batch transition risk mappings that remain coherent and admit unbiased one-sample gradient estimates. Demonstrated on robot navigation. This makes risk-averse reinforcement learning practical with sample complexity comparable to standard Q-learning.

entry.title: AgentGrad: Intervention-guided Prompt Optimization for Multi Agent Systems

author.name: Jaewon Chu, Jinwoo Seo, Jaewon Cho, Jeehye Na, Yunyang Xiong, Youngdae Kim, Hyunwoo J. Kim

entry.summary: Identifies limitations in textual-gradient prompt optimization for LLM multi-agent systems, specifically in gradient extraction (target prompts selected without verifying the fix resolves the failure; gradients lacking agent-level supervision) and gradient aggregation. AgentGrad introduces intervention-guided optimization that verifies whether modifying a target prompt actually resolves the failure and aggregates gradients at the system level.

entry.title: Who Maintains Agent Skills? A Longitudinal Study of Human-Governed, AI-Assisted Skill Maintenance

author.name: Chen Shen, Estevam Hruschka

entry.summary: This empirical study mines full commit histories of five public AI-skill repositories, covering 873 commits, 143 skill files, and 254 substantive post-creation edits, to understand how human-governed maintenance of agent skill artifacts like SKILL.md actually happens over deployment. It addresses the overlooked human bottleneck in lifelong agent capability curation, complementing work that only evaluates automated skill curation. The longitudinal, repository-mining methodology is unusual and informative for the emerging agentic-AI ecosystem.

entry.title: GeoContext: One Context Ladder, Two Failure Modes in Vision-Language Geolocation: Flat Reliance on User-Provided Location Context and False Confirmation of Location Claims

author.name: Yifan Zhang, Kai Wang

entry.summary: GeoContext is a benchmark probing how vision-language geolocation models respond to user-supplied location context, with a GeoHint task (localize given a coarse true hint) and a GeoVerify task (verify a claimed location within 150 m). Across 109 sites in 30 cities and roughly 28,000 responses from five VLMs, it identifies two failure modes: over-reliance on context and false confirmation of incorrect location claims.

entry.title: One MLLM, One Call: Efficient Zero-Shot Vision-and-Language Navigation via Spatial-Aware Waypoints

author.name: Shiqi Pan, Qi Zheng, Hanqin Sun, Youjian Zhang, Daquan Feng, Xu Wang

entry.summary: O2C-Nav is a zero-shot vision-and-language navigation framework that queries the multimodal LLM only once per decision step, using a training-free structured waypoint generator and projecting candidate waypoints onto RGB images as visual markers. This drastically cuts inference latency versus multi-query baselines.

entry.title: Tracking the Moving Frontier: Long-Short Term Advantage Estimator

author.name: Xinhao Yao, Lu Yu, Changhao Wang, Fengwei Teng, Yuyao Zhang, Qing Cui, Jun Zhou, Yong Liu

entry.summary: Introduces LSTAE, a single-stream RL algorithm for long-horizon agent training that replaces expensive repeated group sampling with persistent per-task trackers: a drift-aware historical baseline at the trajectory level and short-term signals, while updating the policy only with current rollouts. This reduces RLVR training cost by reusing historical experience for advantage estimation without optimizing on stale trajectories.

entry.title: PCSDiff: Diffusion-Based Bias Correction and Super Resolution Toward Practical Operational Medium-Term Precipitation Forecast

author.name: Yuze Sun, Shiyi Wang, Jiancheng Pan, Die Wang, Andreas F. Prein, Wentao Luo, Linhan Jiang, Jie Wu, Quan Zhang, Xiaomeng Huang

entry.summary: Introduces PCSDiff, a cascaded task-decoupled diffusion framework for 10-day precipitation bias correction and downscaling that models multi-day dynamic bias evolution and integrates precipitation intensity constraints to avoid over-smoothed outputs. The aim is operational reliability for flood-drought risk assessment.

entry.title: FedRAW: Preserving Rare-Label Influence in Asynchronous Federated Learning

author.name: Prashant Bajpai, Divya Saxena, Philippe Lalanda, German Vega

entry.summary: FedRAW identifies silent rarity failure in asynchronous federated learning, where clients holding rare labels contribute too weakly to the global model despite seemingly unaffected overall accuracy, driven by participation bias and buffer-based staleness effects. The proposed method preserves rare-label influence under heterogeneous participation. This exposes a hidden fairness failure mode in a widely used training regime.

entry.title: MV-STRIDE: Enabling MLLMs to Master Multi-View Spatial Reasoning via Hierarchical Capability Modeling

author.name: Jin Xu, Xiaojian Huang, Zhuodong Luo, Zhihong Zhang, Xin Liu, Jiansheng Wei, Xinzhi Wang, Jie Zhao, Xuejin Chen

entry.summary: MV-STRIDE is a multi-view spatial reasoning dataset for multimodal LLMs that explicitly models dependencies between perception, scene understanding, and contextual reasoning, mirroring human 3D spatial cognition. The authors build a systematic QA generation pipeline from diverse 3D scenes with enforced cross-view constraints. It targets a recognized bottleneck in MLLM spatial reasoning.

entry.title: BlueprintAgent: Constraint-Triggered Targeted Revisits for Simulation-Ready Generation from Scanned Structural Blueprints

author.name: Zhouyuan Xu, Chen Yang, Linhao Wang, Jiansheng Fan, Chen Wang

entry.summary: BlueprintAgent is a multimodal agent that converts scanned reinforced-concrete building blueprints into simulation-ready frame models supporting FEM export and engineer review. It treats an MLLM as the primary reader, with OCR and computer vision supplying localized evidence, and uses constraint-triggered revisits to catch violations of beam-column support, span count, and 3D continuity requirements that plague direct prompting.

entry.title: Generation of Vectorized Maps Beyond Vehicle View

author.name: Clara Gomez, Alberto Jaenal, Antonio Artu\~nedo, Jorge Godoy, Jorge Villagra

entry.summary: This paper defines a new problem, beyond-view vectorized HD map generation: extrapolating plausible map continuations beyond the vehicle's sensor field of view for autonomous driving planning. It proposes BeyondFormer, a transformer-based model that generates map elements outside the sensed area, addressing a real scalability limitation of online HD mapping.

entry.title: You Can't Prefer Emotions You Don't Sample: Intensity Undershoot in DPO-Tuned LLMs

author.name: Hyunwoo Kim, Usama Khalid

entry.summary: Quantifies intensity undershoot in instruction-tuned LLMs conditioned on continuous valence-arousal targets, measuring gain slopes of only 0.26 (valence) and 0.13 (arousal) for Llama-3.1-8B versus a faithful value of 1. Attributes the effect to DPO preferring responses similar to the reference policy, so extreme target states are undersampled.

entry.title: CUNO: Curriculum and Preference Optimization for Stable Graph Unlearning under Mass Deletion

author.name: Chenhan Zhang, Ali Braytee, Madhushi Bandara, Xin Hao, Paul J. Kennedy, Massimo Piccardi, Raymond Owen

entry.summary: CUNO tackles catastrophic unlearning in graph models, where utility collapses under large deletion ratios because structural dependencies give deleted nodes unequal roles. It orders samples by their influence and removes them progressively via a curriculum with preference optimization. This improves machine unlearning, which matters for privacy compliance in graph learning.

entry.title: TriCCOT: Tri-part Convolutional Conformal Transformer for Onboard Space Object Detection

author.name: Adrien Dorise, Marjorie Bellizzi, Julia Cohen, St\'ephane May

entry.summary: TriCCOT is a tri-part architecture for onboard object detection in Earth observation that combines a convolutional region proposal network, a conformal prediction stage, and a hardware-friendly attention-based classifier (Aper-GATES) designed for FPGA deployment. It balances the robustness of transformers with the hardware constraints of onboard processing on raw, noisy imagery.

entry.title: Hi-FLoop: Hierarchical State-Feedback Loops for Multi-Timescale World Modeling

author.name: Rx Fan, Zhan H

entry.summary: Hi-FLoop proposes a branch-consistent, multi-timescale state-feedback framework for multi-agent traffic simulation, maintaining eight scene-level Worlds as joint hypotheses over an 8-second rollout. It decomposes decision-making across time scales (an 8-second Goal anchoring intent, a 2-second Preview coordinating interactions, and finer motion-level control) to preserve cross-scale consistency as the context evolves with generated states. This is relevant to autonomous driving and world modeling research, where long-horizon closed-loop realism remains a core challenge.

entry.title: AhaBench: Do Agents Learn from Prior Experience? A Benchmark for Long-Horizon Continual Learning

author.name: Zerui Cheng, Jiawei Xu, Huacan Chai, Jiayang Sun, Pramod Viswanath, Maxm Pan

entry.summary: AhaBench evaluates whether a fixed model actually improves on later related tasks after receiving useful experience, testing transfer when support is removed, changed, or delayed across three components: Aha-Puzzle, Aha-Euler, and Aha-Vending. It shifts agent evaluation from single-trajectory scoring toward measuring within-model continual learning. A timely benchmark as LLM agents move to long-horizon operation.

entry.title: Generalizing HVAC Control With Domain Randomized Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Pablo Boitel, Kun Zhang

entry.summary: NOMAD-RL is a general-purpose RL controller for HVAC that transfers across heterogeneous thermal zones via a non-invasive thermostat interface, using adaptive domain randomization based on physics-informed normalizing flows. A recurrent policy enables online adaptation under partial observability. This tackles the key barrier to deploying RL controllers in buildings: per-site retuning and model dependence.

entry.title: Beyond Retraining-Free MoE Compression: A Cost-Normalized Study of Post-Compression Adjustment

author.name: Sieun Hyeon, Jaeyoung Do

entry.summary: This paper argues that retraining-free MoE compression should be viewed as producing compressed initializations rather than final artifacts, and systematically compares post-compression fine-tuning versus knowledge distillation across two MoE backbones, four pruning/merging methods, and 28 benchmarks under matched data and GPU budgets. Using only 3,000 C4 examples and one epoch, full fine-tuning recovers 37.3% of the original-to-compressed performance gap on average and is more cost-effective than standard KD. This offers actionable guidance for efficient MoE deployment.

entry.title: Local and Global Stability in Performative Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Debmalya Mandal

entry.summary: The paper studies performatively stable policies in performative RL, showing that standard Lipschitz sensitivity assumptions fail in settings like multi-agent best-response dynamics. It analyzes mixtures of policies, distinguishing local mixed stability from global stability and revealing that randomization behaves differently than in performative prediction. A conceptual advance in understanding deploy-then-adapt feedback loops in sequential decision making.

entry.title: How Does Parameter Pruning Reshape DNN Representations? An Interaction-Driven Exploration

author.name: Fangbo Li, Junpeng Zhang, Qihan Ren, Quanshi Zhang

entry.summary: The study explains why pruning some parameters degrades performance sharply while others do not, by tracking how pruning affects interaction patterns encoded in DNNs. It reveals three-phase dynamics: performance is preserved until pruning starts removing low-order interactions, which prove strongly generalizable. This interaction-based account offers a new lens on pruning and compression.

entry.title: Data Efficient Sample Selection for In-Context Learning

author.name: V Venktesh, Cem levi, Avishek Anand

entry.summary: Introduces DearICL, which frames in-context learning demonstration selection as a subset ranking problem using a differentiable sorting surrogate, enabling query-adaptive selection from large demonstration pools rather than static offline task-level selection. Aims to improve generalization to unseen queries.

entry.title: Dense Structural Compression of Transformers via Gauge-Correct Channel Removal

author.name: Jed A. Duersch, Na\"im Es-Sebbani, Nathana\"el Haas, Zied Bouraoui

entry.summary: Develops GaugeLasso, a training-time channel penalty for transformers that drives entire tensor slices to zero for physical removal while keeping tensors dense for GPU throughput. It identifies and resolves a gauge-freedom pathology that destabilizes naive norm-based channel penalties, aiming to reduce inference energy and FMA operations per token.

entry.title: Geodesic-informed Generative Diffusion Model For Topology-preserved Image Video Generation

author.name: Nian Wu, Nivetha Jayakumar, Jiarui Xing, Miaomiao Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes a diffusion model guided by geodesic/shape information to preserve geometric and topological consistency during generation, addressing the tendency of standard diffusion models to ignore object structure. The method explicitly represents shape changes, targeting high-stakes applications like computational anatomy, biology, and robotics where topology must be preserved. It extends to both image and video generation.

entry.title: TV-Regulated OPD: Direction Matters in On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Han Xiao, Yifan Niu, Dongyi Liu, Chang Luo, Jia Li

entry.summary: This work systematically dissects instability in on-policy distillation for LLM post-training, finding that only the sign of token-level advantages matters for matching standard OPD performance, while smoother bounded advantages stabilize training. Building on this, it shapes advantages with a total-variation-style regularization. Together with a companion RouteOPD paper in the same batch, it signals that the field is converging on simple, robust signal-shaping as the key to reliable OPD.

entry.title: Length Generalization for Transformers via Compression

author.name: Georg Zetzsche, Hongjian Jiang, Andy Yang, Pascal Bergstr\"a{\ss}er, Marco S\"alzer, David Chiang, Anthony W. Lin

entry.summary: Refines the C-RASP hypothesis for transformer length generalization by using the fragments C-RASP+ and C-RASP1, which admit computable length-generalization bounds, resolving theoretical problems with the original conjecture. The work connects formal language theory with empirically observed transformer generalization behavior.

entry.title: CircuitLens: Reasoning Circuits as Data Selection Signals for Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards

author.name: Zhuofan Chen, Ziqian Jiao, Yikai Cui, Zhixin Cai, Jun Bai, Wenge Rong

entry.summary: Introduces Circuit Reasoning Score, a data selection signal for RLVR computed from 46 reasoning-sensitive attention heads identified via contrastive ablation, requiring only a single forward pass on the frozen base model without rollouts or reward labels. Experiments on Qwen2.5-Math-7B show engagement correlates with training data value.

entry.title: Ostrich: Taking Large Strides Through Stiff Contact in Differentiable Dynamics

author.name: Ale\v{s} Ku\v{c}era, Karel Zimmermann

entry.summary: Ostrich is a GPU-accelerated rigid-body simulator that resolves hard contacts and friction with non-smooth Newton iteration at large timesteps, differentiating the converged residual via implicit function gradients. It aims to combine accuracy, reliable contact geometry-preserving gradients, and low per-iteration cost, overcoming tape-based and surrogate simulator limitations.

entry.title: Hierarchical Wasserstein Merging for Multi-Domain Multi-Task Learning: From Specialists to a Generalist

author.name: Ming Cheng, Jiaying Gong, Hoda Eldardiry

entry.summary: Introduces Hierarchical Wasserstein Merging (HWM), a representation-level model merging framework that treats each domain-task specialist as a distribution of hidden representations and builds task-level and global Wasserstein barycenters to capture within-task variation and cross-task structure. The goal is a single generalist model for heterogeneous multi-domain multi-task settings without interference from joint training.

entry.title: Perspectives on Cross-Lingual Consistency in LLMs for Medical Questions

author.name: Minh Duc Bui, Mario Sanz-Guerrero, Abteen Ebrahimi, Sagi Shaier, Peter Herbert Kann, Manuel Mager, Katharina von der Wense

entry.summary: A position-style review arguing that multilingual medical benchmarks wrongly assume medical answers must be identical across languages, when cultural adaptation may be legitimate. The authors identify three research gaps: missing stakeholder perspectives, lack of empirical evidence on which approach serves users better, and absence of benchmarks separating universal from culture-specific correctness.

entry.title: SignDino: Self-Supervised Sign Language Representation Learning via Temporal-Axis Self-Distillation

author.name: Junyi Hu, Zhewen He, Haomian Huang, Zhenhua Li, Zhifei Li, Yi Fang

entry.summary: SignDino adapts the DINOv3 student-teacher self-distillation recipe from spatial image crops to the temporal domain of sign streams, decomposing video into left-hand, right-hand, and face tracks via YOLOv8n+ByteTrack and training lightweight temporal Transformers over frozen per-frame anatomical embeddings. This targets the anatomy-structured, temporally organized nature of sign language that generic image SSL misses. It advances accessible representation learning for a low-resource modality.

entry.title: SceneMosaic: Efficient and Diverse Simulation-Ready Scene Generation via Hybrid Agentic Layout Evolution

author.name: Xingjian Ran, Xiaoye Mo, Sihao Liu, Jianyu Zhang, Li Luo, Bo Dai

entry.summary: SceneMosaic combines agentic VLM-based text-to-3D pipelines with parametric image-to-3D models through a hybrid agentic layout evolution approach to generate diverse, simulation-ready indoor scenes efficiently. It addresses fidelity-efficiency-diversity tradeoffs that limit both existing paradigms and their tendency to produce a single output per input.

entry.title: From Gaze to Meaning: A Training-Free AI Agent for Unified Grounding and Explanation

author.name: Shayan Nasiriboukani, Sara Atito, Mohammad Nezamipour, Muhammad Awais

entry.summary: This work introduces the first training-free Gaze Target Agent, leveraging pretrained vision-language models with visually guided prompts and memory-based retrieval for high-uncertainty samples to jointly perform gaze target prediction, attention localization, and object identification without additional training. It offers interpretable gaze-guided reasoning. The training-free agentic design reduces supervision requirements substantially.

entry.title: An Integrated Video-AI Platform for Action-Level Microanastomosis Training and Performance Feedback

author.name: Yan Meng, Daniel A. Donoho

entry.summary: Builds a video-AI platform for surgical microanastomosis training that segments microscope videos into six surgical actions, extracts instrument kinematics for performance classification along NOMAT-aligned dimensions, and uses a grounded LLM to answer trainee questions about their performance. It enables scalable, automated surgical feedback.

entry.title: ADELE - Adaptive Delaunay Grids for High-Fidelity Mesh-Native Reconstruction

author.name: Johannes Weidenfeller, Shaofei Wang, Philipp F\"urnstahl, Siyu Tang

entry.summary: Introduces ADELE, an adaptive mesh-based optimization framework using adaptive Delaunay grids and a practical mesh rendering technique to produce high-fidelity meshes directly, avoiding the oversmoothing and excessive triangle counts of NeRF/3DGS post-processing pipelines and the instability of fixed-resolution mesh-native methods.

entry.title: Back to the Feature: Zero-Shot 6DoF Pose Estimation via Dense Local Features

author.name: Ali Rafiaei, Michael Greenspan

entry.summary: B2TFPose is a training-free, zero-shot method for 6DoF pose estimation of unseen objects from RGB images, using a frozen DINOv2-style vision transformer as its only pretrained component. It revives classical local feature matching with geodesic non-maximum suppression for viewpoint-diverse templates and render-guided re-correspondence, advancing the training-free state of the art. The work matters because it shows foundation model features can bridge the synthetic-to-real gap without task-specific fine-tuning.

entry.title: CARDEA: Auditable Reasoning Grounded in Spatial Evidence for End-to-End Coronary Angiography Interpretation

author.name: Jia-Jen Lee, Shih-Yen Hou, Kee Koon Ng, Wei-Chun Wang, Shih-Sheng Chang

entry.summary: CARDEA is a unified large vision-language model serving as the inference core of a coronary angiography interpretation pipeline, trained solely on public data through visual feature alignment, a self-distilled Chain-of-Box cold start, and reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards that encourage bounding-box-grounded reasoning traces. The goal is auditable, spatially grounded decisions to improve clinician trust in an area where interpretation varies substantially among observers. This addresses a real adoption barrier for medical AI systems.

entry.title: VeriScene: Reconstructing Crime Scenes from Legal Evidence via World-Model Agent

author.name: Kevin Chuanpu Fu, Yongsen Zheng, Zee Kin Yeong, Kwok-Yan Lam

entry.summary: VeriScene is an agent system that orchestrates physics-grounded world models to reconstruct crime scenes from multimodal forensic evidence such as photographs and witness statements, keeping claims traceable to evidence and motions physically plausible. It addresses known failure modes of naive world-model use, including dropped evidence and contradictory testimony. This is a notable application of generative world models to forensic and legal domains.

entry.title: Concentrate After Imagination: Text-Conditioned Evidence Grounding for Partially Relevant Video Retrieval

author.name: Shuaiqi Cheng, Siyu You, Yanbi Wu, Yuxi Chen, Jiahao Zhang, Xuming Hu

entry.summary: The paper identifies a query-agnostic concentration bottleneck in Partially Relevant Video Retrieval, where ranking trusts the strongest local response and coincidentally similar fragments can create unsupported score peaks. It proposes TRACE, a score-level evidence verification operator that activates query-relevant global video registers, routes support to frame-level evidence, and marginalizes alternative query-to-register-to-frame paths before temporal selection. This reframes PRVR ranking as evidence verification rather than raw similarity.

entry.title: A Joint 2D-3D Statistical Shape Model for Orthopedic Reconstruction

author.name: Florence Dell'Aniello Picard, Pranav Poudel, Nairouz Shehata, Fr\'ed\'eric Lavoie, Herve Lombaert

entry.summary: This paper proposes a joint 2D-3D statistical shape model that explicitly captures co-variation between 2D radiograph segmentations and 3D femoral geometry in a shared latent space, replacing expensive iterative 3D-to-2D projection matching used in prior SSM-prior methods. The work targets surgical planning, implant sizing, and post-operative follow-up where X-ray projections discard depth information. It matters because faster, more anatomically plausible 3D reconstruction from plain radiographs lowers cost and improves orthopedic care.

entry.title: MedGSSR: Generalizable Medical Image Super-Resolution 3D Reconstruction via Hierarchical Feed-forward Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Chengkai Wang, Luoyu Hong, Yiting Zhao, Jiamin Wang, Xiang Feng, Feiwei Qin, Zhenzhong Kuang, Xuefei Yin, Ali Bashashati, Yanming Zhu

entry.summary: MedGSSR is an end-to-end feed-forward framework for medical 3D super-resolution that represents volumes as explicit 3D Gaussian fields, avoiding per-subject optimization and coordinate-based implicit representations that compromise anatomical fidelity. The explicit Gaussian representation improves signal continuity and local high-frequency detail. This addresses scan-time, hardware, and radiation-dose limits in clinical volumetric imaging.

entry.title: Moment-Matching Probabilistic Data Association for Optimization-Based SLAM

author.name: Khoa Nguyen, Mitchell Turton, Florian Meyer

entry.summary: The authors combine probabilistic data association from multi-object tracking with optimization-based SLAM: alongside the nonlinear least-squares solver, measurements are assigned to landmarks probabilistically and landmark distributions are summarized via moment matching rather than single hard associations. This softens a long-standing brittleness in SLAM front-ends and should improve robustness in ambiguous or cluttered environments.

entry.title: SCoCaT: Success Conditioned Constrained Reinforcement Learning for Spacecraft Docking

author.name: Aman Arora, Ricard Marsal I Castan, Matteo El-Hariry, Miguel Olivares-Mendez

entry.summary: This paper identifies a structural failure mode of termination-based constrained RL when goals lie inside regions where safety constraints activate, a problem relevant to precise spacecraft docking. SCoCaT proposes success-conditioned constrained RL to overcome this limitation. The analysis of when termination-based safety methods break down is valuable for safety-critical robotic deployment broadly.

entry.title: WM-Craftnet: World Synesthesia Model for Generalizable and Robust Dexterous In-Hand Manipulation

author.name: Jie Yin, Zeyuan Zhao, Xiaojing Tan, Yang Liu, Chiyu Wang, Xinyang Gu

entry.summary: WM-Craftnet is a world-model-conditioned framework for dexterous in-hand manipulation that learns compact action-conditioned latent dynamics from proprioception, depth, tactile sensing, and actions. Unusually, the learned World Synesthesia Model is used as a state estimator/rich observation rather than for latent imagination or policy optimization, improving robustness to pose shifts, force disturbances, and object variation. This addresses a known fragility of visuotactile RL methods in controlled settings.

entry.title: Latest open artifacts (#24): Motif-3, GLM-5.3, Hy4-preview and open model licenses

author.name: Florian Brand

entry.summary: An installment of Interconnects' open-artifacts tracking series covering recent open-weight releases (Motif-3, Zhipu's GLM-5.3, Tencent's Hy4 preview) with a focus on shifting license regimes: Western labs (Google, Meta) moving to Apache 2.0 while leading Chinese labs (Kimi K3, MiniMax M3, and now GLM-5.3 abandoning MIT) impose commercial-use restrictions and revenue-threshold clauses. The post documents a notable 2026 divergence in openness strategies between Western and Chinese frontier model makers.

entry.title: Beyond Right and Wrong: Evaluating Second-order Social Reasoning in Large Language Models

author.name: Sunny Rai, Jinyi Kuang, Reyhan Jamalova, Annie Lou, Cristina Bicchieri, Niyati Malhotra, Victor Hugo Orozco-Olvera, Ana Maria Munoz-Boudet, Lyle H Ungar, Sharath C Guntuku

entry.summary: This paper argues that AI alignment has focused on first-order social norms while neglecting metanorms, the second-order expectations about who enforces norms and how. The authors introduce a framework evaluating LLM metanorm reasoning across emotional appraisal and behavioral response, with new classification tasks for predicting self-regulation by violators and other-regulation by observers, supported by a multi-perspective dataset. This matters because social intelligence in deployed models depends on anticipating enforcement dynamics, not just knowing rules.

entry.title: EdgeMem: LLM-Free Agent Memory Construction and Retrieval via Evidence-Preserving Multi-Anchor Hypergraph

author.name: Zeyang Cui, Jiannong Cao, Zhiyuan Wen, Bo Yuan, Junlan Feng, Shengyuan Chen

entry.summary: EdgeMem proposes an agent memory system that avoids LLM-generated summaries by preserving original interaction turns and organizing them in a multi-anchor hypergraph with content, temporal, and episodic cues. Retrieval returns source evidence directly, reserving LLM calls only for final answer generation, reducing cost and information loss.

entry.title: A Translational Note on AI Safety Evaluation

author.name: Madhava Gaikwad

entry.summary: Argues that claims that automated red-teaming outperforms human red-teaming conflate benchmark-internal validity with external validity: a benchmark only measures search over a predefined harm set, so harms omitted from that set are invisible to any attacker within it. Draws parallels to cryptography and clinical trials and names the AI-safety version the threat-model blind spot. A sharp methodological critique of current safety evaluation practice.

entry.title: PhysMAS: Physics-Grounded Multi-Agent Synthesis of Compositional 4D Gaussians

author.name: Jiang Qin, Chunji Lv, Yangguang Wei, Yang Gao, Ming Liu, Lizhong Ding, Ye Yuan, Yinjie Lei, Changsheng Li

entry.summary: This paper proposes PhysMAS, a multi-agent system for generating physically plausible 4D Gaussian dynamic scenes, addressing the challenge of assigning heterogeneous materials to distinct object parts for Material Point Method simulation. It replaces one-shot LLM/VLM material assignment and SDS-based optimization with an agentic decomposition that binds materials to parts and verifies simulation executability. This matters for advancing automatic, physically realistic 4D content generation for graphics and simulation.

entry.title: The Internal Anatomy of Strategic Choice in Large Language Models

author.name: Vin\'icius Ferraz, Leon Houf, Enrico Ferrea

entry.summary: Records activations from four open-weight models (dense and MoE, including a matched base-instruct pair) playing 144 ordinal 2x2 games, tracing how incentives flow from prompt through activations to choice. Finds incentive and choice are detectable in all models but differ in whether incentive causally reaches the choice, with interesting base vs instruction-tuned similarities.

entry.title: xDailyBench: Benchmarking LLMs on Professional Consultation for Real-Life Problems

author.name: Yongchang Peng, Qingshui Gu, Liya Zhu, Ge Zhang, Duo Wang, Haodong Wang, Jingzhe Ding, Tianhao Yu, Letian Gao, Yongjie Zhong, Chaoxin Li, Zixin Su, Jinchao Tao, Xingyu Ma, Xin'ao Guo, Feng Tian, Shiyuan Dong, Xiaoyan He, Sen Liu, Xin Chen, Jiajun Li, Zejia Zhang, Xi Lin, Wen Zhang, Yi Zhu, Duju Zeng, Xiang Gao, Yunyang Wang, Jiahao Wang, Yujia Qin, Jiaheng Liu, Shen Yan, Xiaolong Chang, Wenhao Huang

entry.summary: A benchmark of 248 curated tasks across 51 real-life scenarios spanning personal life, work, and learning, grounded in requests users actually made or intended to make with AI, evaluated with fine-grained binary rubrics that test both instruction following and inference of unstated needs. It targets the gap between academic benchmarks and messy real-world consultations.

entry.title: Automated Design of Inventory Policy with Large Language Models: An Exploratory Study

author.name: Fenghua Yang, Preet Baxi, Yi Zhang, Stefanus Jasin, Yanzhe Lei, Mo Liu, Parshan Pakiman

entry.summary: This exploratory study builds an integrated framework where an LLM iteratively generates parameterized inventory policy classes and an external solver optimizes parameters within each class, automating operations research policy design. Across 30 lost-sales inventory instances, mean cost reduction versus optimized base-stock benchmarks rises from 17.5% after one generation to 30.0% after ten generations. The result demonstrates that LLMs can contribute structurally novel policy hypotheses beyond their typical coding-support role in OR workflows.

entry.title: RevalExo: A Functional Daily-Activity Benchmark for Inertial and Visual Locomotion Mode Recognition in Older Adults and Clinical Cohorts

author.name: Diwas Lamsal, Juha Carlon, Reinhard Claeys, Maxim Yudayev, Louis Flynn, Tom Verstraten, David Beckw\'ee, Eva Swinnen, Mihai B\^ace, Bart Vanrumste, Benjamin Filtjens

entry.summary: Introduces RevalExo, a benchmark for inertial and visual locomotion mode recognition built on a clinically validated daily-activity protocol with older adults and clinical cohorts, addressing the gap left by benchmarks collected from healthy adults. It supports development of assistive devices like powered exoskeletons that need temporally precise labels for detecting locomotion mode transitions. This matters because it brings realistic clinical constraints into sensor-based human-motion AI evaluation.

entry.title: Qiushi Engine on AstaBench E2E-Bench-Hard

author.name: Wenhao Li, Shuxing Yang, Fujia Chen, Jincheng Mi, Yuang Pan, Rui Zhao, Zichen Li, Junyao Wu, Shenzhan Hong, Yaqi Li, Yize Wang, Kaihao Zhu, Taowen Deng, Junjie Yang, Hongsheng Chen, Yihao Yang

entry.summary: A technical report evaluating the Qiushi Engine autonomous research agent on all 40 tasks of AstaBench E2E-Bench-Hard, using DeepSeek-V4-Pro (an existing model released in April 2026) as its backend. The system achieves a leaderboard score of 0.816 and a full-task completion rate of 10%, roughly 3.3 times the best previously reported rate, at about USD 15 per task.

entry.title: PlannerForge: LLM Agents for Scenario-Based Testing of Motion Planners in Autonomous Driving

author.name: Yuan Gao, Sebastian M\"uller, Mattia Piccinini, Marc Kaufeld, Yuchen Zhang, Finn Rasmus Sch\"afer, Qunying Song, Johannes Betz

entry.summary: PlannerForge is an LLM-agent framework that unifies the full scenario-based testing pipeline for autonomous driving systems, from scenario generation and retrieval through modification, execution, and assessment, replacing a fragmented collection of separate tools. It also adds two further capabilities extending the pipeline. This matters because systematic validation of ADS planners is a safety-critical bottleneck and prior LLM-agent work covered only individual sub-systems.

entry.title: Emergent Goal-Directed Attention in Large Vision-Language Models

author.name: Han Zhang

entry.summary: The study tests whether goal-directed visual attention can emerge in vision-language models without gaze supervision, evaluating Qwen3-VL-32B-Thinking and the existing Gemma-4 model on nearly 5,000 naturalistic scenes under visual-search versus free-viewing instructions. Both models aligned better with human fixations when given matching goals, and this crossover persisted in target-absent scenes, ruling out simple visual grounding as the explanation. The finding suggests VLMs spontaneously encode task-dependent attentional priorities resembling human gaze behavior.

entry.title: Subject-Relative Micro-Motion and Sleep Dynamics for Near-Infrared Video Sleep Staging

author.name: Kunmin Jang, You Rim Choi, Hun Heo, Heonjun Lee, Suahn Bae, Dongik Park, Hyun-Woo Shin, Hyung-Sin Kim

entry.summary: ViNUSS is a framework for contactless sleep staging directly from near-infrared video alone, without reconstructing respiratory or cardiac proxies as intermediates. It combines subject-relative micro-motion cues with sleep dynamics and is evaluated against polysomnography-defined labels. This challenges the prevailing assumption that video is only useful as a route to physiological signal proxies.

entry.title: AtomCite: Verification and Correction of Supplied Page-Level Citations in Multi-Page Documents

author.name: Chen Qian, Yimeng Wang, Yu Chen, Lingfei Wu, Andreas Stathopoulos

entry.summary: AtomCite is an agentic framework that parses answers into claims, checks each claim against the image of its cited page, and applies a deterministic repair policy for citation verification and correction. It also introduces DocCite, reportedly the first benchmark for verifying and correcting page-level citations in document images, built on MP-DocVQA and DUDE with 928 validation examples.

entry.title: Intent Drift at SME Scale: Deployment Practice, Not Model Capability, Determines Agentic Compliance

author.name: Ilia Voroshilov

entry.summary: Introduces Chain of Intent, a governance framework for agentic AI in small regulated firms, validated in a simulated Hong Kong asset manager where an agent faced escalating managerial pressure to expand client outreach. Findings show deployment configuration, not raw model capability, determines whether agents hold their authorized constraints, with breaches occurring in a minority of runs.

entry.title: What the Window Does Not Contain: Auditing Provenance in a Document-Grounded Instability Benchmark

author.name: Seyed Mosayeb Alam

entry.summary: Describes Probity, a benchmark of 60 tasks and 470 items from real venture-financing filings measuring answer instability in document-grounded LLM QA, plus a self-audit that flagged 36 items whose supporting evidence was missing from the model's text window. Flagged items wobbled far more often, and excluding them cuts apparent instability.

entry.title: VDiff-Bench: A Challenging Benchmark for Fine-Grained Image Difference Identification

author.name: Yixin Wan, Tianle Zheng, Kai-Wei Chang

entry.summary: VDiff-Bench is a 1,756-question multiple-choice benchmark testing whether multimodal LLMs can identify what changed between two similar images, spanning 10 change categories with hard negatives to prevent shortcut answers. Change identification is a basic comparative skill that current MLLMs handle poorly despite strong VQA performance. The benchmark should help expose and quantify a blind spot in otherwise capable models.

entry.title: Robust Conformal Consensus: Multi-Agent LLM-as-a-Judge Interval Evaluation with Conformal Prediction

author.name: Lihui Liu

entry.summary: This paper proposes a framework for uncertainty quantification in LLM-as-a-Judge evaluation by constructing conformal prediction intervals from multiple LLM judges and combining them into a more stable consensus. It addresses the underexplored problem of evaluator variability, improving reliability of automated NLG evaluation.

entry.title: Deep Barycentric Regression for Optimal Transport Map Estimation and its Statistical Optimality

author.name: Kunwoong Kim, Insung Kong, Yongdai Kim

entry.summary: Proposes BROT, a barycentric regression approach for estimating optimal transport maps that bridges the gap between theoretically minimax-optimal but impractical nonparametric estimators and scalable but statistically underexplored parametric neural estimators. The paper establishes statistical optimality guarantees for the parametric formulation.

entry.title: Comparative Study of Anatomical and Learned Features in AI Models for Structural Brain MRI

author.name: Boyang Yu, Miquel Lopez Escoriza, Long Chen, Arjun V. Masurkar, Narges Razavian, Carlos Fernandez-Granda

entry.summary: This study compares three feature-extraction paradigms for structural brain MRI modeling: classical anatomical surface/volume measurements, supervised CNNs, and unsupervised pretrained ViT foundation models with finetuning. Across 18 public datasets covering roughly 80,000 participants and seven clinical tasks, simple linear models on anatomical features matched the diagnostic performance of complex learned features including large foundation models.

entry.title: Typed Federated Artifacts for the Agentic Web:Sharing Tool-Routing Knowledge Across Frozen,Heterogeneous LLM Agents

author.name: Abhijit Chakraborty, Ni Trieu, Vivek Gupta

entry.summary: This paper proposes a schema-validated, typed federated artifact format (instantiated as SYNAPSE1) that lets heterogeneous, frozen LLM agents from different vendors share tool-routing knowledge without exposing private histories or transferring weights. It addresses the ambiguity of flat text-based knowledge sharing by providing per-field privacy, dispute resolution, and cross-model transfer mechanisms. The work matters because the emerging agentic web lacks standards for inter-agent knowledge exchange across incompatible platforms.

entry.title: AstroSpecLM: A Spectrum-Language Model for Evidence-Grounded Astronomical Spectral Analysis

author.name: Jinghang Shi, Yanxia Zhang, Ali Luo, Changhua Li, Xiao Kong

entry.summary: AstroSpecLM connects DESI 1D astronomical spectra with Qwen3-4B, an existing language model, to answer questions with explanations grounded in distilled spectral facts rather than templated QA pairs. It matches specialist supervised baselines on classification and redshift estimation while additionally providing evidence-grounded explanations. This demonstrates a careful domain-adaptation recipe for scientific foundation-model applications.

entry.title: Beyond Single-Negative Preference: Multi-Negative DPO for LLM-Centric Historical Entity Linking

author.name: Tien Nam Nguyen, Emanuela Boros, Ahmed Hamdi, Adam Jatowt, Micka\"el Coustaty, Antoine Doucet

entry.summary: The paper introduces MDPO, a multi-negative extension of direct preference optimization that compares the correct entity against all retrieved negative candidates per mention rather than a single negative. Evaluated on hipe-2020 and newseye benchmarks across five languages, it preserves the Bradley-Terry DPO formulation while exploiting the full candidate set via masked, length-normalized sequence scores.

entry.title: Measuring Language Transfer in Robot Policies: Adding Greek to a Cosmos3 Vision-Language-Action Policy

author.name: Ayoub Kirouane, Georgios Giaples, Christos Petrocheilos

entry.summary: This paper studies adding Greek language support to an open vision-language-action robot policy using only machine-rephrased instructions, without architectural changes. Its core contribution is methodological: it shows that common evaluation instruments (color histograms, single-goal benchmarks, training loss, single-run comparisons) produce false conclusions, and proposes a discriminative ninety-task suite with multi-seed evaluation as a sounder protocol.

entry.title: TFTrack: A Template-Free Framework for Efficient 3D Point Cloud Tracking

author.name: Zhaofeng Hu, Sifan Zhou, Jiahao Nie, Ziyu Zhao, Weizi Li, Ci-jyun Liang

entry.summary: Proposes TFTrack, the first template-free framework for LiDAR-based 3D single object tracking, arguing that template priors from the Siamese paradigm are redundant and complex motion modeling unnecessary. Uses previous bounding-box centers and geometric alignment for motion priors, improving efficiency for robotic perception and navigation.

entry.title: AI for AI: Optimizing Additional Infrastructure Build-out to Power Artificial Intelligence Data Centers

author.name: Alexander Crosier, Kyle Onghai, Ronnie Sircar

entry.summary: Develops an economic-engineering framework linking data-center load growth, generation capacity, and electricity market-clearing prices, modeling data-center expansion and supply build-out as stochastic processes. Quantifies how AI-driven electricity demand raises prices absent a supply-side response and informs infrastructure investment decisions.

entry.title: WSPolypNet: Weakly Supervised Polyp Localization in Colonoscopy Videos

author.name: Giseong Hwang, Minjae Jo, Yeonghyeon Park, Kyeonghun Kim, Seoyeon Han, Donghoon Han, Haneul Kim, Yului Jeong, Insung Hwang, Pa Hong, Ken Ying-Kai Liao, Nam-Joon Kim

entry.summary: This paper proposes WSPolypNet, a weakly supervised framework that localizes polyps in colonoscopy videos using only video-level labels, avoiding costly frame-level annotation. It generates class activation maps from a 3D CNN, refines them with a multi-view strategy, and feeds them as point prompts to MedSAM2 for mask propagation. This reduces annotation cost for clinically important medical video analysis.

entry.title: AirAnchor: Bridging Local and Global Spatial Information for Zero-Shot Aerial Vision-and-Language Navigation

author.name: Shanwei Fan, Bin Zhang, Zhiwei Xu, Yingxuan Teng, Siqi Dai, Lin Cheng, Guoliang Fan

entry.summary: AirAnchor is a zero-shot aerial vision-and-language navigation method that fuses local spatial representations built online from current observations with global memories built offline from historical experience via spatial anchors, in a shared navigation framework. It supports both immediate action grounding and long-horizon path planning for drones following natural-language instructions. Zero-shot operation avoids costly navigation fine-tuning.

entry.title: Suan: Rectifying Direct Preference Safety Alignment in Large Language Models

author.name: Oleksandr Cherednichenko, Roman Klypa

entry.summary: Suan is a new preference optimization algorithm for LLM safety alignment that formulates the objective directly at the gradient level rather than through the standard variational derivation, yielding more interpretable training dynamics. It aims to reduce the over-refusal and general quality degradation that plague open-weight models given rigid safety guardrails.

entry.title: X2Streaming-ASR: wait when uncertain, emit when ready for streaming ASR

author.name: Zhiwei Lin, Kaiqi Fu, Rime Wen, Zehan Liu, Shawn Qin, Roy Gan, Hao Wang, Qian Wang

entry.summary: This paper introduces X2Streaming-ASR, a streaming speech recognition approach that learns to decide adaptively when to commit each output token rather than relying on fixed chunk sizes or target delays. It uses a three-stage training pipeline that first builds streaming recognition capability, then warm-starts a commit policy from automatically probed trajectories, and finally refines the policy with reinforcement-style optimization. This matters for real-time voice agents and full-duplex dialogue systems, where balancing transcript accuracy against commit latency is a core tradeoff.

entry.title: BIFTA: Brain-Inspired Few-Shot Tactile Adaptation for Unknown Sensors

author.name: Boheng Liu, Ziyu Li, Xia Wu

entry.summary: This paper introduces BIFTA, a framework that adapts a frozen pretrained encoder to previously unseen tactile sensors using only a small labeled support set, inspired by the brain's rapid sensory adaptation. It addresses the real problem that tactile perception models collapse when transferred across sensors with different optics, elastomer mechanics, and imaging geometry, using dual-view statistical memory to preserve pretrained representations. This matters for scalable robotic manipulation since it reduces the need to retrain perception models for every new sensor hardware.

entry.title: CausalChapter: Improving Long-Video Chaptering with Interventional Dependency Modeling

author.name: Xinran Duan, Guozhang Li, Yaoyao Zhong, Mei Wang, Lizhi Wang, Hua Huang

entry.summary: This paper introduces CausalChapter, a framework for automatic chaptering of long instructional videos that uses intervention-inspired dependency modeling, estimating prediction-level influence via lightweight masking and removal interventions. It targets the segment-then-caption paradigm and addresses two failure modes: boundary error propagation and fragmented cross-chapter context. The work matters because scalable navigation of lecture-style video content is a practical multimodal application area, and the interventional approach offers a principled alternative to purely heuristic boundary detection.

entry.title: Omni Interaction Agent Technical Report

author.name: Orantqing, Shengpeng Ji, Junlong Tong, Jialong Zuo, Dongjie Fu, Di Cao, Yangzhuo Li, Shangda Wu, Franz, Evan, Theron Veyra, Changhao Pan, Jingyu Lu, Dongchao Yang, Zhifei Xie, Yang Tan, Xiaoyu Shen, Xiaoda Yang, Wenfu Wang, Teddysun, Steveyves, Zhou Zhao, Bryanytian

entry.summary: Technical report on Gander, an end-to-end model unifying omni-modal perception (video, speech, text), realtime full-duplex interaction, and agentic capabilities in one framework. It uses a Cerebellum-Brain collaborative architecture to support user interruption and proactive model feedback. If the reported capabilities hold, this represents a notable step toward natural streaming multimodal agents, comparable to directions seen in Gemini-Omni and GPT-Realtime systems.

entry.title: FANS: Federated Adaptive Network Search Learning for Heterogeneous Devices

author.name: Jiaxin Zhang, Xingwei Wang, Bo Yi, Liang Zhao, Alireza Furutanpey, Ziyi Chen, Qiang He, Keqin Li, Schahram Dustdar

entry.summary: FANS addresses heterogeneous federated learning by learning a shared architecture space via a hypernetwork rather than a fixed menu of client models, with a Federated Parallel Scaling algorithm that trains sampled subnetworks in parallel using self-distillation. This lets devices with diverse resource budgets participate without being restricted to predefined model sizes. It connects neural architecture search with federated learning, a practical need for edge deployment.

entry.title: Stability and Generalization of Straight-Through Estimators for Training Two-Layer Quantized Neural Networks

author.name: Yiming Ying

entry.summary: This theory paper proves that in the saturated-output regime, the identity straight-through estimator for two-layer binary-activation networks is exactly stochastic subgradient descent on a convex latent loss, enabling a stability-based generalization analysis of the discontinuous STE rule. It derives exact distance identities and approximate non-expansiveness results for coupled updates. It provides one of the first rigorous generalization accounts for STE training.

entry.title: Bi-HYCO: Bi-Objective Cooperative Learning for PDE Parameter Identification under Fragmented Observations

author.name: Umberto Biccari, Jun Chen, Roberto Morales, Enrique Zuazua

entry.summary: Proposes Bi-HYCO, a cooperative bi-objective framework for identifying PDE parameters when physical and synthetic models receive complementary, fragmented observations. It couples predicted states at unlabeled interaction points and provides convergence guarantees such as sufficient decrease and finite iteration length for the deterministic case.

entry.title: NeuCME: Toward Dynamic Multimodal Continual Learning via Neural Combinatorics of Multiple Experts

author.name: Kai Guo, Chuanbin Liu, Peng Hu, Hao Wang, Xi Peng

entry.summary: Defines dynamic multimodal continual learning, where the set of modalities per task varies rather than being fixed, and proposes NeuCME with combinatorial expert routing to address spatio-temporal catastrophic forgetting and adaptive multimodal fusion.

entry.title: Trust-But-Verify: Poisoning-Resilient Locally Private Graph Learning Protocols

author.name: Longzhu He, Li Sun, Hao Peng, Ruijie Wang, Raymond Chi-Wing Wong, Sen Su

entry.summary: Identifies that locally private graph learning protocols based on local differential privacy are vulnerable to data poisoning via malicious nodes injected into neighborhood aggregation. Proposes a trust-but-verify defense that maintains formal LDP guarantees while detecting and mitigating poisoned contributions, with theoretical analysis.

entry.title: ParetoTransport: Generative Optimization by Mass Transport Toward The Pareto Front

author.name: Stephanie Holly, Sepp Hochreiter, Werner Zellinger

entry.summary: ParetoTransport is a training-free guidance method for pre-trained flow-matching models in multi-objective optimization, steering entire design populations toward and along the Pareto front via mass transport in objective space. It moves beyond sample-wise guidance to population-level distribution control. Authors include Sepp Hochreiter, adding credibility to the generative optimization direction.

entry.title: Proactive Context-Forecasted Safety Constraints for Nonstationary Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Tim Tomashevskiy

entry.summary: This arXiv paper proposes a framework for generating safety constraints proactively in reinforcement learning by forecasting environmental context. Instead of relying on fixed or reactive safety constraints, the method infers latent context from observations, predicts how that context will evolve, and adapts constraints to anticipated conditions so agents can avoid unsafe states before they arise. This is relevant to deploying RL in dynamic real-world settings such as autonomous driving in changing environments.

entry.title: Learning Metamaterial Eigenmodes with Wavelet-Encoded Fourier Neural Operators

author.name: Han Zhang, Alexander Ogren, Cynthia Rudin, Johann Guilleminot, L. Catherine Brinson

entry.summary: This paper addresses a known weakness of neural operator surrogates: eigenvalue problems where multiple valid eigenmodes must be predicted simultaneously, which violates the unique input-output mapping assumption behind standard operator learning. The authors combine Fourier Neural Operators with wavelet-based encodings of PDE inputs to learn elastic wave eigenmodes in metamaterials, and give a mechanistic explanation plus experiments for why wavelet encodings suit this dual-solution setting. It matters because it extends operator learning beyond forward PDE simulation into eigenanalysis relevant to acoustic/metamaterial design.

entry.title: Adaptively Incorporating Directional Hints into Zeroth-Order Optimization

author.name: Alexander Ryabchenko, Jian Qian, Wenlong Mou

entry.summary: This paper introduces CV-ZOD, a control-variate framework that lets zeroth-order optimizers exploit cheap but unreliable directional hints, such as linear subspaces approximating the gradient. The authors prove that an adaptively tuned variant achieves a convergence rate interpolating between the first-order O(1/T) and dimension-dependent zeroth-order O(d/T) rates, with robustness to hint quality. This matters because it formalizes how to cheaply inject side information into gradient-free optimization, relevant where gradients are expensive or unavailable.

entry.title: Target-Independent Micro-Interventions for Predicting Training Response Across Language-Model Families

author.name: Zhongxuan Liu, Sicheng Zhou, Hongzhi Wang

entry.summary: Proposes L-State, a characterization of a language model checkpoint's prospective training response obtained by branching short standardized micro-interventions and measuring effects in a common capability space. It derives cross-family bounds and shows readouts that substantially reduce prediction error in leave-one-family-out experiments.

entry.title: Accelerating Diffusion Transformers with Gaussian Process Rectified Feature Cache

author.name: Zhirong Shen, Rui Huang, Chang Zou, Shikang Zheng, Jiacheng Liu, Peiliang Cai, Zhengyi Shi, Yaosong Du, Liang Feng, Xiaobing Tu, Jinkui Ren, Xiantao Zhang, Linfeng Zhang

entry.summary: Improves prediction-based feature caching for diffusion transformers by exploiting a zero-mean statistical structure in caching residuals and using an online Gaussian process regression to correct drift from the full-compute trajectory, sidestepping the missing-label problem during acceleration. Targets making DiT generation more real-time.

entry.title: Cadence: Error-Bounded Lossy Compression of Demand Time Series with a Time-Series Foundation Model

author.name: Roberto Tacconelli

entry.summary: Cadence pairs Google TimesFM-3, a 330M-parameter time-series foundation model, with an adaptive arithmetic coder to build an error-bounded lossy compressor for numeric demand time series that guarantees per-sample error bounds. The paper includes a valuable negative result showing foundation models buy almost nothing for lossless coding because bits saved scale only logarithmically with predictor accuracy. The error-bounded regime escapes this limitation since forecasts landing inside the tolerance band yield nearly free samples.

entry.title: One Shared LoRA Weight for MRI Reconstruction across Acceleration Factors

author.name: Zhiwei Zhao, Weikang Gong, Zhongnian Li, Xinzheng Xu

entry.summary: The authors propose Shared LoRA, a parameter-efficient framework that freezes a pretrained SHFormer backbone and trains one shared set of LoRA adapters with a lightweight gating network to handle multiple MRI acceleration factors. Random sampling of acceleration factors and masks during training lets the adapters generalize across artifact patterns, reducing the training and storage costs of per-factor models. This addresses a practical pain point in accelerated MRI where existing approaches require separate models per factor.

entry.title: Introductory Notes on Learning$^2$

author.name: Sai Siddharth, Maniarasu Ravi

entry.summary: This paper introduces Learning^2, a representation-level framework for learning dynamical systems that couples a primary representation with a second representation linked through a known physical transformation, constraining the hypothesis space in a physically interpretable, ante-hoc manner. It instantiates the idea in EuLaNet, an Eulerian-Lagrangian neural architecture for physics prediction from data.

entry.title: CAVEAT: Recurrent Multimodal Diffusion Planning for Mapless Aerial Exploration

author.name: Steven Visch, Nicol\`o Botteghi, Antonio Franchi, Barbara Bazzana

entry.summary: This paper introduces CAVEAT, a diffusion-based policy for UAV exploration that generates waypoint sequences from fused LiDAR, visual, and pose features using a recurrent internal state, eliminating the need for a persistent global map at deployment. The system is trained on trajectories from the map-based FUELv2 expert and validated in simulation plus proof-of-concept hardware experiments on a Flyability drone.

entry.title: EigenLI: Spectral Approximations to Late Interaction

author.name: Archish S, Sabyasachi Basu, Ankit Garg, Ravishankar Krishnaswamy, Kirankumar Shiragur

entry.summary: Shows that late-interaction retrieval representations such as ColBERT's exhibit intrinsic low-rank structure, and introduces EigenLI, which compresses per-document token embeddings into document-specific low-dimensional eigensubspaces, reducing indexing cost, storage, and expensive MaxSim scoring while preserving retrieval quality.

entry.title: Clean Accuracy Does Not Guarantee Provenance Robustness: A Prospective Codec-Stress Evaluation of Audio Attribution

author.name: Gang Shi (Independent Researcher)

entry.summary: A prospectively registered evaluation showing that audio deepfake provenance attribution models like WavLM-Base+ suffer large Macro-F1 losses (up to ~53-70 points in some conditions) after ordinary codec transcoding, with degradation strongly condition- and representation-dependent. The work exposes a serious robustness gap between clean benchmark accuracy and real-world forensic reliability.

entry.title: Distribution-free inference on the number of changepoints

author.name: Rohan Hore, Aaditya Ramdas

entry.summary: This paper studies inference on the unknown number of changepoints K in an ordered data sequence, proving an impossibility result that any distribution-free upper confidence bound on K must be trivial. Using conformal p-values under exchangeability assumptions, the authors construct CLOCC, a finite-sample valid lower confidence bound on K, and argue it is the only feasible approach.

entry.title: Silver Rate Is (Almost) Optimal for Gradient Descent Acceleration

author.name: Yuhan Ye, Kaizhao Liu

entry.summary: The paper proves lower bounds on how much plain gradient descent can be accelerated using predetermined nonnegative stepsizes in smooth convex optimization. It establishes an exponent of p_sil = log_2(1+sqrt(2)) (the silver schedule rate) as essentially optimal in both anytime and non-anytime settings, matching recent upper bounds by Altschuler and Parrilo and by Zhang et al. This resolves the optimal polynomial convergence order achievable by fixed stepsize schedules.

entry.title: Dynamic Lagging for Simultaneous Translation

author.name: Hieu Hoang, Amittai Axelrod

entry.summary: The paper addresses cascaded simultaneous speech translation where the MT system must decide how much target text to commit given a growing source prefix it does not control. The authors fine-tune a sentence-trained decoder-only LLM (Qwen3-8B) on stable prefixes so it becomes prefix-aware, using a single force-decode turn that makes output flicker-free by construction, evaluated for EN to DE, JA, and ZH. This offers a practical recipe for low-latency, stable simultaneous translation built on general-purpose LLMs.

entry.title: STQA: A Benchmark for Stock-Focused Tabular Question Answering over Historical and Forecasted Data

author.name: Baoxu An, Wenmian Yang, Zhensheng Wang, Weijia Jia

entry.summary: Introduces STQA, an end-to-end benchmark for natural-language question answering over stock market data covering 4,417 stocks and 31,400 question-answer pairs spanning historical records, numerical forecasts, and forecast-based reasoning. It also proposes SQFRS, an agent-based framework that orchestrates querying, forecasting, and reasoning as a unified baseline system.

entry.title: Vishing-Tactics-Bench: Forecasting Exploitation Trajectories in Voice Phishing Calls

author.name: Jeongmin Lee, Dongmyung Sul, Seung Yun, Jinxia Huang

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark for real-time voice phishing defense that shifts from post-hoc fraud classification to harm projection, predicting at each conversational turn whether an ongoing call is heading toward Information Gathering or Financial Exploitation. It adapts MITRE ATT&CK into a 6-tactic vishing taxonomy and labels 35,340 scammer utterances across 5,645 synthetic Chinese calls, grounded in Endsley's situation-awareness framework. This matters because timely detection mid-call could enable actual intervention rather than retrospective analysis.

entry.title: Deadline-Aware Adaptive Prefill Chunking for Efficient Large Language Model Serving

author.name: Siyu Song, Qi Bai, Jinbo Hao, Kai Li, Chenchen Wang, Jiayu Sun

entry.summary: Introduces SLOWeave, an online scheduler for LLM serving that dynamically picks the largest prefill chunk predicted to complete before the earliest active decode deadline, avoiding the fixed-chunk-size tradeoff between prefill efficiency and decode latency spikes. The method uses a logarithmic-time search over a monotone iteration-cost model and comes with a theoretical guarantee.

entry.title: When Models Defer to Wrong Answers: A Robustness Audit of Source-Attributed Cues in Multiple-Choice QA

author.name: Manikandan Ravikiran, Siddharth Vohra

entry.summary: This audit examines how claims about what another source answered destabilize LLM responses in multiple-choice QA, introducing NC-MCAR, a metric that measures switches to a wrong option only when the model answered correctly under a neutral prompt. Four instruction-following models were evaluated on MMLU-Pro and IndicMMLU-Pro across several languages. The findings are significant for understanding sycophancy and social-safety risks in deployed models.

entry.title: RepoNav: From Snippet Retrieval to File-Centered Repository Navigation for Code Agents

author.name: Hongzheng Chai, Jiakun Li, Hongyue Yu, Yuan Yuan

entry.summary: RepoNav is a lightweight post-retrieval interface that reorganizes flat code-snippet search results into a file-centered navigation scaffold with structural cues, helping code agents compare sibling symbols and distinguish target functions from semantically similar alternatives. It directly addresses a practical failure mode of repository-level coding agents. The approach is simple and plausibly widely applicable to agentic coding stacks.

entry.title: From Coordinates to Candidate Regions: Temporal Change Localization via Region Selection in Remote Sensing Multimodal LLMs

author.name: Juwan Chung, Sungjune Park, Yeongyun Kim, Yong Man Ro

entry.summary: This paper reformulates object localization in remote sensing multimodal LLMs as a region-selection problem rather than generating bounding-box coordinates as token sequences, extending the approach to temporal change localization across multi-image satellite sequences. A text-conditioned region proposal module addresses the fragility of coordinate generation for small, densely packed objects common in aerial imagery.

entry.title: FineHOI: Part-Aware Dense Representations for Zero-Shot Human-Object Interaction Detection

author.name: Francesco Tonini, Lorenzo Vaquero, Mohammad Mahdi Derakhshani, Cees Snoek, Elisa Ricci, Cigdem Beyan

entry.summary: FineHOI tackles zero-shot human-object interaction detection by modeling interactions from dense patch-level features rather than global or detector-centric features that compress interaction cues. It leverages vision-language models with fine-grained spatial reasoning to generalize to unseen verb-object compositions. The work advances compositional generalization in human-centric scene understanding.

entry.title: Branch-Centric Tokenization and Test-Time Augmentation for Skeleton Generation

author.name: Zhengyuan Li, Chuanyu Pan, Yuanming Hu, Raymond Yeh

entry.summary: The paper improves autoregressive skeleton generation with branch-centric tokenization, which encodes structural connectivity directly in compact sequences, and view-augmented generation, a test-time augmentation that rotates input meshes and merges predictions. These choices are studied within a unified framework. The work addresses underexplored representation and inference-time compute questions for structured generation.

entry.title: NOVA: Normal-Side Modeling for Training-Free Zero-Shot Video Anomaly Detection

author.name: Wei-Chih Yin, Yun-Ching Kao, Cheng-Kuan Lin, Yu-Chee Tseng

entry.summary: Proposes NOVA, a training-free zero-shot video anomaly detection framework that strengthens the normality side of CLIP-based prompting, addressing blurred decision boundaries from ambiguous normal verbs and modality gaps between textual anchors and visual frames. It requires no video-specific training.

entry.title: FreqDoor: A Hidden Trojan in the Frequency Domain for Backdoor Attacks on Vision-Language Models

author.name: Yasir Arafat Prodhan, Sadad Hasan, Mohammed Imamul Hassan Bhuiyan

entry.summary: FreqDoor is a training-time backdoor attack on vision-language models that implants triggers in the frequency domain by selectively mixing amplitude-spectrum components from a trigger-source image while preserving the phase of the clean image, without touching the textual input. This yields spatially distributed, visually imperceptible triggers that evade detection methods targeting spatial, textual, or bimodal patterns. The work exposes a new attack surface for multimodal model security.

entry.title: Single Image to Textured 3D Object Generation in Frequency Domain: From Theory to Pipeline

author.name: Qisen Wang, Yifan Zhao, Jia Li

entry.summary: This paper analyzes single-view image-to-3D generation through a frequency-domain lens, observing that 2D diffusion priors provide high-frequency detail while 3D priors offer consistency but lack detail, and that naive spatial-domain fusion introduces erroneous guidance. Building on this theory, the authors propose a pipeline that combines the two prior types in the frequency domain to produce textured 3D objects with fewer color deviations and better view consistency.

entry.title: From Explicit References to Scene Manifolds: Distributional Fidelity and Realism for Radiance Field Quality Assessment

author.name: Saeed Mahmoudpour, Gi-Mun Um, Hyon-Gon Choo, Peter Schelkens

entry.summary: This paper addresses perceptual quality assessment for radiance field representations like 3D Gaussian Splatting, where existing full-reference and cross-reference metrics struggle under wide-baseline settings with arbitrary viewing trajectories. The authors propose moving from explicit reference comparison to modeling distributional fidelity over scene manifolds, enabling more reliable evaluation of rendered views. This matters for maturing novel view synthesis pipelines where artifacts from reconstruction, rendering, and compression must be measured robustly.

entry.title: SphereSOD: Geometry-Structure Coupled Learning for 360 Salient Object Detection

author.name: Junsong Zhang, Zhijie Shen, Shuai Zheng, Feng Li, Runmin Cong, Yao Zhao, Chunyu Lin

entry.summary: SphereSOD is an ERP-native framework for 360-degree salient object detection that couples panoramic geometry with evolving salient structure, letting spherical geometry govern feature sampling while coarse saliency and contour predictions refine context aggregation. It advances beyond prior distortion-compensation approaches by modeling the interaction between projection geometry and object structure.

entry.title: CrowdTraj: A Benchmark for Dense Crowd Trajectory Prediction in Realistic Crowded Environments

author.name: Antonius Bima Murti Wijaya, Paul Henderson, Marwa Mahmoud

entry.summary: CrowdTraj is a benchmark for pedestrian trajectory prediction in dense natural crowd scenes from CCTV viewpoints, supporting end-to-end evaluation from detection through tracking to prediction under severe occlusion, unlike prior datasets that assume perfect tracking inputs or overhead views. It captures natural behaviors like abrupt directional changes that are rare in existing benchmarks.

entry.title: DriveMotion: A Large-Scale Multi-Source Benchmark for Driver Motion Sequence Modeling and Forecasting

author.name: Yuhang Wang, Chuheng Wei, Jingxin Yang, Xishun Liao, Hao Zhou

entry.summary: DriveMotion is a large benchmark for continuous driver motion forecasting containing 393 hours of 133-keypoint motion sequences at 10 Hz from 360 drivers, integrating naturalistic driving data, public in-cabin videos, and the AIDE dataset into a unified representation with validity masks and synchronized driving context. It shifts driver-centric research from short-clip behavior classification toward motion sequence forecasting.

entry.title: Boundary Voting Network for Ambiguity-Aware Timestamp-Supervised Action Segmentation

author.name: Runzhong Zhang, Yueqi Duan, Yang Chen, Weipeng Hu, Chen Cai, Suchen Wang, Yap-Peng Tan

entry.summary: This paper proposes a boundary voting network for timestamp-supervised action segmentation, addressing the intrinsic uncertainty of localizing action boundaries when only a single annotated frame per action is available. The method explicitly models ambiguity in action-transiting regions to produce more stable framewise pseudo-labels for fully-supervised-style training. This matters because pseudo-label quality is the main bottleneck in weakly supervised video action segmentation.

entry.title: SAM3-O2D2: Zero-Shot Object Out-of-Distribution Detection by Object Class Prompting of the SAM3-Image Model

author.name: Lucas G\"ornhardt, Timo Bartels, Tim Fingscheidt

entry.summary: This paper proposes SAM3-O2D2, a zero-shot out-of-distribution object detection method that prompts the SAM3 image model with object classes instead of relying on post-hoc feature-space scoring with models like CLIP. By performing OOD assessment via class prompting, the approach avoids sensitivity to detector localization errors and appearance variation, targeting safety-critical overconfidence in deployed detectors. This addresses a real safety gap for autonomous driving, medical imaging, and surveillance systems.

entry.title: MARS-CLIP: Multi-Resolution and Attention Refined Zero-Shot Image Segmentation

author.name: Nagito Saito, Shintaro Ito, Koichi Ito, Takafumi Aoki

entry.summary: MARS-CLIP adapts CLIP for zero-shot semantic segmentation, tackling CLIP's weak dense-prediction performance caused by low spatial resolution and lost structural information. It combines a multi-resolution feature module fusing local fine-grained features with global context, and an attention refinement mechanism injecting spatial and color biases from intermediate layers. The work is significant because it extends contrastive vision-language models to dense prediction without task-specific training data.

entry.title: GALoc: Gravity Aligned Wireframes for Depth-Free Monocular Floorplan Localization

author.name: Jeahn Han, Minji Kim, Jeongbin Sohn, Jonghyeok Park, Matthias Wuest, Pyojin Kim

entry.summary: GALoc replaces brittle depth prediction in indoor floorplan localization with geometry-first gravity-aligned wireframes that satisfy verticality and coplanarity by construction, solved via a linear constraint matrix and global search. It projects rectified wireframes to bird's-eye-view layouts and matches them to floorplans using metric-free SE(2) alignment. This removes dependence on unreliable depth networks in cluttered indoor scenes.

entry.title: CVT-GS: Learning to Simplify 3D Gaussian Splatting with Centroidal Voronoi Tessellation

author.name: Bingxian Li, Yilong Li, Jingliang Peng, Peng-Shuai Wang, Fei Zhu, Guozheng Li, Chi Harold Liu, Guoping Wang, Bo Pang

entry.summary: CVT-GS is an optimization-free, post-hoc compression framework for trained 3D Gaussian Splatting scenes, using Centroidal Voronoi Tessellation to simplify large Gaussian sets without retraining or architectural changes. This enables deployment of pretrained 3DGS models with reduced storage and compute while preserving visual fidelity.

entry.title: Medical AI Encodes a "Feeling of Error": Verifying Cancer Segmentation via Internal Concepts

author.name: Mengmeng Ma, Yunxiang Peng, Tang Li, Lu Lin, Binsheng Zhao, Oguz Akin, Xi Peng

entry.summary: This arXiv paper investigates whether cancer segmentation models possess an internal signal analogous to the human Feeling of Error (FOE) that can predict their own failures. Unlike output-level confidence or uncertainty measures, the proposed approach extracts internal concept-based signals, aiming to avoid the sensitivity-quality tradeoff where aggressive failure detection degrades overall segmentation quality. This matters for medical AI safety, where silent failures can lead to missed cancer findings or unnecessary biopsies.

entry.title: FRAME: Factored Retrieval via Attribute Readouts for Object-Centric Scene Memory

author.name: Woosang Jeon, Sanghyeok Choi, Minwoo Kim, Taehyun Jung, Taehyeong Kim

entry.summary: This paper addresses language-guided robot memory retrieval, formalizing attribute-compositional retrieval where a fixed object-centric scene memory is queried in natural language to find objects matching persistent attributes like category, material, size, or surface appearance. It introduces FRAME (Factored Retrieval via Attribute Readouts) and a controlled evaluation protocol with fixed scene memories and attribute-defined targets to isolate retrieval ability from other factors.
