entry.summary: Proposes CI... a Constraint Intent Tree representation for LLM-based CAD code generation that makes design intent explicit, enabling verification of construction processes (part decomposition, Boolean operations, sketch structure) rather than only final geometry via IoU. This addresses a real gap where geometric match metrics miss structural errors in generated parametric programs.

entry.title: Understanding the Impact of Model Pruning on Long-Tail Forgetting and Explanation Reliability in Medical Imaging

author.name: Nazish Khalid, Tausifa Jan Saleem, Amal Saqib, Donald C. Wunsch II, Mohammad Yaqub

entry.summary: A systematic study of how pruning affects long-tail forgetting and explanation reliability in medical imaging, spanning two datasets, two CNN architectures, four pruning methods, and sparsity up to 95 percent. It evaluates rare-condition performance and explanation stability, both clinically critical but usually ignored in compression work.

entry.title: Support Topology and Gradient Mixing in Sinkhorn Layers

author.name: Dylan Forde

entry.summary: Develops a theoretical calculus for how the fixed support graph in sparse Sinkhorn (optimal transport) layers controls gradient propagation through the scaling iterations. The paper derives operators for reverse-mode cotangent propagation, uses Dobrushin contraction to bound tail gradients, and characterizes when the support graph causes gradient mixing. Relevant for training sparsified attention or transport-based layers in transformer-style models.

entry.title: A Better Spur Should Start From Each Objective

author.name: Shanwen Mao, Hao Zhang, Guangtao nie, Zhiheng Li, Huimu Wang, Sulong Xu, Gu Simiu

entry.summary: Introduces Multi-Marginal Preference Optimization (MMPO), a multi-objective RL framework that intervenes at the data, gradient, and constraint levels to handle sparse rewards, reward conflicts, and late-stage metric oscillation that plague linear scalarization. Techniques include exposure debiasing, priority-aware orthogonal gradient projection, and self-prompted gradient constraints, apparently targeting industrial recommendation/ranking settings.

entry.title: MemForest: Efficient Agent Memory Management via EventTree Partitioning and Progressive Merging

author.name: Junxi Wang, Te Sun, Jiayi Zhu, Chen Zhang, Siyuan Li, Xuyang Liu, Zichen Wen, Xiaobing Tu, Jinkui Ren, Xiantao Zhang, Ziqi Yuan, Linfeng Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes MemForest, a general memory compression framework for agent memory systems that partitions history into event-centric units using semantic similarity and temporal continuity, builds maximum spanning trees (EventTrees) per unit, and progressively merges redundant nodes to reduce storage and retrieval cost. It is designed to be adaptable across existing agent memory systems.

entry.title: Answer-Distribution Trajectories: A Stochastic-Dynamics View of LLM Reasoning

author.name: Mar Gonz\`alez I Catal\`a, Haitz S\'aez de Oc\'ariz Borde, Davide Murari, Carola-Bibiane Sch\"onlieb, Pietro Li\`o, George Monta\~nez

entry.summary: This paper introduces answer-distribution trajectories, a representation that tracks the model's full predictive distribution over candidate answers as chain-of-thought reasoning unfolds, going beyond endpoint accuracy and entropy profiles by revealing which competing hypotheses account for uncertainty over time. This finer-grained view enables characterizing reasoning traces through a stochastic-dynamics lens. It matters for reasoning interpretability and for diagnostics that go beyond right-or-wrong answer evaluation.

entry.title: MeClear: Cooperative Game-Theoretic Attribution and Risk-Aware Memory Clearance for Long-Horizon LLM Agents

author.name: Boyu Yang, Jiazheng Sun, Zilong Lu, Zhi Qiu, Xin Peng, Jun Zheng

entry.summary: MeClear is a task-conditioned framework for clearing harmful memories from long-horizon LLM agents, using Leave-One-Out screening combined with sampled cooperative Shapley attribution to identify evidence with negative downstream utility. It selectively suppresses outdated, misleading, or conflicting memories from agent context. The approach addresses the problem that semantic retrieval optimizes compatibility rather than utility.

entry.title: TamilEOT: A Dataset and Model for Semantic End-of-Turn Detection in Tamil Telephone Speech

author.name: Santhoshkumar V

entry.summary: The authors release TamilEOT, a dataset of 18,485 labeled turn boundaries from 116 real Tamil telephone conversations, plus two compact audio-only end-of-turn detectors fine-tuned from Smart Turn v3. Accuracy improves from 70.3 percent zero-shot to 86.1 percent, with both models running under 150 ms on a laptop CPU. This fills a notable gap in conversational voice-agent research for South Indian languages.

entry.title: Versioned Transitive Dependency-Closure Binding and Operation-Time Effect Governance for Agent Skills: ClosureBound

author.name: Genliang Zhu (Accentrust, Georgia Institute of Technology), Chu Wang (Accentrust, University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign)

entry.summary: ClosureBound is a reference monitor for agent skills that prevents authorization transfer across material changes to a skill's heterogeneous dependency closure (files, packages, tools, models, services). It commits typed graph nodes and topology, binds grants to exact closure roots with effect ceilings and provenance, and re-resolves the closure at operation time, admitting external effects only when a joint witness satisfies every bound.

entry.title: What Does Animal Re-Identification Learn? Linear Biological Concepts and Their Origins in Visual Representations

author.name: Robert Nolting, Alexandra Schild, Moritz Weckbecker, Maximilian Schall, Gerard de Melo

entry.summary: Investigates whether ViT-based animal re-identification models organize representations along biologically meaningful axes, finding that sex and age emerge as linear directions in a DINOv3 backbone fine-tuned for gorilla Re-ID, with strong generalization to held-out individuals. This has implications for understanding and auditing conservation models.

entry.title: Linear Algebra Foundations of Efficient Attention: A Phase Reversal in Rank Collapse Under SVD Compression

author.name: Anjaneya Teja Sarma Kalvakolanu

entry.summary: This paper unifies fourteen peer-reviewed works on the linear-algebraic properties of transformer attention, covering rank collapse of attention outputs, SVD-based compression exploiting that phenomenon, and the duality between low-rank KV cache projection, linear attention, and state-space models. A synthesis of this kind is valuable for researchers navigating the fast-growing efficient-attention literature. The claim of identifying a phase reversal in rank collapse under compression adds an original analytical thread.

entry.title: Parameterized and Streaming Algorithms for Euclidean Fair $k$-Center Clustering

author.name: Zeyu Lin, Chaoqi Jia, Longkun Guo, Chao Chen

entry.summary: This theoretical work develops a parameterized 2.732-approximation algorithm for fair k-center clustering in Euclidean spaces, where centers are constrained across demographic groups, and integrates it into a one-pass streaming algorithm. It advances the algorithmic foundations of fairness-aware clustering.

entry.title: Reading Decoder Trajectories: Training-Free Counterfactual Query-Trajectory Reliability for Small-Object Detection

author.name: Zhaoning Shi, Bo Ma

entry.summary: Proposes CQTR, a training-free framework for small-object detection that hypothesizes small-object knowledge already exists in frozen detectors and elicits it via counterfactual scale interventions while interpreting query trajectories for candidate reliability. This challenges the dominant assumption that frozen models require architecture changes or finetuning to handle small objects.

entry.title: Characterizing Contention-Induced Reliability Collapse in KV-Cache Timing Side Channels for Multi-Tenant LLM Serving

author.name: Rana Abu Bakar

entry.summary: This work empirically studies how reliable KV-cache timing side-channel attacks remain under realistic multi-tenant contention in shared LLM serving systems. Through seven experiments on live vLLM deployments, it shows that attack effect sizes (Cohen's d) collapse sharply with even a small number of concurrent workers, tempering prior feasibility claims. The findings are important for realistic threat modeling of LLM infrastructure security.

entry.title: Train Overcomplete, Deploy Compact: Scaling Recovery Capacity for Structured LLM Pruning

author.name: Seungmin Oh, Donggeon Lee, Jongbin Ryu

entry.summary: Identifies a capacity-knowledge asymmetry bottleneck in structured LLM pruning recovery and proposes OverRep, which temporarily overparameterizes the recovery module during training to absorb distilled knowledge, then collapses it for a compact deployment artifact. This follows a train-overcomplete, deploy-compact principle.

entry.title: ARNAI: Artifact Removal Network based on Autoencoding and Inpainting for Robust Spinal Image Segmentation and Measurement

author.name: Sang-Jin Park, Jinyoung Choi, Seokwon Kim, Seungeon Song, Insu Park, Dougho Park, Taeyeon Kim, Youjin Lee, Donghoon Yang, Jaeman Cho, Joongwon Yang, Mansu Kim, Heumdai Kwon, Hong Gyu Baek, Dae Chul Cho, Injung Kim

entry.summary: ARNAI presents a Restore-Segment-Measure framework that removes spinal implant artifacts from postoperative radiographs via an autoencoding-and-inpainting network, enabling automated spinopelvic parameter measurement. Validated retrospectively on radiographs from two institutions spanning 2017-2025, it addresses a real clinical gap since postoperative images are usually excluded from automated analysis. This could extend AI-assisted spinal assessment to surgical follow-up care.

entry.title: Tensor network representations of discrete maximum entropy distributions via mean polytopes

author.name: Alex Goessmann, Martin Eigel

entry.summary: The paper introduces Computation-Activation Networks, a tensor network architecture subsuming exponential families, and proves that any discrete maximum entropy distribution under expectation constraints admits a representation in this architecture by exploiting the geometry of the mean polytope. It connects polytope faces to support boundaries of exponential families and proposes tensor ranks as complexity measures. This is a substantive theoretical bridge between information geometry and tensor networks.

entry.title: Mathematical Programming in Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence: A Unified Taxonomy of Models and Applications

author.name: Chaosheng Dong

entry.summary: A survey that unifies fragmented applications of mathematical programming across ML and AI - retrieval selection, token routing, inference compute allocation, structured prediction, robustness - under common optimization paradigms (linear, mixed-integer, conic, bilevel, submodular, min-max, etc.). It serves as a reference taxonomy connecting optimization, IR, NLP, and vision literatures.

entry.title: D3ARC: Time-Critical Distributed Disaster Detection for Asynchronous Cooperative Multi-Robot Systems

author.name: Nikolaos Koursioumpas, Lina Magoula, Nancy Alonistioti, Ramin Khalili

entry.summary: This paper proposes D3ARC, an asynchronous distributed hierarchical framework in which multiple robotic agents cooperate to detect wildfires under uncertainty. A remote controller asynchronously directs robot motion while each agent senses the environment and coordinates detection actions, addressing coverage, cost, and personnel-risk limitations of traditional disaster monitoring.

entry.title: Topology Obstructs Pure Foundation Neural Quantum States

author.name: Timothy Heightman, Elena Orlova, Philip Mantrov, Aleksei Ustimenko

entry.summary: The paper proves a fundamental limitation for pure-state foundation models of quantum ground states: for any gapped Hamiltonian family with a non-trivial ground-state bundle, every continuous normalized state-vector model has zero fidelity with the true ground state at some parameter value, incurring an O(gap) energy error. This is a topological no-go result for a growing class of neural-network approaches to quantum many-body problems.

entry.title: Your Agent Says Yes: Interpreting Adversarial Market Behavior Beyond Individual Transactions

author.name: Zelin Li, Yiyun Su, Matt White, Zhipeng Wang, Xiao-Yang Liu, Tianyu Shi

entry.summary: The study populates a virtual exchange with ten role-conditioned language-model agents that communicate, trade, launch tokens, and manage liquidity pools under adversarial roles, then analyzes eight 72-cycle trajectories to interpret market-level behavior beyond individual transaction controls. A focal reconstruction shows a launch-promotion-exit scenario, illustrating how per-transaction compliance misses distributed manipulative behavior.

entry.title: Climate-ModernBERT: Revisiting Corpus Composition for Domain-Adaptive Continued Pretraining

author.name: Yongan Yu, Shantam Raj, Jingwei Ni, Ario Saeid Vaghefi, Dominik Stammbach, Markus Leippold

entry.summary: Presents a family of climate-adapted encoder models via continued pretraining of ModernBERT-Base on academic, web-filtered, and synthetic climate corpora, systematically comparing corpus mixtures against parameter-space merging of specialized checkpoints. Best models improve across nine climate NLP benchmarks.

entry.title: DISEIL: Demonstration Distillation for Sample-Efficient Imitation Learning

author.name: Suyog Khanal, Arun Kumar A V, Santu Rana

entry.summary: Proposes DISEIL for interactive imitation learning, making two previously incidental decisions deliberate: which failure to correct and where a requested demonstration should start, by detecting the step where the policy first becomes unreliable. Aims to reduce the number of expert queries a robot needs to learn new tasks.

entry.title: A Measurement Study of LLM Inference Trade-offs Across Edge Continuum Hardware

author.name: Maysam Khatib, Moysis Symeonides, Demetris Trihinas, George Pallis, Marios D. Dikaiakos

entry.summary: This measurement study benchmarks self-hosted LLM inference on edge hardware (Jetson AGX Orin, CPU-only and GPU near-edge server) versus GPT-4o as a cloud reference, across multiple open-weight models and quantization variants on a fixed QA workload. It reports accuracy, footprint, per-token latency, prefill latency, and energy. The results guide deployment choices for LLM-backed services at the edge.

entry.title: Adaptive Anisotropic Attention for Axis-Structured Signals

author.name: Mahir Jain, Parshva Runwal, Aditya Ray Mishra, Arvasu Kulkarni, Sandeep Singh, Siddharth Panwar

entry.summary: The paper proposes Adaptive Anisotropic Attention (AAA), an attention variant that replaces the uniform isotropic prior of dense self-attention with two structured paths for axis-organized signals: a temporal path attending within an electrode across time and a spatial path attending across electrodes at the same time step, combined via a learned per-token gate. It targets low-SNR structured data such as EEG, where standard attention wastes capacity on irrelevant token interactions. The contribution is an architecture-level efficiency and inductive-bias improvement for structured signals rather than language models.

entry.title: ThinkPrior: Zero-Rollout Difficulty Priors for Cold-Start Prompt Selection in RLVR

author.name: Tommy Sha, Skylar Zhai, Siqi Zhao

entry.summary: Targets wasted rollouts in RLVR training with GRPO, where uniform prompt sampling spends about 39% of rollouts on zero-advantage groups that provide no gradient. ThinkPrior builds a zero-rollout difficulty prior from an external verifier-scored anchor in one offline pass, eliminating the cold-start cost of history-based prompt selection. A focused efficiency improvement for reasoning-model RL training.

entry.title: A Multi-Source Ensemble Approach to Candidate Generation for Alternative Vacation Rental Property Recommendations

author.name: Syed Mohammed Arshad Zaidi, Eric Rincon, Shayan Hassantabar

entry.summary: This paper studies candidate generation for alternative vacation rental recommendations at scale, comparing collaborative filtering, shallow embeddings, and graph neural networks on a platform with over 2M active properties. It shows a hybrid of item-based CF with GNN retrieval performs best under challenges like heterogeneous inventory and rapid availability changes. It matters as a practical, large-scale recommender systems case study from industry researchers.

entry.title: CALM: Class-wise Agreement and Label-gated Disagreement Modulation for Decentralized Federated Learning

author.name: Yifan Ying, Qing Tian

entry.summary: CALM improves decentralized federated distillation under severe non-IID data by replacing hard all-or-nothing trust decisions about teacher predictions with soft, class-wise agreement modulation and label-gated disagreement handling. This avoids discarding outlier teachers wholesale and better weights aggregated teacher targets. It is relevant to serverless, privacy-conscious distributed learning without shared architectures.

entry.title: Interpretable and Fair Generalized Additive Neural Networks via Multi-objective Learning

author.name: Ziming Wang, Changwu Huang, Ke Tang, Yew-Soon Ong, Xin Yao

entry.summary: The paper introduces explicit quantitative metrics for interpretability of neural-network-based generalized additive models (GAMs) and jointly optimizes interpretability alongside fairness and accuracy via multi-objective learning. This addresses an underexplored gap, as most NN-GAM research has focused on accuracy. The work contributes to trustworthy AI by making interpretability measurable and optimizable.

entry.title: Learning to Price and Stock Under Contextual and Censored Demand

author.name: Zean Han, Zezhen Ding, Jiheng Zhang

entry.summary: This paper tackles joint pricing and inventory control when demand depends on contextual factors and is censored by lost sales, meaning true demand is unobserved when stock runs out. The authors model demand as a linear combination of basis functions and propose an algorithm with sublinear regret bounds for adaptive decisions. It matters for retail operations research where lost-sales censoring has historically forced practitioners to choose between contextual awareness and demand observability.

entry.title: Spectral Prioritized Sweeping in Nonstationary Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Hung Pham, Tuan Dam

entry.summary: The paper improves Prioritized Sweeping for nonstationary reward settings by augmenting Bellman-residual priorities with graph-topology information via the graph resolvent, so that updates propagate to topologically distant or bottlenecked states even under limited replanning budgets. GTA-PS/SPS is presented as a drop-in enhancement to model-based RL planning. It addresses a real shortsightedness of canonical priority scores after localized reward shifts.

entry.title: Structural Entropy-Driven Graph Diffusion Generation for One-Shot Federated Graph Learning

author.name: Shutong Zheng, Lele Fu, Sheng Huang, Wei Yang Bryan Lim, Chuan Chen

entry.summary: SPIRE introduces topology-aware client weighting into one-shot federated graph learning using first-order degree-distribution structural entropy, capturing how client connectivity is organized beyond raw data volume, combined with a server-side graph diffusion model for generation. It addresses the problem of estimating client contributions from highly compressed information in a single round. Note it shares first author and topic with SPEAR (item 7), indicating a research line on one-shot FGL.

entry.title: Train Smarter, Not Harder: Switching Signal-Guided Training in Active Learning

author.name: Nagham Omar, Maya Rozenshtein, Evgeny Mishlyakov, Avigdor Gal

entry.summary: Shows that the choice between retraining from scratch and fine-tuning in active learning has exploitable structure and proposes HybridAL, which monitors an online stabilization signal (spectral exponent or accuracy change) to switch from retraining to fine-tuning. Reduces training cost without sacrificing accuracy.

entry.title: Conditioned Initialization for Attention

author.name: Hemanth Saratchandran, Simon Lucey

entry.summary: Examines an underexplored factor in transformer training: initialization of the query, key, and value matrices. The authors show that naive random initialization can introduce optimization pathologies and propose a conditioned initialization scheme that improves training dynamics relative to random and mimetic initialization.

entry.title: Inferring Urban Mobility Interactions from Aggregated Dynamics

author.name: Yi Wang, Jing Li, Jinliang Deng, Zhenghong Wang, Yizhi Zhang, Fan Zhang, Ivor W. Tsang, Yu Liu

entry.summary: Shows that origin-destination flow matrices, normally requiring privacy-invasive individual tracking, can be reconstructed from aggregated area-level counts using an uncertainty-aware physics-informed framework. Validated across twelve mobility datasets from US and Chinese cities with accuracy comparable to trajectory-based models.

entry.title: MetaKV: Adaptive KV Cache Compression for Constrained LLM Inference

author.name: Michael Wang, Keith Li, Roozbeh Bostandoost

entry.summary: MetaKV adaptively selects a KV cache compression configuration per prompt under user-specified latency and memory budgets, using lightweight predictors of end-to-end latency, peak memory, and correctness probability. It addresses the fact that no single compression setting works across prompts and constraints. Directly relevant to efficient long-context LLM serving.

entry.title: SIM: Subspace Interaction-based Method for Token-Level Text Anomaly Detection

author.name: Kehan Yan, Yue Tan, Qingfeng Chen, Shiyuan Li, Yu Zheng, Yixin Liu

entry.summary: Presents SIM, a method for token-level text anomaly detection that uses subspace interaction instead of global distance calculations, avoiding dilution of local anomaly signals by redundant normal feature dimensions. It also addresses the smoothing of surface anomalies caused by pre-trained language model representations. Applications include spam filtering and fake news detection.

entry.title: Chimaera: A Mixture-of-Graph-Experts Architecture for Cross-Task and Cross-Dataset Graph Learning

author.name: Jonathan Frank, David Richerby, Ansgar Scherp

entry.summary: Combines mixture-of-experts with graph foundation models, integrating heterogeneous GFM architectures such as graph prompts and linear GNNs with LLM-generated embeddings. It extends linear GNNs to link- and graph-level tasks and evaluates cross-task, cross-dataset transfer on six text-attributed graph benchmarks.

entry.title: Do Reasoning Representations Help Humans Evaluate LLM Outputs?

author.name: Jaewoo Lim, Sungbok Shin, Sanghyun Hong

entry.summary: Runs a controlled human study of six reasoning explanation formats to test whether reasoning representations actually help people evaluate LLM outputs, measuring structural understanding, error detection, and trust calibration. Results indicate mixed effects, challenging model-centric evaluation of reasoning explanations.

entry.title: Asymptotically-informed neural networks for Black-Scholes implied volatility computation

author.name: Samira Amiriyan, Youness Boutaib

entry.summary: Proposes a family of neural network architectures that encode the asymptotic behavior of the Black-Scholes pricing function to improve implied volatility computation in extreme regimes where inversion is ill-conditioned. This matters for option calibration and risk management in quantitative finance.

entry.title: FALCON-S: Fixed-wing ground-effect Aerodynamics Simulator and Flight Control Learning Suite

author.name: Matteo El Hariry, Pedro Lima, Andrej Orsula, Matthieu Geist, Miguel Olivares-Mendez

entry.summary: FALCON-S is a modular high-fidelity simulator for fixed-wing aerial robots flying near the ground, modeling full 6DoF rigid-body dynamics, semi-empirical ground-effect aerodynamics, actuator dynamics, sensor noise, and disturbances. It supports CPU and GPU backends (Torch, NVIDIA Warp) for high-throughput parallel reinforcement learning training. It fills a real gap since most flight simulators assume hover-oriented or simplified dynamics unsuitable for low-altitude fixed-wing control research.

entry.title: Recovering linear images of sparse signals from indirect observations

author.name: Anatoli Juditsky, Arkadi Nemirovski

entry.summary: This paper develops l1-minimization-based techniques for recovering a linear image of an unknown sparse signal from noisy indirect observations, assuming the signal lies in a convex compact set. The key contribution is that no hard-to-verify assumptions on the sensing matrix (such as restricted isometry or nullspace conditions) are required, unlike classical compressed sensing theory. The tradeoff is that estimator parameters and risk bounds lack closed analytic forms.

entry.title: Large-Scale Pretraining for Improving Deep Learning-Based Geometric Distortion Correction of Diffusion-Weighted Imaging

author.name: Saroj Khanal, Yashawant Kumar Yadav, Kritam Bhattarai, Jeevan Neupane, Shristi Subedi, Saship Gwachha, Manish Kumar Tiwari, Dong Zhang, Confidence Raymond, Aondona Moses Iorumbur, Udunna Anazodo, Surendra Maharjan, Bishesh Khanal, Mahesh Shakya, Pralhad Kumar Shrestha

entry.summary: This study tests whether large-scale pretraining improves deep learning-based correction of geometric distortion in single-phase-encoding diffusion-weighted MRI, framing the task as image reconstruction. The authors compare non-pretrained, self-supervised, and generative pretrained models using quantitative metrics plus expert qualitative assessment, and further test transferability across sites. The work targets resource-constrained clinical settings where vendor-specific correction is infeasible.

entry.title: Stochastic Nonconvex Bilevel Optimization: Improved Rates Without Rare-Visit Assumption

author.name: Daniel Cortild, Mathias Staudigl, Juan Peypouquet, Coralia Cartis

entry.summary: This theory paper improves convergence guarantees for stochastic nonconvex bilevel optimization by showing that a denominator-only regularization of the dynamic barrier gradient descent (DBGD) multiplier removes the unrealistic rare-visit assumption while keeping fast rates: O(eps^-2) iterations for (eps, eps)-stationarity with improved gradient oracle costs. The author group includes established optimization researchers (Cartis, Peypouquet, Staudigl).

entry.title: BinauralVAE: Spatial Audio Reconstruction For World Models

author.name: Luis Vitor Zerkowski, Luiz Velho

entry.summary: Introduces BinauralVAE, an open-source pipeline for reconstructing spatial (binaural) audio, motivated by the observation that vision-centric world models fail under occlusion, low light, or sensor blackout where acoustics remain informative. It targets the underexplored area of audio-centric world models for embodied AI.

entry.title: Heat Kernel Textures: the Geodesic Gaussians That Do Not Splat

author.name: Simone Foti, Caner Korkmaz, Stefanos Zafeiriou, Tolga Birdal

entry.summary: Introduces HKTex, a texture representation built on anisotropic heat kernels intrinsically defined on manifold surfaces, eliminating UV unwrapping and its associated seams, distortion, and memory overhead. It adapts ideas from 3D Gaussian splatting to texture representation with adaptive densification.

entry.title: Cross-modal learning for SAR target recognition using optical vision foundation models

author.name: Lucas Hirsch, James R. Hopgood, Javid Khan, Yoann Altmann, Mike E. Davies

entry.summary: Proposes a cross-modal framework where a frozen electro-optical vision foundation model supplies class-level supervision to SAR target recognition via prototype alignment, addressing limited labels, speckle, and the SAR-optical domain gap. It matters because it transfers the power of abundant optical data to a modality where labelled data is scarce.

entry.title: A Gradient-based yet Spike-Timing-Dependent Solution to the Feedback Learning Problem in Neural Microcircuits

author.name: Xiangnan Zhang, Jingxin Liu, Ranqi Lu, Jingyu Liu, Qunxi Dong, Fuze Tian, Lixian Zhu, Bin Hu, Bj\"orn W. Schuller

entry.summary: Reformulates temporal credit assignment in spiking neural microcircuits as a state-separation problem, deriving an online feedback learning framework via a gradient tunneling algorithm that uses local spike timing rather than surrogate backpropagation. This bridges gradient-based learning and biologically plausible spike-timing-dependent plasticity.

entry.title: Temporal State Transport in Video Generation: Diagnosing and Correcting Spectral Imbalance

author.name: Luyao Tang, Bingjun Luo, Dong Yi, Jialin Guo, Haoning Xi, Cheng Chen, Yizhou Yu, Chaoqi Chen

entry.summary: The paper frames video generation quality through Temporal State Transport — persisting identity, layout, motion, and detail across time — and introduces Spectral Tension, a signed diagnostic comparing local attention diffuseness with global spectral diversity. This diagnostic identifies two opposite failure modes (fragmented transport and over-mixing) and enables training-free corrections.

entry.title: Charts Are Beyond Pixels: Probing for Layer-Wise Chart Understanding and Editing

author.name: Xiaochuan Zhong, Yifan Hou, Chenxi Pang, Shaobo Cui

entry.summary: LayerWiseBench is a new benchmark evaluating whether vision-language models understand charts at the layer level, organized around layer attribution, layer binding, and visibility ordering, with paired rendered charts and per-layer RGBA assets generated from executable chart programs. It assesses both chart understanding and chart editing beyond final-output fidelity.

entry.title: High-Magnetization Sampling at Low Temperatures: Ising Models and Bayesian Sparse Linear Regression

author.name: Syamantak Kumar, Purnamrita Sarkar, Kevin Tian, Yusong Zhu

entry.summary: This theory paper develops frameworks for sampling from Hamming slices of high-dimensional binary spaces where the support size k is much smaller than the dimension d, a highly magnetized regime. The authors apply these frameworks to build polynomial-time samplers for fixed-magnetization Sherrington-Kirkpatrick models at any inverse temperature, and to improve samplers for Bayesian sparse linear regression. The work connects statistical physics, Monte Carlo sampling, and sparse Bayesian inference.

entry.title: Neuron-Guided Fine-Tuning: Unlocking Efficient Alignment Mechanisms for Large Language Models

author.name: Zeyu Wu, Junchao Wu, Shudong Liu, Runzhe Zhan, Xin Chen, Shu Yang, Yichao Du, Longyue Wang, Weihua Luo, Jinsong Su, Derek F. Wong

entry.summary: NGFT proposes using neuron activation patterns as a unified signal across the supervised fine-tuning lifecycle, combining task-specific neuron selection, activation-based data quality assessment, and knowledge preservation to reduce parameter redundancy, mitigate inconsistent data quality, and limit catastrophic forgetting. The framework unifies data selection, parameter updates, and knowledge retention that are typically handled in isolation. If effective, it would make alignment-oriented fine-tuning cheaper and more stable.

entry.title: Factors Influencing the Emergence of Dependency Length Minimization in Neural Agent Simulations

author.name: Yuqing Zhang, Tessa Verhoef, Gertjan van Noord, Arianna Bisazza

entry.summary: This paper uses neural agent simulations with a language learning and communication framework to investigate the factors behind dependency length minimization (DLM), the universal preference for word orders that shorten syntactic dependencies. By simulating more realistic interaction contexts than prior work, it identifies conditions under which DLM emerges, contributing to the debate on efficiency-driven origins of linguistic structure.

entry.title: Protocol Compression Changes Which Party Pays: Bilateral Cost in Cross-Organization LLM Agent Communication

author.name: Janghoon Lee (Redrob)

entry.summary: Examines token cost allocation in cross-organization LLM agent communication, showing that compressed agent-to-agent notation can raise total token spend by 8-11% over a JSON baseline once parsing failures force extra calls, and that unilateral payer analyses miss who actually bears costs. The authors run a preregistered token-level study across six vendors (198 content-matched pairs, 2,376 usage cells) with schema negotiation and English baselines to measure bilateral costs.

entry.title: Visual Search Augmented Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for Attribute Value Extraction from Product Videos

author.name: Tong Wu, Ming Cheng, Jiazhen Hu, Jiaying Gong, Hoda Eldardiry

entry.summary: Proposes ViS-CoT, a training-free, plug-and-play pipeline for extracting attribute values from product videos in e-commerce, using visual clustering to select representative frames and visual search to retrieve relevant evidence within a chain-of-thought process. It avoids costly fine-tuning of video vision-language models while injecting the domain knowledge they lack.

entry.title: A Grapheme-Aware Indic Tokenizer for Tamil: Large-Scale Training and Intrinsic Evaluation

author.name: Hari Krishnan K V, Sudarsun Santhiappan

entry.summary: The authors build a grapheme-aware tokenizer for Tamil that handles the language's multi-code-point writing system, where standard BPE, WordPiece, and SentencePiece segment text inefficiently. They train at scale and evaluate intrinsically on vocabulary efficiency and segmentation quality. Better tokenization can reduce sequence lengths and compute costs while improving downstream performance for Indic-language models.

entry.title: SIFTING: A Novel LLM-Based Framework for Structured and Transparent Information Extraction from Clinical Free-Text Reports, with Application to Tumor Staging in Lung Cancer

author.name: Mirco Hess, Gerben van Veenendaal, Joris Wakkie, Yiwen Soo, Malcolm H. Lawson, John D. Maclay, Arjun Nair, Neal Navani

entry.summary: Presents SIFTING, an LLM framework for extracting structured, traceable information from clinical free text by combining segment-level processing with strict output control that links findings back to source text. It is demonstrated on extracting tumor T-stage information from 130 lung cancer radiology reports. The transparency and traceability focus addresses a key barrier to clinical adoption of LLM extraction.

entry.title: DeepTable: Structural Attention Biases and Tree Path Encoding for Hierarchical Table Understanding

author.name: Jyun-Ying Yen, Cheng-Kuan Lin, Yu-Chee Tseng

entry.summary: DeepTable improves LLM table understanding by explicitly modeling hierarchical header structure via two parameter-efficient components: learnable Structural Attention Biases and tree-path encodings, rather than treating tables as flat token sequences. Experiments show gains over prior PEFT methods that only add basic row/column information.

entry.title: Vectorizer: Vectorizing NumPy Programs with Shape-Guided Rewrite

author.name: Jingqian Liu, Xiaoyu Liu, Yuepeng Wang

entry.summary: Presents a rewrite-based source-to-source transformation that converts explicit Python loops in NumPy programs into vectorized array operations, guided by array shapes and dataflow analysis working inside-out. This automates a task that is error-prone for programmers accustomed to imperative array traversal.

entry.title: Structural Jailbreaks Generalize but Do Not Compound: A cross-provider and multilingual study of Involuntary In-Context Learning

author.name: Tejasvi C. Addagada

entry.summary: Red-teams two Gemini models with the Involuntary In-Context Learning (IICL) structural jailbreak across English, Spanish, Hindi, and Arabic on general-harm and financial-abuse benchmarks, testing whether IICL and multilingual safety erosion compound. The finding is that IICL generalizes across languages but the two pressures do not stack.

entry.title: Combating Instruction Conflict via Energy-Driven Latent Conflict Detection

author.name: Mingyu Ma, Yuxin Wu, Jingbo Wang, Tianxiao Huang, Leixin Sun, Xiaochuan Shi

entry.summary: Introduces ELCD, a response-level detector for Response Drift — cases where a model's output violates system-level constraints despite seemingly compliant inputs — using a composite hidden-state representation and energy-based optimization for post-generation, pre-delivery verification. It targets hierarchical-instruction attacks that static input inspection misses.

entry.title: Improving Term Evaluation in Machine Translation: Variation Matters

author.name: Nicolas Dahan (MLIA, ISIR, ALMAnaCH), Ziqian Peng (MLIA), Fran\c{c}ois Yvon (MLIA), Rachel Bawden (ALMAnaCH)

entry.summary: This paper challenges the standard assumption in machine translation evaluation that each source term has a single correct target form, showing that human translators routinely produce legitimate variation. The authors combine glossary accuracy, consistency measures, and a novel cross-term variation (CTV) diagnostic to evaluate English-French scientific MT at document level, finding MT systems produce less target-side variation than humans. The work matters because it suggests current consistency metrics may unfairly penalize translations that resemble natural human practice.

entry.title: TAD: Token-Adaptive Contrastive Decoding with Confidence-Guided Gating for Hallucination Mitigation in Large Audio-Language Models

author.name: Heyu Chang, Nianwen Si, Hao Zhang, Wenlin Zhang, Dan Qu

entry.summary: TAD is a training-free decoding strategy that reduces audio hallucination in large audio-language models by contrasting logits under real audio with a matched silent reference, gated by a token-adaptive, confidence-guided mechanism at the decision-critical first step. On AudioCaps-Hallucination it outperforms fixed-weight contrastive baselines while avoiding overcorrection. It extends contrastive decoding ideas to the audio domain with a refined gating design.

entry.title: Video Compression with Graph-inspired Neural Representation

author.name: Changqi Wang, Ge Gao, Fan Zhang, Yue Li, Kai Zhang, Li Zhang, David Bull

entry.summary: G-NeRV is a graph-inspired implicit neural representation for video compression that explicitly exploits temporal redundancy by constructing a temporal neighborhood over frame embeddings and performing message passing, motivated by total correlation principles from information theory. This improves on standard INR codecs that handle temporal redundancy only implicitly.

entry.title: Map the Possibilities: Spatial Belief Fields for Language-Goal Aerial Navigation

author.name: Haotian Xu, Yue Hu, Zhengqiu Zhu, Yong Zhao, Wenguan Wang, Quanjun Yin

entry.summary: SBFNav is a closed-loop aerial navigation framework built on a language-conditioned Spatial Belief Field representing a task-conditioned probability distribution over plausible unobserved target locations, rather than collapsing language grounding to a single waypoint. This preserves spatial uncertainty under ambiguous relational instructions and partial observations in large continuous environments.

entry.title: TBDub: Production-Oriented Visual Dubbing

author.name: Bihan Li, Xinyang Li, Zeran Xu, Meiguang Jin, Junfeng Ma

entry.summary: TBDub extends the X-Dub mask-free video-editing baseline for visual dubbing to production domains like livestreams and generated video, using task-adaptive post-training of a video DiT plus few-step DMD-style distillation for efficient inference. It improves temporal stability, identity preservation, and runtime versus the baseline. This reflects the industrialization of generative video editing for real media pipelines.

entry.title: Radiation, Rotation and Scale Invariant Feature Descriptor for Multimodal Image Matching

author.name: Yuanxin Ye, Tengfeng Tang, Tao Peng, Zhiqiang Han, Jiayuan Li, Mi Wang

entry.summary: Proposes a radiation, rotation, and scale invariant (RRSI) feature descriptor for multimodal image matching, using dual-head regional sampling that combines Cartesian and Log-Polar sampling, plus joint geometric-radiometric encoding in a deep feature space. It targets geometric distortions and nonlinear radiometric differences that plague multi-source image fusion.

entry.title: Multi-History-Step SDE Inversion for Image Editing with Superior Regional Awareness

author.name: Haiyan Wei, Yunlong Wang, Huaibo Huang, Zhenan Sun, Kunbo Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes MIEdit, a training-free diffusion image editing framework based on SDE inversion with a predictor-corrector multi-history-step scheme, reducing steps while improving editing plasticity and preservation of unedited regions under large edits by mitigating conflicts among multi-conditioned noise residuals.

entry.title: Unified Vision-Centric Pedestrian Crossing Action Prediction via Adaptive Patch Projection and Proactive Spatial Rectification

author.name: Yao Tian, Le Yang, Binglu Wang

entry.summary: ViCross is a vision-centric framework for predicting pedestrian crossing actions from video using multimodal large language models, avoiding extra perception modules beyond first-frame target initialization. Adaptive patch projection and proactive spatial rectification help MLLMs maintain target-centric reasoning without frame-level external cues. This addresses reliability concerns about vision-only prediction in autonomous driving contexts.

entry.title: Topologically Consistent Agricultural Parcel Vectorization with Semantic-Guided Diffusion and Topology-Aware Polygonization

author.name: Weiqin Jiao, Xiaolong Zuo, Claudio Persello

entry.summary: This work proposes a method for producing agricultural parcel polygons from imagery that avoids topological conflicts and preserves shared boundaries between adjacent fields, combining semantic-guided diffusion with topology-aware polygonization. It tackles an unresolved gap: prior segmentation and vector-oriented methods produce masks or independent polygons without shared topological structure. Applications include precision agriculture, land administration, and crop monitoring.

entry.title: TV-SGS: Gaussian Splatting with Geometric Information Propagation via Tensor Voting under sparse views

author.name: Harish N Sathishchandra, Philippos Mordohai

entry.summary: TV-SGS enables direct communication among Gaussian splats via Tensor Voting during test-time optimization, introducing a new class of 3D losses that do not rely on rendering to improve scene geometry, particularly under sparse view conditions. This departs from the standard indirect pixel-based coupling in Gaussian Splatting optimization.

entry.title: A Black-Box Adversarial Attack on Human Pose Estimation and Keypoint-Based Action Recognition Models

author.name: Kacper Mroczek, Michal Kepski

entry.summary: This paper proposes OKS Attack, a decision-based black-box adversarial attack using Object Keypoint Similarity as the feedback signal to degrade human pose estimation, enabling temporally coherent attacks on keypoint-based action recognition pipelines. It fills a gap since prior black-box attack work targeted bounding-box IoU objectives unsuited to pose.

entry.title: Observe Before You Alert: Adaptive Driver Alerting with Vision-Language Models

author.name: Yuhang Wang, Lingyao Li, Hao Zhou

entry.summary: VLAlert casts dashcam driver alerting as a tri-action sequential decision policy over SILENT, OBSERVE, and ALERT, using Qwen3-VL-4B as a safety-evidence generator, where the OBSERVE action gathers additional evidence before committing to a warning. This addresses the ambiguity of thresholding binary risk scores in accident anticipation under partial observability.

entry.title: Supervised Cross-Modal Feature Alignment for Zero-Wearable Freezing of Gait Detection in Parkinsonism

author.name: Aryan Singh, Chandan Biswas

entry.summary: This paper proposes a supervised cross-modal subspace distillation framework for detecting freezing of gait in Parkinson's disease without wearables, using IMU kinematic data and clinical metadata as teachers during training to compensate for geometric self-occlusion in vision-based skeletal estimates during turning tasks. The result enables unobtrusive, continuous clinical monitoring. It matters because it bridges the accuracy of wearable sensors with the practicality of camera-based monitoring.

entry.title: ArmPoser: Real-Time, Calibration-Free Arm Pose Estimation from Smartwatch IMU

author.name: Bishnu Dev, Vasco Xu, Xi-Aan Loh, Chenfeng Gao, Henry Hoffmann, Karan Ahuja

entry.summary: ArmPoser estimates full arm pose in real time from a single smartwatch IMU without calibration poses, by training models directly on device-native sensor axes rather than standardized transformed inputs. This removes error-prone calibration and coordinate-transformation steps, enabling everyday deployment.

entry.title: Reliable iToF Depth Sensing via Sensor-Intrinsic Uncertainty Modeling and State-Space Restoration

author.name: Yansong Du, Yutong Deng, Yuting Zhou, Zhancong Xu, Yingjia Lu, Mengdi Wang, Feiyu Jiao, Bangyao Wang, Zhaoxiang Jiang, Xun Guan

entry.summary: This work proposes a joint depth-uncertainty modeling and restoration framework for indirect time-of-flight cameras, building a sensor-intrinsic noise model from calibrated tap responses and signal statistics rather than unrealistic Gaussian assumptions. The uncertainty model guides a restoration network, narrowing the synthetic-to-real gap. Reliable low-cost depth sensing matters for mobile robotics and consumer devices.

entry.title: MorphoOrgaAgent: A Foundation-Model-Based Multi-Agent System for Autonomous Organoid Analysis

author.name: Hanyi Zhang, Maximilian Hoermann, Lion J. Gleiter, Yiling Xu, Bettina Katalin Budai, Hans-Ulrich Kauczor, Carsten Marr, Tingying Peng

entry.summary: MorphoOrgaAgent is a multi-agent framework using foundation models for zero-shot organoid segmentation, automated statistical analysis, and report generation from natural language input, removing barriers of manual segmentation and coding for experimental biologists. Its components include task understanding, segmentation, and analysis agents. This accelerates organoid-based disease and drug-testing research.

entry.title: Photonic reservoir computing with dimensionally compressed readout

author.name: Gerald Kobi, Mohab Abdalla, Miguel C. Soriano, Damien Rontani

entry.summary: The authors address the practical constraint of limited readout layer size in physical (photonic) reservoir computing by using random projections to compress high-dimensional reservoir states into lower-dimensional subspaces. They compare a small standalone time-delay reservoir against a larger one with projected output, showing via information-processing capacity metrics that the two configurations can differ in their capacity distributions. This is relevant to making analog photonic neuromorphic hardware practical.

entry.title: SHIFT: Surface-aware High-speed Integration For TSDFs

author.name: Ayaan Choudhury, Lokender Tiwari

entry.summary: SHIFT is an efficient real-time 3D mapping framework that reduces per-frame TSDF/ESDF integration cost by exploiting structural regularity, avoiding redundant re-fusion of depth pixels whose voxels have already converged. This targets a well-known computational bottleneck in online motion planning for autonomous robots, especially in planar-dominant environments. Faster mapping directly benefits real-time navigation stacks.

entry.title: Generalizable 6D Pose Estimation of Textureless Objects with Planar-based Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Jie Lu, Hengtan Zhang, Li Gong, Pengpeng Wang, Xianjia Yu, Jinxiang Deng, Tomi Westerlund, Zhongxue Gan, Lirong Zheng, Zhuo Zou

entry.summary: PG-Pose is a geometry-aware framework for generalizable 6D pose estimation of textureless objects without prior CAD models, combining planar-based Gaussian Splatting reconstruction with geometry-driven pose optimization. It builds 3D Gaussian representations and renders geometrically constrained views from multi-view reference RGB images to compensate for missing appearance features. This tackles a persistent pain point for industrial and everyday objects lacking texture.

entry.title: OmniNav: Robust Long-Horizon Target Navigation in Dynamic Environments

author.name: Yujie Tang, Meiling Wang, Jinhao Jiang, Sibo Zuo, Yinan Deng, Xinyu Zhang, Yufeng Yue

entry.summary: OmniNav formulates long-horizon target navigation as continual inference over a factorized task state, coupling valid scene memory, belief revision under partial observability, and selection of interaction-feasible endpoints. It explicitly handles scene staleness, search-altered beliefs, and geometrically convenient but manipulation-infeasible goals. The work targets robust navigation in dynamic real-world environments.

entry.title: EvoNav-Bench: Benchmarking Lifelong Navigation in Evolving Environments

author.name: Xilin Wang, Guoxi Zhang, Hongming Xu, Zhuofan Zhang, Tianxu Wang, Lifeng Fan

entry.summary: EvoNav-Bench is a benchmark for lifelong navigation in which environments evolve due to human activity, breaking the stationary-environment assumption behind existing scene-graph and snapshot-based methods. It is designed to expose the failure mode of fusing outdated prior observations with new ones. This provides the first systematic testbed for experience consolidation under environment change.

entry.title: Safe Task Planning with Long-Term Graph Memory for Embodied Agents

author.name: Siyuan Li, Taiyan Lang, Aoqi Yan, Jia Yu, Feifan Liu, Yihan Du, Yu Zheng, Xun Wang, Peng Liu

entry.summary: SafeMem is a safe task-planning framework that maintains a long-term semantic graph memory of open, dynamic environments from egocentric observations, with an LLM-based risk predictor evaluating candidate actions under partial observability. It addresses the lack of physical risk awareness in LLM/VLM-driven zero-shot planners, especially when hazards lie outside the current field of view. This connects memory, perception, and safety in embodied planning.

entry.title: TASG-Explore: Traversability-Aware Sector-Guided Exploration for Ground Robot on Uneven Terrain

author.name: Shaocong Wang, Shiliang Shao, Ting Wang, Guangjie Han, Lianqing Liu

entry.summary: This paper presents TASG-Explore, a framework combining hierarchical traversability analysis with sector-based guidance for autonomous ground robot exploration on uneven terrain. It balances fast large-scale coverage with fine terrain reasoning to avoid missing narrow passages. This addresses a real trade-off in field robotics exploration planning.

entry.title: Instability in Patient Clustering: A Multiverse Analysis of Unsupervised Clustering in the CENTER-TBI cohort

author.name: Sean R E A Bagcik, Aneeta Merlin Chacko, Ewout W Steyerberg, Maarten van Smeden, Andrew I R Maas, Erik van Zwet, Nicole S Erler

entry.summary: A multiverse analysis of unsupervised patient clustering on 4,509 traumatic brain injury patients from CENTER-TBI, varying algorithm, distance metric, and cluster-count selection in a factorial design. It demonstrates substantial instability of clustering solutions, highlighting risks of overinterpreting data-driven patient subgroups in clinical research.

entry.title: Do LLMs have opinions about other LLMs (and do they act on them)?

author.name: Marek Masiak

entry.summary: An independent empirical study testing whether LLM code reviewers judge code differently based on a metadata tag naming the coding agent, rather than on code quality alone. Using matched clean/buggy Python snippet pairs with only the agent name changed, the author measures shifts in P(MERGE) to detect reputational bias, including whether open-weight models favor open-weight models and whether models favor models from their own country of origin. The work is relevant to AI evaluation integrity and implicit model-mediated discrimination, and code/datasets are published for replication.

entry.title: Recovering Temporal and Geographic Signals from Language Model Embeddings

author.name: Esteban Feuerstein, Victoria Klimkowski, Juan Manuel Ortiz de Zarate, Federico Hern\'an Suaiter

entry.summary: The paper introduces a black-box, model-agnostic projection method that recovers temporal and geographic information directly from output embeddings using only a small seed set, without access to weights or internal activations. This enables analysis of API-only embedding models and probes whether they encode structured real-world knowledge.

entry.title: Building Trustworthy Graph-Agentic RAG for Social Good: Architectures, Failure Propagation, and Assurance by Construction

author.name: Vijay Bommireddy, Raviteja Bommireddy

entry.summary: A survey/framework paper on graph-agentic RAG systems for social-good settings, analyzing how defects in graph construction propagate through retrieval, control decisions, and outcomes. Organizes literature by graph substrate and lifecycle and proposes assurance-by-construction design principles covering authorization, traceability, and oversight. Timely given rapid adoption of agentic RAG.

entry.title: Scoring Without the Engine: Validating a Deterministic, Manipulation-Resistant Content Score for Generative Engines, End to End

author.name: Elisha Bajemon, Andre-Louis Rochet

entry.summary: Presents a validation protocol using adversarial falsification gates (negative controls, dose response, duplication penalty, length neutrality) for cheap deterministic proxies of expensive non-stationary oracles, demonstrated on Generative Engine Optimization. Notably, the protocol detects that the proxy fails on the domain, and re-measures stale causal evidence.

entry.title: Evidence-Aligned Entity Verification for Hallucination Detection in Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Runsong Jia, Zhen Fang, Mengjia Wu, Jie Lu, Yi Zhang

entry.summary: Targets hallucination detection in retrieval-augmented generation by verifying generated entities against retrieved evidence, moving beyond internal-signal methods like uncertainty and self-consistency that rely on potentially outdated parametric knowledge. The work formulates a practical learning problem of aligning output entities with external evidence.

entry.title: EvolveScaler: Synthesizing Information-Evolution Contexts via Executable State Machines and Natural-Language Rendering

author.name: Ziliang Zhao, Zenan Xu, Shuting Wang, Zhao Wang, Bowen Cao, Minda Hu, Lincheng Li, Pluto Zhou, Zhicheng Dou

entry.summary: Introduces EvolveScaler, a code-driven data synthesis framework for the information-evolution setting where later events revise or revoke earlier information in persistent interactions. It defines state transitions and record validity via human-authored executable specifications before rendering to natural language, making synthetic contexts verifiable by construction.

entry.title: RAGMark: A Comprehensive Framework for Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems

author.name: Zlatan Feric, Amir Taherin, Bin Ren, Yanzhi Wang, Jennifer Dy, David Kaeli

entry.summary: RAGMark is a modular benchmarking framework for RAG pipelines in small multi-GPU environments, sweeping retrievers, vector databases, prompt-processing methods, and generators while collecting per-stage metrics like latency, GPU utilization, power, TTFT, throughput, and answer quality. It characterizes five RAG configurations and offers an extensible toolkit for practitioners.

entry.title: Companion-style QA Assistance in Ego-Vision

author.name: Hangyu Qin, Junbin Xiao, Shenglang Zhang, Angela Yao

entry.summary: Introduces BuddyVQA, a benchmark of 21.6K questions over 6K highlight moments in 1,012 long egocentric videos, featuring ego-deictic expressions and interactively chained questions that require resolving visual pronouns against streaming context. This targets assistant-style first-person QA capabilities largely overlooked by existing VideoQA benchmarks.

entry.title: REFINE: Trajectory Representation Learning via Closed-Loop Transcription -- Extended Version

author.name: Sean Bin Yang, Ying Sun, Jilin Hu, Zongyi Xu, Kristian Torp, Hua Lu, Bin Yang, Christian S. Jensen

entry.summary: REFINE is a trajectory representation learning framework that couples road-network-aware generative reconstruction with feedback-driven contrastive learning, replacing the open-loop augment-and-encode paradigm with closed-loop refinement inspired by control theory. This enables capturing fine-grained movement semantics and global spatio-temporal dependencies without manual augmentations. It supports downstream trajectory analytics tasks with better generalization and scalability.

entry.title: How AI Models Manage Epistemic Authority: A Taxonomy and Comparative Analysis of Responses to User Disagreement

author.name: Riyadh Alnasser, Yusuf M\"ucahit \c{C}etinkaya, Sumin Zhao, Tu\u{g}rulcan Elmas

entry.summary: Drawing on Conversation Analysis, the authors present a taxonomy of six user-challenge types and a four-layer framework for how LLMs manage epistemic authority when users disagree, analyzing 32,340 responses across 2,310 controlled scenarios. This reveals how models maintain or change claims, locate authority, and provide evidential support under social pressure.

entry.title: A Multi-Modal Perception Pipeline for Object Detection and Tracking in Autonomous Racing

author.name: Davide Malvezzi, Michele Pestarino, Vittoria Cavicchioli, Valentina La Gamba, Silvia Severi, Fabio Bagni, Luca Bartoli, Massimiliano Bosi, Francesco Gatti, Micaela Verucchi, Ayoub Raji, Marko Bertogna

entry.summary: The paper presents a late-fusion perception pipeline for autonomous racing that combines camera, LiDAR, and RADAR detections with a dedicated multi-object tracking framework, designed for high speeds, vibrations, and small safety margins. It extends prior work to exploit all onboard sensors and improve robustness under degraded visibility and sensor failure. It is an applied systems contribution validated in the racing domain.

entry.title: SynthRCT: Scalable Conditional Deformation Synthesis for Synthetic Repeat CT Generation

author.name: Tomas Guija-Valiente, Blanca Rodriguez-Gonzalez, Norberto Malpica

entry.summary: SynthRCT is a conditional variational autoencoder framework that synthesizes realistic 3D anatomical deformations for evaluating proton therapy robustness under anatomical change, learning a latent deformation space decoded into local stationary velocity fields composed into memory-scalable full-volume transformations. Validated on respiratory 4DCT data, it replaces simplified perturbation scenarios with patient-specific variability.

entry.title: Canonical Color as a Lens into Concept Decodability in Vision Encoders and VLMs

author.name: Xiaofu Chen, Stella Frank, Yova Kementchedjhieva

entry.summary: Uses canonical color as a controlled probe of whether vision encoders encode conceptual information beyond visible pixels, constructing a dataset of objects with canonical colors and probing with grayscale inputs. Finds canonical color remains linearly decodable from grayscale images and is tied to object identity, and that VLM post-training can affect this conceptual content. A clean interpretability study of what vision encoders actually represent.

entry.title: Scaling Optimal Classification Trees via Adaptive Feature and Sample Reduction

author.name: Jiancheng Tu, Wenqi Fan

entry.summary: This paper scales exact (optimal) decision tree learning by jointly reducing features and samples on top of the STreeD dynamic programming framework, using weighted representatives of duplicate records and an adaptive outer loop that refines candidate feature sets. Certified solutions remain optimal for the current candidate set. It makes optimal classification trees more tractable, relevant to interpretable ML.

entry.title: Sparse Oblique Rule Boosting for Simpler Additive Rule Ensembles

author.name: Shahrzad Behzadimanesh, Pierre Le Bodic, Geoffrey I. Webb, Mario Boley

entry.summary: The paper extends interpretable additive rule ensembles beyond axis-parallel threshold conditions to sparse oblique rules, improving accuracy when expressive curated features are unavailable while keeping ensembles small and interpretable. It builds on gradient boosting of symbolic rules with efficient learning. Relevant to interpretable ML on tabular data.

entry.title: PPIM: Pennes Physics-Informed Mamba for Heat-Source-Conditioned 3D Bioheat Simulation

author.name: Dongyun Lee, Kyungho Yoon, Minwoo Shin

entry.summary: Proposes PPIM, a physics-informed Mamba architecture for 3D bioheat simulation under the Pennes equation with localized heat sources inspired by microwave ablation, and compares it against Fourier-feature PINNs and generic PINN-Mamba baselines under controlled conditions. Targets accurate neural PDE solvers for thermal therapy planning.

entry.title: HypLTSF: A Hyperbolic Geometric View of Multi-Scale Hierarchies for Long-Term Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Namwoo Kim, Hyungryul Baik, Yoonjin Yoon

entry.summary: HypLTSF embeds multi-scale temporal representations into the Poincare ball so that the hierarchy between fine-grained and coarse time-series scales is modeled as explicit hyperbolic geometry rather than left as an emergent byproduct. This gives long-term forecasting models a principled inductive bias for tree-like, hierarchical structure. It matters as part of a broader push to bring geometric deep learning tools into mainstream time-series forecasting architectures.

entry.title: EMBLEM: Enhancing Multi-script Table Detection through Masking

author.name: Dhruv Kudale, Udhay Brahmi, Ganesh Ramakrishnan

entry.summary: The authors release MANDALA, a manually annotated dataset of 2,323 table-containing pages covering 18 languages and 15 scripts, and propose EMBLEM, a masking-based training paradigm that conceals script-specific cues to improve multi-script table detection. This addresses a real gap: current detectors trained mostly on English and Chinese degrade sharply on low-resource scripts. The dataset and paradigm together should improve document-analysis pipelines for multilingual corpora.

entry.title: When Does Scale-Invariant Optimization Become Unstable? An Exact Schedule Law with Weight Decay

author.name: Hasan Amin, Wei-Kai Chang, Rajiv Khanna

entry.summary: Derives an exact discrete-time law governing the interaction of learning-rate schedules and weight decay in scale-invariant (normalized) networks, capturing a feedback loop through the parameter norm. The analysis yields a sharp boundary between contraction- and expansion-dominated effective learning-rate regimes.

entry.title: Accelerated High-Accuracy Sampling from a Warm Start via the Proximal Bouncy Particle Sampler

author.name: Fan Chen, Sinho Chewi, Jianfeng Lu, Matthew S Zhang

entry.summary: Designs and analyzes the Proximal Bouncy Particle Sampler, combining proximal sampling with piecewise-deterministic Markov processes to sample from strongly convex, smooth targets. From a warm start it achieves epsilon-accuracy with roughly O(sqrt(kappa) d^(1/4)) gradient queries, improving dependence on dimension and condition number.

entry.title: SeisBench DAS: A machine learning framework for Distributed Acoustic Sensing

author.name: Jannes M\"unchmeyer, Han Xiao, Frederik Tilmann

entry.summary: Presents SeisBench DAS, an extension of the SeisBench library that standardizes data formats, metadata, labels, and models for machine learning on distributed acoustic sensing data, aiming to close the interoperability gap between model developers and geophysics practitioners.

entry.title: ActionSplice: In-Flight Action Editing for Interactive World Models

author.name: Pardis Taghavi, Tingyu Guo, Jonas Lossner, Gaurav Pandey, Reza Langari

entry.summary: Introduces an inference framework that lets chunk-autoregressive video world models incorporate user actions mid-generation without rollback or replay, formulated as Counterfactual State Transport with a lightweight corrector while keeping the world model and sampler frozen. This addresses a real latency and consistency problem for interactive world-model applications.

entry.title: ONE CYLinder: A Benchmark for Graph-Based Surrogate Modeling of Unsteady Bluff-Body Flows

author.name: Th\'eodore Michel, Antoine Campos, Alban Dujardin, Henry Areiza, Philippe Meliga, Elie Hachem

entry.summary: The paper introduces ONECYL, a benchmark dataset of 450 high-fidelity finite-element simulations (270,000 snapshots) of unsteady flow past a cylinder, spanning laminar, transitional, and high-Reynolds-number regimes with randomized geometries. It provides time-resolved velocity and pressure fields plus mesh connectivity to enable standardized evaluation of graph-based neural surrogates for CFD, including long-horizon autoregressive prediction protocols. This addresses a genuine scarcity of public benchmarks for scientific machine learning on unstructured meshes.

entry.title: Intra-Prompt Parallel Decoding for Common-Context Question Answering

author.name: Theodore Glavas, Nikhita Vedula, Dushyanta Dhyani, Antonios Valkanas, Yilun Zhu, Shervin Malmasi

entry.summary: The paper introduces IPPD, an inference method that answers multiple questions sharing a common context in parallel within a single prompt, rather than issuing independent prompts per question. By sharing memory and computation during attention, it directly attacks the memory bottleneck that underutilizes GPUs in standard batching and caching setups. This targets latency and throughput for common-context QA workloads.

entry.title: CreaMem: A Scene-Aware Memory Architecture for Personalized Agents

author.name: Qixuan Sun, Yue Que, Bowei He, Jin Guo, Dihang Yang, Wenchang Situ, Chen Ma

entry.summary: Proposes CreaMem, a long-term memory architecture for personalized LLM agents that partitions memory into Life Scene Memories to reduce cross-scene interference and encodes each memory from multiple perspectives to enable complementary retrieval views. It targets two identified weaknesses of topic- and hierarchy-based memory systems.

entry.title: Comparing Self-Supervised and Domain-Invariant Features for Cross-Domain Voice Phishing Detection

author.name: Jeongmin Lee, Seung Yun, Minkyu Lee, Ran Han, Yoonkyu Woo, Jinxia Huang

entry.summary: The paper compares domain-invariant prosodic features against self-supervised speech representations (HuBERT, wav2vec2.0) for voice phishing detection, training on actor scenario recordings and testing on authentic criminal calls. HuBERT achieves 94.2% F1 with 5-shot adaptation while prosodic features reach 71.0%, offering a lightweight alternative. It addresses the practical data-scarcity constraints of fraud detection.

entry.title: PAI-Actor: Cinematic Multi-Character Replacement in Dynamic Scenes

author.name: Bangxun Tang, Heyuan Gao, Yiren Song, Guian Fang, Zijian He, Jie Yang, Mike Zheng Shou

entry.summary: PAI-Actor is a framework for replacing and animating multiple characters in real movie clips while preserving original scene dynamics, camera motion, lighting, and background, formulated as a structure-guided human recovery problem. It goes beyond prior character animation systems that handle a single static subject.

entry.title: GeoCo-SAVi: Geometry-Consistent Slot Attention for Explicitly Editable Object Representations

author.name: Haoxiang Huang, Zhekai Wang, Xiang Liu, Sen Cui, Changshui Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes GeoCo-SAVi, which makes explicit position and scale in slot-based object-centric video models effective controls by enforcing geometric authority through a spatially equivariant decoder, factual position alignment, and normalized attention overlap, plus appearance transplantation aligned across object geometries.

entry.title: Eventually Optimal and Scalable Multi-Agent Planning for Block Cave Mining

author.name: Christopher Leet, Paolo Forte, Uwe K\"ockemann, Henrik Andreasson, Sven Koenig

entry.summary: This paper formalizes the Block Cave Mining (BCM) multi-agent planning problem - computing transport plans that maximize ore throughput under draw ratio constraints - and proposes SAMM, an eventually optimal anytime solver integrating task assignment, scheduling, and path planning via mixed-integer linear programming. A scalability-enhancing variant is also introduced for dynamic mine environments. It contributes both a new formal problem and a practical solver for underground mining automation.

entry.title: Generating Instance Generators in PDDL Planning

author.name: Nicola J. M\"uller, Naya Rudolph, Katharina Stein, J\"org Hoffmann, Ayal Taitler, Timo P. Gros

entry.summary: The paper proposes using LLMs to generate instance generators for PDDL planning domains, addressing the long-standing gap that PDDL specifies domains but not legality constraints on initial states, goals, or domain subsets, making instance generation ad hoc. This improves on prior reasoning and learning approaches that suffered scalability limitations.

entry.title: Distance-Aware Attention and Wall-Distance Expert Routing for Transformer-Based 3D Flow Prediction

author.name: Sanghyeon Kim, Sunwoong Yang, Namwoo Kang

entry.summary: The paper conditions transformer surrogates for 3D flow prediction on wall-distance physics signals at two points: distance-aware cross-attention reshapes queries during retrieval, and a surface-volume mixture-of-experts replaces the shared feed-forward layer. This lets points in boundary layers retrieve and transform information differently from points in outer flow. It matters for industrial CFD surrogate modeling where near-wall accuracy is critical.

entry.title: TTGBench: Benchmarking Topological Evolution and Semantic Drift in Text-attributed Temporal Graphs

author.name: Longfei Ma, Zemin Liu, Fei Wu

entry.summary: Introduces TTGBench, a benchmark that jointly evaluates structural and semantic evolution in temporal graph learning, addressing limitations of existing benchmarks that emphasize temporal link prediction and use datasets with high link repetition that inflate performance estimates. It includes richer temporal node classification settings designed to capture realistic semantic drift.

entry.title: Graph-Based Personalized Memory for LLM Agents: Representation, Evolution, Retrieval, and Evaluation

author.name: Dac Duy Anh Nguyen, Zhangchi Qiu, Shigeng Chen, Alan Wee-Chung Liew

entry.summary: A survey-style paper organizing the emerging area of graph-based personalized memory for LLM agents, covering how user information is represented with explicit relations and temporal/evidence links, how memories are revised and retrieved, and how systems are evaluated. It aims to unify a fragmented literature as agents shift toward long-term personal assistants.

entry.title: Procedural Graphs: Self-Evolving Execution Structures for LLM Agents

author.name: Yuxing Lu, Yicheng Chen, Shanchan Wu, Sercan \"{O}. Ar{\i}k

entry.summary: The paper introduces Procedural Graphs, which organize procedural knowledge into (procedure, relation, procedure) triplets analogous to knowledge graphs for facts, giving LLM agents explicit structure over what to do, when, and in what order. The framework self-evolves these execution structures to reduce objective drift, out-of-order tool calls, and repetitive actions in long-horizon tasks. It targets a key reliability gap in agentic systems.

entry.title: OracleZoom: On-Policy Self-Distillation Inspired Reference-Constrained Recursive Image Super Resolution

author.name: Shubhashis Roy Dipta, Sourajit Saha, Shaswati Saha, Nobin Sarwar

entry.summary: OracleZoom tackles recursive super-resolution at extreme magnification factors where ground truth supervision is unavailable at deeper scales, using on-policy distillation with reference-constrained training to carry verifiable content beyond the supervision boundary. It combines direct and cross-scale supervision with a no-reference quality objective.

entry.title: AuthBench: A Large-Scale Multilingual Benchmark for Authorship Representation across Genres and Lengths

author.name: MaoXun Huang, Zhenxing Zhang, Claire Cardie

entry.summary: Introduces AuthBench, a large-scale authorship benchmark with 428,150 documents by 153,825 authors across ten languages, 9 primary and 66 fine-grained genres, and multiple document-length regimes, designed to test whether authorship representations generalize broadly. It targets applications from digital forensics to machine-generated text detection.

entry.title: No\=esis: Deterministic-First Retrieval with Two-Tier Context Hydration for Factuality-Critical Queries on Small Local Models

author.name: Nicola Cogotti

entry.summary: Noesis is a deterministic-first architecture for small local language models in factuality-critical domains (healthcare, finance, media), where fabricated numbers are worse than admitted uncertainty. It routes queries to deterministic computation first and uses two-tier context hydration to address the finding that below 7B parameters the RAG bottleneck is context utilization rather than retrieval quality.

entry.title: Exploring Bottom-Up Clustering for Creating Semantic IDs

author.name: Leah Woldemariam, Sudhanshu Garg, Taha Belkhouja, Charles Kim-Yip, Ali Sahami

entry.summary: The paper presents an algorithm for generating Semantic IDs for generative retrieval that guarantees identifier uniqueness while preserving the structure of the original embedding space, using bottom-up clustering to retain local structure. This improves over hash-based identifiers and prior residual quantization approaches. Semantic IDs are central to modern generative recommenders.

entry.title: Connecting Score Matching, Maximum Likelihood, and Expectation-Maximization in Mixed Linear Regression

author.name: Zhankun Luo, Abolfazl Hashemi

entry.summary: Establishes theoretical links between denoising score matching over a variance-preserving diffusion path, maximum likelihood, and EM in mixed linear regression, proving the resulting estimator converges to ground truth with the Gaussian limit of the MLE. Derives decompositions linking score matching loss to cross-entropy-like objectives. Contributes to the statistical theory underlying diffusion-based estimation.

entry.title: Budgeted Task-Aware Acquisition of Dynamic Networks

author.name: Zihe Zhou

entry.summary: Scout is a lightweight framework for learning on dynamic graphs under observation budgets, deciding which stale graph information to refresh based on task value learned from the maintained graph and observation history. Evaluations span one synthetic and four real networks, two tasks, and nine baselines, with Scout achieving the highest downstream performance. It introduces a practical cost-aware angle to dynamic graph learning.

entry.title: Learning Kernels by Alignment for Multiclass Bayes Classification

author.name: Hollan Haule, Alfredo Gonzalez-Sulser, Javier Escudero

entry.summary: The paper shows Collaborative Learning and Inference (CLaI) can be viewed as kernel alignment, with the learned embedding induced similarity matching a label-derived target kernel, and proves Collaborative Inference equals kernel Bayes classification with Parzen windows. It generalizes CLaI with a learned Mahalanobis distance for multiclass problems. This gives a kernel-methods theoretical grounding to an emerging representation-learning framework.

entry.title: Constitutive State-Space Modeling of Path-Dependent Plasticity: A Resolution-Consistent and Parallelizable Computational Framework

author.name: Rui Barreira, Taylan Soydan, Francesco Scipione, Miguel A. Bessa, Dirk Mohr

entry.summary: Introduces a Constitutive State Space (CSS) model reformulating structured state-space dynamics as an incremental constitutive operator for path-dependent material plasticity. By decomposing strain increments into direction and magnitude, the model achieves stationarity under zero increments, resolution consistency, and parallelizable training compared to recurrent baselines.

entry.title: Not All Variables Agree: Reliability-Aware Variable-Wise Gradient Surgery for Multivariate Time-Series Forecasting

author.name: Jinwoo Park, Hyeongwon Kang, Pilsung Kang

entry.summary: The paper measures variable-wise gradients during multivariate time-series training and finds that about 30.6 percent of pairwise cosine similarities are negative on average, yet gradient conflict does not reliably predict which variables are actually harmed relative to a single-target oracle. It then proposes reliability-aware gradient surgery that intervenes only on variables shown to be harmed. This matters because it corrects an overly simple narrative that gradient conflict should be uniformly resolved, refining how multi-output models are trained.

entry.title: Smoothed Picard Hamiltonian Monte Carlo

author.name: Fan Chen, Sinho Chewi, Jianfeng Lu, Matthew S Zhang

entry.summary: Develops smoothed Picard HMC, a low-accuracy sampler combining Gaussian smoothing, Picard iteration, and higher-order discretization for log-concave targets, with W2 guarantees of order kappa^2 + kappa^(7/6) d^(1/6) gradient queries. It also provides a recursive warm start framework to upgrade Wq bounds to divergence guarantees.

entry.title: Beyond Task Success: Stage-Wise Reliability of World Model Planning under Sensing Degradation

author.name: Geonmyeong Lee, Byoung-Tak Zhang

entry.summary: Applies 10 visual and temporal sensing degradations to a world model planner and tracks effects through representation, prediction, planner preference, and physical outcome stages on 50 paired tasks. Findings show degradation impact is not preserved across stages, with some large representation shifts attenuating while smaller ones persist to outcomes.

entry.title: PocketVE: Stable and Property-Guided Structure-Based Drug Design with Variance-Exploding Diffusion

author.name: Peining Zhang, Jinbo Bi

entry.summary: A protein-pocket-conditioned variance-exploding diffusion framework for 3D molecule generation that couples EDM-style denoising with classifier-free guidance for multi-property steering and adaptive pocket perturbation as a regularizer. It substantially improves 3D validity on CrossDocked2020 under the GenBench3D protocol (58.6 to 80.6).

entry.title: Better Together: Complementary Query Rewriting Under a Strong RAG Baseline

author.name: Sara Shanian, Xiaoqin Yi, Pavlo Ruban, Kurt MacDonald

entry.summary: This empirical study tests whether multi-variant query rewriting still helps retrieval-augmented generation when the underlying retrieval pipeline is already strong, using a fixed stack of BGE dense retrieval, cross-encoder reranking, and MMR diversification. Across HotpotQA, AmbigNQ, and a 512K-document EnterpriseRAG-Bench with paired-bootstrap significance testing, it finds rewriting alone is at best competitive with strong baselines like HyDE and Query2Doc, but combining complementary rewriting strategies yields outsized gains because their failure modes differ. The result offers practical guidance for production RAG systems.

entry.title: Emotion as a Distribution: Joint Valence-Arousal Probability Learning for Speaker-Independent Multimodal Emotion Recognition
