author.name: Tingyi Lin, Wen-Ren Yang, Kuanwei Chen

entry.summary: The paper argues emotion recognition should output a distribution over the valence-arousal plane rather than a hard label, training a text+speech system with 2D Gaussian soft targets under KL/cross-entropy loss and a 9x9 probability matrix output. It compares Transformer and Mamba (1/2/3) backbones in a fixed pipeline under strict speaker-independent IEMOCAP evaluation, aimed at counseling support. The probabilistic framing and rigorous evaluation protocol are its main strengths.

entry.title: Same Problem, Different Field: Cross-Domain Solution Import via Domain-Stripped Computational Fingerprints

author.name: Eryk Kulikowski

entry.summary: The paper proposes distilling papers into domain- and method-name-stripped computational fingerprints (a free-text mechanism skeleton plus controlled facets) so that cross-field instances of the same problem, such as Kalman filtering appearing under different names in control, pharmacokinetics, and geoscience, can be matched for solution import. A tunable facet-selectable distance enables retrieval of cross-field solution pairs. This is a novel take on scientific knowledge transfer beyond topical embeddings.

entry.title: Generalist Open-World Temporal Perception

author.name: Cristian Sminchisescu

entry.summary: This position paper by a prominent researcher lays out a vision for generalist open-world perceptual systems that represent biological forms, physical structures, and artifacts as coherent temporally persistent processes within a multimodal world model. The proposed system would infer geometry, articulation, semantics, interaction structure, and uncertainty from raw multimodal streams while maintaining identity through occlusion and viewpoint change. It frames the temporal perceptual substrate as essential for next-generation natively temporal and multimodal AI.

entry.title: PRG-Fusion: Orchestrating Generative Priors with Reconstruction Evidence for Driving View Synthesis

author.name: Sipeng He, Jialei Chen, Zhen Fang, Dongchun Ren, Feng Zhao

entry.summary: PRG-Fusion targets photorealistic driving video synthesis along specified trajectories for closed-loop simulation by combining reconstruction-based neural rendering, which is geometrically consistent but artifacts-prone under novel viewpoints, with generative models, which handle arbitrary trajectories but struggle with temporal and geometric consistency. The framework uses region-wise reconstruction evidence to orchestrate where generative priors are applied. This is directly relevant to scalable autonomous driving simulation.

entry.title: CNsEMD: An Expert-Annotated Multi-Field-Strength MRI Dataset and a Hyperspherical Manifold Network for Multimodal Cranial Nerve Parcellation

author.name: Lei Xie, Junxiong Huang, Guoqiang Xie, Jiawei Zhang, Jiahao Huang, Tianling Lyu, Ye Wu, Mingchu Li, Shoujun Yu, Shanshan Wang, Qingrun Zeng, Yuanjing Feng

entry.summary: CNsEMD provides an expert-annotated multimodal dataset for cranial nerve parcellation covering 202 subjects across 3T, 5T, and 7T MRI scanners, addressing the scarcity of public annotations for these tiny, low-contrast, slender structures. Alongside the dataset, the authors propose a hyperspherical manifold network tailored to the tubular morphology and complex trajectories of cranial nerves. This enables fair benchmarking and supports neuroanatomical analysis and neurosurgical planning.

entry.title: Mitigating Shortcut Learning: Texture-Penalized Prototype Networks

author.name: Akshay Anilkumar Girija, Elena Hoemann, Frank K\"oster, Sven Hallerbach

entry.summary: TPPN introduces an architectural Texture-Penalization Branch that suppresses local high-frequency texture cues, pushing CNN backbones toward shape-biased representations to reduce shortcut learning and failures under texture shifts. Unlike much prior work it does this without resource-intensive augmented datasets. Prototype-based classification then operates on these purified shape features for more robust predictions.

entry.title: NEO-BENCH: A New Multi-Source Benchmark for Generalizable Astronomical Streak Detection

author.name: Jiayou He, Jessica Yao

entry.summary: NEO-BENCH is a multi-source benchmark of 8,376 images from five astronomical datasets, including Hubble Space Telescope imagery, for evaluating generalizable detection of near-Earth-object streaks in long-exposure images. It addresses the problem that existing detectors are evaluated on single-source data, providing limited evidence of cross-source robustness. This supports planetary defense and astronomy applications.

entry.title: Distributed Secure Learning Control for Large-scale Multirobots under Stealthy Actuator Attacks

author.name: Xinglong Zhang, Qingwen Ma, Cong Li, Hui Yin, Changxin Zhang, Yueying Wang, Wei Pan, Xin Xu

entry.summary: This paper integrates reinforcement learning into distributed model predictive control (DMPC) for multirobot systems while providing security guarantees under stealthy actuator attacks. It addresses the risk that compromised agents spread malicious influence through neighbor communication, offering provable performance and security properties for the hybrid RL-DMPC scheme. The work sits at the intersection of learning-based control and cyber-physical security.

entry.title: Anti-Gravity Walking by a Flying Humanoid Robot via Thrust-Rate Input Whole-Body Model Predictive Control

author.name: Kazuki Sugihara, Kei Okada

entry.summary: The authors propose a real-time whole-body MPC framework enabling a flying humanoid robot to walk on ceilings and other anti-gravity surfaces. Formulating control in thrust-rate input space smooths the discontinuities in dynamics caused by contact switching, avoiding destabilizing thrust spikes. This extends humanoid locomotion beyond flight and ground walking into complex 3D environments.

entry.title: Conditional Timed Partial Orders: An Expressive and Interpretable Framework for Robot Task Specification and Planning

author.name: Sebastian Escobar, Morteza Lahijanian

entry.summary: This paper extends Timed Partial Orders with richer relative-timing constraints and environment-conditioned event activations, yielding conditional TPOs for interpretable robot task specification. Planning reduces to MILP, and a decomposition algorithm mitigates the computational intractability introduced by the added expressivity. The work strengthens the formal-methods toolkit for human-readable robot task plans.

entry.title: Real-time Puncture Detection and Recovery for Pneumatic Soft Actuators

author.name: Tejonidhi R. Deshpande, Tingyu Cheng, Josiah Hester

entry.summary: The authors propose a puncture detection and severity estimation system for pneumatic soft actuators using a single inertial measurement unit, training anomaly detectors on extracted motion features. They also introduce a recovery mechanism for damaged actuators. This addresses a genuine practical barrier to deploying soft robots outside the lab.

entry.title: CriticGen: Generation-Aware Evaluation as Actionable Feedback

author.name: Huifang Du, Zecheng Zuo, Sen Wang, Chenghao Fan, Haofen Wang, Yehui Yang

entry.summary: CriticGen proposes a fine-grained, generation-aware evaluation framework that converts LLM evaluation into actionable refinement: it generates sample-specific scoring rubrics across subjective, objective, and self-derived constraint categories, then uses them to jointly produce a score, explanation, executable refinement suggestion, and an improved answer. This addresses the common problem that LLM evaluators produce generic, non-actionable critiques disconnected from the generation process.

entry.title: Agentic Pressure: The Endogenous Entropy of Reliable Autonomy

author.name: Hengle Jiang, Ziying Luo, Ke Tang

entry.summary: The paper identifies Agentic Pressure, a non-adversarial destabilizing force that emerges in long-horizon agents when the cost of complying with constraints conflicts with goal achievement, and formalizes it theoretically as a ratio of required work to overcome environmental friction against available resources. Unlike jailbreaks, this alignment pressure is endogenous to interaction dynamics.

entry.title: MARBO: Relational Belief Grounding for LLM Agents in Social Deduction Games

author.name: Hwang Yechan, Bae Sangjun, Kim Jeongmo, Bang Sangwoo, Han Seungyul

entry.summary: Introduces MARBO, a belief-grounded preference optimization framework for LLM agents in social deduction games, where preference feedback is provided only when actions and speech are supported by reliable relational beliefs about hidden roles. Improves strategic consistency, especially for compact LLM agents. A clean testbed linking belief modeling to behavioral optimization.

entry.title: EmoMed: An Emotionally-Aware Agent for Multimodal Medical Support with Real-Time Information Retrieval

author.name: Ivan Nasonov, Nikita Glazkov, Ivan Makovetskiy, Mikhail Mozikov, Daniil Sukhorukov, Andrey Savchenko, Ilya Makarov

entry.summary: EmoMed is a multimodal medical consultation agent that adapts response tone and detail based on detected user emotional states while grounding clinical answers via web fact-checking and an API-connected medical knowledge base. It is evaluated across seven frontier LLMs including GPT, Claude, Gemini, Llama, Qwen, and Grok models using LLM-as-judge and MedQA-style metrics. The work matters because it combines affect-awareness with factual grounding in a safety-sensitive healthcare domain.

entry.title: Quantile-Led Feature Extraction for Multi-Horizon Predictive Maintenance in Industrial Manufacturing Systems

author.name: David J Poland, Daniele Ravi, Na Helian

entry.summary: Introduces a dual-stage MLP-QRNN feature extraction framework that learns quantile-based conditional distributions per sensor channel, evaluated across 1-hour to 30-day horizons on 72 machines in 9 facilities with a fixed downstream classifier. Shows representation learning for predictive maintenance should be treated as a tunable stage rather than fixed preprocessing.

entry.title: When Intelligence Becomes Agency: A Theory of Governed, Proactive Agency for Symbiotic AI Systems

author.name: Jo\~ao Dias Ferreira

entry.summary: Develops a conceptual and formal framework for governed proactive agency in persistent AI assistants, addressing the activation problem - when an agent should act, ask, monitor, defer, or refrain - and tying situated activation to continuing authorization and accountability. It synthesizes commitment, appraisal, mixed-initiative interaction, and delegation research.

entry.title: PRIMUS: Identity, Governance, and Verification for Multi-Agent Federations

author.name: Sasank Annapureddy, Anjaneya Prasad Thamatani

entry.summary: Presents PRIMUS, coupling prime-power agent identity with BLS aggregate signatures for multi-agent federation governance, deriving a safe-kill threshold that reduces false-positive agent termination from 80 percent to 0.00 percent under 10 percent channel noise, plus closed-form economic boundaries for verification machinery steering generate-and-test loops.

entry.title: Vision: Data-Centric Anchoring for Robust and Interpretable Agentic AI

author.name: Arun Vignesh Malarkkan, Xinyuan Wang, Yanjie Fu

entry.summary: A position paper arguing that the brittleness and opacity of LLM-based agents share a root cause in the data lifecycle: observational interaction logs lack counterfactual structure, so no model-centric method can recover invariances the data never contained. It proposes Data-Centric Anchoring as a research agenda unifying robustness and interpretability through controlled, counterfactual data collection.

entry.title: Beyond Coherence: Benchmarking Professional Editing-Technique Execution in Multi-Shot Audio-Video Generation

author.name: Tianyi Zeng, Junchao Liao, Yujie Wei, Ziying Zhang, Litao Li, Tianyi Wang, Zhichao Wei, Shuyao Xu, Wenwen Qiang, Siyu Zhu, Zhenghao Zhang, Long Qin

entry.summary: Introduces CutCraft, claimed to be the first benchmark measuring whether multi-shot audio-video generators actually execute professional editing techniques (shot structure, transition grammar, audio-video cuts, montage) rather than merely producing coherent output. It pairs structured multi-shot prompts with explicit editing specifications and a hierarchical hybrid evaluation framework.

entry.title: GoAnt: Quality-Diversity Multi-Agent Search for Alpha Factor Discovery in Market Microstructure Data

author.name: Stella Zhao, Tommy Sha

entry.summary: GoAnt is a quality-diversity multi-agent search framework for discovering symbolic alpha factors from market microstructure data, using non-communicating Explorer, Exploiter, and Connector agents coordinated by a shared adaptive Mental Map and a Queen dispatcher that reallocates evaluation budgets. It targets the common failure of overfitting to predictive proxies that collapse after execution costs and redundant exploration of similar factor families. The work matters for applying quality-diversity search to quant finance with execution-robustness built into the search objective.

entry.title: ProToMEx: Rapid, Interpretable Explanations via Structured Representations

author.name: Athina Georgara, Adarsh Valoor, Sarvapali D. Ramchurn

entry.summary: ProToMEx introduces a model-agnostic explainability paradigm that uses probabilistic topic models to produce latent topics representing high-level reasons for classifier decisions, moving beyond per-feature importance scores. It provides both global explanations of overall model behavior and local explanations for individual predictions. The work addresses a recognized limitation of standard post-hoc feature-attribution explainers.

entry.title: Full-Page Optical Music Recognition of Handwritten Monophonic Scores

author.name: Adrian Rosello, Antonio R\'ios-Vila, David Rizo, Jorge Calvo-Zaragoza

entry.summary: This work extends end-to-end Transformer-based optical music recognition to full-page handwritten monophonic scores, a setting largely unexplored compared to typeset music. The authors introduce a synthetic full-page score generator to study which pretraining factors matter most for transferring to handwritten collections, avoiding reliance on staff segmentation pipelines. It is a solid domain-specific advancement bridging document AI and digital humanities.

entry.title: Closed-Loop Evaluation of Bird's-Eye-View Maps from Cross-View Transformers as Inputs to Behavior-Cloning Policies

author.name: Felipe Carlos dos Santos, Eric Antonelo, Gustavo Claudio Karl Couto

entry.summary: This work evaluates in closed loop (CARLA simulator) whether Cross-View Transformer-predicted BEV maps can replace ground-truth BEV maps as inputs to behavior-cloning driving policies, using a six-channel representation covering road surface, route, lanes, and vehicles. It quantifies how perceptual errors in predicted maps propagate to closed-loop driving performance, a gap in the sim-to-real transition.

entry.title: A solution to the Erd\H{o}s Problem #1040

author.name: Ioannis Tzachristas

entry.summary: A pure mathematics paper proving that for any compact subset of the complex plane with logarithmic capacity one, the infimum of planar areas of unit lemniscates of monic polynomials vanishes, resolving Erdos Problem #1040 without regularity assumptions. The proof combines harmonic polynomials, harmonic measure, and L1 approximation by empirical measures.

entry.title: Explainable Deep Learning for Price-Trade Dynamics: From Black-Box Forecasts to Effective Parametric Models

author.name: Manuel Naviglio, Fabrizio Lillo

entry.summary: Uses deep feed-forward networks on high-frequency returns and signed volumes not merely for prediction but for structural discovery in market microstructure, applying Shapley-based explainability to extract nonlinear dependencies beyond linear VAR benchmarks. The findings inform the construction of effective parametric models.

entry.title: ExpertLens: Visualizing Embedding Spaces for Post-Hoc Explainability in MoE Enhanced Retrievers

author.name: Effrosyni Sokli, Isaac Roberts, Alexander Schulz, Barbara Hammer, Gabriella Pasi

entry.summary: Proposes ExpertLens, a post-hoc explainability framework for MoE-enhanced dense retrievers that shifts from scalar feature attributions to representation-level global interpretability via discriminative embedding space visualization.

entry.title: Multiple Myeloma Lesion Segmentation on Whole-Body Diffusion-Weighted Imaging via Efficient Anatomical Anticipation and Multimodal Confirmation

author.name: Mengmeng Zhang, Shengqian Huang, Junde Zhou, Xiaoping Wu, Hao Luog, Jing Wanga, Yicheng Sun, Jiao Li, Haibo Zhang, Sheng Xie, Fan Wangg, Qin Wangc, Huadan Xue, Yisheng Lv, Fei-yue Wang

entry.summary: The authors propose a two-stage pipeline for automated segmentation of multiple myeloma lesions in whole-body diffusion-weighted MRI, replacing costly manual bone ROI annotation with an anatomical anticipation stage and using ADC maps via multimodal confirmation rather than simple channel fusion. This addresses a real clinical pain point, as lesion burden measurement guides myeloma treatment assessment. It demonstrates how domain constraints can be encoded to reduce annotation costs in medical imaging.

entry.title: Recovering Weak Signals with Normalizing Flows

author.name: Sarod Yatawatta

entry.summary: The author uses normalizing flow models to reconstruct weak scientific signals that are distorted or suppressed during calibration subtracts of dominant nuisance signals, e.g., in radio astronomy. The method exploits statistical invariance of target signals and includes a theoretical treatment alongside demonstrations.

entry.title: Discovering Translation-Worthy Languages with E-Values

author.name: Wajdi Ben Saad, Safa Madiouni

entry.summary: Frames the decision of when to route multilingual documents through machine translation before classification as a statistically controlled problem, using paired e-processes with familywise error control to compare direct versus translation-assisted prediction per language. On SIB-200 and MASSIVE the router selects translation for a small, data-driven subset of languages while improving held-out accuracy.

entry.title: ECOKV: Geometry-Aware KV Cache Eviction via Complementary Diversity Metrics

author.name: Chin Ting Hsu, Yu-Syuan Xu, Ling Zou, Hsien-Kai Kuo, Wen-Huang Cheng

entry.summary: Analyzes limitations of cosine-similarity-based diversity metrics for KV cache eviction in multimodal LLMs, noting that normalization discards magnitude information and anisotropy yields uniformly high similarities, and proposes a geometry-aware composite metric using complementary Euclidean and angular signals. This reduces memory and compute overhead while preserving model quality.

entry.title: WAPP: Safe Learning of Positive Security WAF Policies from Live Traffic

author.name: Heba Osama, Zeyad Ahmed, Mohamed Amgad, Ahmed Saafan, Jana Elfeky, Mariam Abdelati, Haitham Ghalwash

entry.summary: WAPP is a framework for learning positive (allowlist-style) web application firewall policies from live traffic, combining trust filtering, deterministic rule synthesis, confidence scoring, and pre-enforcement validation to avoid contamination from malicious requests in training data. It is evaluated on three controlled applications using a live Coraza server with the OWASP Core Rule Set. The work complements signature-based WAFs, which struggle against novel or mutated attack payloads.

entry.title: Novel Methods for Catheter and Guidewire Segmentation in X-ray Fluoroscopy under a Federated Learning Setting

author.name: Chayun Kongtongvattana

entry.summary: This thesis presents a structure-aware federated learning framework for segmenting catheters and guidewires in X-ray fluoroscopy, addressing privacy constraints that prevent centralized training across hospitals. Contributions include the CathAction benchmark with over 600,000 annotated frames, a shape-sensitive loss based on signed distance maps, and evaluation on real animal and phantom data. The work targets safety-critical computer vision for endovascular procedures.

entry.title: Emo-DVS: A Multimodal Benchmark for Privacy-Aware Emotion Recognition with Event Cameras

author.name: Jiaqi Chen, Qinfu Xu, Hao Zhuang, Liyuan Pan

entry.summary: Presents Emo-DVS, a tri-modal benchmark combining event camera, audio, and text modalities for privacy-aware emotion recognition in real-world settings. Event cameras reduce facial identity exposure while offering high dynamic range, and the benchmark addresses the small-scale, single-modality limitations of prior event-based emotion datasets.

entry.title: Deep Learning for Biopsy-Free Subtyping of Basal Cell Carcinoma from Dermatoscopic Images

author.name: Alexandros Papadopoulos, Chrysa Episkopou, Ioannis Sarafis, Aimilios Lallas, Anastasios Delopoulos

entry.summary: This preliminary study fine-tunes pretrained vision transformers to subtype basal cell carcinoma directly from a single dermatoscopic image, potentially replacing invasive, costly biopsies for guiding treatment aggressiveness. Given limited labeled data, the authors rely on ViT transfer learning with repeated stratified validation. If validated at scale, non-invasive subtyping would be clinically significant.

entry.title: Towards a Resilience-Theoretic Foundation for Adversarial Robustness in Industrial Control System Anomaly Detection

author.name: Branka Stojanovi\'c, Andreas Flatscher, Michael Somma

entry.summary: The paper connects component-level adversarial robustness of ML anomaly detectors in industrial control systems to system-level resilience certification frameworks (absorb-recover-adapt). It positions adversarial robustness as an instantiation of resilience theory, aiming to bridge the gap between robustness evaluation and formal resilience guarantees for cyber-physical systems. This is a conceptual/foundational contribution for securing critical infrastructure ML.

entry.title: Distributed Lag Neural Additive Models

author.name: Calle Helmersson, Shivang Pandey, Leonardo Olivetti, Elena Raffetti

entry.summary: DLNAMs are neural-additive counterparts to Distributed Lag Non-linear Models, learning nonlinear exposure-lag response surfaces with neural components instead of prespecified spline cross-bases, while preserving additive interpretability. The method includes uncertainty quantification via a Laplace approximation combined with ensemble variation, and simulations show it generally outperforms DLNM baselines.

entry.title: When Superpixels Fail on Documents: A Study of Segmentation for LIME Explanations

author.name: Quentin Telnoff, Emanuela Boros, Micka\"el Coustaty, Robin Jarry, Fabrice Crohas, Antoine Doucet

entry.summary: This study examines how the segmentation step of LIME explanations affects their reliability for document image classification, showing that standard natural-image superpixels (Quickshift, SLIC) align poorly with document structure. Using RVL-CDIP, the authors demonstrate that OCR-based and grid-based document-aware segmentations substantially improve explanation consistency, correctness, and local fidelity.

entry.title: Human mutation field reveals an equilibrium-like structure with irreversible circulation

author.name: Isabella Caranzano, Daniel Maria Busiello, Stefano Priorelli, Amos Maritan, Piero Fariselli

entry.summary: The authors construct a human mutation field from context-dependent forward-to-reverse substitution probabilities and show it decomposes into a dominant gradient component (an effective energy landscape) plus a smaller reproducible curl component indicating non-equilibrium circulation. Using a Siamese neural network on seven-base germline data, they infer a mutational landscape, connecting sequence evolution to stochastic thermodynamics.

entry.title: Decentralized Safe Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning via Predictive Shielding

author.name: Yacine El Yamani, Hanna Krasowski, Elena Vanneaux

entry.summary: The paper proposes a decentralized multi-agent RL safety framework combining predictive shielding with model-based finite-horizon Q-learning, allowing agents to safely adapt pre-trained policies during deployment without centralized coordination. It addresses reactive-shield limitations near unseen obstacles and improves scalability and adaptability under distribution shift.

entry.title: LLMs for Social Network Modeling: From Network Generation to Dynamic Processes

author.name: Shikha Mallick, Alex Thomo, Akrati Saxena

entry.summary: First comprehensive survey of LLMs for social network modeling, organizing scattered literature into network generative models and dynamic process models, and covering how LLMs simulate context-aware social behavior beyond classical network models. Useful unifying reference for an emerging interdisciplinary area.

entry.title: Synergistic Fusion of Topological Structure and Temporal Semantics of Mobility for Urban Region Embedding

author.name: Namwoo Kim, Jeeyun Chang, Kanghoon Lee, Yoonjin Yoon

entry.summary: This work improves urban region embeddings by modeling temporal dynamics of human mobility, which prior fusion approaches largely ignore, and by capturing joint signals that emerge only when views co-occur rather than fusing views additively. The resulting representations benefit downstream urban sensing tasks such as crime and income prediction. It advances geospatial representation learning.

entry.title: OntoKG-EQ: A provenance-grounded, competency-question-governed knowledge graph for auditable analyst querying

author.name: Furqan Nasir, Muhammad Atif Saeed, Muhammad Ehsan, Sher Jeel Ahmad, Abdul Moiz Altaf

entry.summary: OntoKG-EQ is a knowledge-based system for equity-market analysis in emerging markets that makes analyst queries reproducible, evidence-linked, and auditable. It couples a bounded ontology governed by five frozen competency questions with a provenance-aware knowledge graph where every class, property, shape, and metric is justified by one of those questions, materializing market data into a temporally explicit, inspectable structure. The work targets the well-known trust and reproducibility problems of ad-hoc spreadsheet-driven financial analysis.

entry.title: SQLMorph: Query Mutation and Fine-Grained Metrics for Text-to-SQL Evaluation

author.name: Mohammadhossein Malekpour, Mohamed Riahi, Maxime Lamothe, Amine Mhedhbi

entry.summary: Presents SQLMorph, a framework for evaluating Text-to-SQL systems by automatically mutating queries to generate harder, reproducible evaluation sets, using Join Query Expansion and Textual Query Augmentation. It targets the gap between public benchmarks and enterprise schema complexity. Relevant to practical deployment of NL-to-SQL agents in industry.

entry.title: Nonlinear elliptic homogenization with the parametric Deep Ritz method

author.name: Conor Rowan

entry.summary: This work extends neural network solvers (parametric Deep Ritz method) to nonlinear elliptic homogenization problems, where the homogenized constitutive relation depends on macroscopic state rather than a constant tensor. This allows learning coarse-grained material behavior for heterogeneous materials with fine periodic features. It contributes to the growing field of scientific machine learning for multiscale PDEs.

entry.title: A dictionary learning framework for graphs via filters and optimal transport

author.name: Jinchuan Liao, Dai Hai Nguyen

entry.summary: The authors propose a graph dictionary learning framework where graphs are represented as zero-mean Gaussian distributions derived from filtered Laplacians and approximated by barycenters of learned atom graphs under a new graph comparison metric called fGOT. They introduce a tractable surrogate (sfGOT) that handles graphs without known node correspondence and provide a novel interpretation via the Hilbert-Schmidt Independence Criterion. The framework is trained end-to-end with backpropagation.

entry.title: Connectome-to-Function: Conditional Generative Latent Representations for Reservoir Computing

author.name: Zhuolin Yu, Xingyu Liu, Yuanhao Jia, Yunhang Xiao, Hairuo Xue, Feihan Sun, Guozhang Chen

entry.summary: The authors propose a conditional generative latent framework that encodes neural connectome graphs into a compact structural space usable for reservoir computing, moving beyond hand-crafted structural descriptors. The work bridges connectomics and machine learning by mapping brain-circuit structure to computation. It is notable for neuro-AI intersection work, though its reach is primarily within computational neuroscience.

entry.title: MetaRSI / RSI2: A Meta-Recursive Self-Improving System for Recursive Self-Improving Systems Themselves

author.name: Zihan Tan, Leixin Sun, Zitong Shi, Yitao Liu, Jiajun Wu, Nathaniel Brooks, Jiaru Qian, Xiaoran Shang, Suyuan Huang, Yi Ding, Yangxu Liao, Mukai Li, Qiushi Sun, Shudong Liu, Xuankun Rong, Xiaohang Yu, Zhuo Chen, Hejia Geng, Chenxin Li, Aozhou Wang, Zengji Tu, Robert Tang, Yuxin Zhan, Eric Jiang, Yuxin Wu, Jianqing Zhang, Xiao Liang, Fang Wu, Haochi Zhang, Alexander Marlow, Guancheng Wan

entry.summary: MetaRSI-v1 argues that recursive self-improvement has been validated only on machine-checkable domains like coding and math, and proposes extending RSI to open-ended scientific and meta-scientific domains via a scheduled composition of typed operators including Data-R. The large author list and ambitious framing target general capability improvement beyond formal verification. This touches directly on AI self-improvement safety-relevant territory.

entry.title: Model-Adaptive and Risk-Constrained Frequency Hopping Against Predictive Jammers

author.name: Yanbo Chen, Xinjing Zhou

entry.summary: Introduces D-PACT-AFH, an adversarial contextual-bandit framework for adaptive frequency hopping against predictive jammers, combining a global linear learner with partitioned local learners and online model selection. Variants incorporate channel hit-risk constraints and KL-projection-based risk budgets, with oracle-style theoretical guarantees.

entry.title: AI and TCAD for Inverse Design and Defect Discovery: From Simple Machine Learning to LLM

author.name: Hiu Yung Wong

entry.summary: A review/perspective on simulation-augmented machine learning for semiconductor device design, using Technology Computer-Aided Design (TCAD) to generate training data where experimental data is scarce. Shows autoencoder models and noise engineering on TCAD data can learn latent physics and transfer to experimental data, extending up to LLM-based approaches for defect discovery.

entry.title: No-Regret Mixing of LRU and LFU with Optimal Switching Cost

author.name: Younes Ben Mazziane, Xinying Zou

entry.summary: Studies whether existing caching policies that combine LRU and LFU via online-learning expert mixing (LeCar, Cacheus) achieve sublinear regret against the better of the two on every request sequence. The paper resolves this question and derives a mixing scheme with optimal switching cost guarantees.

entry.title: MpSub: A Momentum $p$-Dimensional Subspace Trust-Region Method for Derivative-Free Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models

author.name: Yuyang Wang, Haoyu Yao, Pengcheng Xie

entry.summary: MpSub is a zeroth-order method for LLM fine-tuning that searches a momentum-augmented low-dimensional subspace using central-difference gradient estimates and a trust-region update, avoiding backpropagation memory costs and sensitive per-task learning rates. This addresses a practical efficiency concern as derivative-free fine-tuning gains attention for privacy and memory reasons. The approach could matter if it scales to larger models.

entry.title: Streaming Hierarchical Inference with Tabular Foundation Models

author.name: Vitor Crista, Afonso Louren\c{c}o, Diogo Martinho, Goreti Marreiros

entry.summary: HINT is a hierarchical edge-cloud inference framework for tabular foundation models in high-throughput streams, using a graph-based approximate nearest neighbor memory to process confident samples locally and offload uncertain ones with retrieved context to a cloud TFM. It addresses latency and communication overhead in TFM deployment. Relevant as tabular foundation models move toward production streaming settings.

entry.title: Nystr\"om Attention Matches Full Attention for Cross-Sectional Stock Prediction

author.name: Kunhan Guo

entry.summary: This work decomposes the inter-stock attention module of the MASTER stock-prediction model and finds a paradox: the learned attention is nearly uniform, yet forcing exact uniformity destroys predictive discrimination. Spectral analysis shows the useful deviation is low-rank, which explains why the authors' Nyström low-rank attention (m=32 landmarks) matches full O(N^2) attention at O(mN) cost, with equivalence certified via TOST across multiple seeds. The result offers a principled efficiency gain for cross-sectional financial prediction and a useful methodological template for analyzing when sparse attention approximations succeed.

entry.title: Certified Topological Interaction in Neural Representations: Class Disentanglement Is Mostly Pairwise

author.name: Sushovan Majhi

entry.summary: The paper measures class disentanglement in neural representations as certified topological interaction between labeled point clouds, using the Intersection Euler Characteristic Profile computed via a single Alpha-complex sweep, with exact permutation tests and a separation certificate attached to every number. Across 111 trained networks and 52,650 certified measurements it finds disentanglement is depth-graded and largely pairwise. This brings statistical rigor to a representation-quality notion usually assessed via descriptive curves.

entry.title: HOPE: Heterophily-Aware Open-Set Node Classification with Pseudo-Extrapolation

author.name: Yumeng Dai, Yue Tan, Yixin Liu, Chenxu Wang, Pinghui Wang, Tao Qin

entry.summary: Addresses open-set node classification on heterophilic graphs, where standard homophily-based methods fail because cross-class connectivity entangles representations. HOPE uses pseudo-extrapolation to handle structural mixture and improve unknown-class rejection.

entry.title: PlayTrain: An Efficient Reinforcement Learning Framework for LLM-Generated Adaptable JavaScript Games

author.name: Ryan Truong, Lance Ying, Samuel J. Gershman, Kazuki Irie

entry.summary: Presents PlayTrain, a framework that uses LLMs to generate JavaScript video-game environments from minimal prompts and runs them in standard gym environments for RL training, allowing humans and agents to play the same games. It demonstrates multiple use cases for rapidly creating and adapting RL environments.

entry.title: Architectural and Regularization Components in Deep Learning Medical Image Registration: Systematic Ablation Study

author.name: Nabira Rashid

entry.summary: A controlled ablation study disentangling whether affine pre-alignment architectures or regularization losses drive performance in deep learning brain MRI registration. Using OASIS data, four variants of a 3D U-Net pipeline are compared across accuracy and deformation metrics. It addresses a common confound in the registration literature where enhancements are adopted jointly.

entry.title: Infrastructure-based Monocular 3D Vehicle Localization Framework with Experimental Validation

author.name: Akos T. Kopeczi-Bocz, Tian Mi, Gabor Orosz, Denes Takacs

entry.summary: Presents a one-stage framework that maps roadside monocular camera images directly to vehicle ground-plane position, dimensions, and yaw, bypassing separate detection-then-geometry pipelines. A synchronized roadside camera plus UAV pipeline provides ground-truth labels and real experimental validation.

entry.title: Toward Sustainable Distributed LLM Inference: A Systems Synthesis and Research Agenda for an Energy-, Carbon-, and Cache-Aware llm-d Control Plane

author.name: Twinkll Sisodia

entry.summary: Synthesizes recent systems research on energy, carbon, batching, KV-cache reuse, and placement into a research agenda for sustainability-aware distributed LLM inference control planes such as llm-d. The contribution is explicitly integration and agenda-setting rather than new benchmarks.

entry.title: Characterizing Privacy Risks of Quantum Machine Learning with Emergent Quantum-Native Access

author.name: Liou Tang, James Joshi, Ashish Kundu

entry.summary: Studies privacy risks of quantum machine learning under a threat model where adversaries have quantum computing capabilities and access to quantum outputs, going beyond the classical-only QML-as-a-service assumption. It maps classical ML leakage channels plus quantum-unique risks in an emerging quantum-native setting.

entry.title: CAROL: Context-Aware Online Learning for Fuzzer Scheduling

author.name: Zirui Liu, Mengfan Xu, Juan Zhai, Shenglong Yao, Shiqing Ma

entry.summary: CAROL is an online learning scheduler for ensemble fuzzing that allocates CPU time among multiple fuzzers using each fuzzer's current context rather than fixed rules and compact historical summaries. The paper first shows empirically that past-reward rankings are unreliable and that predictive signals do not transfer across targets, motivating the context-aware approach.

entry.title: Large Classification-Risk-Optional Label Acquisition

author.name: F. Setoudehtanzangi, Geoffrey J. McLachlan

entry.summary: Studies optimal allocation of a limited labeling budget to minimize multiclass zero-one classification risk. The proposed acquisition criterion combines Fisher information from acquired labels with the local geometry of excess risk, valuing labels by their alignment with parameter directions that perturb the Bayes decision boundary.

entry.title: AstraMoE-SR: Trajectory-Guided Diffusion for Blind Satellite Jitter Deblurring and Super-Resolution

author.name: Yi-Chung Lai, Chin-Tien Wu, Yu-Chih Chen

entry.summary: Presents AstraMoE-SR, a single-image diffusion framework that jointly corrects spatially varying motion blur from pushbroom satellite platform jitter and performs super-resolution, inferring camera trajectory rather than estimating a blur kernel and requiring no auxiliary measurements.

entry.title: Graph neural networks and the energetic cavity method for combinatorial optimization

author.name: Joe Bacchus George, George T. Cantwell

entry.summary: Studies GNNs for finding approximate ground states of Ising models, showing that vanilla GNNs underperform classical mean-field heuristics such as leading-eigenvector methods and the min-sum/energetic cavity method. Small modifications incorporating these heuristics into the GNN are then explored to close the gap.

entry.title: The Role of Uncertainty in Assessing the Fairness of Machine Learning Models

author.name: Francesca Panero, Ernst C. Wit, Marco Scutari

entry.summary: Argues that fairness assessments of ML models, particularly in high-stakes domains, require quantifying uncertainty around model selection and fairness metric estimates, and develops frequentist and Bayesian approaches beyond single point estimates. This addresses a common weakness in the fairness literature where a single model-metric tradeoff is reported.

entry.title: Flexible Motion Generation from Language and Style References

author.name: Kai Weixian Lan, Bodie Criswell, Briana Fedkiw, Zhan Zhang, Joseph Teran, Daniel Holden

entry.summary: FlexMoGen synthesizes human motion conditioned jointly on natural language descriptions and style reference clips, preserving semantic content while transferring fine-grained stylistic traits like timing and articulation. Authored with Daniel Holden, a leading motion-synthesis researcher, it offers artists finer control for animation pipelines.

entry.title: Non-Adaptive 1-Bit Mean Estimation: Minimax Rates and the Sample-Interval Tradeoff

author.name: Ivan Lau, Jonathan Scarlett

entry.summary: This paper studies distributed 1-bit mean estimation and answers negatively the question of whether adaptivity is necessary: for every k>1, a non-adaptive protocol attains the adaptive 1-bit minimax rate under bounded central moments. It also examines the sample-interval tradeoff in query design.

entry.title: A Closed-Form Estimator and Diagnostic Battery for Anchor-Judge Error Correlation, Under a Single-Common-Factor Model

author.name: Veerendra Kumar Sunkavalli

entry.summary: This paper studies when an anchor reference set used to decompose LLM-judge panel error can be assumed uncontaminated, showing that under a single-common-factor model with at least two judges and two anchors, quality variance, common-mode variance, and per-anchor contamination correlations are point-identified in closed form. It also shows a designated clean-anchor estimator can be badly misled by contaminated companions.

entry.title: A Rubric-Guided Large Language Model Solution for Opioid Use Disorder Computable Phenotyping

author.name: Mengxian Lyu, Paredes Pardo, Cheng Peng, Ziyi Chen, Mengyuan Zhang, Jieting Li Lu, Gary M Reisfield, William M Greene, Jenny Lo-Ciganic, Yonghui Wu

entry.summary: The paper presents a rubric-guided LLM framework with Optimization by PROmpting (OPRO) for identifying opioid use disorder from electronic health records, where diagnosis codes are often missing and evidence lies in clinical notes. An expert-derived 18-item rubric steers the LLM to extract supporting text and assign OUD flags, validated against chart review by two physicians on 253 patients including 68 positive cases. This supports clinical interventions through more accurate computable phenotyping.

entry.title: From Two Passes to One: Compact and Efficient Target-Stance Extraction

author.name: Ethan Mines, Bonnie Dorr

entry.summary: This paper introduces a one-pass joint architecture for Target-Stance Extraction that predicts both the target topic and author stance in a single forward pass, cutting trainable parameters by nearly 50% at a modest 4-7 F1 cost. It also shows that standard target-scrubbing evaluation practices artificially depress target accuracy, and that retaining explicit target mentions improves F1 by at least 6 points.

entry.title: Reliability, validity, and diagnostic evidence for multi-model LLM short-answer scoring

author.name: Chunyi Zhao, Chao Li

entry.summary: Evaluates repeated multi-model LLM scoring of short answers on 996 SciEntsBank responses, with GPT, DeepSeek, and Qwen scoring every response across three independent runs on five OCG-PRES rubric dimensions. The study assesses reliability, validity, severity, diagnostic value, and failure cases against official labels, arguing that single-model single-run evaluation is insufficient evidence for assessment use.

entry.title: PTCG: Persona-guided Tree-based Counterargument Generation

author.name: Eunbeen Son, Yohan Jo, Joonsuk Park, JinYeong Bak

entry.summary: PTCG combines Tree-of-Thoughts-style stepwise generation and pruning with speaker-persona selection to produce multiple diverse counterarguments to a claim, estimating the author persona from the original argument. Evaluation via LLM-as-a-Judge, classifier-based, and human assessments indicates improved diversity and persuasiveness over single-counterargument baselines. The work targets balanced discourse and critical-thinking support applications.

entry.title: An LLM-Associated Register Shift in Korean Journal Abstracts: A Morphology-Aware Excess-Vocabulary Study, 2018-2026

author.name: Aron Lee (INTFRAME Research)

entry.summary: Adapts the excess-vocabulary methodology for detecting LLM influence in scholarly writing from English to Korean using morphology-aware statistics on 398,296 KCI abstracts from 2018 to August 2026, with Vietnamese abstracts as comparison. It finds no effect in 2023, onset in late 2024, and a rise through 2025 flattening in mid-2026, with specific words like sisahada appearing far above trend, yielding lower-bound estimates of LLM-processed abstracts. Extends the science-of-LLM-writing literature to a new language and writing system.

entry.title: MeRoTune: RoPE-Safe Merging with a Tunable Dial

author.name: Salman Faroz

entry.summary: Shows that learned correction matrices for weight averaging of fine-tuned models only cancel exactly under rotary position embeddings (RoPE) when they commute with RoPE's per-position rotation, and proposes a RoPE-safe merging fix with a tunable dial. This corrects a subtle but widespread flaw in model-merging methods applied to modern open-weight LLMs.

entry.title: ConversationalVoice: Full-Duplex Speech Data from Real Conversations through Source-Faithful Reconstruction and Conversation-Grounded Expansion

author.name: Richard Yucheng He, Baodong Cao, Chen Xu, Yihang Liu, Tairan Chen

entry.summary: Introduces a pipeline converting real two-speaker conversation excerpts into three training-data artifacts — separated speaker tracks, source-faithful reconstructions preserving turn-taking and overlap, and conversation-grounded expansions — to support full-duplex speech models. This addresses the scarcity of data preserving interruption, overlap, and backchannel behavior.

entry.title: Compositional Multilingual and Behavioral Attribute Steering

author.name: Hyun Gu Kang, Daniil Gurgurov, Tanja Baeumel, Josef van Genabith, Simon Ostermann

entry.summary: Investigates whether additive, training-free composition of steering vectors for language, jailbreak, and conciseness attributes preserves individual steering effects across four instruction-tuned models. Finds single-attribute steering is reliable within appropriate layer-strength combinations, with abstract behaviors favoring middle layers and language favoring earlier layers, and characterizes when two-vector composition succeeds.

entry.title: Which Forms of Caregiver Feedback Support Grammar Learning? A Reinforcement-Learning Study of Child-Like Language Models

author.name: Jing Liu, Marianne Schweitzer, Abdellah Fourtassi

entry.summary: Uses small GPT-2-style models pretrained on CHILDES child-directed speech as controlled learners, fine-tuning them with RL reward models capturing four caregiver feedback types. Structural alignment yields the clearest grammaticality improvements in free generation, offering computational evidence about which social feedback signals support grammar acquisition.

entry.title: Navigating the digital spectrum: Assessing political bias, stability, and downstream fairness in Large Language Models

author.name: Luka Debevc, Nishan Chatterjee, Antoine Doucet, Senja Pollak, Matej Martinc

entry.summary: Introduces a robust Political Compass Test framework sampling 300 configurations across an eight-dimensional perturbation space (language, framing, instructions, format, persona), evaluating eight Gemma 3 and Qwen 3 models across 14 languages and quantization levels. Most models lean Libertarian-Left on average, but instruction phrasing, language, and answer format substantially shift measured coordinates.

entry.title: Seeing Without Understanding: Large Language Model Evaluation of Mobile User Interface Quality, Failure Taxonomy, and Architectural Explanation

author.name: Md Rejaul Korim Sadi, Golam Mostofa Naeem, Toufiqur Rahman Tasin, Syed Mostofa Moosa, Mahmudul Hasan Emon, Mahmudur Rashid, Ferdus Ahmed

entry.summary: This study systematically evaluates LLMs as judges of mobile UI quality using the full RICO dataset of 66,261 screens, refining a 15,000-screen evaluation corpus and producing a failure taxonomy plus architectural explanation of why LLM judgments fall short. It fills a gap in understanding whether LLMs can reliably replace heuristic or human UI evaluation at scale. The taxonomy is useful for anyone building UI-understanding systems.

entry.title: KABURI-TTS: Phoneme-Keyed Activity-conditioned Bi-channel Utterance Rendering for Interaction

author.name: Ryuichiro Higashinaka, Shinnosuke Takamichi, Tetsuji Ogawa

entry.summary: KABURI-TTS synthesizes two-channel conversational speech conditioned on a per-speaker phoneme raster and derived voice activity, aiming to reproduce human-like overlaps, backchannels, and interruptions needed for full-duplex spoken dialogue. The decoupled phoneme module makes the pipeline robust to simultaneous two-party phenomena. This supports research on natural real-time spoken dialogue systems.

entry.title: An overview of 3D Vision-Language Models

author.name: M\'arcus Lobo, Vitor Matias, Afonso Paiva, Jeov\'a Farias, Tiago Novello, Moacir Ponti

entry.summary: A survey of 3D vision-language models that align 3D embeddings with CLIP-style pretrained image and text representations, enabling zero-shot classification, cross-modal retrieval, and open-vocabulary recognition of 3D shapes and scenes. It organizes this emerging area for readers coming from task-specific 3D deep learning backgrounds.

entry.title: CoRe-SAM3: Conditional Semantic--Visual Reconciliation for SAM3 Crack Segmentation

author.name: Shipeng Liu, Liang Zhao, Dengfeng Chen

entry.summary: The paper diagnoses functional differences between SAM3's prompt-conditioned semantic and native visual representations on five crack datasets, finding the semantic stream carries most task information while visual representation utility depends on semantic state. Based on this, CoRe-SAM3 introduces a conditional reconciliation mechanism to fix weak-crack misses, background false activations, and boundary errors in crack segmentation.

entry.title: ChildGaze: A Benchmark Dataset for Collaborative Behavior Understanding in Children

author.name: Sindhuja Penchala, Saketh Reddy Kontham, Prachi Bhattacharjee, S. Nima Mahmoodi, Daniel Fonseca, Sareh Karami, Mehdi Garemani, Sudip Mittal, Shahram Rahimi, Noorbakhsh Amiri Golilarz

entry.summary: Introduces ChildGaze, a child-centered behavioral annotation dataset built on the ChildPlay video collection, labeling each child per frame as collaborative or non-collaborative. The dataset enables research beyond gaze estimation toward higher-level analysis of shared attention and peer interaction in child development.

entry.title: Physico-Geospatial Grounded Scene Interpretation for Mobile Robotics

author.name: Nicolas Schuler, Janik Kurtz, Lea Dewald, Marcel Sauber, F\'elicia Teferle, J\"urgen Graf

entry.summary: Augments the output of frozen, unmodified VLMs for robotic scene interpretation by fusing semantic descriptions with OpenStreetMap building/street data plus positional, temporal, and metric sensor information via LLM-based fusion, demonstrated on outdoor university campus recordings.

entry.title: LASSNet: Level-Aware Availability-Conditioned Spatial-Semantic Fusion for Brain Tumor Segmentation with Missing MRI Modalities

author.name: Haobin Chen, Ao Chang, Rundong Wang, Zhicheng Li, Zhihao Tang, Heqin Zhu

entry.summary: LASSNet tackles brain tumor segmentation when some MRI modalities are missing, hypothesizing that fusion should be conditioned jointly on which modalities are available and on the feature hierarchy. High-resolution lateral features preserve spatial detail while bottleneck features encode cross-modality semantics, and the network adapts fusion accordingly. This matters for robust clinical systems where scans are incomplete due to cost, protocol variation, or patient condition.

entry.title: NutriBench-Kitchen: Benchmarking Embodied AI for Nutrition Management

author.name: Yulin Wei, Xiangchen Wang, Jianhui Pan, Jinyu Xiao, Zheng Tan, Ruozai Tian, Guanhua Chen, Feng Zheng

entry.summary: NutriBench-Kitchen formalizes Embodied Nutrition Management, the task of tracking nutrition-relevant events, maintaining a persistent food state, and performing knowledge-grounded, constraint-aware planning in dynamic kitchens. The benchmark contains 1,500 manually verified question-answer tasks, filling a gap between static food-understanding evaluations and embodied cooking action benchmarks.

entry.title: Proximity-CLIP: Text-Guided Semantic Proximity Learning for Zero-Shot Anomaly Detection

author.name: Manwen Yang, Leqian Ding, Yu Guo, Fei Wang

entry.summary: Proximity-CLIP addresses the geometric dilemma in zero-shot anomaly detection with vision-language models, where enforcing orthogonality between normal and anomalous text prototypes disrupts pre-trained structural continuity. It introduces visually-calibrated semantic proximity learning with bounded dynamic regularization to learn an appropriate semantic margin for guiding visual adaptation.

entry.title: Social Intuition vs. Machine Reasoning: Anticipating Human-Robot Interaction from multiple modalities

author.name: Raphael Lorenzo-Louis, Bertrand Luvison, Serena Ivaldi

entry.summary: This human-robot interaction study benchmarks humans against lightweight pose-based models and vision-language models on predicting whether a person intends to interact, from the service robot's egocentric viewpoint. Using a 100-track pilot subset of HUI360, humans beat pose-only models by a modest margin, but with full video human advantages shrink, suggesting VLMs and models approach human social anticipation in richer modalities. Results inform how robots should decide when to initiate interaction.

entry.title: Re-engineering SORT-based algorithms for low-cost small object tracking from omnidirectional footage

author.name: Xin Shu, Meegan Gower, Yvonne Buckley, Anil Kokaram

entry.summary: This paper adapts SORT-style multi-object tracking to low-cost omnidirectional cameras applied to flying animals in remote environments, introducing a seam-aware Kalman motion model and seam-aware association costs to handle equirectangular projection discontinuities. It matters because most MOT research assumes standard field-of-view cameras and heavyweight appearance encoders, making it ill-suited for cheap 360-degree ecological monitoring deployments.

entry.title: BarkNet-Lite: A Lightweight Texture and Colour Network with the BarkBD Benchmark for Bark-Based Tree Species Recognition in Bangladesh

author.name: Aroshi Ali, Saad Ahmed, Md. Khalid Syfullah

entry.summary: The authors release BarkBD, a 14,258-photo smartphone dataset of 20 Bangladeshi tree species across multiple weather conditions, and propose BarkNet-Lite, a 2.96M-parameter texture-plus-color network trained from scratch achieving about 96.6% single-image accuracy. This supports biodiversity monitoring and forest inventory in tropical regions where taxonomic expertise is scarce.

entry.title: TaskGuard: Task-Conditioned Restoration Utility for Risk-Aware Object Detection

author.name: Vung Pham

entry.summary: TaskGuard studies whether a candidate image restoration actually helps downstream object detection, introducing a post-hoc controller for frozen restoration-plus-detection pipelines that predicts task-benefit via the interaction of restoration residuals with detector sensitivity. Regional counterfactual analysis reveals substantial within-image heterogeneity in restoration utility.

entry.title: SoftRerank: Hierarchical Soft Fusion with Candidate-Label Reranking for Long-Tailed Micro-Action Recognition

author.name: Yichi Zhang, Zhichao Xia, Yanjun Chi, Lingsi Zhu, Yuefeng Zou, Jun Yu, Qingsong Liu, Jianqing Sun, Shengping Liu

entry.summary: This paper tackles micro-action recognition, where subtle low-intensity human behaviors are hard to classify due to weak visual signals and long-tailed label distributions. The authors fine-tune InternVideo2.5 end to end, add hierarchical soft fusion with coarse and group-conditioned heads, and introduce a lightweight candidate-label reranker, combined with class-balanced sampling and inverse-frequency reweighting on the MA-52 dataset. This matters because fine-grained behavioral understanding has applications in healthcare, affective computing, and human-state monitoring.

entry.title: TRIUNE-Net: Harmonizing Scale, Shape, and Efficiency in Pancreatic Tumor Segmentation

author.name: Amir Hossein Saleknia, Alireza Kheyrkhah, Sanaz Karimijafarbigloo, Reza Azad, Sina Houshmand, Ulas Bagci, Dorit Merhof, Alaa Sulaiman

entry.summary: TRIUNE-Net is a lightweight 3D segmentation architecture for pancreatic tumor segmentation in CT volumes, designed to handle extreme scale variability and irregular tumor morphology while remaining deployable in resource-constrained clinical settings. It combines stage-adaptive dilated convolutions for multi-scale context aggregation with serial lightweight shape-modeling components. Its significance lies in balancing accuracy with computational efficiency for medical imaging deployment.

entry.title: GOLF: Global Observation with Local Focus for Calibration-Aware Stereo Interaction Field Estimation

author.name: Minqiang Zou, Riqiang Jin, Zhi Lv, Dong Luo, Lianghai Tian, Zhenyu Zhao, Qi Xu, Tong Wu, Mochen Yu, Yao Tang

entry.summary: GOLF is the first-place solution to the SHOW3D Interaction Field Estimation Challenge at HANDS@ECCV 2026, predicting 3D vectors from hand joints to the closest object point given egocentric stereo views. It combines DINOv3 ViT-H adapted with LoRA, local hand/object evidence sampling, and Plucker-ray geometry, achieving an official score of 27.61 and mean ADE of 27.96 mm, improved further by ensembling. This documents strong competition-level performance in hand-object interaction estimation.

entry.title: Evaluation Principles for MRI-MRA Registration in Trigeminal Neuralgia: An ROI-Centered Neurovascular Benchmark

author.name: Xupeng Zhang, Xihang Wang, Michael Xie, Haoyuan Liang, Hau Ern Lien, Oishika Das, James Feghali, Risheng Xu, Peirong Liu

entry.summary: This paper formulates trigeminal neuralgia MRI-MRA fusion as an ROI-centered neurovascular registration evaluation problem and constructs a clinical benchmark, arguing that whole-brain registration metrics poorly capture the clinically relevant small trigeminal region. It establishes evaluation principles accounting for partial vessel annotations, variable TOF-MRA contrast, and field-of-view mismatch.

entry.title: RGB Input Pipelines: Throughput, GPU Memory, and Transformation Coverage

author.name: Vladimir Iglovikov

entry.summary: A careful benchmark of seven data-loading and augmentation input paths from five libraries, measuring throughput and peak GPU memory across 57 matched recipes on an NVIDIA L4, with 759 recorded measurements. It finds DALI and AlbumentationsX lead on throughput among commonly shared recipes. This is a valuable practical reference for practitioners optimizing training input pipelines.

entry.title: Scene Graph-Driven Haptic Feedback for Safety Enhancement in Robotic Ophthalmic Surgery via Physically Simulated iOCT

author.name: Danial Arbabi, Korab Hoxha, Angelo Henriques, Mirza Imamovic, M. Ali Nasseri

entry.summary: The paper presents a haptic feedback system for robotic subretinal injection that builds a real-time surgical scene graph from simulated intraoperative OCT, then uses a deterministic rule-based engine to generate state-dependent haptic cues on the surgeon's input device. A user study with 16 participants on a phantom head evaluated the system. It addresses the sensory gap in high-precision robotic microsurgery.

entry.title: Inverse Digital Marbling: Recovering Gesture Programs with a Replay Adjoint

author.name: Tianqi Liu, Yushan Han, Hang Liu

entry.summary: This work recovers executable gesture programs for deposition-based digital marbling: given a target image, it optimizes an ordered program of capsule insertions using a replay adjoint that reconstructs intermediate states with an exactly area-preserving, closed-form invertible transport. The PyTorch implementation uses 8.7x less memory than checkpointing baselines at 2,000 gestures. It is an elegant contribution at the intersection of graphics, differentiable programming, and craft.

entry.title: Bundle Length Tradeoffs in Decentralized Multi-Robot Task Allocation Under Degraded Communications

author.name: James Lott, Vahraz Honary

entry.summary: This paper systematically characterizes the role of bundle length B in decentralized multi-robot task allocation algorithms (ACBBA, PI, HIPC) under both ideal communication and 25% packet loss across 300 paired scenarios. It quantifies MinSum cost reductions from increasing B and resolves whether tuning under ideal communication transfers to degraded conditions. This fills a genuine empirical gap in a widely used family of algorithms.

entry.title: RoboDreamer: Anticipatory Humanoid Locomotion with Predictive State-Space Models

author.name: Zhe Li, Yangyang Wei, Xichen Yuan, Zhenzhe Zhang, Weihao Yuan, Shanghang Zhang, Jianfei Yang

entry.summary: RoboDreamer is a two-stage teacher-student framework for humanoid locomotion that trains a teacher on clean observations and distills a student under randomized continuous temporal masking, forcing the policy to infer missing current information from history. At inference the masking interface enables implicit closed-loop action refinement and optional multi-step action chunking, with Mamba as the temporal backbone. This improves stability under imperfect sensing while exploiting temporal context.

entry.title: M3-Tele: A Unified Multimodal Teleoperational Framework for Compliant Whole-Body Mobile Manipulation

author.name: Hengxiang Chen, Shenwen Deng, Yujian Ma, Gan Ma, Qiang Li, Nutan Chen

entry.summary: M3-Tele is a unified teleoperation framework that jointly handles multimodal perception (aligned visual, tactile, force, proprioceptive streams) and compliant whole-body coordination for contact-rich mobile manipulation. It aims to improve the efficiency and quality of demonstration collection, which in turn benefits downstream policy learning. It targets a gap where teleoperation systems treat perception and whole-body compliance separately.

entry.title: Localized Visual Feature Aggregation via Focus Pooling for Visuomotor Policies

author.name: Ruiyu Wang, Zheyu Zhuang, Danica Kragic, Florian T. Pokorny

entry.summary: The paper shows that intermediate CNN features already preserve localized, control-relevant visual context but that existing pooling fails to aggregate it, and introduces FocusPool, an attention pooling module that selectively aggregates localized features for visuomotor policies. This improves data efficiency without input preprocessing like cropping. It is a lightweight architectural contribution for policy visual encoders.

entry.title: A Controlled Comparison of Manual and Teleoperated Intraocular Instrument Motion for an Input Device

author.name: Korab Hoxha, Mirza Imamovic, Angelo Henriques, M. Ali Nasseri

entry.summary: This study rigorously compares manual versus teleoperated intraocular instrument motion in robotic microsurgery, holding instrument, eye model, and tracking constant so the control interface is the only variable. Sixteen participants achieved equal task outcomes on a commercial ophthalmic simulator. It empirically tests the common but rarely measured claim that surgical robot input devices preserve surgeon technique.

entry.title: Can People Distinguish Human and AI Agency in Humanoid Teleoperation? A Preliminary Study of Agency Perception

author.name: Xiang Li, Koya Dendo, Keigo Minamida, Yuto Nakamura, Per Ola Kristensson, Jun Rekimoto

entry.summary: The authors built Ghost-in-the-Loop, a teleoperation framework supporting both human and AI control of a humanoid's voice, expressions, and gestures under a consistent embodiment, and ran a preliminary study (N=50) on whether observers can tell them apart. Participants often could not distinguish human from AI control in brief interactions, relying on naturalness and timing cues. This has implications for transparency, trust, and disclosure in human-robot interaction.

entry.title: Dynamic Latent Space Modeling of Inhomogeneous Poisson Network Processes with Applications to International Relations

author.name: Jie Jian, Owen G. Ward, Jiguo Cao

entry.summary: Proposes a dynamic latent space model for continuous-time relational event data where Poisson event intensities depend on node activity and time-varying latent distances modeled with B-splines. The paper proves identifiability, develops a scalable minibatch SGD algorithm, and applies the method to international relations event data.

entry.title: Compiling VGDL into Causal Models

author.name: Mohit Jiwatode, Bodo Rosenhahn, Alexander Dockhorn

entry.summary: The paper proposes a deterministic framework that compiles games specified in Video Game Description Language into Dynamic Structural Causal Models, enabling causal reinforcement learning with ground-truth causal structure instead of inferring it from noisy gameplay traces or hallucination-prone LLM outputs. This directly targets the problem of RL agents exploiting spurious correlations and LLMs hallucinating game rules.

entry.title: CWF: A Collaborative Writing Framework for Personalized and Reliable Popular Science Writing

author.name: Ruibiao Fu, Di Tang, Yunlong Yang, Ran Wang, Sicheng Lu, Peixuan Wu, Xiaoyu Fan, Jiacheng Ma, HaoZhe Luo, Yang Xiao

entry.summary: The paper defines the task of personalized, reliable popular science writing — adapting explanations to readers of different cognitive levels while preserving factual accuracy — and contributes a 39,134-entry dataset plus the PSCB benchmark evaluating audience adaptation and factual accuracy jointly. It also proposes DA-MoE, which decouples audience adaptation from domain knowledge to reduce data and compute needs.

entry.title: A Three-Tier Persona Vector for Controllable User Simulation in Agentic Evaluation

author.name: Rahul Khedar, Eshita, Sneha Teja Sree Reddy Thondapu, Mayank Malhotra, Arup Kumar Das, Jitesh Chandra Mishra, Arun Menon, Avinash Karn, Mouli V

entry.summary: Proposes a three-tier persona vector with 23 operationalized dimensions (categorical demographics, continuous behavioral traits, and dynamic emotional states) plus scenario difficulty levels, to generate diverse, realistic user inputs for evaluating tool-augmented LLM agents. It addresses the problem that flat role descriptions produce near-identical simulated conversations regardless of scenario.

entry.title: SeRV: Semantic-Aligned Residual Vector Quantization for American Sign Language Generation

author.name: Hongyu Wu, Xu Wu, Tianhao Wu, Jiawei Yu, Phuc Nguyen, Jian Liu, Yi Wu

entry.summary: SeRV introduces a semantic-aligned residual vector quantization tokenizer for American Sign Language motion generation, adding sentence-level and token-level text-motion alignment supervision to a space usually optimized only for reconstruction. This aims to produce semantically consistent, fine-grained ASL motion from limited paired data, an underexplored accessibility application.

entry.title: MemCorr-DP: Counterfactual Correspondence Conditioning for a Diffusion Policy Guided by a Reference

author.name: Tan Su, Haoxiang Yang, Ruxin Wang, Binghui Xie

entry.summary: Presents MemCorr-DP, a diffusion policy for visuomotor control that lifts frozen foundation-model image matches into explicit 3D relations between the current scene and a reference trajectory, trained with a counterfactual paired objective. This improves robustness to simultaneous changes in object position and camera viewpoint over behavior-cloned baselines.

entry.title: Revisiting Thinning Methods for Kernel Learning Problems

author.name: Blanca Cano-Camarero, Yago R. Aguado-Carrillo-de-Albornoz, \'Angela Fern\'andez-Pascual, Jos\'e R. Dorronsoro

entry.summary: The paper introduces Backward Kernel Herding, an algorithm that constructs representative dataset subsets in a Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Space by iteratively removing points rather than adding them, matching state-of-the-art subset selection quality while accelerating the subsampling process when the reduced size is under half the dataset.

entry.title: From Citations to Contributions: LLM-Assisted Credit Scoring of Research Articles

author.name: Sana Ebrahimi, Suraj Shetiya, Abolfazl Asudeh

entry.summary: The paper proposes contribution-based credit scoring for research articles via a contribution tree that decomposes a paper's importance between original contribution and cited prior work, grounded in a cooperative-game view of scientific credit. LLMs serve as noisy comparative estimators of local importance, and the model extends to co-author credit.

entry.title: GoDeep: Annotation-Free Open-Vocabulary 3D Scene Understanding via Language-Space Lifting

author.name: Thodoris Betsas, Anastasios Doulamis, Andreas Georgopoulos

entry.summary: Proposes an annotation-free open-vocabulary 3D segmentation pipeline that uses a vision-language model purely as a translator producing entity-level descriptions, aggregated in a language-only embedding space without a 3D training corpus or per-domain encoder. Achieves competitive results on ScanNet++ and demonstrates cultural-heritage applications. Avoids the bag-of-words limitations of CLIP-space lifting.

entry.title: A budget-dependent crossover between coverage- and response-based training-set selection for machine-learned interatomic potentials

author.name: Jia Bi, Alin-Marin Elena

entry.summary: This study compares structural-coverage versus response-guided (model disagreement) training-set selection for machine-learned interatomic potentials across budgets, retraining MACE models on GAP-20 Carbon and revised MD17. It finds the better selector depends on the retained data budget, with a crossover between the two strategies. The result offers concrete guidance for compressing training data in computational chemistry.

entry.title: Semi-Supervised Learning under Spatially Biased Sampling

author.name: Bright Wiredu Nuakoh, Francky Fouedjio, Stephen Bradshaw, Yaw Kwaafo Awuah-Mensah, Wei Hong Tan, Emet Arya, Ebenezer Afrifa-Yamoah

entry.summary: The paper studies how semi-supervised learning degrades when labeled data comes from spatially biased sampling, independently varying distribution mismatch, spatial autocorrelation, and non-stationarity in a controlled synthetic framework plus real datasets like PovertyMap-WILDS. It diagnoses whether cluster and manifold assumptions survive such bias. Important for geospatial and environmental ML where preferential sampling is the norm.

entry.title: Nearly Tight Rademacher Bounds for Sparsely Activated Neural Networks

author.name: Xiaoyu Li, Zhizhou Sha, Jiaojiao Jiang, Junbin Gao, Andi Han

entry.summary: Provides nearly tight Rademacher complexity bounds for input-dependent sparse activation in one-hidden-layer ReLU networks, removing an explicit dimension factor up to logarithms. Matching lower bounds show how sparse per-input activation changes statistical complexity relative to dense width.

entry.title: LatentMD: Benchmarking Markdown Boundary Failures in LLM-Generated Text

author.name: Sungjune Lee, Myungjoo Kang

entry.summary: Introduces LatentMD, a benchmark and CLI for diagnosing CommonMark fence-boundary failures in LLM-generated Markdown, separating content correctness from format correctness. Across 4,179 prompts and about 37,600 generations from 9 LLMs, boundary failures prove widespread even when content is correct.

entry.title: A Systematic Analysis of Automatic Differentiation versus Discretization-based Constraints for Physics-Informed PDE Solvers

author.name: Xing Guo, Hongwei Tang, Zewei Meng, Yidong Zhang, Shaoqiu Xiao, Feng Liu

entry.summary: Conducts a systematic empirical comparison of automatic-differentiation-based PINN constraints versus discretization-based alternatives, motivated by AD's known weaknesses with higher-order derivatives and discontinuous solutions. Aims to map when each paradigm is applicable for physics-informed PDE solving.

entry.title: Speed Limit for Information Acquisition in Stochastic Learning Dynamics

author.name: Shuta Kobayashi, Andreas Dechant

entry.summary: Formulates SGD as a Markovian process and derives a Fisher-information flow speed limit bounding how fast trainable parameters can acquire information about latent data variables, decomposing information flow into drift and noise contributions. The bound is verified in tractable basis-function linear regression where it reproduces characteristic learning timescales.

entry.title: Some Tokens Behave like Magnets: Revealing Linguistic Organization in the Layers of Language Models

author.name: Andrew Liu, Devan Srinivasan, Gerald Penn

entry.summary: This interpretability study identifies magnetic vectors inside LLMs whose surrounding token representations are systematically elongated or compressed depending on alignment with the vector, in a two-polarity attract-repel pattern. The authors find statistically significant linguistic structure: function words consistently act as repelling magnets in early layers, and magnets reorganize polarity in characteristic ways deeper in the network. This sheds light on how representations self-organize across layers.

entry.title: EviMap: Evidence-Grounded Hierarchical Topic Maps for Exploring Unlabeled Corpora

author.name: Zhiyin Tan, Changxu Duan

entry.summary: EviMap is an interactive system for exploring unlabeled text collections that produces hierarchical topic maps where every label and grouping is traceable to supporting evidence, addressing the trade-off between scale (clustering/topic models) and verifiability (qualitative coding). It emphasizes auditability of the initial thematic map that shapes downstream analysis. The evidence-grounding angle differentiates it from one-shot LLM summarization.

entry.title: Uni-Light: An Ultra-Lightweight Framework via Uncertainty-Aware Knowledge Distillation for Brain Tumour Segmentation

author.name: Libing Kuang, Soren Salehi, Ziling Wu, Ahmad P. Tafti, Armaghan Moemeni

entry.summary: Uni-Light addresses the high computational cost of 3D brain tumor segmentation from multi-modal MRI by combining multi-scale convolutions with an uncertainty-aware knowledge distillation scheme that steers the student model toward hard-to-classify regions, plus a signed distance field boundary loss. The goal is to retain segmentation fidelity in complex tumor regions while drastically reducing compute. This is relevant for deploying segmentation in resource-constrained clinical settings.

entry.title: One for All: Generalist Foundation Model for Cross-Sensor Skeleton Representation Learning

author.name: Jeonghyeok Do, Yun Chen, Munchurl Kim

entry.summary: SOfA is presented as the first generalist foundation model for sensor-unified skeleton representation learning, overcoming heterogeneity in joint counts, indexing protocols, and topologies that previously required sensor- or dataset-specific models. It introduces a fixed scheme to accommodate the dimensional gap caused by varying joint counts and is trained with self-supervised learning on large-scale unlabeled data. This could unify motion understanding across capture modalities.

entry.title: CRISP: Corneal Confocal Microscopy Real-Time Image Stitching Pipeline

author.name: Qincheng Qiao (Department of Endocrinology and Metabolism, Qilu Hospital, Shandong University, Jinan, China), Puli Zhang (Department of Endocrinology and Metabolism, Shanghai Sixth People's Hospital Affiliated to Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine, Shanghai, China), Jian Zhou (Department of Endocrinology and Metabolism, Shanghai Sixth People's Hospital Affiliated to Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine, Shanghai, China), Xinguo Hou (Department of Endocrinology and Metabolism, Qilu Hospital, Shandong University, Jinan, China)

entry.summary: CRISP is an open, real-time image stitching pipeline for corneal confocal microscopy that builds wide-field mosaics of the sub-basal nerve plexus to improve the reproducibility of in vivo nerve health assessment. Existing approaches rely on offline post-processing, extra hardware, or rigid acquisition protocols, which CRISP avoids.

entry.title: When Semantically Consistent Encoding Meets View-Label Heterogeneity Modeling: A Unified Framework for Incomplete Multi-View Multi-Label Learning

author.name: Chengliang Liu, Bo Li, Bob Zhang, Yanghao Zhou, Jie Wen, Wenwu Wang

entry.summary: V2L unifies representation-level and decision-level approaches for incomplete multi-view multi-label learning, combining robust semantic aggregation across partially observed views with label-aware modeling of view-specific evidence. The key insight is that different labels of different instances may require different views, addressed via adaptive rather than fixed fusion. This improves robustness while retaining discriminative view-specific cues.

entry.title: DriftParking: Trajectory Modeling via Drifting Field for End-to-End Automated Parking

author.name: Ziyan Wang, Dong Li, Weibo Wang, Yinyin Lu, Jiayu Xie, Jiamao Gu, Dongpeng Zhang

entry.summary: DriftParking is a one-step end-to-end trajectory generation framework for automated parking that reconstructs the drifting-field paradigm for high-precision conditional generation. It replaces distribution-level attraction with conditional one-to-one attraction toward paired expert trajectories, adding expert-centered constructive repulsion to improve trajectory quality and endpoint alignment in highly constrained spaces. This targets the joint goals of inference efficiency, precision, and executability.

entry.title: Wearable Multimodal Human-Machine Interface for Integrated Hand Intentions Decoding in Dynamic Teleoperation

author.name: Jiaxuan Li, Yinshi Wu, Xiao Zhang, Hongyu Wang, Renzhen Le, Zhenzhi Ying, Liming Shu

entry.summary: The authors present MI-DHMI, a wearable interface combining high-throughput surface EMG sensors with hand- and forearm-mounted IMUs to simultaneously decode hand pose, gestures, and grasping force for teleoperated grasping. A unified decoding framework handles multiple intention types under optically challenging conditions. This advances teleoperation interfaces where camera-based sensing alone is unreliable.

entry.title: A Distributed Consensus Particle Filter for Target Tracking using Autonomous Surface Vessels

author.name: Carter Noh, Kyle Crandall, Connor Yates, Corbin Wilhelmi

entry.summary: The paper augments classical particle filters for decentralized maritime target tracking, strategically spreading particles when agents lack informative updates from teammates to avoid overconfident local estimates under intermittent communication. It is validated with real unmanned surface vessels on a lake. The demonstration on physical hardware under communication constraints is a notable strength.

entry.title: SAFER-Activities: A Dataset for Smart Assessment of Fall Events and Routine Activities

author.name: Diwas Lamsal, Pramod Wickramatilake, Jednipat Moonrinta, Mongkol Ekpanyapong, Matthew N. Dailey

entry.summary: Introduces a 66-hour multi-camera video dataset for fall detection and activity monitoring with 85,310 frame-level annotated instances across 30 action classes, including a dedicated wheelchair-use subset. Benchmarks 2D/3D skeleton and RGB models for online action recognition.

entry.title: Condition aware learning enables robust prediction of oligonucleotide melting behavior across diverse chemistries and assay conditions

author.name: Danielle L. Ferreira, Lifeng Lin, Adam Aslam, Nicholas Chang, Rebekah G. Baig, Edgar Baculi, Zoey Cao, Melanie Senn
