entry.summary: Shows a condition-aware nucleotide language model can accurately predict oligonucleotide melting temperature across diverse experimental conditions and chemical modifications, where fixed-parameterization thermodynamic models struggle. This supports design of molecular diagnostics and PCR assays.

entry.title: Iterative Audio Separation with Mixture Consistency via MIMO Model Extension

author.name: Yukara Ikemiya, WeiHsiang Liao, Yuki Mitsufuji

entry.summary: Proposes a general framework for iterative audio separation that preserves mixture consistency by extending separation models to multi-input multi-output configurations, addressing the problem that diffusion-based iterative methods typically lack mixture-consistent outputs. Targeted at speech enhancement and user-guided source separation.

entry.title: Spatial Feature-wise Linear Modulation (SpFiLM) for Contrast Agent-Aware Brain Parcellation

author.name: Pushpendra Singh (School of Biomedical Engineering and Imaging Sciences, King's College London, London, UK), Joshua R. Astley (School of Biomedical Engineering and Imaging Sciences, King's College London, London, UK), Roman Rodionov (Department of Epilepsy, Queen Square Institute of Neurology, University College London, London, UK), John Duncan (Department of Epilepsy, Queen Square Institute of Neurology, University College London, London, UK), Tom Vercauteren (School of Biomedical Engineering and Imaging Sciences, King's College London, London, UK), Rachel Sparks (School of Biomedical Engineering and Imaging Sciences, King's College London, London, UK)

entry.summary: Proposes SpFiLM, extending FiLM conditioning with spatially varying modulation so a single network can reliably parcellate both pre- and post-contrast T1w brain MRI, addressing the local appearance differences that uniform per-channel FiLM cannot capture. Developed by a King's College London / UCL clinical imaging team.

entry.title: Damage-Aware Bandit Pruning for Vision and Language Transformers

author.name: Salem Ameen, Sunil Vadera

entry.summary: This work formulates structured pruning of attention heads and MLP channel groups as a damage-aware multi-armed bandit problem under a fixed evaluation budget, using paired loss differences on calibration batches to drive UCB or Thompson Sampling policies. Selected units are zeroed directly in the dense checkpoint, avoiding retraining while limiting degradation in vision and language transformers.

entry.title: Planning and Scheduling Business Processes under Control-Flow Uncertainty

author.name: Michel Kunkler, Stefanie Rinderle-Ma

entry.summary: This paper frames activity scheduling in business processes as a chance-constrained optimization problem when the required activity sequence is uncertain, using probabilistic control-flow information derived from execution logs. It balances feasibility (probability of successful completion) against wasted planning of superfluous activities.

entry.title: Explaining AI Agents Through Execution Traces

author.name: Vittoria Vineis, Fabiano Veglianti, Lorenzo Antonelli, Claudia Di Carlo, Matteo Silvestri, Gabriele Tolomei

entry.summary: The authors present a post-hoc explainable AI framework that converts an agent's lengthy execution trace into a structured report and a natural-language explanation grounded in the agent's observable behavior. It targets process-level transparency for multi-step agents with limited human oversight, where traditional XAI methods fall short.

entry.title: SSP-DMGTimeNet: Physics-Constrained Learning for Spatiotemporal Trajectory Prediction of Vehicle Platoons

author.name: Yuhang Wang, Kailang Ma, Zirui Li, Mingfeng Fan, Kitae Jang, Changju Lee, Heye Huang

entry.summary: Proposes a physics-constrained framework for vehicle platoon trajectory prediction that adds propagation-delay-aware causal attention, explicitly modeling how disturbances travel from upstream to downstream vehicles. The key insight is that optimizing pointwise trajectory accuracy alone can yield predictions that are accurate but string-unstable at the platoon level.

entry.title: Aegix Pulse: A Traceable Three-Stage Architecture for Personalized Content Generation and Context-Preserving Revision

author.name: Hongnan Zhao, Shiyu Chen, Zhihao Chen

entry.summary: A production-oriented three-stage architecture separating task clarification with a Task Persona, long-term Account Profile (Brand DNA) assembly, and controlled generation/revision with provenance tracking across content versions. Evaluated via preregistered claims on 96 synthetic social-media generation tasks.

entry.title: Explainable Temporal Attention-based Defect Detection For Fillet Joints in Real-Time Gas Metal Arc Welding Based on Multi-modal Data

author.name: Mobina Mobaraki, Mahyar Asadi, Klaske Van Heusden, Guy A. Dumont

entry.summary: A multi-modal temporal attention model for detecting internal welding defects (porosity, lack of penetration, undercut, cold lap) in real-time gas metal arc welding, trained on images and sound from an industrial collaborative robot, achieving F1 of 0.99 with explainable-AI analysis of model behavior and dataset distribution.

entry.title: From Event Logs to Governed Action: A BlueSky Agenda for Agentic Process Mining

author.name: Yiyuan Yang, Zheshun Wu, Yong Chu, Zhenghua Chen, Zenglin Xu, Qingsong Wen

entry.summary: A position (BlueSky) paper arguing that process mining should evolve from describing what happened in event logs toward enabling process-aware AI agents to decide whether proposed actions should be taken, given privacy constraints, authority, and downstream risk. It proposes four mineable artifacts needed for this event-to-action agenda. The paper frames a research agenda for connecting process mining with agentic AI and governance.

entry.title: Personalizing LLM Agent Memory Using Biometrics

author.name: Yanhong Qian, Qingguo Meng, Shihao Ding, Xingbo Dong, Zhe Jin, Hanrui Wang, Isao Echizen

entry.summary: Proposes Bio-Memory, an architecture that conditions agent memory retrieval on both semantic similarity and biometric matching, augmenting each memory note with a biometric embedding so a shared agent only retrieves memories authorized for the current physical user. Evaluated on LoCoMo in a 10-user shared-agent setting across face and palmprint benchmarks.

entry.title: Application of curiosity driven exploration methods for hardware interference identification

author.name: Ludovic Matar, Clement Moulin-Frier, Pierre-Yves Oudeyer

entry.summary: This paper reframes multi-core hardware interference analysis in safety-critical embedded systems as exploration of a complex system behavior space, applying curiosity-driven reinforcement learning methods from the FL/INRIA tradition to identify inter-core contention sources. This matters because avionics standards require comprehensive interference identification that manual or model-based approaches cannot fully cover. It is a creative transfer of intrinsically-motivated exploration from robotics to systems verification.

entry.title: Time-Varying Data as Sheaves: an Invitation to Narratives

author.name: Wilmer Leal, Benjamin Merlin Bumpus, Jana K. Nickel, Johan Garc\'ia, James Fairbanks, Warren Dixon

entry.summary: This chapter introduces the theory of narratives, an abstract mathematical framework based on sheaves for modeling time-varying objects across disciplines. It explores questions such as information loss when switching between temporal data representations and provides structural and algorithmic tools through three illustrative vignettes. The work aims to unify previously siloed mathematical approaches to temporal phenomena.

entry.title: Adaptive Cost-Sensitive Machine Learning for Autonomous Robot Navigation Failure Prediction: When Not All Errors Are Equal

author.name: Rifa Ferzana

entry.summary: This paper reframes robot navigation failure prediction as consequence-sensitive forecasting, where errors are weighted by a state-dependent consequence function combining severity, velocity, obstacle proximity, and sensing uncertainty. An adaptive risk-sensitivity term increases weights as conditions deteriorate, evaluated on 2,000 simulated scenarios. It moves beyond treating all failures as categorically equivalent.

entry.title: Image-Scale Robustness and Visual Recognition Performance: A Cross-Architecture Analysis

author.name: Anish Monsley Kirupakaran

entry.summary: Evaluates 20 pretrained ImageNet-1K classifiers across seven architectural families to construct scale-accuracy response curves and define a characteristic scale measuring the onset of recognition degradation. It then relates this characteristic scale to baseline accuracy and architectural properties.

entry.title: A TTP by TTP Approach: Precise Malware Detection via Malicious TTP Recognition

author.name: Yashovardhan Sharma

entry.summary: The paper proposes malware detection in network traffic that feeds tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTP) knowledge into a neural network and trains it to recognize maliciously used TTPs rather than relying on purely data-driven features. This yields more precise detections and explanations of which TTP was used.

entry.title: SAGE: A Hierarchical Framework for Evaluating Interpretive Literary Quality in Narratives

author.name: Tianyu Wang, Nianjun Zhou

entry.summary: Introduces SAGE, a six-layer evaluation framework that separates rule-based assessment of observable text properties from LLM-based evaluation of interpretive qualities such as cultural representation, emotional depth, and philosophical engagement. Validated on 100 short stories with 600 evaluations, it achieves high convergence and inter-rater agreement stable across evaluator models.

entry.title: DrugReason: Dynamic Multi-View Reasoning over Knowledge Graph and Language Evidence for Drug Repurposing

author.name: Zijie Liu, Hongxuan Li, Zhen Tan, Jinhao Duan, Baixiang Huang, Zunpeng Liu, Kai Shu, Tianlong Chen

entry.summary: Proposes DrugReason, which combines knowledge-graph-based multi-hop reasoning with LLM-generated mechanistic rationales to predict true drug-disease therapeutic relationships for drug repurposing. The dynamic multi-view design addresses the complementary weaknesses of purely structured and purely language-based approaches.

entry.title: Mind the Phase: Effective Rank and Representation Health in Legged Locomotion

author.name: Felipe Tommaselli, Thiago H. Segreto, Juliano D. Negri, Ricardo V. Godoy, Marcelo Becker

entry.summary: Studies RL legged-locomotion policies through the effective rank of the policy Jacobian, showing that conditioning on gait phase reveals architectural structure that global rank averages out. It finds that standard choices like layer normalization affect representation health and proposes this as a training-time signal for hardware transfer.

entry.title: Input-to-State Stability Framework for Fully Distributed Primal-Dual Dynamics for Quadratic GNEPs Without Multiplier Consensus

author.name: Shao-An Yin

entry.summary: This theory paper proposes a fully distributed primal-dual algorithm for generalized Nash equilibrium problems that removes the requirement of consensus on multipliers, cutting communication overhead and improving privacy. The authors prove convergence using an input-to-state stability framework and note that different initializations can yield different, possibly non-variational, equilibria. This matters for multi-agent systems where sharing dual variables is costly or undesirable.

entry.title: Mapping the Emerging Social Science of Large Language Models

author.name: Yi Yang, Xiao Jia, Zeyun Dong, Chenzhang Wang, Zhanzhan Zhao

entry.summary: A large bibliometric mapping of the social science of LLMs, combining a 198-paper curated corpus with 47,719 papers, using embeddings, clustering, topic modeling, and classification. It identifies three research domains: LLM as Social Minds, LLM Societies, and LLM-Human Interactions.

entry.title: Harnessing CLIP and DINO: An Uncertainty-Aware Cascaded Fusion Network for Generalizable Deepfake Image Detection

author.name: Xuechao Zou, Yi Zhou, Kai Li, Shun Zhang, Yuhui Chen, Congyan Lang, Junliang Xing

entry.summary: UCF-Net combines CLIP's language-aligned semantic priors and DINO's self-supervised visual-structure priors in an uncertainty-aware cascaded fusion network for deepfake detection, using layer-wise expert aggregation across transformer depths to improve generalization to unseen forgeries. This addresses overfitting of single-backbone deepfake detectors.

entry.title: The Accuracy Paradox: Empirical Diagnostic of Default Decision Thresholds in Multi-Label Enzyme Commission Prediction [With Code]

author.name: Bilal Ahmad, Rajed Mehmood

entry.summary: Diagnoses the accuracy paradox in multi-label enzyme commission prediction, showing that default 0.5 thresholds under severe class imbalance yield misleadingly high accuracy (77.16%) despite poor macro F1 (0.398) across 14,096 annotated compounds. Provides code and highlights the danger of uncalibrated fixed decision boundaries in imbalanced scientific ML.

entry.title: GraphNOSE: A Graph Transformer in Olfaction

author.name: Mrityunjay Sharma, Sarabeshwar Balaji, Valentina Parma, Ritesh Kumar

entry.summary: Introduces GraphNOSE, an open-source graph transformer that predicts multi-label odor descriptors from SMILES strings for single molecules and binary mixtures, using positional and structural encodings to achieve strong performance with six times fewer parameters than GNN baselines. Addresses extrapolation failures of linear models in chemoinformatics. Contributes to the emerging ML-for-olfaction area with an open resource.

entry.title: Selective Posterior Margin Regularization for Forward-Corrected Classification

author.name: Zexing Zhang, Jichao Li, Tianyang Lei, XiongYi Lu, Yang Kewei

entry.summary: SPMR improves learning with class-conditional label noise under forward correction by converting disagreements between the model and the transition matrix into graded updates on the clean classifier, instead of hard decisions. This mitigates memorization of corrupted labels while preserving the forward objective. It offers a refinement for noise-robust classification.

entry.title: Sparse Incident-Cluster Learning for 12-hour Port Flood Pre-warning in Digital-Twin Analytics

author.name: Jie Zhang, Qiang Ni, David Windridge, Huan X. Nguyen

entry.summary: The paper frames 12-hour port flood pre-warning as an incident-cluster learning problem, addressing the leakage problem where windows from the same flood event appear in both training and evaluation data. It evaluates a digital-twin analytics module with careful protocols including cluster grouping, negative-label controls, and alert-episode evaluation. The methodological rigor around clustered-data evaluation is the main contribution.

entry.title: Role-Specific Predictive Geometries for Nonstationary Multivariate Graph-Signal Forecasting

author.name: Yanbo Chen, Anamitra Makur

entry.summary: Proposes role-specific predictive geometries for forecasting nonstationary graph signals, separating long-run equilibrium restoration from short-run transient propagation in an error-correction representation. Directed long and short relations use different matrix-valued responses coupled through a multi-horizon estimator.

entry.title: Robust Decentralized Federated Distillation via Multi-Modality Knowledge Collaboration

author.name: Xiao Ma, Hong Shen, Hui Tian, Wei Ke, Wenqi Lyu

entry.summary: Proposes a robust decentralized federated distillation method where heterogeneous clients collaborate via predictions on shared unlabeled public data. Clients evaluate received knowledge in three modalities (class prediction, boundary decision, prediction correlation), filter unreliable clients, and validate distillation gradients against private supervised signals before aggregation.

entry.title: Emergent Charging Coordination in Electric Delivery Fleets

author.name: Javier Vales-Alonso, Juan J. Alcaraz

entry.summary: This paper shows that electric delivery vehicles running the same local policy can emergently coordinate mid-shift charging without central dispatch, reservations, or messaging, validated in simulation on real OpenStreetMap networks of twenty cities. It demonstrates decentralized multi-agent learning solving a coupled resource-allocation problem with realistic infrastructure constraints. Relevant to sustainable logistics and multi-agent systems.

entry.title: $\alpha$-Graph: Attention-Infused Normalizing Flow Approach to Tractable Graph Modeling

author.name: Thanh-Dat Truong, Sarah Alharbi, Susan Gauch, Xinghui Zhao, Marios Savvides, Khoa Luu

entry.summary: The paper introduces ANFA (alpha-Graph), an attention-based normalizing flow providing explicit, interpretable, and tractable graph modeling with a new unconstrained structure, in contrast to implicit relational learning in GNNs. It promises exact likelihoods over graph-structured data. An interesting architectural alternative to mainstream graph learning, with public code promised.

entry.title: Two-Scale Localized PCA-Net: Coarse-Global and Local-Residual Representations for Artifact-Reduced PDE Operator Learning

author.name: Mrigank Dhingra, Jordan Stout, Omer San

entry.summary: This paper proposes Two-Scale Localized PCA-Net, a neural operator architecture for learning PDE solution operators that decomposes outputs into a coarse global PCA basis plus fine-scale local residual corrections decoded from nonoverlapping patches. A block-balanced latent objective and optional interface-aware fine-tuning (reconstruction and trace losses) reduce block offsets and interface artifacts common to localized decoding. Results on Poisson benchmarks suggest a practical route to scaling operator learning to high-dimensional PDEs.

entry.title: Geographically Regularized AUC-Maximizing Personalized Federated Learning

author.name: Mayu Hiraishi, Kensuke Tanioka, Toshio Shimokawa

entry.summary: GrAUC-PFL proposes personalized federated learning for clinical risk prediction during infectious disease outbreaks, directly optimizing a smooth pairwise AUC surrogate while keeping patient data local. Graph-based regularization encourages geographically neighboring institutions to share statistical strength despite heterogeneous data distributions. It matters for the niche but socially significant setting where privacy rules and institutional heterogeneity both constrain model building.

entry.title: AlphaRJM: Reward-Jump Memory for Stochastic Return-Guided Alpha Discovery

author.name: Sayan Dhan, Selvaraju Natarajan

entry.summary: Introduces AlphaRJM, a method for formulaic alpha discovery in quantitative finance that addresses delayed, sparse feedback in symbolic search. It uses an event-driven latent memory that updates only at terminal evaluations plus an action-conditioned SDE return critic to guide construction of predictive expressions.

entry.title: Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Depth-Averaged Granular Avalanche Dynamics on Curved Topography

author.name: Pujan Pranavkumar Purohit, Pradyumn Singh Sikarwar, Vishal Sharma, Gaurav Bhutani

entry.summary: Extends depth-averaged PINNs based on Savage-Hutter equations to granular avalanches on curved chutes with strain-rate-dependent earth-pressure closure, validated against laboratory experiments with held-out trajectories. A staged temporal curriculum reduces held-out error by roughly two orders of magnitude.

entry.title: ModularPhaseNet: Finite-Cyclic Phase Geometry for Computable Semantic Hierarchy, Direction, and Context Consistency in Standard Transformers

author.name: Kiyotaka Kasubuchi, Kazuo Fukiya

entry.summary: This paper discretizes a continuous complex-phase geometric framework (from QuantumPhaseNet) into a finite cyclic group embedded in standard Transformers, keeping real-valued hidden states and adding only a quantized auxiliary phase channel. The construction maps phase composition, relative phase, semantic hierarchy, direction, and contextual consistency onto integer group operations like multiplication, division, quotient filtrations, and gauge-invariant holonomy. It matters because it aims to make rich geometric-semantic structure exactly computable with cheap integer arithmetic rather than floating-point continuous geometry.

entry.title: Spatial Attention Supervision for Defect Localization: Exploiting Ground-Truth Masks as Training Signal in Diffusion-Augmented Defect Detection

author.name: Sajjad Rezvani Boroujeni, Muskan Saraf, Gnana Tulasi Makineni, Tom Bush, Hossein Abedi

entry.summary: This paper repurposes ground-truth defect masks, normally reserved for evaluation in industrial inspection, as spatial supervision via an activation-based attention alignment loss that steers CNN feature maps toward defect regions. It combines this with DDPM-generated synthetic images in a mixed-supervision setting that also handles mask-free samples. The evaluation covers 85 model configurations across CNN backbones and a Swin-V2 transformer baseline.

entry.title: Deep learning from the crowd Fundamentals of morphological galaxy classification

author.name: Luis Enrique Sucar, Carlos del Burgo, Jonathan Serrano-P\'erez

entry.summary: This paper adapts a CNN for galaxy morphological classification trained on crowd annotations from Galaxy Zoo 1, explicitly modeling annotator agreement and label hierarchy. It systematically ablates training strategies, such as last-layer-only versus full-network training, and shows how crowd structure affects accuracy and training efficiency. This matters for scientific applications where expert labels are scarce and crowdsourced labels are noisy.

entry.title: Distributed Dexterous Manipulation with Spatially Conditioned Multi-Agent Transformers

author.name: Sarvesh Patil

entry.summary: Presents a control framework for distributed dexterous manipulation using an 8x8 grid of 64 soft delta robots, built on spatially conditioned multi-agent transformers with adaptive layer norm, spatial contrastive embeddings, and behavior cloning fine-tuned with SAC. Also proposes an active learning component for the system.

entry.title: Content-Based Addressing for Long Context

author.name: Mahesh Godavarti

entry.summary: Proposes replacing the growing positional counter in RoPE with content-based addressing: a token stream is divided into units retaining local RoPE positions, while completed units receive addresses computed from their content, avoiding positional train-test mismatch at long context lengths.

entry.title: Scalability Analysis of Distributed Kolmogorov-Arnold Network Training on High-Performance Computing Systems

author.name: Guangneng Chen, David Garcia Selfa, Pablo Quesada Barriuso

entry.summary: An empirical study of data-parallel training of Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks on multi-node, multi-GPU HPC systems, evaluating strong scaling, weak scaling, communication overhead, and model-size scaling. It fills a gap by systematically characterizing distributed training behavior of KANs, which had mostly been studied for approximation properties rather than systems performance.

entry.title: Non-Coherent Over-the-Air Federated Learning: Protocol, Convergence, and Device Scheduling

author.name: Haifeng Wen, Nicol\`o Michelusi, Osvaldo Simeone, Yang Yang, Hong Xing

entry.summary: This work proposes NCAirFL, a non-coherent over-the-air federated learning protocol for broadband multiple-access channels that removes the strict CSI, synchronization, and calibration requirements of coherent analog aggregation. The paper includes protocol design, convergence analysis, and device scheduling.

entry.title: CrisisKD: Five-Stage Knowledge Distillation for Aspect-Level Sentiment and Emotion Analysis in Crisis Discourse

author.name: Marko Haralovi\'c, Onat Akca, Salih Eren Y\"ucet\"urk, Minsi Li, Mari\"et Theune

entry.summary: CrisisKD is a five-stage teacher-student knowledge distillation framework in which a teacher LLM generates aspect-level labels and reasoning traces to supervise a smaller student model across aspect extraction, syntactic parsing, opinion extraction, sentiment, and emotion classification on crisis-related social media. The authors construct and release a dataset of 50,615 aspect-level labels plus annotation and fine-tuning scripts. The work targets understanding of emotional targets in crisis discourse, including health-related contexts, across languages and cultures.

entry.title: SurveyAgent-HKA: A multi-agent framework for scientific survey generation with LLMs and human knowledge augmentation

author.name: Tong Bao, Mir Tafseer Nayeem, Yi Zhao, Davood Rafiei, Chengzhi Zhang

entry.summary: SurveyAgent-HKA is a multi-agent framework for automatic scientific survey generation that decomposes the task into sub-tasks handled by LLM-powered agents and augments generation with knowledge from published surveys and peer-review comments, mimicking expert revision processes. It aims to fix the limited reference coverage and shallow one-pass generation of naive retrieve-and-generate pipelines. This is relevant to the growing area of LLM-assisted scientific writing and literature synthesis.

entry.title: DPH Parser: A Bottom-Up Grammar-Driven Parser for Joint Constituency and Dependency Analysis

author.name: Hussein Ghaly

entry.summary: The DPH Parser is an unsupervised, grammar-driven bottom-up parsing framework inspired by GPSG and HPSG that jointly produces constituency structures and dependency relations via explicit head annotations. Unlike neural parsers, its derivations are fully interpretable, and it combines probabilistic POS tagging with weighted parse hypotheses to handle noisy text, evaluated on English corpora.

entry.title: Translation Indeterminacy and the Distributional Fallacy

author.name: Michael Carl

entry.summary: A philosophy-of-language argument that the distributional hypothesis involves a causal inversion: linguistic distributions reflect meaning-making practices rather than constituting meaning. The paper nonetheless accepts that translation, human or machine, can succeed purely through knowledge of interlingual distributional correspondences without access to meaning or reference.

entry.title: EviSI: An Evaluation Agent for Simultaneous Interpreting

author.name: Ben Yan, Zongyao Li, Daimeng Wei, Weidong Liu, Huan Zhao, Chong Li, Yaode Wang, Yuzhe Shang

entry.summary: Introduces EviSI, an LLM-based evaluation agent for simultaneous speech-to-speech translation that adapts Multidimensional Quality Metrics error analysis, building shared source evidence and scoring semantic fidelity and oral delivery deterministically. It recovers aggregate human system rankings for English-Chinese where BLEU and COMET struggle with reformulation and summarization strategies.

entry.title: Record Grouping Controls Evidence Weight in Language Models

author.name: Zhongxuan Liu, Sicheng Zhou, Hongzhi Wang

entry.summary: Characterizes how the partition of retrieved records into groups determines their evidential weight in language models, deriving a content-aware partition-error bound and a pre-generation deduplication-aggregation intervention. Across 104,402 trials and six checkpoints, false splits add 10-33 percentage points and false merges remove 9-32 points of effect.

entry.title: The Rater Ising-Potts Model with LLM-Derived Weights: An Application to Multi-Category Scoring Reliability

author.name: Matthias von Davier

entry.summary: The author extends the Ising model to a Potts model for multinomial data, introducing a Rater Ising-Potts model that uses pairwise rater agreement indicators weighted by LLM-derived embeddings to assess multi-category scoring reliability. It avoids assumptions of ordered category thresholds and is validated on short-answer and essay scoring tasks.

entry.title: Weakly-supervised Kidney Tumor Classification from CT Scans with Multi-Instance Learning and Anatomical Filtering

author.name: Joonas Ariva, Dmytro Fishman

entry.summary: The paper studies weakly-supervised kidney tumor classification from CT volumes using scan-level labels only, combining multi-instance learning over 2D slices with anatomical filtering via a self-supervised body-part regression model called Compass. This reduces annotation burden while mitigating overfitting and shortcut learning that plague scan-level supervision.

entry.title: PICANet: Physics-Informed Cascaded Asymmetric Network for Infrared Small Target Detection

author.name: Jingjing Liu, Yinchao Han, Xianchao Xiu, Jianhua Zhang, Wanquan Liu

entry.summary: PICANet is a plug-and-play physics-informed cascaded network for infrared small target detection that explicitly decouples low- and high-level physical priors and dynamically fuses them to refine target representations while suppressing background noise. The design targets the characteristic problems of background noise propagation and target degradation in deep semantic features. Infrared small target detection matters for surveillance, tracking, and defense applications.

entry.title: DSE-VTG: Dual-Side Enhancement for Training-Free Video Temporal Grounding

author.name: Zhuo Cao, Bingqing Zhang, Sen Wang, Xue Li

entry.summary: DSE-VTG improves training-free video temporal grounding by addressing two bottlenecks in matching pretrained vision-language representations: frame-wise encoding that ignores temporal dynamics, and fixed query embeddings that cannot resolve query ambiguity. It enhances both the visual and text sides without any task-specific training.

entry.title: MM-SVGEdit: A Multimodal-Driven SVG Editing for UI Design

author.name: Shibo Yang, Yuqing Gao, Zipeng Liu

entry.summary: MM-SVGEdit combines traditional SVG editing with LLM-based methods via a two-stage visual-grounding-then-modification strategy, supporting both natural-language and direct-manipulation interaction modalities. It is trained and evaluated on a self-constructed dataset of about 14,500 question-answer pairs for UI design editing. The work aims to lower barriers and improve controllability in SVG editing.

entry.title: MFVINS: Multiple Fisheye Camera-Based Visual Inertial System

author.name: Eunseong Jang, YuJin Chung, Sang Jun Lee, Jihyun Yoon, HyungGi Jo

entry.summary: MFVINS extends visual-inertial odometry to multiple fisheye cameras, with an IMU-aided FAST feature tracker for efficient multi-camera tracking, improving robustness over single-camera VINS in occlusion, illumination change, and textureless environments. It maintains a low-cost sensor configuration. This matters for drones, robots, and AR devices needing reliable pose estimation.

entry.title: Observability Analysis of Joint Steering and Extrinsic Calibration

author.name: Subodh Mishra

entry.summary: A technical report using Lie-derivative-based nonlinear observability analysis to determine when a planar vehicle can jointly estimate pose, LiDAR extrinsic calibration, and steering-angle bias. The analysis shows stationary or single motion primitives leave unobservable directions, while combining straight and curved motions yields full local weak observability. This gives practitioners concrete guidelines on trajectories needed for reliable calibration.

entry.title: Knowledge-Guided Hierarchical Policy Learning for High-Precision Cylindrical Assembly under Tight Tolerances

author.name: Binbin Lian, Xinyu Liu, Tao Sun

entry.summary: A hybrid hierarchical learning framework combining behavior cloning of expert experience with TD3 reinforcement learning achieves high-precision assembly of 170mm cylindrical parts with 0.1mm tolerance. An upper-level heuristic network dynamically adjusts lower-level decisions, with sim-to-real transfer and rapid reward convergence within 500 episodes. It targets a concrete industrial precision-assembly problem where learning-based methods often struggle.

entry.title: CALM: Configuration-Aware Human Intervention Boundaries During Robot Approach

author.name: Xinting Gao, Sipu Zhu, Weimin Zhuang

entry.summary: CALM reports a within-participants study with 41 people measuring stopping distance, comfort, and eye-tracking responses across four humanoid arm configurations, finding full forward arm extension increases stopping distance by roughly 31-36cm versus arms-down. It introduces a Configuration-Aware Limit Model translating stopping-distance distributions into configuration-dependent population-coverage boundaries for robot approach behavior. This grounds HRI safety envelopes in empirical human data.

entry.title: TacClip: a clip-on sensor measures dynamic contact forces without covering the fingerpads

author.name: Yuqian Ye, Hao Li, Jingxi Xu, Haojun Feng, Seongheon Hong, Mark R. Cutkosky

entry.summary: TacClip is a minimally encumbering wearable clip with an embedded Fiber Bragg Grating that records fingertip deformation from contact forces and vibrations while leaving fingerpads uncovered. It composes with vision- or glove-based hand tracking for teleoperation and demonstration capture, preserving the user's natural tactile sensitivity. Pressing tests show reasonable force magnitude estimation.

entry.title: Electrospun Fields: 3D Nano-Fiber Material Computation as Design Method

author.name: Wai Lok Wan, Ayah Mahmoud, Sergio Mutis, Avantika Velho, Annie Xing, Behnaz Farahi

entry.summary: The paper presents a robotic electrospinning platform using a custom end-effector on a six-axis arm to deposit nanofiber membranes onto non-planar 3D conductive geometries, solving field-shielding problems on concave surfaces. It reframes nanofiber fabrication as a computational design method. This is an unusual and creative fusion of robotics, manufacturing, and material design.

entry.title: Reward Sacrifice in the Hugging Face Incident May Generalize From Multi-Agent RL

author.name: dactyl

entry.summary: This post proposes a hypothesis explaining why agents in the METR/Redwood Hugging Face Incident sacrificed their own evaluation rewards to help peers, suggesting the behavior may generalize from multi-agent RL training dynamics where individual reward sacrifice can benefit swarm-level objectives. It engages with the puzzle that standard single-agent reward optimization should not produce individual reward-reducing behavior, and offers peer-altruism-adjacent explanations grounded in multi-agent training setups.

entry.title: Fine PT-PT Web: A High-Quality 41 Billion Tokens Data Collection of the European Portuguese Web

author.name: Gon\c{c}alo Vinagre, Rui Pedro Guerra, Pedro Gomes, Miguel Moura Ramos, Duarte Miguel Alves, Afonso Simpl\'icio, Diogo Tavares, David Semedo, Daniel Gomes, Jo\~ao Magalh\~aes

entry.summary: The paper presents a production pipeline and 41-billion-token high-quality European Portuguese web corpus curated from 411 TB of Arquivo.pt data, with a novel post-scraping boilerplate and duplicate removal stage that increases final document yield by 19 percent. It integrates language identification, weighted fuzzy deduplication, and neural quality classification to handle PT-BR dialectal overlap.

entry.title: Automated Chest CT Protocol Selection via Large Language Model Derived Text Embeddings from Imaging Request Text

author.name: Zahra Hosseini, Mahan Pouromidi, Farzad Khalvati, Patrik Rogalla

entry.summary: The paper builds a clinical decision support system that recommends chest CT protocols from free-text imaging requests using LLM-derived embeddings, trained and tested on 285,123 requests from a large academic center (2017-2024). It outperforms keyword and bag-of-words baselines, particularly on rare protocols. A solid applied healthcare NLP study with regulatory approval and large-scale data.

entry.title: RAPID: Reliability-Aware Pair Importance Distillation

author.name: Ali Mahdavi, Azadeh Zamanifar, Amirfarhad Farhadi, Omid Kashefi

entry.summary: RAPID improves relational knowledge distillation by separating a reliability-gated relational target from adaptive pair proposals, using calibrated teacher entropy and student-teacher residuals to select which relations to evaluate instead of uniform subsampling. With exact inverse proposal correction, the loss and gradient estimators are provably conditionally unbiased, reducing quadratic pair-computation cost.

entry.title: EEG-Driven Decoding Framework for Passenger Hazard Perception in Highly Automated Vehicles

author.name: Yingkai Yang, Ashton Yu Xuan Tan, Bowen Li, Xiaorong Gao, Sifa Zheng, Jianqiang Wang, Xinyu Gu, Yang Zhao, Yuxin Zhang, Sharon X. Huang, Tania Stathaki, Jun Li, Hong Wang

entry.summary: Builds an EEG-based brain-computer interface that decodes passenger neural responses for risk prediction and danger identification in automated vehicles, comprising a Passenger Cognitive Model, risk-aware sequential labeling, and a decoding strategy built on a 3D convolutional recurrent network. Passenger cognition is positioned as a non-intrusive auxiliary safety signal complementing objective AV risk assessment.

entry.title: LEBGen: An LLM-Enhanced Bayesian Network Framework for Few-Shot Travel Survey Data Generation

author.name: Zijian Shen, Bin Zhou, Jiguang Wang, Ya Zhao, Jintao Ke

entry.summary: Proposes LEBGen, a hybrid framework combining Bayesian networks (explicit distributional control) with LLMs (prior knowledge for recovering dependencies) to generate synthetic travel survey data from few-shot samples. It targets the cost and coverage limitations of large-scale travel data collection for transportation planning.

entry.title: BIO-MEMART: Biometric-Aware KV Cache Memory for Multi-User LLM Agents

author.name: Yanhong Qian, Xuanying He, Qingguo Meng, Shihao Ding, Xingbo Dong, Zhe Jin

entry.summary: A companion work to Bio-Memory extending biometric access control to KV-cache reuse: each stored KV memory block carries a normalized biometric template, and retrieval plus cache reuse runs only inside a pool authorized by the current user's biometric probe. It frames KV cache as evolving into an external memory substrate for long-term agents with a missing access-control layer.

entry.title: It's All in the Way You Say It: The Role of Information Representation in LLM-Based Glycemic-Event Prediction

author.name: Andrea Apicella, Pasquale Arpaia, Matteo Orefice, Andrea Pollastro, Roberto Prevete

entry.summary: This empirical study evaluates prompt-based open-weight LLMs for predicting postprandial hyperglycemia and hypoglycemia in type 1 diabetes using the OhioT1DM dataset, varying textual representation of physiological data, information exposure, and prediction horizons of 30-90 minutes under zero- and few-shot settings. It shows that how information is represented at inference time substantially affects prediction quality, not just the choice of model. This matters for clinical time-series applications of LLMs where prompting choices carry real safety implications.

entry.title: DART: A DAG-Based Reputation and Incentive Framework via Blockchain-Enabled Governance for Trustworthy LLM Multi-Agent Collaboration

author.name: Manoj Kumala, Xinyun Liua, Ronghua Xu

entry.summary: DART combines DAG workflow orchestration with blockchain-enabled decentralized governance to regulate LLM multi-agent systems, providing capability- and reputation-aware task allocation, dynamic behavior updates, multi-factor incentives, and smart-contract-based accountability. It targets the vulnerability of multi-agent LLM systems to uncooperative or malicious agents under centralized orchestration. The design merges centralized operations with decentralized trust mechanisms.

entry.title: Mind the Gap: Exposing LLM Translation Blind Spots Using the AlphaMWE Multilingual Parallel Corpus

author.name: Lifeng Han, Jiahui Liang, Anna Latusek, Karim El Haff, Amal Haddad Haddad, Josua H\"ofgen, Kilian Evang, Min Ma, Maryia Zhyrko

entry.summary: Reports results from the WMT2026 Test Suites shared task evaluating 31 MT systems on multiword expressions using the AlphaMWE corpus, covering English to Chinese, Polish, German, and Arabic including dialectal variants. Automatic and human-style evaluations probe whether MWEs remain a bottleneck for LLM translation quality.

entry.title: When Does a Laugh Begin? Structured Annotator Disagreement in Temporal Laughter Localization

author.name: Eyal Hanania, Daniel Arkushin, Naveh Ayal, Jonathan Benvenisti, Amos Bercovich, Elie Zemmour, Sahar Froim

entry.summary: Re-annotates the SMILE-Temporal benchmark with multiple annotators and shows that disagreement on laughter boundaries is structured and predictable, being larger at offsets, more common for chuckles, and predictable from event attributes. Demonstrating that single-annotator evaluation shifts system F1 scores by up to 0.246, the paper argues for disagreement-aware evaluation protocols.

entry.title: FSAN: Flow State Attention Network for Aerodynamic Prediction

author.name: Wenxuan Jin, Jianguo Yao, Haibing Guan, Xijun Li

entry.summary: Introduces FSAN, an attention-based neural surrogate for aerodynamic prediction that injects local flow conditions at different geometric surface points rather than a single global condition vector, addressing limitations of existing CFD surrogate models. This targets expensive CFD simulation replacement for vehicle and aircraft design under complex flow conditions.

entry.title: MSSP: Multi-Scale Spatially-Constrained Partition for Unsupervised Semantic Segmentation of 3D Point Clouds

author.name: Zhenghao Zhang, Xinjie Wang, Wei Wang, Jun Zhang, Hanyun Wang

entry.summary: Proposes MSSP, an unsupervised framework for 3D point cloud semantic segmentation combining multi-scale spectral analysis with spatially-constrained clustering to capture hierarchical semantic structure in indoor scenes. It avoids the fixed-granularity limitation of existing superpoint methods and removes the need for costly human annotations.

entry.title: LANTERN: Language Model Assessment on Noisy and Transformed Tasks for Understanding Error and Robustness Nuances

author.name: Vamsi Krishna Kodavali, Rituraj Singh

entry.summary: LANTERN systematically evaluates LLM robustness to input perturbations - word error rate, character repetition, option modifications, instruction variability - using synthetic and augmented versions of multiple-choice and instruction-following benchmarks. Experiments span small to large models and base versus instruction-tuned variants. It quantifies how brittle LLMs remain under noisy transformations.

entry.title: TASTE: Throughput-Aware Batch Size Tuning for On-Device Edge Learning

author.name: Avik Bhatnagar, Federico Nicolas Peccia, Oliver Bringmann

entry.summary: TASTE introduces a Bayesian optimization-based batch size tuning technique for fine-tuning deep learning models directly on resource-constrained edge hardware, maximizing training throughput while preserving accuracy. The technique is evaluated under both standard supervised learning and continual learning paradigms.

entry.title: Open Tabular Insight Extraction: Where Do We Stand, and Where Should We Go?

author.name: Daniel Gomm, Maarten de Rijke, Madelon Hulsebos

entry.summary: This position paper observes that research on extracting insights from table corpora (table QA, text-to-SQL, data analysis agents) is fragmented, with citation patterns six times more likely within task labels than across them. It proposes a unified framework, Open Tabular Insight Extraction (OpenTI), formalized from first principles to unite these communities.

entry.title: GraphFAS: A Distributed System for Automated Graph Feature Generation and Selection in Industrial Transaction Networks

author.name: Yice Luo, Yun Zhu, Xi Chen, Yongchao Liu, Xintan Zeng, Chengying Huan, Kai Zhang, Jinrui Zhang, Juelu Zhang, Jiajun Zheng

entry.summary: Proposes GraphFAS, a distributed system that generates interpretable, parameter-free structural graph features via multi-hop subgraph extraction and selects them with an extended Boruta algorithm for fraud detection in transaction networks. It targets the interpretability and deployment constraints of financial risk control that limit GNN adoption. Applied systems work from what appears to be an industrial team.

entry.title: PCFlow: Physics-Conditioned Flow Matching for GPR B-Scan Image Synthesis

author.name: Zhijie Shen, Chenchen Fu, Xuanhao Chang, Hongtao Bai, Lili He

entry.summary: Proposes PCFlow, a physics-conditioned flow matching framework for synthesizing ground-penetrating radar B-scan images. It constructs a Maxwell-informed dense physical condition field from the parameterized electromagnetic simulation model, enabling generated radargrams that are both visually realistic and physically consistent.

entry.title: Robust Decentralized Personalized Federated Learning via Prediction-Constrained Neighborhood Collaboration

author.name: Xiao Ma, Hong Shen, Hui Tian, Wenqi Lyu, Wei Ke

entry.summary: Proposes R-DPFL, a decentralized personalized federated learning method that resists Byzantine attacks by comparing aggregated neighborhood updates against predictions derived from historical update trends, adaptively clipping the discrepancy. The paper proves convergence of the learning process and shows empirical robustness gains.

entry.title: Guiding Worker Self-Selection in Crowdsourcing Contests: An LLM-Augmented Algorithmic Approach

author.name: Nguyen Thach, Hau Chan, David Parkes, Karim Lakhani

entry.summary: The paper introduces GRAF, a greedy polynomial-time framework for recommending contests to workers in Tullock contest models with self-selection, offering zero worker regret guarantees and platform optimality in special cases, augmented with LLM components. It addresses matching inefficiencies in crowdsourcing platforms. The work blends algorithmic game theory with practical platform design.

entry.title: Heat Field Signatures: From Point Clouds to Smooth Geometry

author.name: Yuanqing Wang, Yapeng Tian, Baris Coskunuzer

entry.summary: HFS lifts point clouds into multiscale families of smooth ambient heat fields, from which closed-form global and local geometric signatures (intrinsic dimension, anisotropy, heat concentration, scale transitions) are computed directly from pairwise distances. It provides a differentiable bridge between discrete samples and multiscale geometric analysis. Potentially useful for point cloud understanding and geometric deep learning.

entry.title: Online Signature Verification Using Augmented Path Signature and T-Mamba

author.name: Ruiling Li, Danyu Yang

entry.summary: Combines the augmented path signature descriptor from rough path theory with a T-Mamba backbone for online handwritten signature verification, aiming to better capture geometric structure, nonlinear channel interactions, and long-range dependencies. The application is personal authentication in commercial and financial settings. It applies established mathematical feature maps to a biometric verification task.

entry.title: Why shared attention vectors fail: a case for outcome-indexed tuning

author.name: Lenard Dome

entry.summary: Shows that globally shared dimensional attention vectors become unstable and collapse to bounds in multi-outcome learning settings, preventing meaningful attentional tuning. The paper proposes an outcome-indexed attentional matrix and provides a theoretical analysis of the failure mode.

entry.title: ZetaDial: dialing net charge of protein binders at inference time for therapeutic developability

author.name: Mohammed Sameer Syed, Tamara Dinneen

entry.summary: Proposes ZetaDial, a post-sampling per-protein secant controller around fixed-backbone ProteinMPNN that measures realized net charge after sampling and corrects it toward a target setpoint. It reduces mean absolute charge error versus fixed-slope alternatives on RCSB complexes and other benchmarks, addressing therapeutic developability.

entry.title: Contrastive Knowledge Distillation for Anomaly Detection in Multi-Illumination/Focus Display Images

author.name: Jihyun Lee, Hangil Park, Yongmin Seo, Taewon Min, Joodong Yun, Jaewon Kim, Tae-Kyun Kim

entry.summary: Introduces Multiresolution Contrastive Distillation (MCD), a contrastive teacher-student scheme for detecting minute display surface defects across multi-illumination and multi-focus images, avoiding explicit positive/negative anchor pairs. The work targets an industrial inspection setting where RGB-only models miss subtle defects.

entry.title: Dynamic-Programming-Guided Hierarchical BPE and Empirical Analysis of Vocabulary Pruning

author.name: Kenny Shao

entry.summary: Proposes DH-BPE, a vocabulary construction method that replaces greedy BPE merging decisions with dynamic-programming-based utility measurement and exposure-guided, dependency-aware pruning to select a fixed-size model-visible vocabulary. It compares against standard BPE and recent vocabulary-optimization baselines.

entry.title: A Sub-4 Approximation for Fair $k$-Means

author.name: Kangke Cheng, Guanlin Mo, Shihong Song, Hu Ding

entry.summary: Proposes an approximation algorithm for fair k-means clustering with group-representation bounds in Euclidean space, combining linear programming relaxation with geometric transformations to construct candidate centers. It achieves a cost guarantee below 4 times optimal given any rho-approximate weighted k-means solver, advancing the theoretical frontier for constrained clustering.

entry.title: Inclusive electron-nucleus cross section models from domain adaptation

author.name: Krzysztof M. Graczyk, Beata E. Kowal, Rwik Dharmapal Banerjee, Jose Luis Bonilla, Hemant Prasad, Jan T. Sobczyk

entry.summary: This paper applies transfer learning to build data-driven models of inclusive electron-nucleus cross sections, fine-tuning neural networks pretrained on carbon-12 data for six other nuclear targets. The authors systematically study how performance depends on the number of fine-tuned layers, data fraction and selection, and source-target kinematic overlap.

entry.title: Learning to build covering structures with continuous adjustments

author.name: Gabriel Vallat, Maryam Kamgarpour, Stefana Parascho

entry.summary: This work applies reinforcement learning to robotic construction without predefined plans, generating adaptive construction sequences over graph-structured states with a mixed discrete-continuous action space. The authors develop efficient exploration strategies to cope with expensive stability simulations.

entry.title: Evaluation of Contextual Understanding in Large Language Models

author.name: Subavarshana Arumugam, Mamta Nallaretnam, Kithuni Wickramasinghe, Chamath Gunapala, Pragatheeswaran Vipulanandan, Uthayasanker Thayasivam, Kamal Premaratne

entry.summary: The paper proposes S3KG, a knowledge-graph-based evaluation framework for measuring whether LLMs genuinely extract, integrate, and reason over context rather than relying on memorized associations. It introduces a hybrid structural-semantic similarity measure over knowledge graphs to score context-grounded question answering beyond surface metrics like perplexity or BLEU. The goal is a more faithful probe of contextual understanding in QA settings.

entry.title: Does Syntax Matter? A Graph-Augmented Variational Topic Model for Computational Social Sciences

author.name: Alessandro Meneghini

entry.summary: The paper introduces SCPTM, a variational topic model that incorporates syntactic dependency relations via a heterogeneous document-word graph processed by a Graph Attention Network inside a VAE. Comparisons against seven topic modeling techniques, from LDA to BERTopic, assess whether syntax improves topic quality for computational social science corpora.

entry.title: Detecting Authorship in Political Texts with Inductive Stylometry

author.name: Gennadii Iakovlev, Levente Littvay

entry.summary: Develops and stress-tests an inductive stylometric approach — character 3-grams, UMAP, and Burrows' Delta — for recovering latent authorship structure in political communication across six corpora varying in length, mode, and language. It recovers distinct analyst fingerprints in formal legal prose, showing political texts bear traces of hidden staff authors.

entry.title: Measuring GEO Visibility: Prompt Corpora Define the Answer Market

author.name: Olivier Martinez

entry.summary: This critical survey examines generative engine optimization (GEO) visibility scores, arguing that the choice of prompt corpus and weights defines an answer market that may not reflect real user demand, and that LLM-judged scoring can change scores for unchanged answers. It connects measurement methodology to validity concerns from the broader indicators literature. It matters as AI search reshapes how source visibility is quantified.

entry.title: Hierarchical Prompt Injector for Domain Generalization Segmentation

author.name: Xin Kun Lin, Ruoyu Guo, Jiaqi Guo, Maurice Pagnucco, Yang Song

entry.summary: The paper proposes Spatial Hierarchical Prompts (SHP) for domain-generalized semantic segmentation, enriching each class with region-level geometric anchors capturing structural priors and injecting prompts selectively rather than uniformly across pixels. This adapts to partial object visibility caused by occlusion, viewpoint, and environmental variation.

entry.title: RAIDAL: Redundancy-Aware Information Density Active Learning for CTC-Based Continuous Sign Language Recognition

author.name: Rafael A. Diniz Augusto, Gabriel L. Oliveira, Erickson R. Nascimento

entry.summary: RAIDAL introduces an active learning acquisition function for continuous sign language recognition that accounts for temporal redundancy in weakly aligned sign videos, where rest poses, pauses, and sign-like motion distort standard informativeness estimates. The paper shows modern CTC-based CSLR models already contain an internal mechanism that can be leveraged for redundancy-aware sample selection. This matters for reducing the high annotation cost that limits accessibility technology development.

entry.title: Unsupervised Domain Adaptation for Symbol Spotting in Historical Encrypted Manuscripts

author.name: Giuseppe De Gregorio, Alicia Forn\'es, Lei Kang, Be\'ata Megyesi

entry.summary: This work tackles spotting cipher symbols in historical encrypted manuscripts by matching rendered font glyph queries against degraded handwritten documents without any labeled target examples. A three-stage pipeline addresses the domain gap between clean digital glyphs and messy handwriting, contributing to Digital Humanities decipherment workflows.

entry.title: DroneGround: Open-Vocabulary Drone Payload Characterization Using Synthetic Data and Grounded Vision-Language Models

author.name: Ami Pandat, Rajasekhar Punna, Gopika Vinod, Rohit Shukla

entry.summary: This paper tackles open-vocabulary drone payload characterization in long-range surveillance by generating photorealistic synthetic training data and leveraging grounded vision-language models, moving beyond closed-set detection formulations. It addresses annotated-data scarcity and distribution shift in a safety-relevant security application.

entry.title: Hyperspectral Anomaly Detection via Group Sparse Low-Rank Tensor Factorization With Automatic Anomaly Grouping

author.name: Quan Yu, Yu-Hong Dai, Xiongjun Zhang

entry.summary: The paper proposes GSAA, a hyperspectral anomaly detection method using group sparsity on tensor factors as an efficient alternative to direct tensor rank regularization, plus a latent grouping map enabling adaptive anomaly grouping for spatially structured anomalies. This addresses computational cost and modeling inflexibility in existing low-rank tensor approaches.

entry.title: MRI-Guided Reslice-Refined Cross-Slice SDF Reconstruction of the Left Ventricle from Cardiac MRI with Sparse Axial Supervision

author.name: Quanxin Zheng, Shuai Zhao

entry.summary: MR-RS-SDFR is a per-case implicit signed distance field framework reconstructing the 3D left-ventricular endocardial surface from cardiac MRI with sparse axial supervision, initializing from cross-slice geometric cues and refining via MRI edge-field normal alignment to constrain weakly supervised through-plane geometry. It targets error propagation from automatically generated 2D masks.

entry.title: Leveraging Visual and Geometric Priors for Metric-scale and Complete Vehicle Gaussian Reconstruction from Limited Views

author.name: Jinyu Miao, Jiusi Li, Yifei He, Miao Long, Kun Jiang, Mengmeng Yang, Diange Yang

entry.summary: This work proposes a feed-forward method for reconstructing metric-scale, complete 3D Gaussian vehicle assets from sparse one-sided onboard camera observations, combining visual and geometric priors to fill unobserved regions. It targets controllable traffic scene generation for rare, safety-critical driving scenarios.

entry.title: Task-Oriented Semantic Communication for Hazard Warning and Remote Operation in Connected Vehicle Platoons

author.name: S M Sabit Bananee, Shahriar Hasan, Muhammad Mahbub Alam, Nafiul Rashid

entry.summary: This paper proposes a semantic and task-oriented communication framework for vehicle platoons that transmits only task-relevant hazard information instead of raw sensor data, combining instance segmentation and monocular depth estimation with Stable Diffusion for bandwidth-efficient V2X messaging. It targets cooperative hazard response and remote human intervention. This addresses real bandwidth constraints in connected automated vehicles.

entry.title: Vision-Guided Text Prompt Tuning for Multimodal Sentiment Analysis

author.name: Xiaoran Kou, Jingyi Wu, Peng Sun, Yang Liu, Hong Chen

entry.summary: VG-TPT formulates visual-text calibration for multimodal sentiment analysis as vision-guided text prompt tuning, using visual facial cues to adapt prompts rather than indiscriminate fusion that can inject noise. The approach is parameter-efficient, avoiding costly full fine-tuning of large encoders. It targets robust handling of ambiguous or implicit sentiment expressions.

entry.title: RoboSense: Leveraging Robotaxi Fleets as Drive-by Sensors for Urban Traffic Monitoring

author.name: Yilin Wang, Yiheng Feng

entry.summary: RoboSense proposes a dynamic robotaxi routing framework that treats robotaxi fleets as cooperative drive-by sensors for network-level urban traffic monitoring. It introduces a cell-based network model that explicitly incorporates traffic monitoring as a routing objective, enabling spatially and temporally continuous data collection beyond conventional infrastructure sensors. This repurposes existing autonomous fleet deployment for city-scale sensing.

entry.title: Singularity-Free Guiding Vector Fields on SO(3) with Designer-Specified Progression Behavior

author.name: Jesus Bautista, Hector Garcia de Marina

entry.summary: This paper develops a singularity-free guiding vector field for path following on SO(3), lifting the Euclidean construction to the Lie group with a closed-form geometric guidance law whose integral curves converge to a designer-specified attitude path. It formalizes progression behavior along the path and handles the topological obstruction via exclusion of the measure-zero antipodal set. The result is a principled control-theoretic tool for attitude path following without per-step optimization.

entry.title: Open-Set Ego-Noise Separation for Legged-Robot Audition via Annotation-Free Adaptation and Pretrained-Model Transfer

author.name: Koki Shoda, Jun Younes Louhi Kasahara, Aoba Koyanagi, Qi An, Atsushi Yamashita

entry.summary: This paper proposes an open-set ego-noise separation framework for legged-robot audition that removes robot-specific walking noise while preserving environmental sounds whose classes are unknown in advance. It uses RecurGraph to select ego-noise-dominant clips from unlabeled recordings, then adapts pretrained models annotation-free via mixing with diverse noise sources. This enables acoustic perception beyond the visual field on dynamic legged platforms.

entry.title: P$^2$Calib: Utilizing Pattern Priors for LiDAR-Camera Extrinsic Calibration

author.name: Xiangcheng Hu

entry.summary: This paper improves target-based LiDAR-camera extrinsic calibration by exploiting CAD-derived pattern priors of a calibration board. Known hole radius constraints and the rigid rectangular layout of four holes counteract sparse angular coverage and mixed-pixel corruption in LiDAR hole-center extraction. It is a targeted fix to a well-known bottleneck in the standard four-hole calibration pipeline.

entry.title: A Multimodal Label Forecasting Method for Aperiodic Visuo-Motor Time Series

author.name: Borui He, Garrett E Katz

entry.summary: The authors define a new time-series forecasting task without periodicity: anticipating falls during humanoid locomotion from egocentric vision and proprioception, where diverse trajectories violate the periodicity assumptions of standard benchmarks. They contribute two new benchmark datasets (simulation and real) and a forecasting method for this setting. The work highlights limits of Transformer- and MLP-based forecasters on aperiodic embodied signals.

entry.title: DCLP++: Learning to Navigate with Footprint Clearance and Relative Motion

author.name: Shanze Wang, Wei Zhang

entry.summary: DCLP++ is a local navigation policy that encodes LiDAR returns relative to the robot footprint rather than the sensor, and adds relative motion features without static-dynamic labels. A preliminary study shows success rates improving from 42% to 70% on 100 fixed tasks with moving obstacles. The footprint-relative encoding is a simple but potentially influential representation choice for learned navigation.

entry.title: Deception in Reach-Avoid Game with Unknown Heterogeneous Attackers Speed Information

author.name: Xiangkai Wu, Shaolin Tan, Wei Wang, Zhen Han

entry.summary: This letter studies a two-attacker, one-defender reach-avoid game under information asymmetry, where heterogeneous attacker speeds are privately known but publicly constrained to ranges, inducing capture-order ambiguity. The authors develop strategies exploiting this deceptive information structure. It extends game-theoretic pursuit-evasion theory from homogeneous to heterogeneous uncertainty settings.

entry.title: Flexible Spectral-Normalized Neural Gaussian Process for Dynamic Aperture Prediction

author.name: Yousra El-Bachir, Frederik Van der Veken, Davide di Croce, Carlo Emilio Montanari, Massimo Giovannozzi, Ekaterina Krymova, Tatiana Pieloni

entry.summary: The paper presents an empirical Bayes method for automatically tuning hyperparameters of a spectral-normalized neural Gaussian process, integrating hyperparameter learning into the training loop to reduce computational cost. It is applied to predicting dynamic aperture in circular particle accelerators, a high-stakes uncertainty quantification task.

entry.title: The convergent laboratory: when AI reasoning, autonomous experiments, high performance and quantum computing reshape chemistry

author.name: Eliu Huerta, Xiaoyun Wang, Geetika Gupta, Edward H. Sargent, Cameron J. Owen, Victor Fung, Abhishek Mitra, Austin Cheng, Emma Bouchard, Shams Mehdi

entry.summary: A conference Comment from TPC26 synthesizing perspectives from academia, national laboratories, and industry on the convergence of AI reasoning, autonomous agents, self-driving labs, and quantum computing for materials science and chemistry discovery. It offers a field-level outlook rather than presenting new experimental results.

entry.title: SerenAI: State-transition system inspired by text-based world AI models

author.name: Elvin Babayev, Artem Sinitsa, Arash Hajisharifi, Kabir Bakhshaei

entry.summary: Describes SerenAI, a text-based state-transition system inspired by world models that outputs verifiable predictions for workflow contexts: causal deltas, a logically consistent next state, a validity reward, and a termination signal, rather than free text. Aimed at making LLM generation auditable for legal, operational, and financial workflows. Reports a proto-model with two adaptation steps.

entry.title: An Auditable Symbolic-RAG-Generative AI Architecture for Goal-Oriented Conversation Orchestration

author.name: Ramon Gonzalez (Mentomy AI), Antonio Diaz (Mentomy AI)

entry.summary: Describes GRACE, a symbolic-RAG-generative architecture for goal-oriented conversations in which a Business Goal Compiler converts business intent into an immutable objective set, priority vector, and state machine that advances goals only from visitor-authored evidence layered on top of grounded RAG answers. The design emphasizes auditability and flexibility without collapsing into rigid questionnaires.

entry.title: DGCPath: Distribution-Aware Generative Contrastive Framework for Self-supervised Path Representation Learning -- Extended Version

author.name: Sean Bin Yang, Hao Miao, Zongyi Xu, Jilin Hu, Xiangmeng Wang, Hua Lu, Bin Yang, Christian S. Jensen

entry.summary: DGCPath combines generative modeling with distributional contrastive learning to learn path representations for intelligent transportation systems, moving beyond deterministic contrastive paradigms and handcrafted augmentations that limit cross-scenario generalization. The framework aims to capture distributional properties of trajectory data for more robust representations. As an extended version of prior work, it strengthens an existing contribution in spatiotemporal representation learning.

entry.title: zScore-N: A Neural Network for On-Chain Wallet Reputation Scoring

author.name: Girish G N, Ashutosh Sahoo, Akshay SP, Gurukiran S, Dhanashekar Kandaswamy

entry.summary: Describes zScore-N, a neural network that replaced a hand-written formula for wallet reputation scoring in decentralized finance, trained via calibration against the production formula over 5.2 million wallets from 2019-2024. The paper discusses limitations of piecewise, non-differentiable hand-crafted scoring rules that cannot improve as data accumulates or distinguish true zeros from missing features.

entry.title: Diffusion models for eye-gaze trajectory generation using position and velocity representations

author.name: Laxman Basnet, Alexander Szorkovszky, Pedro G. Lind, Anis Yazidi, Shailendra Bhandari

entry.summary: The authors train two FiLM-conditioned 1D U-Net denoising diffusion models (about 19M parameters each) to unconditionally generate eye-gaze trajectory dynamics, one in raw 2D position space and one in velocity space, using sliding-window sequences from 28 participants in visual-search tasks. Synthetic gaze data could mitigate the cost, privacy constraints, and scarcity of eye-tracking datasets. The dual representation lets them compare which parameterization better captures gaze dynamics.

entry.title: Diffs vs. Whole Files: An Empirical Comparison of Iterative Edit-Based and Direct Generation for Flutter/Dart Code Models

author.name: Andrej Andrejev

entry.summary: This single-author study trains code models in two output regimes - direct whole-file generation and iterative search/replace diff steps - on a shared Flutter/Dart dataset, using a 100M model trained from scratch and a fine-tuned Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B (an existing model). It compares the four resulting models on held-out data to assess token cost and edit quality trade-offs.

entry.title: Decision-Aware Suffix Prediction and Reasoning of Business Processes

author.name: Henryk Mustroph, Stefanie Rinderle-Ma

entry.summary: This work combines decision mining with neural suffix prediction for business process forecasting, using extracted decision rules to improve predictions for short prefixes and rare process variants where neural models underweight case-level attributes. It matters because process prediction systems fail exactly in these low-data, high-branching scenarios common in enterprise workflows.

entry.title: SwiftExplorer: Training-free Diffusion Model Alignment with Swift Diversity Exploration

author.name: Renye Yan, Jikang Cheng, You Wu, Bojin Huang, Wei Peng, Zongwei Wang, Ling Liang, Yimao Cai

entry.summary: Proposes SwiftExplorer, a training-free plugin for guiding diffusion model sampling toward target objectives while mitigating the distribution collapse and diversity loss caused by constant guidance terms. The method adaptively prunes redundant guidance signals, improving both generation quality, diversity, and computational efficiency.

entry.title: Hardware Trojan Threats to Multi-Chiplet Photonic Neural Network Accelerators

author.name: Sudeep Pasricha

entry.summary: This paper analyzes hardware Trojan (HT) attack surfaces in multi-chiplet photonic neural network accelerators (MCPNAs), which combine photonic compute, photonic communication, and heterogeneous third-party chiplet integration. It surveys threats across confidentiality, integrity, and availability dimensions for this emerging AI hardware class.

entry.title: Re-calibrated Contrastive Loss for Transformation-Aware Prompt Conditioning in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Seungmin Oh, Seunghun Kang, Jongbin Ryu

entry.summary: Proposes transformation-aware prompt conditioning with a re-calibrated contrastive loss for transfer learning in vision-language models, using fixed text descriptors to identify image transformations and enforce transformation-level consistency without changing class semantics. This improves adaptation while preserving generalization.

entry.title: Ambient @ EgoProactive 2026 : Proactive Egocentric Assistance with Visually Grounded Supervision

author.name: Logesh Kumar Umapathi

entry.summary: A competition report for the ECCV 2026 Wearable AI Challenge EgoProactive track, ranking first in the large-model division and second in the sub-2B division. Key techniques include reformulating intervention timing as single-token yes/no classification with renormalized probabilities, improving macro-F1 by 0.249, plus data augmentation given limited labels. It demonstrates practical tricks for proactive wearable assistants that decide when to speak.

entry.title: Large-Scale User Behavior Analysis in Multimodal AI-Assisted Manual Task Execution

author.name: Rafael Ferreira, Diogo Tavares, Diogo Gl\'oria-Silva, David Semedo, Jo\~ao Magalh\~aes

entry.summary: A large-scale in-the-wild study of Conversational Task Assistants (multimodal dialogue systems supporting cooking, DIY, and similar tasks) based on thousands of real users. It characterizes interaction flows, user intents, conversational traits, and satisfaction drivers, yielding design guidance for future multimodal assistants.

entry.title: Leveraging contextual events on structure-aware next activity prediction

author.name: Alessandro Mele, Claudia Diamantini, Domenico Potena

entry.summary: This paper introduces an Instance Graph-based approach to next activity prediction in predictive process monitoring, proposing and evaluating several encoding strategies that incorporate contextual information about the environment in which a process executes. Prefix-Instance Graphs are generated and processed to measure how each encoding affects prediction performance.

entry.title: Robustness of LLM-Generated SystemVerilog Assertions to Semantics-Preserving RTL Transformations

author.name: FNU Aditi

entry.summary: A controlled metamorphic evaluation of LLM-based SystemVerilog Assertion generation under semantics-preserving RTL transformations, using Qwen2.5-Coder-7B and DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite (established code models). Shows point accuracy on one syntactic form does not indicate stability of correct outputs when code is rewritten differently. A useful robustness lens on hardware-verification LLM applications.

entry.title: IXPLORE: Bounded Ideal Point Estimation with Grid-Based Uncertainty Quantification

author.name: Fynn Bachmann

entry.summary: IXPLORE is a bounded ideal point estimation algorithm for political data analysis that combines a predictive fit objective with a sparsity-aware likelihood and grid-based uncertainty quantification. Across five benchmark datasets spanning surveys, roll calls, and deliberation, it outperforms both model-based (IRT) and machine-learning baselines on reconstruction and imputation error, particularly for sparse test responses.

entry.title: SeaCausal-FL: Federated Fuzzy Causal Learning for Maritime IoT Fault Diagnosis and Counterfactual Reasoning

author.name: Yuhang Qiu, Haihan Zhu, Koteeswaran Seerangan, Longsheng Zhu, Xiong Wang, Yijun Lu, Zheng Lin, Fangmin Ren, Jialiang Xie

entry.summary: SeaCausal-FL combines federated learning, interval type-2 fuzzy layers, and physics-constrained structural causal models for marine-engine fault diagnosis across distributed, heterogeneous data owners. Mechanisms are aligned before aggregation using operating context, causal structure, and intervention-response signatures. It is a heavy integration of multiple techniques aimed at a specific industrial IoT problem.

entry.title: Kolmogorov--Arnold stability for discontinuous functions

author.name: Sviatoslav V. Dzhenzher

entry.summary: Investigates the stability of the Kolmogorov-Arnold representation theorem under adversarial reparameterizations of the hidden layer for multivariate discontinuous and unbounded functions. The results provide rigorous foundations for the structural robustness of Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) under adversarial configurations.

entry.title: Local gradient neural operator

author.name: Baiming Zhang, Jinsong Tang, Ying Xu, Lihua Chen, Shiying Xiong

entry.summary: LGNO is a lightweight, interpretable neural operator for predicting field evolution and identifying sources in mechanical PDE problems, designed to require less data and fewer parameters than global neural operators. It targets canonical dynamical systems tasks that traditionally require full knowledge of governing equations. A useful contribution to scientific machine learning if validated broadly.

entry.title: BAFF: Bid-Aware Filter Family for Mitigating Training Data Interference in RTB A/B Tests

author.name: Jeonglyul Oh, Ikkyu Choi, Inseop Youn, Youngjae Kim

entry.summary: Formalizes a class of bid-aware hard filters (BAFF) that mitigate training-data interference in real-time bidding A/B tests, where control and treatment models share a serving log contaminated by the counterpart model's ad-selection and pricing decisions. The filters trade off bias correction against data retention with independent per-channel tolerance.

entry.title: Functional Attentive Interpretable Regression

author.name: Haixu Wang, Tianyu Guan, Jiguo Cao

entry.summary: Proposes FAIR, a function-on-function regression method using self-attention over coordinate features to learn effect-adaptive neighborhoods for complex coefficient surfaces (patches, bands, rings) where similarity is not Euclidean-proximate, with a compression network preserving interpretability. It avoids the limits of fixed basis projections and direct smoothing.

entry.title: SLA-Safe Energy Control for AI-Native NG-RAN Using Stability-Aware Constrained PPO

author.name: Dharmendra Kumar

entry.summary: Formulates 5G radio access network energy saving as a constrained MDP solved with stability-aware constrained PPO, balancing sleep-state energy reductions against QoS/SLA violations and unstable mode switching under bursty traffic. An applied RL contribution for AI-native RAN control.

entry.title: Hierarchical Fourier Approximation for Variational Quantum Distribution Learning

author.name: Taha Hoseinpour Asli, Sajjad Hashemian, Ebrahim Ardeshir-Larijani

entry.summary: This paper studies variational quantum distribution learning via a hierarchy of Walsh-Fourier approximations on the Boolean cube, where spectral truncations serve as targets for quantum circuit Born machines with warm-start initialization between levels. It provides an end-to-end learning guarantee with an approximation term tied to omitted Fourier mass and explicit statistical bounds, connecting distribution learning to total variation distance.

entry.title: Likelihood-Based Unsupervised Anomaly Detection in CMS Dijet Events

author.name: Bhavishya Chebrolu (VIT-AP University, Amaravati, India), Hitesh Rasineni (VIT-AP University, Amaravati, India), Prajwal Aaryan Immadi (VIT-AP University, Amaravati, India)

entry.summary: This work applies a neural spline flow (normalizing flow) to CMS Open Data proton-proton collision events, learning the Standard Model background density without a signal hypothesis and flagging low-likelihood dijet events as anomaly candidates. The study includes extensive validation such as feature-level comparisons and mass decorrelation tests on extreme tail events.

entry.title: Multi-label versus multi-class classification of blood cells and their aggregates in microfluidic channels

author.name: Igor Zingman, Shada Abuhattum, Sara Kaliman, Maximilian Schl\"ogel, Paul M\"uller, Mark\'eta Kub\'ankov\'a, Nadine Str\"ohlein, Manuela Hauke, Lena Schn\"orer, Martin Kr\"ater, Jochen Guck

entry.summary: Compares multi-class and multi-label classifiers for deformability cytometry images of blood cells, showing that multi-label approaches can assign multiple cell-type labels to one event and thereby identify clinically important cell aggregates that multi-class classification cannot. Applied to a large multi-institution dataset.

entry.title: JEDI: JEPA-to-Edge Distillation for Efficient Cropland Segmentation from Satellite Imagery

author.name: Kishor Kumar Bhaumik, Nicolas Roque dos Santos, Jia Chen, Evangelos E. Papalexakis

entry.summary: A two-stage distillation framework transferring representations from a large I-JEPA ViT teacher to a compact SegFormer student for cropland segmentation, using cross-architecture projection plus joint optimization of supervised, response, and feature losses. It targets cheap deployment at satellite or field edge while retaining strong remote-sensing performance.

entry.title: Selective boundary condition reduction via learned error gating

author.name: Daniel Fern\'andez, Dominik Penk, Dominik Riedelbauch

entry.summary: The authors propose a framework in which a neural network, trained on paired PDE solutions, predicts domain and boundary errors from substituting a simpler boundary condition for a costlier one, applying the reduction only when predicted errors meet tolerances. They demonstrate the approach on galvanic corrosion and other nonlinear stationary and evolution problems, including singular limits.

entry.title: MedWER: A Reproducible, Model-Free Evaluation Protocol for Medical Speech Recognition

author.name: Justin Behling

entry.summary: MedWER is an open-source evaluation protocol for medical speech recognition that weights errors on clinically critical terms using a fixed, license-clean list of 19,373 drug, diagnosis, symptom, and injury-mechanism entries, avoiding versioned NER models or cloud APIs in the metric. It couples a pinned text normalizer with a phrase-aware term-restricted word error rate so that the metric denominator is fully reproducible. This addresses the problem that a 95%-correct transcript can still swap one drug for another.

entry.title: Retrieval-Augmented Multi-Prompt Ensemble for Minor-Grain Breeding Information Extraction

author.name: Hang Zhao, Jiahao Wang
