entry.summary: IPGeoAI reframes city-level IP geolocation from static database lookup to sequential modeling, using a Transformer encoder to capture hierarchical dependencies in IP subnet structures, with LLM-based semantic fusion of auxiliary signals. It targets failure cases of heuristic and database methods, especially in IPv6 and mobile networks. An applied networking/deep learning hybrid.

entry.title: Does the Selected Object Reach the Reader? Auditing Identity Handoffs in Grounded Language-Model Pipelines

author.name: Siddharth Vohra, Runmin Jiang, Xiaomo Li, Min Xu

entry.summary: The paper audits identity handoffs in three-stage grounded pipelines (select an object, retrieve passages, answer), auditing 600 HybridQA questions across three selector families. It finds dataset-linked and model-selected object identities diverge in a meaningful fraction of cases, and that body-only BM25 retrieval omits the selected object on 26.6% of resolvable records while hybrid retrieval with reranking omits it on 1.0%. A careful audit of an overlooked failure mode in retrieval pipelines.

entry.title: DODR: Deterministic Operator-Driven Reasoning in Latent Space

author.name: Weicai Huang (Beijing MQPat Technologies, Co., Ltd.)

entry.summary: DODR proposes replacing token-level probabilistic sampling with deterministic matrix operations over reasoning-graph states built from phrase-level semantic units, formalizing Peirce's three inference types as operators in a high-dimensional linear-algebraic space. The aim is to avoid error accumulation and probability-driven reasoning failures in complex logic. This is an ambitious, unconventional rethinking of reasoning architectures.

entry.title: LLM-Assisted Behavioural and Scenario Augmentation for Agent-Based Energy Adoption Models

author.name: Iias Faiud, Hossein Khaleghy, Michael Schukat, Karl Mason

entry.summary: Proposes a hybrid framework using LLMs to design bounded behavioral rubrics and structured scenario specifications for a calibrated agent-based model of solar PV adoption by Irish dairy farms. It preserves the interpretable techno-economic adoption mechanism while enriching it with LLM-derived behavior, avoiding full replacement of the model with LLM reasoning.

entry.title: Compact Bellman-Grounded Cognitive Maps for Cost-Aware Navigation

author.name: Yuzhe Han, Mingkun Xu, Yujie Wu

entry.summary: The paper presents BCM, a compact artificial cognitive map grounded in additive heterogeneous route costs via a self-supervised Bellman objective and coordinate encoding, allowing goals to change without retraining. It also tackles memory efficiency, avoiding the storage blow-up of state-indexed and spectral constructions, demonstrated on weighted grids up to N=1600. It matters as a step toward biologically-inspired, reusable spatial memory for efficient navigation agents.

entry.title: GUT: Quantifying and Optimizing the Reasoning Uncertainty of LLMs via Graph Complexity

author.name: Shuang Liang, Xin-Yu Hu, Xiang-Jun Ou, Shao-Qun Zhang

entry.summary: GUT characterizes LLM reasoning uncertainty by modeling potential reasoning branches as a directed acyclic graph, ensuring comprehensive coverage of divergent chains from the same prompt. It quantifies uncertainty via graph complexity and uses this to optimize reasoning by suppressing unreliable branches.

entry.title: Patterns of Priming in Production: Lexical, Semantic and Structural Alignment in Language Model Generation

author.name: Giulia Pucci, Ruizhe Li, Arabella Sinclair

entry.summary: The study tests whether structural priming, previously shown in LM comprehension, persists in production using controlled sentence-completion experiments on dative constructions. It finds LMs are susceptible to structural priming, especially in semantically coherent sentences, with asymmetric magnitude for double-object datives. This bridges psycholinguistic theory and LM generation behavior.

entry.title: Pitch-class Steering for Diffusion-based Music Generation via Latent-space Probes

author.name: Yushi Ye, Wilson Zheng, Yongyi Zang

entry.summary: The paper presents a lightweight method for steering pitch content in Stable Audio Open by training a small convolutional probe (~125k parameters) to decode frame-level pitch-class activations from the VAE latent space. At inference the frozen probe acts as a differentiable loss, nudging generation toward user-specified pitch sequences without retraining the model. It extends controllable generation from autoregressive to diffusion-based music systems.

entry.title: Dynamic Heterogeneous Graph Representation Learning: A Survey

author.name: Huan Liu, Pengfei Jiao, Jie Yin, Hongjiang Chen, Zhidong Zhao

entry.summary: A survey claiming to be the first systematic review of dynamic heterogeneous graph (DHG) representation learning, covering discrete-time and continuous-time settings under a unified formal definition. It organizes methods that preserve both structural semantics and temporal dynamics in evolving heterogeneous networks. Useful as a reference point for researchers modeling evolving complex systems.

entry.title: How a Chatbot's Response Style Shapes a Classroom: A Multi-Agent Simulation of Students Consulting AI

author.name: Rin Tamai, Yuya Dan

entry.summary: This work builds a virtual classroom simulation with 20 student agents who, when stressed, consult either a friend or a counselor AI (using Gemini 2.5 Flash, an existing model), tracking state variables like stress, happiness, self-reliance, and AI dependence over time. It explores how chatbot response styles designed to maximize user satisfaction may reinforce mistaken beliefs and foster dependence. The agent-based approach enables observation of population-level psychological dynamics that are hard to study in real settings.

entry.title: A Verifier-Guided Explainable Reasoning Framework with Gold-Anchored QLoRA, Task-Aware Mixture-of-Experts, and Group-Relative RLVR

author.name: Thi Kim Trang Vo, Nam Tien Le, Thi Kim Nguyet Vo, Minh Khang Tran, Duy Phuong Tran

entry.summary: The paper proposes a verifier-guided explainable reasoning framework for educational question answering, adapting Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct with gold-anchored QLoRA and routing problems to appropriate symbolic verifiers (FOL/Z3 for logic, formula-aware solvers for physics). Verifier feedback drives candidate evaluation, self-revision, and reward construction in group-relative RLVR training. The goal is making LLM explanations more grounded and machine-checkable.

entry.title: ProToMEx: Rapid, Interpretable Explanations via Structured Representations

author.name: Athina Georgara, Adarsh Valoor, Sarvapali D. Ramchurn

entry.summary: ProToMEx introduces an explainability paradigm based on Probabilistic Topic Models that learns latent topics representing high-level reasons for classifier decisions, moving beyond per-feature attribution. The framework is model-agnostic and provides both global and local explanations of model behavior. It aims to articulate combinatorial decision patterns that feature-attribution methods struggle to express.

entry.title: SMILE: Bridging Continuous Optimization and Discrete Symbolic Recovery

author.name: Mansooreh Montazerin, Antonio Ortega, Ajitesh Srivastava

entry.summary: SMILE is a hybrid symbolic regression framework with three stages: structural analysis of compositional hierarchy, continuous optimization of a network with interpretable activations, and symbolic recovery via structured pruning. It aims to combine gradient-based search speed with discrete symbolic exactness, addressing slow convergence in combinatorial expression spaces. Symbolic regression matters for interpretable scientific discovery.

entry.title: Beyond Homoscedasticity: Decoupled Uncertainty Optimization for Deep Imbalanced Regression

author.name: Juncheng Zhou, Jiaxi Lu, Weijing Zeng, Zhong Li, Hao Qi, Jingsong Cui

entry.summary: This paper addresses deep imbalanced regression by rejecting the uniform-uncertainty assumption of MSE-style losses and identifying a gradient coupling problem in heteroscedastic negative log-likelihood that weakens learning signals for rare tail samples. It proposes a decoupled uncertainty optimization objective for long-tailed continuous prediction tasks like age estimation and protein activity prediction. The work targets the common setting where scarce tail samples carry the highest practical value.

entry.title: Self-Supervised Pretraining of Molecular Graph Encoders with LeJEPA

author.name: Micha{\l} Kulczykowski, Rafa{\l} {\L}ab\k{e}dzki

entry.summary: Adapts LeJEPA, a predictor-free joint-embedding architecture with Sketched Isotropic Gaussian Regularization, to molecular graphs, evaluating GPS and D-MPNN encoders on antibiotic-activity and ogbg-molhiv datasets under a rigorous multi-seed bootstrap protocol. The key finding is that pretraining improves learned representations and frozen probes but does not robustly improve finetuning performance. This is a valuable negative/nuanced result for molecular self-supervised learning.

entry.title: Candidate Comparability Before Promotion: Conditional Validation in Adaptive Network Intrusion Detection

author.name: Roberto Fern\'andez-Barrios, Iker Pastor-L\'opez, Amaia Pikatza-Huerga, Pablo Garc\'ia Bringas

entry.summary: The paper examines a methodological gap in adaptive network intrusion detection systems: drift alarms trigger retraining, but promotion decisions for challenger models may depend on how the challenger was constructed. Using CICIDS2017, UNSW-NB15 and ToN-IoT benchmarks, the authors run controlled comparisons of nine update policies with nested candidate-size controls and strict feature-vector role separation. This is essentially a rigorous evaluation-protocol study for a security-relevant model-update decision.

entry.title: MURAL: Multimodal Uncertainty-aware Recommendation via Adaptive edge Learning

author.name: Ahmad Mousavi (Department of Mathematics, Statistics American University), Majid Alikhani (Independent Researcher), Yeon-Chang Lee (Department of Computer Science, Engineering Ulsan National Institute of Science, Technology), Roberto Corizzo (Department of Computer Science American University), Yeganeh Abdollahinejad (Department of Biosystems, Agricultural Engineering Michigan State University)

entry.summary: MURAL is a multimodal graph neural network framework for recommendation that replaces static precomputed similarity graphs with dynamically learned topology via an Adaptive Edge Learner combining differentiable retrieval augmentation with uncertainty-aware fusion. It targets two failure modes of current architectures: structural rigidity in the face of evolving preferences and semantic fragility when noisy modality signals are indiscriminately fused.

entry.title: Coupled Control and Wireless World Models for Resilient Remote Robotic Control

author.name: H. P. Madushanka, Sumudu Samarakoon, Mehdi Bennis

entry.summary: Proposes a communication-aware remote robotic control framework using coupled control and wireless JEPA world models that jointly capture robot dynamics and channel evolution from visual observations and radio features, reducing the need to transmit high-dimensional sensory data. The goal is reliable control under limited and unreliable wireless connectivity.

entry.title: Conformal Prediction for Offensive Security

author.name: Giovanni Cherubin

entry.summary: Explores the previously unexamined use of conformal prediction for offensive security, presenting initial findings in privacy-preserving ML attacks and network traffic analysis. It complements the existing literature that has used conformal prediction mainly defensively.

entry.title: A Calibrated Reflection Approach for Enhancing Confidence Estimation in LLMs

author.name: Umesh Bodhwani, Yuan Ling, Shujing Dong, Yarong Feng, Hongfei Li, Ayush Goyal

entry.summary: This paper proposes a Calibrated Reflection framework combining structured reasoning with distance-aware calibration for LLM confidence estimation, including a Maximum Confidence Selection method over all labels, reflection-based prompting, and ordinal-distance-aware calibration. The goal is reliable uncertainty signals for deciding when to trust model outputs versus escalate to humans. Evaluation spans classification-style tasks.

entry.title: MoirfEolas and Cr\'iochScore: Developing Resources for and the Evaluation of Tokenization Alignment with Irish Morphology

author.name: Jane Adkins, Abigail Walsh, Brian Davis, Elaine U\'i Dhonnchadha

entry.summary: This paper introduces MoirfEolas, a dataset of over 35,000 Irish words mapped to their morphological components (eclipses, prefixes, suffixes), and CriochScore, a new metric that measures how well tokenizations align with Irish morphological boundaries. The authors benchmark common tokenization algorithms and find that the Unigram Language Model aligns best with Irish morphology, while identifying trade-offs between morphological alignment and other tokenization properties.

entry.title: Knowing When Not to Answer: Pseudo-Ensembles for Abstention in Music Audio-Language Models

author.name: Aanya Maheshwari, Vatsal Raina

entry.summary: This paper addresses abstention in music audio-language models, where standard multiple-choice accuracy confuses lucky guesses with genuine musical understanding. Instead of expensive independent ensembles, it builds pseudo-ensembles from a single pretrained model by applying answer-preserving input perturbations and averaging the resulting option distributions, yielding a better confidence signal for deciding when to abstain. This improves selective prediction in a multimodal domain at low cost.

entry.title: Retinal OCTA Phenotyping with LLM Reporting for Alzheimer's Disease

author.name: Progga Paromita Dutta, Jeba Maliha, Md Rafiul Kabir

entry.summary: This paper presents an explainable OCTA (optical coherence tomography angiography) pipeline for Alzheimer's disease screening that combines annotation-aware vessel segmentation, layer-specific vascular biomarker extraction, label-free phenotyping, and measurement-grounded LLM report generation. Using 117 images from 39 subjects, it applies segmentation across vascular layers to produce interpretable retinal biomarkers with LLM-written, measurement-grounded reports. The goal is low-cost, population-scale AD screening via non-invasive retinal imaging.

entry.title: FailSAE: Towards Interpretable Failure Prediction for Vision-Language Models via Sparse Autoencoders

author.name: Jie Ma, Zongxi Liu, Yi Zhu

entry.summary: FailSAE uses sparse autoencoder latent activations to predict when a vision-language model like CLIP will fail, framing failure prediction as classification over SAE features via a three-stage pipeline. This provides interpretable signals for risk-aware deployment, unlike opaque confidence scores or auxiliary classifiers. It connects the interpretability literature to the practical problem of selective prediction.

entry.title: FAVE: Foveated Adaptive Visual Encoding for Efficient Fine-Grained Visual Understanding

author.name: Amitangshu Mukherjee, Kaushik Roy

entry.summary: FAVE is a lightweight variable-resolution ViT inspired by human foveation that encodes externally selected regions at high acuity while preserving native geometry, separating where to look from what to encode. Controlled experiments with oracle crops show large gains, including a 9.4-point Top-1 improvement over fixed-resolution ViT on small ImageNet objects. This offers an efficiency path for fine-grained visual tasks where full high-resolution processing is costly.

entry.title: CoMLP: Cooperatively-Gated MLPs for Fine-Grained Cross-Modal Information Fusion in Medical Image Segmentation

author.name: Mingyuan Meng, Shuchang Ye, Mingjian Li, Zhenyu Zhao, Jinman Kim, Lei Bi

entry.summary: Proposes CoMLP, a cooperatively-gated MLP module for fusing multi-modal medical images with clinical reports in segmentation tasks. It avoids the quadratic cost of cross-attention on high-resolution volumetric feature maps while preserving fine spatial detail and cross-modal semantics. Relevant to making multi-modal medical segmentation efficient and accurate.

entry.title: Intrinsic Temporal Adaptation of CLIP for Partially Relevant Video Retrieval

author.name: Hyun Seok Seong, Woojin Jun, SuBeen Lee, Jae-Pil Heo

entry.summary: Proposes an Intrinsic Temporal Adaptation (ITA) framework that adapts the last visual transformer layers of CLIP to attend over neighboring frame groups, adding temporal understanding for partially relevant video retrieval. It targets the problem that frozen CLIP frame features lack temporal structure and video-level predictions rest on imprecise frame evidence. A parameter-efficient adaptation with clear motivation.

entry.title: VoxelFix: Post-Hoc Semantic Correction of Completed 3D Voxel Maps

author.name: Sunesh Praveen Raja Sundarasami, Taehyoung Kim, Johannes Scherer, Toma\v{z} Coti\v{c}, Sivasubiramaniam Subbiah, Andreas Greiner, Paul Spannaus, Sebastian Houben

entry.summary: Studies post-hoc semantic correction of completed 3D voxel maps for aerial robotics, asking whether semantic accuracy can be recovered directly from the finished map while keeping geometry and occupancy fixed. VoxelFix is a graph-based model that corrects perception pipeline errors that persist in automatically built semantic maps. A practical reliability improvement for downstream autonomous tasks.

entry.title: Scalable Detection of Fossil Palynomorphs in Multifocal Digital Microscopy Images

author.name: Abbas Shaikh, Praise Mayor, Patrick Ainlay-Vazquez, Aditya Viswanathan, Teon Golden, Eric Zhang, Ingrid C. Romero, Alexander E. White, Scott Wing, Arko Barman

entry.summary: This paper presents the first scalable end-to-end pipeline for automated detection of palynomorphs (pollen, spores, dinoflagellate fossils) in whole-slide multifocal microscopy images, including methods for decomposing and compressing multifocal slides into tractable 2D tiles. It addresses a major manual-analysis bottleneck in paleoclimate and ancient ecosystem research.

entry.title: Scalable Neural Video Representation Compression

author.name: Tianhao Peng, Ho Man Kwan, Fan Zhang, Shan Liu, David Bull

entry.summary: From the Bristol video coding group, this paper brings scalable video coding (base plus enhancement layers) to INR-based neural video codecs, enabling decoding at multiple bitrate and quality operating points while retaining the fast decoding and competitive coding efficiency of overfitted scene-adaptive codecs. This addresses the inflexibility of existing INR codecs that commit to a single operating point.

entry.title: Scalable Edge-assisted Fusion and Path Prediction for Connected Autonomous Vehicles

author.name: Tyler Landle, Jackson Isenberg, Abhijit Chatterjee, Alexandros Daglis, Umakishore Ramachandran

entry.summary: This systems paper presents edge-assisted world model construction and trajectory prediction for connected autonomous vehicles, fusing data from AVs and roadside units to extend planning beyond onboard line of sight. The work explicitly addresses the Age of Information latency budget required for edge-generated predictions to remain useful to vehicle planners.

entry.title: ToPos: Automated Optimal Positioning on Topographic Manifolds using Constrained Geodesic Voronoi Decomposition

author.name: Rajesh Raveendran, Akseli Vanhamaa, Jaakko Suutala, Antti Tikanm\"aki, Juha R\"oning

entry.summary: Presents ToPos, a framework for terrain-aware optimal placement of spatial reference sites by treating terrain as a 2D manifold embedded in 3D and replacing standard Euclidean Voronoi decomposition with constrained geodesic variants. This avoids the clustering and inaccessible placements of planar methods in high-relief environments.

entry.title: FIRE-LIVWO: Robust LiDAR-Inertial-Visual-Wheel Odometry via Failure-Immune mmWave Radar Enhancement

author.name: Kun Hu, Menggang Li, Kaidi Wu, Zhiwen Jin, Yingjie Zhao, Chaoquan Tang, Eryi Hu, Gongbo Zhou

entry.summary: FIRE-LIVWO is a tightly coupled multi-sensor odometry framework that fuses 4D mmWave radar, LiDAR, visual features, and wheel odometry within a unified VoxelMap using an iterated error-state Kalman filter. It targets SLAM robustness in degraded environments such as underground coal mines where smoke, dust, and self-similar corridors break visual and LiDAR cues. The mmWave radar fallback as a failure-immune channel is the key engineering contribution for odometry drift reduction in extreme conditions.

entry.title: MZ-Rain: Moisture-Budget-Guided Zero-Inflated Model for Station-Level Precipitation Nowcasting

author.name: Yifang Zhang, Shengwu Xiong, Henan Wang, Wenjie Yin, Yuqiang Zhang, Chen Zhou, Hua Chen, Qile Zhao, Pengfei Duan

entry.summary: Proposes a physics-guided, zero-inflated time-series model for station-level precipitation nowcasting that incorporates moisture-budget structure and handles the dominance of dry intervals in precipitation data. Targets agriculture, water management, and disaster prevention use cases.

entry.title: CHAMP: Cross-domain Hybrid Architecture for Matchmaking and Prediction in Online Multi-Player Games

author.name: Kai Wang, Ge Fan, Chaoyun Zhang, Yuyang Jiang, Yuze Liu

entry.summary: Presents CHAMP, a cross-domain matchmaking framework for MOBA games that tackles cold start, cross-rank distribution inconsistency, and data-sparse skill segments via cross-domain transfer for win-rate prediction and team rebalancing. It extends the authors' prior CUPID assignment-re-optimization approach to production-realistic conditions.

entry.title: LLM-Driven Algorithm Design for Quantum Circuit Synthesis based on Binary Decision Diagrams

author.name: Yoonju Sim, Federico Berto, Chuanbo Hua, Jinkyoo Park, Changhyun Kwon

entry.summary: This paper proposes QuantumEvo, an evolutionary framework in which LLMs design variable-ordering heuristics for reversible quantum circuit synthesis from binary decision diagrams, targeting quantum circuit cost directly rather than BDD size as a proxy. This addresses the known gap where BDD size poorly predicts the true quantum cost of synthesized circuits.

entry.title: Beyond Code Generation: Reliability, Verification, and Cost Economics in the Agentic Software Development Lifecycle

author.name: Happy Bhati

entry.summary: This synthesis paper examines how agentic AI coding systems shift the software-delivery bottleneck from writing code to review, integration, testing, security, deployment, and operations, while economics move from per-seat licensing to variable token and infrastructure costs. It synthesizes peer-reviewed software-engineering and field studies to frame where agent gains attenuate. The contribution is an integrative analysis rather than new methods.

entry.title: SimFuse3D: Source-Guided Target Simulation and Confidence-Guided Multi-Stage Localization Reweighting for Cross-Platform 3D Object Detection

author.name: Yongchun Lin, Xinliang Zhang, Yun Zou, Zhixuan Xiao, Liang Lei, Jianya Guo, Yuqiang Zhai, Xiaofeng Wang, HaiKuo Xu, Haoang Li

entry.summary: SimFuse3D tackles cross-platform LiDAR unsupervised domain adaptation by addressing box-point inconsistency in pseudo-labels: it retrieves compatible labeled source instances and simulates them at target locations, aligning point distributions, combined with confidence-guided localization reweighting. This improves self-training robustness when sensor height and viewpoint change. Relevant to autonomous driving perception.

entry.title: A Repeated-Measurement Study for Cultural Analytics of English Song Lyrics Using Five Large Language Models

author.name: E. Cho Smith, Samuel Ho, Dawn Laux

entry.summary: This study evaluates five LLMs as zero-shot annotators of four social constructs in English song lyrics, examining consistency across repeated runs, convergence across models, and transferability of consensus labels to supervised classifiers. It treats LLM annotations as measurements of latent social constructs and tests their reliability before such measurements are used at scale. The work contributes measurement-theoretic standards to LLM-based cultural analytics.

entry.title: LentEx: Generalizable Latent Entity Extraction via Synthetic Data and Instruction-Tuned LLMs

author.name: Umesh Bodhwani, Yuan Ling, Cibi Chakravarthy Senthilkumar, Shujing Dong, Yarong Feng, Hongfei Li, Ayush Goyal

entry.summary: LentEx is a framework for latent entity extraction, identifying implicit, contextually inferred entities in free text, using template-based synthetic data generation and instruction fine-tuning of smaller LLMs. Target applications include RAG, customer persona analysis, and knowledge graph enrichment. The approach sidesteps labeled-data scarcity by generating diverse synthetic training contexts.

entry.title: DART: Depth-as-Target Pretraining for Surgical Vision Foundation Models

author.name: John J. Han, Adam Schmidt, Muhammad Abdullah Jamal, Jie Ying Wu, Omid Mohareri

entry.summary: DART is an RGB-D pretraining recipe built on DINOv2 that folds pseudo-labeled dense depth into pretraining to learn better representations for surgical vision, where natural-image VFMs transfer poorly but scene geometry is highly informative. It exploits off-the-shelf depth models to generate supervision without extra human annotation. The work addresses data-scarcity in a high-value medical domain.

entry.title: RefDiT: Local Attribute Guidance in Reference-Based Image Generation

author.name: Rameshwar Mishra, Srikrishna Karanam, A V Subramanyam

entry.summary: Presents RefDiT, a method for reference-based image generation that provides local attribute guidance when reference scenes contain multiple objects with distinct characteristics, where global-style approaches fail. It addresses localization of relevant reference elements for fine-grained generation. A focused contribution to personalization and reference-driven diffusion generation.

entry.title: PuTR-CouT: Counting-by-Tracking in Camera-Trap Image Sequences

author.name: Fagner Cunha, Juan G. Colonna, Eulanda M. dos Santos

entry.summary: Presents a counting-by-tracking framework for camera-trap image sequences built on transformer-based learned association, tackling species abundance estimation under low frame rates and missing counting labels. It generates synthetic training data using structural priors such as static backgrounds and short temporal bursts. Useful for ecology and conservation monitoring.

entry.title: CrossDepth: Geometry-Constrained Attention for Generalizable Multi-View Surround Depth Estimation

author.name: Samer Abualhanud, Max Mehltretter

entry.summary: CrossDepth improves depth estimation from multi-view surround camera rigs for autonomous driving by addressing cross-image inconsistency from differing camera intrinsics and limited receptive fields, using per-pixel camera-aware ray embeddings and geometry-constrained attention. The goal is more generalizable surround-view depth with minimal image overlap.

entry.title: EyeMakeYou: Identity-, Task-, and Subjective-State-Conditioned Diffusion for High-Frequency Gaze Synthesis

author.name: Kamrul Hasan, Mehedi Hasan Raju, Oleg V. Komogortsev

entry.summary: EyeMakeYou is a diffusion model for synthesizing high-frequency gaze signals conditioned jointly on identity, task, and subjective state, aimed at scaling eye-movement biometrics for VR/AR authentication where real recordings are expensive to collect. It addresses the failure of prior generators that produce visually realistic gaze lacking the behavioral properties needed for biometric validity.

entry.title: Attention-guided super-resolution of 4D flow MRI in carotid arteries

author.name: Ali Mokhtari, Dominik Obrist

entry.summary: This paper presents an attention-based deep learning super-resolution framework for 4D flow MRI of carotid arteries, trained on 120 patients with 240 stenosed arteries to improve hemodynamic biomarkers like wall shear stress and pressure gradients. It could broaden clinical adoption of a powerful but low-resolution imaging technique. Solid medical AI application work.

entry.title: Federated Attack Campaign Detection via Contrastive Encoding of Threat Indicators in Gradient Updates

author.name: Manuel R\"oder, Bibin Babu, Frank-Michael Schleif

entry.summary: FedIoC is a federated learning framework for detecting orchestrated cross-organization cyberattack campaigns without sharing sensitive telemetry. Clients encode structured threat indicators into gradient updates using a supervised contrastive loss over IoC-matched flows, pulling matched embeddings together within each batch. This enables collaborative threat detection across institutional and national boundaries while preserving privacy.

entry.title: Multi-scale Image Representation Compression

author.name: Tianhao Peng, Ho Man Kwan, Fan Zhang, Shan Liu, David Bull

entry.summary: MIRC improves overfitted image codecs in the Cool-chic family by making quantization end-to-end rate-distortion aware rather than a post-training step, and by introducing multi-scale synthesis that exploits cross-scale redundancy. The goal is closing the gap to scene-agnostic codecs while preserving very low decoding complexity.

entry.title: Predicting Spatiotemporal Mobile Sensing-Based PM2.5 Concentrations Using Low-Rank Adapted Spatially Attentive Graph Neural Network

author.name: Om Chiddarwar, Priyanka Mandal, Praveen Kumar Chandaliya, Shriniwas Arkatkar

entry.summary: The authors release a novel mobile-sensing PM2.5 dataset from Surat, India, and propose a spatially attentive graph neural network for short-term air quality forecasting and hotspot identification. Two graph construction strategies are compared: uniform corridor segmentation and adaptive DBSCAN clustering of dense observations.

entry.title: Dynamic Adaptation of the LLM Context for Generating Routines with Coupled Semantics

author.name: Gnaneswar Villuri, Hashmath Shaik, Alex Doboli

entry.summary: The paper identifies static binding as a failure mode of LLM code generation when correctness depends on runtime coupling between routines, and proposes a sample-efficient validation-generation loop. A validation agent extracts structured diagnostics from execution traces to dynamically adapt the generation context. It targets coupled problems spanning optimizers, packing, routing, and symbolic search.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning for improving Large Language Models' Catalan text simplification capabilities

author.name: Arnau Ayguad\'e Domingo, Stefan Bott, Horacio Saggion

entry.summary: This paper applies GRPO with a novel SARI-plus-penalty reward function to post-train an LLM (IberianLLM-7B-Instruct) for automatic text simplification, targeting low-resource languages with a focus on Catalan, using the English ASSET dataset. It demonstrates transfer of simplification capability across languages. Relevant to accessibility and low-resource NLP.

entry.title: TreeFI: Value-Aware Statistical Fault Injection for Deep Neural Networks

author.name: Noam Bires, Marcello Traiola, Angeliki Kritikakou, Elisa Fromont

entry.summary: TreeFI is a value-aware statistical fault-injection methodology for FP32 single-bit faults in DNN activations and weights, using regression trees to partition value distributions into intervals with similar expected bit-flip behavior and allocate injections accordingly. This reduces the injection budget needed for reliability evaluation versus existing statistical approaches. Useful for hardware-fault robustness assessment of neural networks.

entry.title: Adaptive Multi-Granularity Temporal Modeling for Weakly Supervised Video Anomaly Detection

author.name: Changyi Li, Yu Xiao

entry.summary: The authors propose an adaptive temporal modeling framework for weakly supervised video anomaly detection that replaces rigid, hand-crafted temporal priors in standard MIL formulations with multi-granularity modeling that adapts to variations in anomaly durations and video dynamics. This addresses unstable snippet-level predictions, a known weakness of existing WSVAD approaches. The work is relevant as surveillance data outpaces manual annotation capacity.

entry.title: Lightweight Vision Transformer Compression for On-Device Plant Disease Detection in Resource-Constrained Agricultural Field Conditions

author.name: Mahadev Sunil Kumar, Bhavika Gondi, Desaisetty Venkata Satya Sai Swapnith, Gangireddy Rahul Jogi, Sudheesh Manalil, Arnab Raha, Amitava Mukherjee, Parthasarathy Seethapathy, G. Gopakumar

entry.summary: The paper proposes a unified ViT compression framework for on-device chilli plant disease detection, combining Hessian-Balanced Adaptive Block Pruning guided by second-order sensitivity with quantization and knowledge distillation. Unlike prior work treating these compression techniques in isolation, it explores their combined application for resource-constrained deployment. The application targets economically significant Indian agriculture where expert diagnosis is scarce.

entry.title: Evaluating Large Language Models for Forced Outage Risk Prediction: Benefits and Comparison to Machine Learning

author.name: Christos Petridis, Zoran Obradovic, Mladen Kezunovic

entry.summary: This study benchmarks four zero-shot LLMs against two supervised classifiers for predicting weather-related forced outages in a Texas distribution grid across 3, 6, and 12 hour horizons using six years of records. Supervised models outperform LLMs on macro-F1 and precision, though newer LLM generations are competitive. The work provides a useful reality check on LLMs for structured tabular risk prediction.

entry.title: A Fairness Audit of the Duckworth-Lewis-Stern Method: Format-Specific and Gender-Differential Bias, with an Interpretable Calibration Layer for Cricket Target Revision

author.name: Soumyadeep Roy

entry.summary: This is the first large-scale empirical audit of the Duckworth-Lewis-Stern cricket target-revision method, covering 8,150 international matches and 233,550 synthetic interruption scenarios. It documents a 137-run error range across match states and a previously unquantified gender-differential bias in ODIs, and proposes an interpretable calibration layer. The work applies ML fairness auditing techniques to a high-stakes sports decision system.

entry.title: PACE: Propagation-Aware Collaborative Correction for One-Shot Personalized Federated Graph Learning

author.name: Ruizhe Huang, Chengran Li, Xiaochuan Shi

entry.summary: PACE treats collaborative knowledge in one-shot personalized federated graph learning as a compact correction to a client's complete local model rather than a replacement, using rank-r update carriers and diagonal sketches of propagated message moments. The server constructs a propagation-aware, receiver-anchored correction, avoiding the risk of incompatible knowledge overriding reliable local predictions. Convex negative-log-likelihood objectives support the construction.

entry.title: A Comparative Study of Counterfactual Explainers for Graph Neural Networks Enabling Multiple Types of Graph Edit

author.name: Maria Myrto Villia, Filippos Gouidis, Theodore Patkos, Panos Trahanias

entry.summary: This work systematically compares counterfactual explanation methods for graph neural networks that support both edge addition and removal, evaluating trade-offs among explanation size, coverage, and quality. The study aims to map where each method succeeds or fails to guide future research on graph counterfactual explainability.

entry.title: A Constraint-Aware Generative Framework for Synthetic Origin-Destination Demand in Logistics Networks

author.name: Leian Chen

entry.summary: The paper proposes a constraint-aware conditional generative model that synthesizes origin-destination demand matrices for hierarchical logistics networks, conditioning demand distribution on network topology and operational constraints. This enables scenario-based planning under conditions like network reconfiguration and demand shocks, which purely historical-data-driven methods cannot handle. It matters for supply chain resilience and stress-testing logistics operations.

entry.title: FluxDisco: Symbolic Regression for Stoichiometric Dynamical Systems via Monte Carlo Graph Search

author.name: Cassandra Durr (Lancaster University), Alvaro K\"ohn-Luque (University of Oslo), Chris Jewell (Lancaster University), Lloyd A. C. Chapman (Lancaster University)

entry.summary: Proposes FluxDisco, a physics-informed symbolic regression framework for flux-based stoichiometric ODE systems that leverages known stoichiometry to constrain the expression search space and enforce physical adherence. It adapts Monte Carlo Graph Search and demonstrates accurate recovery of governing dynamics across physical and biological systems.

entry.title: Online Change-point Detection for Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Fatemeh Saberi Khomami, Julita Vassileva

entry.summary: This paper proposes Patterns of Past Rewards (PPR), a lightweight, algorithm-agnostic change-point detector for cooperative MARL that smooths agents' return streams and applies statistical drift detection so agents can recognize environmental or objective shifts before adapting. Evaluation uses a custom Speaker-Listener environment based on the Multi-Agent Particle Environment.

entry.title: JLIR: A Julia-Native MLIR-Inspired Intermediate Representation with Automatic JACC Kernel Extraction

author.name: Narasinga Rao Miniskar, Seyong Lee, Keita Teranishi, Jeffrey S Vetter

entry.summary: JLIR is a Julia-native intermediate representation inspired by MLIR that addresses MLIR's poor fit for dynamically specialized high-level languages, whose strict compile-time typing and C++ extension model challenge scientific computing users. It includes automatic extraction of JACC kernels, enabling Julia scientific computing code to remain natural to write while staying optimizable through reusable compiler infrastructure. This targets the gap between dynamic language ergonomics and compiler-optimizable representations.

entry.title: Step Back to Move Forward: Reflection-Aware Preference Optimization for Visual Generation

author.name: Junlong Wu, Jiuzhou Lin, Jia Sun, Boheng Zhang, Huaiqing Wang, Dewen Fan, Houde Liu, Qianqian Gan, Fan Yang, Tingting Gao

entry.summary: RA-GRPO is a reinforcement learning post-training framework for diffusion models that incorporates reflective backward steps to improve exploration in policy gradient methods, addressing local optima that hurt semantic faithfulness and realism in text-to-image and text-to-video generation. It extends GRPO-style preference alignment with a reflection mechanism. This matters for the increasingly active area of RL-based alignment of generative models.

entry.title: HiSfM: Disambiguating Structure-from-Motion via Scaffold-Anchored Hierarchical Reconstruction

author.name: Ziding Zhao, Hainan Cui, Peilin Tao, Shuhan Shen

entry.summary: HiSfM is a hierarchical coarse-to-fine structure-from-motion framework that improves robustness to repeated or symmetric structures and reduces computational cost. It forms strong local camera communities via geometric heuristics, connects them with a compact skeleton of edge-disjoint spanning trees, and verifies skeletal edges with two-view disambiguation. This matters for mapping, localization, and large-scale 3D reconstruction in robotics and vision.

entry.title: LensStyle: Learning the Optical Aesthetics for Controllable Stylized Lens Effect Rendering

author.name: Yachuan Huang, Liwen Xiao, Liao Shen, Qiwen Wang, Huiqiang Sun, Zhiyu Pan, Zhiguo Cao

entry.summary: Introduces LensStyle, a unified framework for controllable rendering of stylized lens effects, jointly modeling continuous and discrete controls over lens aesthetics such as aperture shape, optical vignetting, diffraction, bokeh, and starbursts. It goes beyond accurate blur simulation toward capturing distinctive photographic style. A polished graphics/photography contribution.

entry.title: Development and Evaluation of Ultrasound Image Learning Pipelines for MASLD Risk Stratification

author.name: Guangyi Zhang, Xiaohong Wang, Eugene Cheah, Peng Guo, Brian A. Telfer, Theodore T. Pierce, Anthony E. Samir

entry.summary: This clinical study develops and evaluates deep learning pipelines on B-mode ultrasound and shear wave elastography for liver fibrosis staging and identification of at-risk MASH patients in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, using 250 ultrasound exams with 3-fold cross-validation. It characterizes a currently underexplored role for ultrasound-based deep learning in MASLD risk stratification.

entry.title: Fractional-Order Adaptive Motion Magnification: Phase-Reliability Weighting for Noise-Constrained Video Amplification

author.name: Alejandro Garnung Men\'endez

entry.summary: This paper introduces FrAM, a video motion magnification pipeline that replaces constant temporal and spatial gains with a fractional-order Grunwald-Letnikov derivative and per-pixel weights based on monogenic signal amplitude. The adaptive approach amplifies sub-pixel motion while suppressing sensor noise in textureless regions, and is implemented both offline and as a causal streaming pipeline.

entry.title: Pack It My Way: Triadic Human-Robot Collaboration for Personalized Autonomous Packing

author.name: Sandeep Chowdary Kotapati, Yanxin Gao, Tsung-Chi Lin

entry.summary: Investigates triadic human-robot collaboration for personalized packing, comparing human-expert mediation against voice-agent mediation of resident preference corrections. A user study with a Show-Correct-Generalize protocol evaluates preference correction and generalization across packing tasks.

entry.title: Competence Has a Maintenance Requirement

author.name: Matthew Yotko

entry.summary: Argues that cognitive offloading to AI automation silently erodes human competence, creating organizational failure exposure, drawing on Bainbridge's classic 1983 Ironies of Automation. Contends that the assumption people can regain control of automated systems requires ongoing skill maintenance that is rarely provided.

entry.title: What is the Alignment Community Thinking?

author.name: jonahmattwoodward

entry.summary: Compassion Aligned Machine Learning (CaML) reports results from a community survey on controversial alignment questions, including benchmark value as eval awareness increases, implications of AGI for animals, and AI s-risks. The post frames the survey as an initial probe to spark discussion and gauge how core researchers and community members prioritize issues relevant to embedding broad compassion for sentient beings into AI systems.

entry.title: Where to Look Matters: Learning Influential Views for VLM-based 3D Visual Grounding

author.name: Tsung-Chih Chiang, Hsuan-Kung Yang, Jou-Min Liu, Ting-Ru Liu, Chun-Wei Huang, Quan Kong, Chun-Yi Lee

entry.summary: IVSGround replaces heuristic camera-view selection in zero-shot 3D visual grounding with a learned lightweight view selector trained to pick views providing discriminative evidence, using two-stage rejection sampling with feedback from a reasoning VLM. The paper shows that view choice, prioritizing grounding relevance over mere object visibility, substantially affects VLM-based grounding. This is a useful contribution to embodied and 3D language understanding.

entry.title: STEMPix: A Phase-Transition-Material-Based Pixel Sensor for Resolving Edge-Movement Direction

author.name: Md Rahatul Islam Udoy, Sumeet Kumar Gupta, Deep Jariwala, Ahmedullah Aziz

entry.summary: STEMPix is a CMOS-compatible pixel sensor design using phase-transition materials that computes a 3-bit local edge direction code on-chip, combining pixel-level temporal change with neighboring-pixel spatial edge information. It targets specialized sensing applications where boundary movement direction matters more than full-frame intensity reconstruction, avoiding transfer of full multi-bit frames.

entry.title: Corporate Language Model (CLM): Transforming Tacit and Fragmented Enterprise Knowledge into a Sovereign, Auditable, and Executable Corporate Intelligence Layer

author.name: Fabricio C. Avini, Guilherme Trez

entry.summary: CLM is a proposed framework for turning a firm's structured, unstructured, multimodal, and tacit knowledge into an ontology-grounded enterprise intelligence layer with sovereign deployment and governed execution. It argues enterprise AI fails from lack of a structured substrate rather than model inadequacy, and co-designs knowledge capture, grounding, and actuation. Primarily a position/framework contribution.

entry.title: Towards a universal language of concepts: A survey

author.name: Aishni Parab

entry.summary: A survey proposing programs as a strong candidate for a universal representation of human concepts. It reviews computational models of concept learning that use programs as their concept representation and evaluates progress toward a universal representational language. Connects cognitive science ideas about structured knowledge with program synthesis.

entry.title: Hierarchical Possession-Aware Graph Pointer Network for Pass Receiver Selection

author.name: Jingyi Wang, Da Li, Kaixin Wang, Zhangqin Huang

entry.summary: HPGPN predicts pass receiver selection in football analytics from broadcast-like freeze-frame observations with anonymous, partially visible players, formulating the task as variable-size candidate prediction via a hierarchical possession-aware graph pointer network. It jointly models player interactions, event context, and opponent pressure under partial observability. It is a solid applied contribution to sports analytics under realistic data constraints.

entry.title: Towards Efficient Evaluation of Evolutionary Transfer Optimization: Case Studies on Task-Parameterized Applications

author.name: Yanchen Li, Xiaoming Xue, Kay Chen Tan

entry.summary: Studies evaluation-bottleneck scaling in evolutionary transfer optimization, reformulating serial, application-specific computations (kinematic-arm evaluation, B-spline trajectory evaluation) into parallel-executable forms at two levels: number of tasks and per-task workload.

entry.title: Large Language Models for HVAC Operations in Building Energy Systems: A Critical Review of Methods, Applications, and Deployment Readiness

author.name: Alexander Neubauer, Tianzhen Hong, Han Li, Mengbo Yu, Amin Darbandi, Yannick F\"urst, Martin Kriegel

entry.summary: A systematic review of 66 peer-reviewed studies on LLMs for HVAC operations (2023 to March 2026), classifying them across application and method families and assessing evidence realism, deployment readiness, and responsibility boundaries between LLMs and physical control. It finds the field concentrated in building energy modelling and notes only a small fraction of studies reach deployment-grade realism.

entry.title: Towards Understanding Pause Token Fine-Tuning Dynamics: A Mode Retention Perspective

author.name: Jaehyeon Kim, Suhwan Kim, Nakyung Lee, Yeongoon Kim, Jimin Seo, Giho Lee, Jungwoo Lee

entry.summary: This work investigates how pause tokens reshape fine-tuning dynamics, proposing two hypotheses: pause tokens reduce overwriting of previously learned distributions (mode retention) and boundary-adjacent pause tokens compress downstream-step information. Two controlled synthetic pilots support a training rule consistent with both effects. It moves beyond computational-expressivity explanations of pause-token gains.

entry.title: SCAPES: Semantically Conditioned Autoregressive Prior for Environmental Sounds

author.name: Esteban Guti\'errez, Lonce Wyse, Frederic Font, Xavier Serra

entry.summary: SCAPES is a lightweight generative model for high-fidelity environmental sound textures that operates on the continuous latent manifold of a neural audio codec with high-level semantic conditioning. An overlapping-segmentation strategy enables continuous autoregressive generation while bypassing rigid discrete tokenization. It targets resource-efficient sound synthesis amid rising computational and ecological costs.

entry.title: MABPD: Multi-Agent Bias Probing & Detection via Structured Argument Debate

author.name: Garvit Joshi (Graphic Era University, Dehradun, India), Stavya Dhyani (Graphic Era University, Dehradun, India), Jasmine (Graphic Era University, Dehradun, India), Arun Chauhan (Graphic Era University, Dehradun, India)

entry.summary: MABPD is a training-free pipeline in which three specialized LLM agents analyze news articles for bias from complementary perspectives and resolve disagreements via a Structured Argument Debate protocol with an asymmetric burden of proof for biased claims. It offers an alternative to supervised classification that avoids large annotated corpora. Addresses media bias detection through deliberation rather than training.

entry.title: ReCAST: Restoration-aware Cascaded Stage-wise Training for Obfuscated SMS Risk Classification

author.name: Jieyun Huang, Yi Shen, Kaikai Zhao, Jiangze Yan, Wenjing Zhang, Ping Chen, Ning Wang, Zhaoxiang Liu, Kai Wang, Shiguo Lian

entry.summary: ReCAST is a cascaded training framework for classifying obfuscated Chinese SMS fraud messages, distilling a large teacher's de-obfuscation ability into a deployable student via supervision on span detection, obfuscation type prediction, and text restoration. It targets real-world latency and throughput constraints in production classifiers. Applied NLP for security with a deployment focus.

entry.title: Fast Surrogate Modeling of Excitable and Oscillatory FitzHugh-Nagumo Dynamics with Parametric Neural Operators

author.name: Andrew Franck, Justin Li

entry.summary: The paper trains parameter-conditioned Fourier Neural Operators as fast, differentiable surrogates for FitzHugh-Nagumo voltage and recovery dynamics, conditioning each Fourier layer on a 5D physiological parameter vector via FiLM. This enables rapid parameter sweeps relevant to neuromodulation and inverse biophysical mapping that are expensive with finite-difference solvers. It demonstrates the value of parametric neural operators for excitable media dynamics.

entry.title: A Robust Watermark-based Fingerprint Framework for GNNs Ownership Verification

author.name: Han Zhang, Yan Wang, Guanfeng Liu, Pengfei Ding, Huaxiong Wang, Kwok-Yan Lam

entry.summary: The paper proposes a combined watermark-fingerprint framework for verifying ownership of trained graph neural networks, addressing three limitations of prior methods: performance degradation from OOD watermark graphs, unrealistic surrogate-model assumptions, and over-reliance on specific output levels. Model theft protection for GNNs is increasingly relevant as training costs rise. The framework aims for robust verification without harming model quality.

entry.title: From Deep to Shallow: Unconstrained and Efficient Layer Merging Strategy

author.name: Petro Shulzhenko, Gabriele Spadaro, Enzo Tartaglione

entry.summary: The paper proposes an improved depth-compression strategy that merges layers by linearizing redundant activation functions, overcoming two prior limitations: inability to handle padded convolutions analytically and kernel-size growth that erodes speed-ups. This enables shallower, faster networks for resource-constrained deployment. Efficient inference through structural compression remains an active efficiency frontier.

entry.title: Dimension-Adaptive Batched Lipschitz Narrowing Without Knowing the Zooming Dimension

author.name: Yasong Feng

entry.summary: This short note removes the dependence of A-BLiN (batched Lipschitz narrowing for black-box optimization) on the unknown zooming dimension by selecting edge lengths from the count of surviving cubes. The resulting Count-Adaptive BLiN retains near-optimal regret with log log T batch complexity even when the zooming dimension is unknown.

entry.title: Impact of Data Loss in Postprocessing on Training and Inference of Quantum Neural Networks

author.name: Soraya V. Panambalom, Edoardo Altamura, Nick Chancellor, Jonte R. Hance

entry.summary: A case study of SamplerQNN in Qiskit Machine Learning showing that a postprocessing filter assuming virtual qubit ordering silently discarded 85-99.6% of valid measurements when run on real hardware with over 100 physical qubits. It highlights how simulator-era assumptions break at utility scale in quantum ML.

entry.title: Adaptive Gated Deepfake Detection for Low-Resolution and Resource-Constrained Environments

author.name: Vaishnavi Sen, Cody Laurie, Rashida Hasan

entry.summary: AdaGate-DF is an adaptive gated deepfake detection framework that uses image-quality cues to route samples through a dual multi-exit system, allowing high-quality images to exit early and save compute. It achieves an AUC of 0.9370 on Celeb-DF, outperforming MaD-CoRN and DefakeHop++ while evaluating efficiency trade-offs on Celeb-DF and FaceForensics++.

entry.title: Vectorizing Classical Tamil: Representation Learning for Verse-Commentary Pairs

author.name: Amrit Gopinath, Sangeetha Sivanesan

entry.summary: The authors build a corpus of 1,262 verse-commentary pairs from Classical Tamil and evaluate what recurrent, Transformer, Siamese, mBART-style, and decoder-only models can learn from it, against lexical and string-based controls. Notably, a fixed string of the 25 most frequent commentary words beats the decoder-only model on generation overlap, and canonical correlation analyses probe what representations recover. It is a sober assessment of low-resource representation learning for a classical language.

entry.title: Uncertainty Signals for Network Intent Translation: Risk Ranking and Ambiguity Localization

author.name: Ala' A. Alsamarneh, Omar Alhussein

entry.summary: This paper studies pre-deployment risk in LLM-based intent translation for networking, where high-level intents are translated into low-level network configurations. It uses sampling-based predictive uncertainty for translation-risk ranking and token-level entropy for localizing ambiguity sources, evaluated on an ambiguity-controlled test set across context types and sampling budgets. The work shifts attention from translation accuracy alone toward deployment risk management in intent-based networking.

entry.title: Segmentation of the aorta in 4D flow MRI using 4D convolutional kernels and learning from sparse annotations

author.name: Hinrich Rahlfs, Julio Garcia, Chiara Manini, Markus H\"ullebrand, Sebastian Schmitter, Sarah Nordmeyer, Titus K\"uhne, Heiko Stern, Christian Meierhofer, Andreas Harloff, Sebastian Kelle, Alexander Lenz, Peter Bannas, Jeanette Schulz-Menger, Ralf F Trauzeddel, Anja Hennemuth

entry.summary: The authors develop a fully automated 4D (3D plus time) U-Net for aortic segmentation in 4D flow MRI, using a parameter-efficient hybrid 4D kernel for temporal context and sparse 4D labels derived from existing 2D expert contours, avoiding dense 4D annotation. Training spans 268 scans from 8 centers and 2 vendors with internal and external test evaluation against 3D baselines and semi-automatic tools. This has direct clinical value for reproducible hemodynamic assessment.

entry.title: Counting Beyond Instances: A Benchmark for Group-Individual Object Counting

author.name: Rui Wang, Junyi Huang, Jiahui Li, Qiao Yu, Yixue Hao, Long Hu, Baoru Huang

entry.summary: The paper introduces Group-Individual Object Counting, a new task requiring models to count both individual objects and higher-level semantic groups such as bunches of grapes or stacks of plates, exposing a blind spot in instance-level counting formulations. It provides BunchCount, a real-world benchmark with 1,330 images and over 89,000 individual annotations. This reframes visual counting around semantic units, relevant to embodied and everyday AI applications.

entry.title: SeamFlow: Structure-Aware Flow Matching on Edge Probabilities for Artist-Like UV Unwrapping

author.name: Yuming Zhao, Zangyueyang Xian, Qijian Zhang, Rendong Liang, Qin Jia, Ying He, Junhui Hou

entry.summary: SeamFlow reformulates 3D mesh cutting for UV unwrapping as continuous flow matching in a high-dimensional edge-probability space, learning a deterministic mapping from a Gaussian prior to a target seam-probability distribution. This balances geometric parameterization quality with visual semantic coherence in seam layouts, outperforming both traditional optimization and autoregressive generative approaches. Relevant to graphics pipelines and content creation.

entry.title: InterSing: Explicit Interaction Dynamics for 3D Duet Singing Animation and Beyond

author.name: Yihan Zhou, Zikai Huang, Yuyang Yu, Xuemiao Xu, Cheng Xu, Shengfeng He

entry.summary: Presents a framework for generating 3D head animations for duet singing, modeling interaction as a time-varying engagement signal at musically salient moments such as phrase boundaries and call-and-response passages. It introduces interaction logits to balance individual expressiveness with intermittent coordination between performers. A novel and specialized application beyond solo-driven animation.

entry.title: Optimal Stratified Allocation for Rare-Event Onset Forecasting in Dependent Sequences

author.name: Jaskaran Singh

entry.summary: This paper studies estimation of total risk from a small subsample of a finite population under class-weighted loss with a rare positive class. It derives the exact finite-population variance of the weighted risk estimator under class-conditional sampling without replacement and solves for the optimal stratified allocation, showing the imbalance ratio cancels so equal allocation is the natural default and dominates simple random sampling. An exact bias identity further characterizes cluster-sampling behavior for rare-event onset forecasting.

entry.title: ARIA - An Agentic Framework for Autonomous Testing of Infotainment Systems

author.name: Ant\'onio Azevedo, Bruno Lima, Jo\~ao Pascoal Faria

entry.summary: ARIA is a multi-agent LLM framework that autonomously runs end-to-end tests on Android automotive infotainment systems via visual interaction in a closed loop, addressing brittleness of scripted automation and limitations of single-agent LLM testing frameworks. It targets a domain (automotive infotainment) with manual, costly validation processes. Applied agentic testing work for an industry-relevant setting.

entry.title: Communication-Efficient Personalized Federated Learning via Layer-Wise Multi-Threshold Random Sketching

author.name: Xu Zhang, Xingyu Hou, Jiacheng Cheng, Kaiyuan Feng, Maoguo Gong

entry.summary: The paper proposes layer-wise multi-threshold random sketching for personalized federated learning, improving on one-bit compression methods that apply a single thresholding rule across the whole model. By adapting thresholds to layer-specific parameter distributions and quantization sensitivities, it reduces uplink and downlink costs in bandwidth-constrained settings. This addresses the communication bottleneck that dominates federated training expenses.

entry.title: ResLearn-XR: Residual Learning for Network Traffic and Quality-of-Experience-Aware Modeling in Extended Reality

author.name: Yoga Suhas Kuruba Manjunath, Jie Gao, Lian Zhao

entry.summary: ResLearn-XR is a two-stage residual learning framework for XR network traffic prediction and QoE risk estimation, combining a base sequence model with task-specific residual components for bursty, non-stationary traffic. It introduces a Data Descriptor Algorithm converting packet-level observables into frame-timing-aware descriptors for the QoE branch. An applied networking contribution.

entry.title: CPR-IE:A Compression-Prediction-Resource Intelligence Efficiency Metric

author.name: Xiantao Jiang

entry.summary: CPR-IE is a formal efficiency metric ordering intelligent systems by representational economy, predictive quality, and resource burden, with axiomatic guarantees including Pareto consistency, unit invariance, and derived logarithmic/power functional forms. It separates how resources are represented from how attributes are aggregated. It offers a principled alternative to ad-hoc efficiency comparisons for deployment-constrained models.

entry.title: Cost-Aware Hierarchical Multi-Agent Ransomware Detection and Family Attribution

author.name: Mubashar Iqbal, Asifullah Khan

entry.summary: The authors propose a hierarchical multi-agent system (HMAS) for ransomware detection and family attribution that adaptively escalates from low-cost static analysis to dynamic and memory modalities only when confidence is insufficient, coordinated by a Meta Orchestrator. This reduces computational cost and latency versus conventional always-multimodal pipelines. Applied cybersecurity work with an efficiency-oriented architecture.

entry.title: Beyond a Universal Forecasting Selector: Demand-Conditioned Model Selection across Demand Patterns and Horizons

author.name: Adolfo Gonz\'alez

entry.summary: The study compares five forecasting-model selection mechanisms across 24 models, nine datasets, and horizons from 1 to 12 cycles, finding that no selector dominates and that selection rules should be treated as context-dependent. The proposed CCG-AHSC and CCG-AHSCD selectors are more competitive under specific demand conditions. This is a comprehensive empirical treatment of when different selection rules help in demand forecasting.

entry.title: Representation Redundancy and Structural Complexity in Finite-Field Inversion

author.name: Zheng Zhang, Na Zhang

entry.summary: The authors analyze how the choice of ordered basis affects the algebraic complexity of inversion over finite fields, proving that distinct inversion maps correspond to Galois orbits of bases in an exact n-to-one fashion. They characterize three Boolean formulations by algebraic degree and ANF leap. This is theoretical work on how representation choice governs learnability of arithmetic operations, relevant to neural networks learning cryptographic-style functions.

entry.title: From 80x to 385x: A Best-Matching-Unit Search at the L2 Roof, Measured Against a Symmetrically Tuned Baseline

author.name: Andrew James Amos

entry.summary: This paper tunes both a novel self-organizing-map GPU algorithm (SparseBin) and its cuSPARSE baseline symmetrically, achieving 5.6-10.1x per-epoch speedups over the previously published configuration and raising the margin over the baseline from roughly 80x to 385x. The stated emphasis on symmetric tuning addresses a common methodological flaw in GPU performance comparisons.

entry.title: TNFlow: Amortized Posterior Inference for Trans-Neptunian Object Surface Composition

author.name: Agastya Gaur (University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, SETI Institute), Cristina M. Dalle Ore (Carl Sagan Center, SETI Institute), Alessandra Ricca (NASA Ames Research Center, NASA Ames Research Center)

entry.summary: Presents TNFlow, a transformer plus normalizing-flow model trained as an inverse of the Shkuratov radiative transfer model to infer Trans-Neptunian Object surface compositions from reflectance spectra, returning multimodal posteriors over simplex-valid compositions in about 0.7 seconds on a single CPU core. It generalizes to unseen component combinations and shows qualitative results on real JWST spectra, with identified biases toward some materials. This accelerates planetary science analysis of large spectral surveys.

entry.title: Automatic Speech Recognition for Multilingual Oral History Research

author.name: Sidney Wong, Chelsea Wong She, Eda Tang, Tiana Marshall Wong, Debbie Sew Hoy, Chelsea Wong

entry.summary: A community-led study of ASR adoption for Cantonese oral history preservation in New Zealand, examining how Whisper-based toolkits perform on code-switched, multilingual oral history recordings. The best Whisper configuration achieved a word error rate of 12.10 but with accuracy trade-offs, and the paper reflects on the practical realities of heritage language revitalization. It offers an applied, human-centered perspective on speech technology deployment in low-resource, code-switched contexts.

entry.title: AdaptVPR: Route-Aware Hard Positive Generation for Robust Visual Place Recognition

author.name: Shunpeng Chen, Jingyi Zhang, Changwei Wang, Shengpeng Xu, Yukun Song, Xingtian Pei, Jinzhou Lin, Li Guo, Shibiao Xu

entry.summary: AdaptVPR improves visual place recognition robustness under illumination, weather, season, and occlusion shifts by generating same-place hard positives. It uses a VLM to parse scene attributes and estimate editability, a rule-based scheduler to choose generation routes, and image generation to create diverse appearance variants for training. This addresses the appearance diversity bottleneck in VPR training data.

entry.title: Few-Shot Video Recognition via Hierarchical Metric Learning

author.name: Jiaxin Zhang, Haoran Gao, Xizhan Gao, Zihao Dong, Tingwei Wang, Sijie Niu

entry.summary: HML-FSAR tackles few-shot action recognition by applying progressive hierarchical metric supervision along the full feature pipeline instead of single-prototype supervision at the output, combined with a spatial-enhancement module capturing cross-frame global information. The goal is more generalizable class prototypes for recognizing unseen action categories from few labeled videos.

entry.title: A Semantic Model of Genetic Evidence: A Step Toward Bridging the Basic-Science-Clinic Gap

author.name: Michael Bouzinier, Dmitry Etin

entry.summary: The paper introduces a semantic model for scientific evidence with three core classes, specialized for genetics and structurally aligned to FHIR Evidence with SEPIO-anchored credibility decomposition and SHACL-validated constraints. It addresses the gap between clinical-trial-oriented evidence standards and fine-grained basic-science claims. The contribution is primarily knowledge-representation engineering.

entry.title: Physics-Aware Random Walk Fingerprints for Scalable Power Grid Graph Classification

author.name: Adnan Anwar

entry.summary: The paper introduces MC-PA-RWF, multi-channel physics-aware random walk fingerprints for power-grid graph classification tasks like cascading-failure prediction, extending topology-focused random walk fingerprints with operational edge states. The approach offers a scalable, interpretable alternative to end-to-end GNN training on benchmarks like PowerGraph. It targets the practical need for physically meaningful and tunable-light representations in power systems.

entry.title: Topology-Aware Training and Spatial Diagnostics for Fiber Bundle Segmentation in Tracer Histology

author.name: Joselyn Romero Avila, Kyriaki-Margarita Bintsi, Ermias Habte, Julia F. Lehman, Suzanne N. Haber, Anastasia Yendiki

entry.summary: This paper compares topology-aware loss functions (clDice, Betti matching, Topograph) against BCE-Dice for segmenting axon fiber bundles in macaque tracer histology, using a frozen DINOv3 backbone, reportedly the first such study for this task. It also provides spatial diagnostics for where topological losses help. The work supports validating diffusion MRI tractography against anatomical ground truth.

entry.title: Long Horizon Transformer Quantile Fault Prediction for Multi Site Industrial Predictive Maintenance

author.name: David J Poland, Daniele Ravi, Na Helian

entry.summary: TQRNN30d combines a dual-stage quantile regression feature extractor with a multi-stream temporal fusion classifier to predict machine faults over 30-day horizons from 81-channel sensor data, distinguishing slow degradation from normal operating variation. The quantile-state representation gives an informative classifier interface for long-horizon maintenance. This is relevant to industrial deployment where planning windows span days.

entry.title: MomentQuant: an even more minimalist interval method with linear time complexity for time series classification

author.name: Johann Faouzi

entry.summary: Building on the Quant interval-based time series classifier, this paper introduces MomentQuant, which achieves further speedups via an optimized implementation and a replacement of quantiles with cheaper moments, yielding linear-time time series classification. The work targets the accuracy-versus-compute trade-off in large-scale time series tasks.

entry.title: An Evaluation Framework for Generating Multi-View Images of a Person in a Scene

author.name: Mahir Majid, Young Kyung Kim, Guillermo Sapiro

entry.summary: This paper identifies the lack of paired multi-view data of human subjects at fixed scene locations as a bottleneck for training image-editing diffusion transformers to perform promptable camera-angle changes. The authors evaluate multiple state-of-the-art editing models and build an evaluation framework for spatially consistent multi-view person image generation. This targets a concrete weakness of current generative editing systems.

entry.title: Results from my AI negotiation harness

author.name: Carlos Gorostiza

entry.summary: The author built an open-source harness where two LLM agents, one buyer and one seller, bargain over an indivisible good under alternating offers with private valuations, discounting, and cheap talk, testing Claude Haiku 4.5 and Llama 3.1 8B Instruct. The post reports experimental results and releases both the code and the underlying data for the negotiation dynamics.

entry.title: Data-Optimized Contingency Screening: A Machine Learning Approach to Power System Security

author.name: Joshua Salako, Folajimi Osikomaiya, Olakorede Olamiju

entry.summary: The paper applies classic machine learning classifiers, with SMOTE for class imbalance and PCA for dimensionality reduction, to classify power system contingencies into safe, moderate, or severe levels. Features are extracted via Newton-Raphson load flow with an Overall Performance Index as the safety measure. It is a competent applied study in power grid security screening.

entry.title: The Mirror Agent Model: a Bayesian Architecture for Interpretable Agent Behavior

author.name: Michele Persiani, Thomas Hellstr\"om

entry.summary: The Mirror Agent Model is a Bayesian architecture in which an observer model mirrors the agent's own model, enabling interpretable behavior and explicit/implicit communication of intentions. The paper adds explanation capabilities via off-the-shelf saliency methods and provides preliminary qualitative results. It contributes to legible, interpretable agent design relevant to human-robot interaction and AI safety.

entry.title: Commonsense Reasoning in Computer Vision: Foundations, Recent Advancements, and Future Directions

author.name: Bahar Uddin Mahmud, Sumit Barua, Guan Yue Hong, Ajay Gupta, Hexu Liu

entry.summary: A survey on integrating commonsense knowledge into computer vision, covering how contextual and world knowledge enables models to interpret scenes holistically rather than merely recognizing objects. It reviews foundations, recent advances, and outlines future research directions for visual commonsense reasoning.

entry.title: A Deep Generative Model for Synthesizing Labeled Wireless Signals

author.name: Yuxiao Li, Keke Hu, Santiago Mazuelas, Yuan Shen

entry.summary: The paper proposes IIns-GAN, an inter-instance generative adversarial network that synthesizes realistic wireless signals with position-related labels, addressing the high cost of measuring and labeling real-world wireless sensing data. Unlike traditional environment-model-based synthesis, which requires extensive hyperparameter tuning and yields unrealistic signals, the GAN-based approach adapts to different environment scenarios. This matters for wireless sensing applications (localization, sensing model training) where labeled data scarcity is a bottleneck.

entry.title: When Does an Interpretation Count as Established? The Formation, Evaluation, and Responsibility of Interpretation in Generative AI

author.name: Deyu Jing

entry.summary: This conceptual paper examines how an interpretation generated by AI comes to be recognized as established within sociotechnical processes, introducing three concepts: interpretive appearance, the evaluation contract, and standing substitution. It argues that passing local factuality and citation checks does not establish a humanistic interpretation. The contribution is philosophical framing rather than empirical study.

entry.title: A Schema Bounded Language Model for Refining Robot Policies Without Destabilizing Local Learning

author.name: Chongwen Dong, Mithun Paul Saint-Germain, Pinjari Asif, Carlo R. daCunha

entry.summary: The paper presents a decentralized multi-robot navigation system where three robots with different LLM backends each combine an LLM policy agent, a UCB bandit, and a Double DQN controller, with LLM inference confined to round-level policy refinement rather than tick-level control. Robots communicate cross-LLM through shared round summaries containing policies, outcomes, and learning feedback. The design explores how to inject LLM reasoning into learned control without destabilizing local learning.

entry.title: Phase Transition Frequency as a Training Time Predictor of Test Accuracy in ResNets

author.name: Arunan J

entry.summary: This empirical study shows that the number of discrete class-separability jumps (phase transitions) during ResNet finetuning correlates strongly with final test accuracy on standard i.i.d. benchmarks (r around -0.84 to -0.87 across CIFAR-10/100 with many seeds). The relationship weakens substantially under distribution shift (r = -0.45 to -0.19 on TinyImageNet and CIFAR-10-C). It offers a potential early-signal predictor of training outcomes in vision models.

entry.title: GNN-Guided Graph Coarsening and Adaptive QUBO Penalties for the Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem with Time Windows on a Quantum Annealer

author.name: Youssef Kamel Rezk, Pawe{\l} Gora

entry.summary: This work combines GNN-guided graph coarsening with adaptive penalty calibration to make capacitated vehicle routing with time windows tractable on D-Wave quantum annealers. Evaluated on the Solomon benchmark against simulated annealing, it reduces problem size and improves solution reliability. It is a niche but concrete contribution to hybrid quantum-classical optimization.

entry.title: Measuring the Novelty of Biomedical Papers Using the Latent Distances between Knowledge Units

author.name: Yi Zhao, Heng Zhang, Yuzhuo Wang, Wenqing Wu, Tong Bao, Chengzhi Zhang

entry.summary: This paper proposes a richer measure of scientific paper novelty that goes beyond co-occurrence of knowledge units, incorporating network, semantic, and hierarchical relationships to quantify latent distances. It validates the approach on roughly 142,000 biomedical articles. The work matters for research evaluation and scientometrics, and indirectly for literature-based discovery systems.

entry.title: Temporal Residual Neural Radiance Fields for Monocular Video Dynamic Human Body Reconstruction

author.name: Tianle Du, Jie Wang, Xiaolong Xie, Wei Li, Pengxiang Su, Jie Liu

entry.summary: Proposes Temporal Residual Neural Radiance Fields for dynamic human body reconstruction from monocular video, aiming to improve novel view rendering and new pose synthesis while addressing the capacity and training-time limitations of MLP-based dynamic NeRF methods. An incremental advance in dynamic neural rendering.

entry.title: Learning Spatial-Spectral Refinement and Calibrating Complementary Observations for Hyperspectral Image Super-Resolution

author.name: Liqian Yang, Xingchi Chen, Xinfeng Gui, Xiangyong Cao, Qianxin Yi

entry.summary: The paper proposes a two-stage reconstruction framework for hyperspectral and multispectral image fusion that improves on implicit neural representation baselines by better capturing fine spatial structure and spectral dependencies, and by explicitly exploiting the complementary information of LR-HSI and HR-MSI inputs rather than relying only on degradation-consistency constraints.

entry.title: Research acceleration: The view inside OpenAI

author.name: Thomas Kwa

entry.summary: A LessWrong post by Thomas Kwa that appears to offer an insider-informed perspective on how research is organized and accelerated within OpenAI, including how internal processes may affect the pace of frontier AI development. The supplied content field is empty, so the analysis is based solely on the title, author, and source.

entry.title: Dual-Part Multi-Lateral Branched Network for Multi-Class Segmentation in Cardiovascular Catheterization Angiograms

author.name: Olatunji Omisore, Ahmed Elazab, Ali Shahidinejad, Fariza Sabrina

entry.summary: MLBNet is a dual-part segmentation architecture with multi-lateral encoder blocks and multiple class-skewed decoder heads for simultaneous segmentation of multiple structures in cardiovascular catheterization scenes. It addresses demand for fast, accurate, and explainable multi-class segmentation beyond prior binary-segmentation focus. The contribution is a domain-specific architectural design with accompanying analysis.

entry.title: Modular Deep Recurrent Neural Network: Application to Quadrotors

author.name: Nima Mohajerin, Steven L. Waslander

entry.summary: The paper introduces a modular deep RNN framework that simplifies deploying different RNN architectures and automatically computes derivatives for gradient-based learning. Adding feedforward inter-layer connections improves modeling of high-order dynamics and alleviates vanishing/exploding gradients, demonstrated on learning quadrotor altitude dynamics. The work targets system identification for control applications.

entry.title: How Faithful Is Attribution for Sales Forecasting? A Counterfactual Study

author.name: Glib Kechyn

entry.summary: This paper adds a post-hoc counterfactual interpretability layer to a multi-series WaveNet sales forecaster trained on 174,685 grocery series, producing contributions that sum exactly to the prediction and avoiding artifacts observed with SHAP-style additive attribution. Faithfulness is evaluated with deletion/insertion protocols showing statistically significant effects. It is a focused empirical study of attribution faithfulness in demand forecasting.

entry.title: Variational Continuation for Double Pendulum Periodic Orbits

author.name: Leo Yao, Ziming Liu, Max Tegmark

entry.summary: Presents a Hessian-based, integrator-free method for numerically continuing periodic orbits in dynamical systems, parametrizing orbits as Fourier series with a loss based on deviation from the governing ODEs. Automatic differentiation replaces hand-derived Jacobians, and flat directions of the loss landscape guide the continuation search. Demonstrated on the double pendulum, including orbits near unstable fixed points.

entry.title: VISTA: Dense Multi-Label Classroom Coding with Vision-Language Models

author.name: Andrew Franck, Brendan Ng, Ben Fitzgerald, Zane Derrod, Chris Cianci, Chris Craney

entry.summary: VISTA recasts the COPUS classroom observation protocol, a 24-code instrument with a decade of reliability literature, as a video benchmark for multimodal foundation models requiring dense structured labels every two minutes over long lectures. The paper argues multimodal benchmarking should import reliability methodology from fields like education research to establish noise floors.
