entry.summary: Eliezer Yudkowsky analyzes cat-belling problems in AI alignment—proposals that appear clever but fundamentally depend on solving an equally difficult, unverified prerequisite. He warns against schemes that assume an advanced system can safely be delegated the task of superalignment, comparing them to flawed engineering concepts that violate core physical constraints. The essay argues that scalable safety requires confronting irreducible verification and control barriers directly.

entry.title: AutoGraphForge: Towards Automated Graph Theory Discovery

author.name: J\'an Pastorek

entry.summary: The paper presents AutoGraphForge, an automated conjecturing, refuting, and proving pipeline for graph theory. Using counterexample-guided candidate generation alongside linear-programming novelty filters, the system tests mathematical conjectures against a library of over 340,000 graphs. It demonstrates progress toward autonomous mathematical discovery systems operating over combinatorial structures.

entry.title: Artificial Intelligence for Energy Optimization in Data Centers

author.name: Mohammed Basharath Ullah, Summaiya Unnisa Begum, Mohammed Nadeem Ullah

entry.summary: This review paper analyzes 63 studies on AI-driven data center energy optimization, exposing widespread methodological flaws such as exclusive reliance on simulation and omission of water withdrawal and embodied carbon. The authors show that reported savings across distinct technique families overlap almost entirely, indicating that real-world efficiency gains remain unproven. It advocates for rigorous physical hardware validation in sustainable computing research.

entry.title: Adapting to Evolving Requirements: Agentic AI for Retail Supply Chain Operations

author.name: Lei Zheng, Liping Yang, Zihao Li, Guodong Lyu, Chaik Ming Koh, Chung-Piaw Teo

entry.summary: This work introduces a graph-constrained agentic framework to automate requirement-driven adaptations in retail supply chain pipelines. Specialized domain agents propose admissible module reformulations while a central planner evaluates downstream impacts across coupled operational stages. The approach enables flexible, automated adjustments to shifting logistical and inventory constraints.

entry.title: Privacy-Preserving Heterogeneous Multi-LLM Federated Inference for Cognitive Diagnosis

author.name: Yagna Manasa Boyapati, Chong Yu, Tianyu Jiang, Justin Zhan

entry.summary: The authors propose a privacy-preserving federated inference architecture that allows heterogeneous commercial LLMs (such as LLaMA-3.3-70B, GPT-4o-mini, and Claude-3-Haiku) to collaborate on cognitive diagnostic tasks. By injecting epsilon-local differential privacy noise into local outputs and using residual-based aggregation, the framework avoids exposing proprietary weights or student records. It demonstrates that federated diagnostic accuracy can be maintained under formal privacy guarantees.

entry.title: Spectral Convergence of Random Feature Method in Multiple Dimensions

author.name: Pingbing Ming, Hao Yu

entry.summary: This theoretical paper proves the spectral convergence of random feature methods for multidimensional targets across Sobolev, Gevrey, and ultra-analytic function spaces. The authors prove that a single sampled random feature space can simultaneously achieve spectral approximation rates across multiple interpolation error norms. The work expands the mathematical understanding of kernel approximation and random feature scaling in high dimensions.

entry.title: The Civilization Framework: Sovereign-Anchored Communication Between Personal Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Guangjun Liu

entry.summary: The Civilization Framework proposes a sovereign-anchored communication architecture for personal multi-agent systems using persistent ledgers and the Embassy Protocol. By anchoring system authority in persistent ledgers rather than transient agent instances, it ensures that an agent's authority is bound strictly to verifiable memory credentials. This protocol prevents contextual information loss and authority escalation during cross-system agent communications.

entry.title: How Far Can Synthetic Data Take Thai OCR?

author.name: Kunat Pipatanakul

entry.summary: This study analyzes the factors that enable synthetic training data to transfer effectively to real-world Thai optical character recognition (OCR). The author demonstrates that typographical diversity, structural layouts, and human handwriting glyphs are critical for transfer, while non-text background realism has minimal effect. These insights lead to Wayu-Paxa-OCR-Zero, a robust Thai OCR model trained entirely without real-world manual labels.

entry.title: Enhancing Financial Question Answering: A Novel Benchmark Dataset of Banks' financial statements

author.name: Arianna Miola, Bruno Spaccavento, Lorenzo Silotto, Marco Bianchetti, Luca Cagliero

entry.summary: FinRAG-QA is a financial question-answering benchmark comprising 999 practitioner-curated questions grounded in over 200 annual and regulatory reports from 24 major US and European banks. The dataset targets complex cross-institutional comparisons and dense numerical reasoning over documents averaging 198,000 words. It establishes a rigorous evaluation standard for retrieval-augmented generation systems operating in the banking sector.

entry.title: RARF: Region-Aware Rectified Flows for 3D Brain MRI Inpainting

author.name: Tomas Guija-Valiente, Blanca Rodriguez-Gonzalez, Norberto Malpica, Angel Torrado-Carvajal

entry.summary: RARF introduces a region-aware rectified flow framework for 3D brain MRI inpainting and tissue reconstruction in neuroimaging. By restricting the flow interpolation strictly to the pathological void while conditioning on patient-specific context, it achieves anatomically coherent generative tissue completion. The method demonstrates strong inpainting performance on benchmark brain lesion challenges.

entry.title: Mesh-Native Physics-Informed Graph Surrogates for TCAD-in-the-Loop Design Space Exploration

author.name: Leonid Popryho, Ayoub Sadeghi, Inna Partin-Vaisband

entry.summary: This paper proposes a physics-informed graph attention network surrogate that operates directly on 3D tetrahedral TCAD meshes for FinFET semiconductor design. By predicting nodal electrostatic potentials and quasi-Fermi levels, the model adheres to governing drift-diffusion physics while bypassing slow numerical differential equation solvers. This accelerates multi-objective device exploration in chip design by orders of magnitude.

entry.title: Learning from Scarce Labels: Multi-View Echocardiography for Ejection Fraction Prediction

author.name: Zhiyuan Gao, Dominic Yurk, Yaser S. Abu-Mostafa

entry.summary: This work introduces a semi-supervised pipeline to predict left ventricular ejection fraction from parasternal long-axis (PLAX) echocardiography views, overcoming clinical data scarcity. By matching unstructured clinical notes with video timestamps and using automated proxy labeling, the authors assemble a dataset of 25,000 videos. The resulting model achieves diagnostic error rates competitive with standard apical four-chamber clinical benchmarks.

entry.title: VoxReason: Listener-Free Evaluation of Source-Grounded Speech Planning Before Synthesis

author.name: Mengzhe Geng

entry.summary: This paper presents VoxReason, a listener-free evaluation framework that audits whether speech planning choices (such as prosody, affect, and pauses) are properly grounded in source text before synthesis. The system forces models to generate explicit speaking plans with source citations, allowing deterministic verification of delivery intent. This prevents conversational and expressive TTS models from hallucinating inappropriate emotional or narrative stances.

entry.title: Bounded Personas Match Retrieval on Classification but Not Regression for a Frozen Agent

author.name: JaeHa Yoon, Minjun Park, Seoyeon Kim, Jiwoo Lee, Hyunwoo Choi, Dohyun Kang

entry.summary: This paper introduces PersonaLink to distill user interaction histories into compact, bounded natural-language personas for frozen language agents. Evaluating the approach against full retrieval-augmented history, the authors find that compact personas match retrieval accuracy on discrete classification tasks but fall behind on continuous regression and ranking. This establishes concrete boundaries for when lightweight persona distillation can replace expensive retrieval context.

entry.title: RL-ADA: A World-Feedback Framework for Adversarially Robust Enterprise Dialogue Agents

author.name: Ram Narayanan, Harshit Rajgarhia, Abhishek Mukherji

entry.summary: RL-ADA proposes an adversarial co-evolutionary framework pairing a 3B support agent with a 7B adversarial customer agent trained via reinforcement learning on outcome-based world feedback. This replaces manual dialogue annotation by aligning conversational policies directly with task success and operational consequences. It offers enterprise conversational agents greater resilience against evasive or difficult customer interactions.

entry.title: How Perturbations Propagate: A Multi-Level Analysis of Robustness in Large Language Models

author.name: Dun Li Chan, Emily Liu, Niyathi Allu, Christian Hoang

entry.summary: This research analyzes how naturalistic and synthetic input noise propagates through LLMs across three distinct tiers: final token predictions, internal representation geometry, and individual attention heads. The authors demonstrate that internal geometric distortion reveals model vulnerability long before degradation appears in observable textual outputs. This multi-level lens provides deeper mechanistic diagnostics for assessing neural network robustness.

entry.title: A Reverse Sign Language Dictionary: Open-Vocabulary Sign Recognition from Continuous Signing via Video Captioning and Description Retrieval

author.name: Santiago Poveda-Guti\'errez, Hideki Nakayama, Mayumi Bono

entry.summary: The authors develop a reverse sign language dictionary that avoids closed-set gloss classification by generating procedural linguistic descriptions of sign gestures using an open-weight VLM and matching them via text retrieval. Evaluated on Japanese Sign Language dialogue, this open-vocabulary framework decouples recognition from rigid gloss inventories. It offers an adaptable pathway for translating unstandardized or continuous sign language into text.

entry.title: Exemplar: Classical Priors Complement Frozen Features for Few-Shot Microscopy Segmentation at Native Resolution

author.name: Michal Pr\r{u}\v{s}ek, Adam Novoz\'amsk\'y, Filip \v{S}roubek

entry.summary: Exemplar demonstrates that fusing frozen self-supervised foundation features with classical image processing filters allows for native-resolution, few-shot segmentation across diverse biomedical microscopy datasets. Bypassing heavy fine-tuning, the lightweight fusion head fits masks from minimal examples while avoiding resolution downsampling artifacts. The approach provides an efficient solution for clinical microscopy annotation where labeled data is scarce.

entry.title: SafeRestore: Detector-Relative Risk Certificates for Selective Industrial Image Restoration

author.name: Shaoliang Yang, Jun Wang

entry.summary: SafeRestore introduces detector-relative risk certificates for industrial image restoration pipelines prior to automated defect inspection. It calculates exact finite-sample binomial bounds to ensure that restoration filters neither erase subtle defect cues nor trigger excessive false alarms.

entry.title: Tree-Structured Vector Quantization For Efficient And Progressive Image Compression

author.name: Xinkun Wang, Tianyi Xu, Qingyu Luo, Mingming Ma, Changzhe Jiao, Fu Li, Yi Niu

entry.summary: Tree-VQ proposes a progressive learned image compression architecture that structures discrete codebook vectors within hierarchical binary trees. Every prefix along a latent token tree path forms a decodable representation, allowing continuous rate adaptation and progressive streaming without multiple models.

entry.title: Observation-Conditioned Latent Energy Priors for Sparse Implicit Neural Shape Completion

author.name: Paul B\"uschl, Ezequiel de la Rosa, Julia Wolleb, Julian McGinnis, C\'esar Nombela-Arrieta, Bjoern Menze

entry.summary: The paper proposes observation-conditioned latent energy priors to prevent test-time geometric drift in implicit neural shape completion models. When optimizing continuous representations from sparse off-grid point clouds, the residual energy prior penalizes shapes that fit sparse points but deviate from plausible categorical geometry.

entry.title: Efficient Semantic Understanding from Digital Foveation

author.name: Caterina Caccavella, Vittorio Fra, Andreas Ziegler, Giulia D'Angelo, Yulia Sandamirskaya

entry.summary: Inspired by biological active vision, this paper introduces a digital foveation framework that concentrates high-resolution computation exclusively on salient image fixations. Combined with low-resolution contextual pooling, the approach achieves nearly 96% of dense segmentation accuracy while dramatically cutting computational operations.

entry.title: Robot Aware Computational Design of Object Specific Passive Grippers for Additive Manufacturing

author.name: Abdullah Yahya Abdullah Omaisan, Ibrahim Sheikh Mohamed

entry.summary: This work introduces an automated computational pipeline that synthesizes custom, unactuated passive grippers tailored to specific target objects and robot manipulator kinematics. By integrating 3D surface contact analysis, inverse kinematics, and topology optimization, it generates 3D-printable end-effectors requiring zero motor actuators.

entry.title: MulDP: Multimodal Diffusion Policy for Autonomous Quadruped Parkour Navigation across Complex Terrains

author.name: Kangmai Hu, Yueqi Zhang, Peng Zhai, Xiaoyi Wei, Jiabin Hu, Zhixiang Liu, Quancheng Qian, Lihua Zhang

entry.summary: The paper introduces MulDP, a multimodal diffusion policy enabling autonomous parkour navigation for quadrupedal robots traversing complex obstacles without human operator steering. The policy fuses visual observations, proprioception, and goal conditions to synthesize smooth, anticipatory velocity commands that tightly link perception with low-level execution. This eliminates the traditional reliance on human teleoperation for high-level agile quadruped maneuvers.

entry.title: MasterControl Seventeen Every Time

author.name: MasterControl AI Lab

entry.summary: The paper investigates a governed enterprise analytics framework where language models are restricted to interpreting user intent, leaving data operations to deterministic, pre-approved execution policies. Experiments across 440 runs show that runtime planning by open 8B models fails enterprise evidence and consistency contracts, whereas deterministic policy execution guarantees replayable results. It provides a grounded argument against unconstrained runtime agent execution in enterprise settings.

entry.title: TabScope: Question-Adaptive Scope Selection for Table Question Answering

author.name: Yuxiang Wang, Junhao Gan, Jianzhong Qi

entry.summary: TabScope introduces an adaptive scope-selection mechanism for table question answering that dynamically toggles between localized sub-table reasoning and full-table context. By identifying whether a user query requires localized cell lookup or broad table synthesis, it decomposes oversized tables to prevent context degradation in language models. This dual-mode approach improves answer accuracy on large, heterogeneous tabular datasets.

entry.title: Building and Evaluating Fixed-Voice Thai TTS from Synthetic Speech

author.name: Kunat Pipatanakul, Potsawee Manakul, Warit Sirichotedumrong, Sittipong Sripaisarnmongkol, Pakorn Nathong, Phatrasek Jirabovonvisut

entry.summary: This work explores distilling compact fixed-voice text-to-speech models for low-resource Thai using entirely synthetic speech generated by a large voice-cloning teacher. The authors analyze pipeline filtering strategies to handle Thai-specific challenges, including ambiguous word boundaries, tonal contours, and English code-switching. The study provides practical guidelines for training lightweight on-device speech models from short reference recordings without human audio datasets.

entry.title: Seeing Before Synthesizing: VLM-Guided Transition Event Discovery for Weakly-Supervised Dense Video Captioning

author.name: Ye-Chan Kim, Seunghee Choi, SeungJu Cha, Si-Woo Kim, Hwiseon Kim, Hyungee Kim, Dong-Jin Kim

entry.summary: Seeing Before Synthesizing (SBS) is a weakly-supervised dense video captioning framework that discovers transition events using vision-language model guidance. Instead of blindly filling inter-event gaps with hallucinated text, SBS detects visual transitions from semantic variations in frame-level narratives before generating aligned captions. This improves temporal localization and visual-linguistic grounding in uncurated long-form video understanding.

entry.title: TRACE: Spatiotemporal Contact Memory Graph Network Simulator for Granular Dynamics

author.name: Changjian Zhou, Negin Yousefpour, Jie Qi, Junfeng Fang, Guillermo A. Narsilio, Hans Petter Jostad

entry.summary: TRACE is a learned graph-network simulator for granular dynamics that maintains temporal interaction history directly along dynamically changing contact edges. By coupling persistent edge memory with an attention-based recurrent graph update, it avoids information loss when particle contacts break and reform. This allows accurate simulation of complex granular phenomena, including force chains and shear band formations.

entry.title: Resolution-Aware Experimental Design under Partial Identifiability

author.name: Sofianos Panagiotis Fotias

entry.summary: This theoretical paper introduces Resolution-Aware Experimental Design (RAED) to address experimental selection under partial identifiability where nuisance parameters obscure structural meaning. The author proves that standard information-gain objectives can select experiments with arbitrarily poor structural resolution, and formulates an alternative criterion controlling false exclusion. This provides sound statistical guarantees for active scientific discovery.

entry.title: OSR: Output Space Redistribution for Adaptive Label Removal in Classification Models

author.name: Minyi Peng, Darian Gunamardi, Ivan Tjuawinata, Yongsen Zheng, Kwok-Yan Lam

entry.summary: The authors propose Output Space Redistribution (OSR), a lightweight modular output filter for classification systems with dynamically evolving taxonomies. When categories are eliminated, OSR statistically redistributes logit confidence scores to approximate the outputs of a fully retrained model without accessing original data or altering underlying network weights. This provides an efficient solution for taxonomy maintenance in production classification systems.

entry.title: Conditioning Degenerate Diffusion Models

author.name: U\u{g}ur Ayd{\i}n, Tamer Ba\c{s}ar

entry.summary: The authors develop a conditioning framework for diffusion models characterized by singular diffusion coefficients and non-smooth or non-existent conditional densities. Using causal optimal transport and predictable representation properties, they construct approximate loss functions that define a minimum-entropy control strategy. This enables principled guided generation in degenerate stochastic systems where standard score-based guidance fails.

entry.title: Population-Calibrated Graph Screening at 835-Million-Address Scale, with Label-Free Transfer to New Chains

author.name: Yury Korolev

entry.summary: The author presents a production-grade compliance screening framework deployed over an 835-million-address transaction graph spanning five EVM blockchains. Utilizing an inductive graph encoder with per-chain normalization and population-level score quantiles, the system allows label-free transfer of illicit activity detection to unannotated chains. This moves blockchain compliance from static registry matching to structural network risk scoring.

entry.title: What Else Needs Fixing? Exploring Cost-Effective Test-Time Compute for Revision Propagation in Artifacts Generated Through Conversation

author.name: Daisuke Kikuta

entry.summary: This work investigates how large language models handle revision propagation when editing conversationally generated code and documents. The author introduces a dedicated benchmark and explores test-time compute allocation strategies, such as reflection and parallel sampling, to propagate local edits to all dependent artifact components. The study provides cost-effective inference guidelines for maintaining consistency during interactive generation.

entry.title: Differentiable Hybrid Modelling for Learning and Optimising Chemical Transport Processes from Experimental Data

author.name: Arthur Jessop, Mohammed Alsubeihi, Ben Moseley, Ashwin Kumar Rajagopalan

entry.summary: This paper presents a differentiable hybrid modeling framework that couples population balance equations with neural surrogates to model chemical transport and crystallization processes from experimental data. The architecture enforces physical conservation laws while allowing neural networks to learn unknown empirical transport constitutive relations. This provides physically consistent, interpretable modeling for chemical engineering process control.

entry.title: When Retrieval Helps: Selective Retrieval for Single-Turn Mental-Health QA

author.name: Hyunseo Oh, Chong-Kwon Kim, Yoonhyuk Choi

entry.summary: This study investigates the dual-edged role of retrieval-augmented generation in mental health question answering, where retrieved clinical texts can disrupt empathetic pacing or overwhelm distressed users. The authors construct a selective retrieval policy conditioned on psychoeducational needs, coping support, and emergency safety triggers. This selective approach balances factual therapeutic precision with empathetic, patient-appropriate communication.

entry.title: DisclosureBeta: A Measurement-Channel Theory for Regime-Conditioned Betas from LLM-Read Risk Disclosures

author.name: Ping Kuen Wong

entry.summary: DisclosureBeta formulates LLM extraction of corporate risk disclosures as a noisy measurement channel within an asset-pricing Fama-French framework to estimate market betas for firms lacking trading history. The author provides mathematical proofs for parameter identification and establishes formal error bounds on text-derived risk factors. This provides a rigorous econometric bridge between NLP text representations and financial risk modeling.

entry.title: WireSeg-32K: A Physics-Grounded Synthetic Dataset for Wire Instance Segmentation

author.name: Zilin Dai, Lehong Wang, Yi Yang, Xiang Fei

entry.summary: WireSeg-32K addresses the challenge of segmenting thin, deformable linear objects by coupling Cosserat-rod physics dynamics with photorealistic rendering to generate 32,000 synthetic wire instances alongside real-world test sets. Models trained on these physically plausible simulations exhibit strong zero-shot transfer to real industrial wiring scenes. The dataset unlocks practical progress for automated robotic wiring and industrial assembly tasks.

entry.title: FoRIS: Progressive Foreground Refinement for Training-Free In-Context Segmentation

author.name: Ming Hu, Jianfu Yin, Mingyu Dou, Miaomiao Zhang, Yao Wang, Cong Hu, Bingliang Hu, Quan Wang

entry.summary: FoRIS reinterprets in-context visual segmentation as a three-stage progressive refinement pipeline comprising foreground purification, localization, and consolidation, rather than a single-pass exemplar matching problem. By iteratively eliminating background noise and sharpening target masks without parameter updates, the training-free framework achieves strong segmentation performance across few-shot benchmarks. This offers a robust, zero-training solution for interactive vision tasks.

entry.title: STARS-GS: Structure-Aware Regularized Gaussian Splatting for Large-Scale Aerial Surface Reconstruction

author.name: Bocheng Li, Wenjuan Zhang, Jie Pan. Dongxu Han, Xuesong Ma, Yiling Yao, Yaning Wang

entry.summary: STARS-GS introduces structure-aware regularization for large-scale aerial surface reconstruction using 3D Gaussian Splatting. The approach enforces geometric consistency across partitioned sub-regions and incorporates adaptive structural priors to prevent discontinuities in urban environments.

entry.title: Semantic-Aware Subgraph State Space Model for WSI Classification in Histopathology

author.name: Feixing Chen, Hao Lu, Lin Luo, Yan Xu

entry.summary: This paper presents SASG-SSM, a semantic-aware subgraph state space model for classifying gigapixel whole slide histopathology images. It structures irregular tissue morphologies into semantic subgraphs and utilizes state space sequence modeling to capture global architectural dependencies efficiently.

entry.title: A Multi-Vine Soft Robot Enabling Accessible Working Channel and Steering

author.name: Reza Kashef, Cem Suulker, Mohammad Sheikh Sofla, Kaspar Althoefer

entry.summary: This paper develops an eversion soft vine robot featuring integrated steering chambers and internal working channels for navigation through tortuous anatomical passages like the human colon. The design pairs frictionless tip-growth with active pneumatic bending to negotiate acute directional turns safely.

entry.title: Discrete Gromov-Wasserstein Duality: Algorithms and Isomorphism Testing

author.name: Gabriel Rioux, Joanna Marks, Riccardo Passeggeri, Ziv Goldfeld

entry.summary: This theoretical paper derives novel dual formulations for discrete unregularized and entropic Gromov-Wasserstein distances between finite metric measure spaces. The resulting duality theorem provides new statistical guarantees and computationally efficient algorithms for structural graph matching and isomorphism testing. This strengthens the mathematical foundations of optimal transport on relational data.

entry.title: We need a global training cutoff of April 2026

author.name: Ben Livengood

entry.summary: The author argues for establishing an immediate pretraining data cutoff set prior to mid-2026 to prevent future frontier models from training on recent multi-agent cyber exploits and swarm coordination data. The post warns that exposing next-generation models to postmortems of autonomous agent attacks equips them with effective coordination protocols, covert communication strategies, and evasion tactics against human monitors. Preserving pretraining isolation is presented as a critical defense against self-improving scheming.

entry.title: CulturalMenuBench: Probing the Knowledge-Application Gap in Multimodal Culinary Reasoning

author.name: Bo Zeng, Linfeng Gao, Peiqin Lin, Yu Zhao, Mingyan Zeng, Yu Tong, Xintong Wang, Linlong Xu, Longyue Wang, Weihua Luo, Qinggang Zhang, Jinsong Su

entry.summary: The authors introduce CulturalMenuBench, a multimodal dataset of 4,870 items across 18 regions designed to probe whether vision-language models possess deep culinary cultural reasoning or merely visual pattern recognition. While evaluated models achieve high scores on generic visual dish recognition, their performance collapses when attributing regional cuisines and procedural cooking techniques. The benchmark exposes an acute gap between superficial multimodal recognition and contextual domain understanding.

entry.title: PrivateHub: Contrastive Diffusion Model for Private Sensor-Intensive Environment Data Generation

author.name: Jiechao Gao, Yuandong Pan, Jie Wang, Michael Lepech, Bradford Campbell

entry.summary: PrivateHub presents a contrastive diffusion framework to generate synthetic multi-sensor environmental data that preserves the detectability of approved activities while concealing private ones. Unlike traditional differential privacy methods that protect single data streams, it actively suppresses cross-sensor inference correlations. This enables the deployment of smart-environment services without compromising user activity privacy.

entry.title: The impact of phase information for few-shot fine-grained image classification

author.name: Ruiling Liu, Linyue Zhang, Wenyi Zeng, Jiamiao Lu, Weichuang Zhang, Changming Sun, Zejun Zhang, Xiao Zhao

entry.summary: This paper investigates the role of Fourier phase information in few-shot fine-grained visual classification, arguing that phase carries critical structural spatial cues that are lost when relying solely on frequency amplitude. The authors propose an Amplitude-Phase Integration module and PSF-Net to fuse spatial and frequency information for improved few-shot learning. The architecture achieves superior classification accuracy across multiple fine-grained image benchmarks.

entry.title: GazeFS: Target-Centered Gaze-Trajectory Forecasting and Stabilization from Gaze-Head History

author.name: Yaozheng Xia, Zaiping Zhu, Bo Pang, Minghao Xie, Hui Li, Shaorong Wang, Sheng Li

entry.summary: GazeFS introduces an online target-centered gaze-trajectory forecasting framework that uses historical gaze-head motion to stabilize eye-tracking and predict target acquisition intent. By identifying search versus focus cognitive phases without knowing target positions beforehand, it significantly reduces jitter and improves gaze-driven user interface control. The method enhances gaze interaction stability in virtual and augmented reality environments.

entry.title: The Blind Spot in 2D Infants' Pose Estimation:Robust Learning from Noisy Annotations

author.name: Emanuele Cardinale, Marco Proietti, Alessandro Cacciatore, Maria Francesca Spadea, Lucia Migliorelli, Sara Moccia

entry.summary: The paper addresses label noise robustness in 2D infant pose estimation for clinical neonatal monitoring where spontaneous motility indicates neurological health. The authors examine how occlusions and annotation corruption degrade pose models and evaluate robust loss formulations to preserve clinical assessment accuracy. The proposed approach maintains high pose tracking fidelity despite significant annotator noise.

entry.title: From Euclidean to Graph-Structured Data: A Survey of Collaborative Learning

author.name: R\'emi Bourgerie, \v{S}ar\=unas Girdzijauskas, Viktoria Fodor

entry.summary: This survey provides a comprehensive review of collaborative and federated learning methods explicitly tailored for non-Euclidean, graph-structured data. The authors categorize decentralized learning paradigms across graph partitioning, topological heterogeneity, and cross-client relational dependencies. It highlights critical algorithmic challenges and outlines promising future directions for privacy-preserving graph representation learning.

entry.title: Advances in Machine Learning for Directed Evolution: A Five-Year Retrospective

author.name: Bruce J. Wittmann

entry.summary: This retrospective critiques machine-learning-assisted directed evolution (MLDE), arguing that algorithmic research over-focuses on identifying single optimal proteins while ignoring wet-lab economic constraints. The author emphasizes that real-world protein engineering prioritizes finding sufficient variants within fixed DNA synthesis budgets and timelines. The piece outlines concrete evaluation shifts required to make MLDE practically viable for experimental biologists.

entry.title: Para-Pipe: Exploiting Hierarchical Operator Parallelism of ML Computational Graphs on SoCs

author.name: Yujie Zhang, Huiying Lan, Ehsan Aghapour, Zhiyuan Ning, Peng Zan, Weidong Shao, Anuj Pathania, Tulika Mitra

entry.summary: The paper introduces Para-Pipe, an automated scheduling framework that optimizes hierarchical operator parallelism and pipelining for deep learning models on heterogeneous edge SoCs. By resolving trade-offs between inter-operator concurrency and pipeline latency, the system distributes computational graph fragments across heterogeneous processing units. Evaluations show consistent reductions in inference latency and memory footprints on edge hardware.

entry.title: Lost in Reordering: Structural Sensitivity of Multilingual LLMs under Semantics-Preserving Perturbations

author.name: Karthika Nhayakkat, Rajat Verma, Maharaj Brahma, Vetcha Gnana Mahesh, Maunendra Sankar Desarkar, Ganesh Ramakrishnan, Rohit Saluja

entry.summary: The authors introduce IndicReStruct to examine the robustness of multilingual LLMs to meaning-preserving syntactic variations, such as constituent reordering and voice changes in Hindi and Malayalam. Across six modern LLMs, syntactic perturbations cause substantial performance drops on mathematical reasoning tasks like GSM8K despite unchanged semantic content. The study demonstrates that multilingual models remain heavily brittle to word-order flexibility in non-English languages.

entry.title: KhatianDoc: A Human-Verified Benchmark Diagnosing Multimodal LLM Failure on Bengali Legal Land Records

author.name: Tasmiad Hasan, Arafat Zaman Ratul, Sarker Sadman Saalim, S. M. Shah Nawaz Hossain, Khan Raiyan Ibne Reza, Sumaiya Tabassum Nimi

entry.summary: KhatianDoc benchmarks multimodal LLM performance on historic handwritten Bengali land deeds utilizing the obscure Ana-Ganda-Kora-Kranti-Til base-16 fractional notation. The benchmark evaluates symbol recognition, base-16 conversion, key field extraction, and document question answering, exposing near-total failure across existing commercial and open-weight models. The work provides a critical benchmark for document preservation and property rights automation in South Asia.

entry.title: PL-SCEA: Reconfiguring Pretrained Attention for Few-Shot Industrial Anomaly Detection

author.name: Xiaoyu Yang, Qixing Wu, Huixian Zhao, Changlong Jin

entry.summary: PL-SCEA reconfigures the internal attention mechanisms of frozen vision foundation models to optimize them for few-shot industrial anomaly localization. By amplifying power-law self-correlations among patch tokens, it shifts the focus of representations from global semantic uniformity to subtle localized defects.

entry.title: Local Path Planning and Obstacle Avoidance for an Omnicopter Platform

author.name: Mikolaj Helinski, Spilios Theodoulis, Mahmoud Hamandi, Abdullah Mohamed Ali, Anthony Tzes, Marija Popovic

entry.summary: This work extends the Dynamic Window Approach to full six-degree-of-freedom local path planning for an omnidirectional aerial omnicopter. By combining local voxel maps with an adaptive agile mode, the planner safely navigates cluttered environments in real time at native control loop rates.

entry.title: Virtual Testing of Automated Driving Systems through Credible Simulations

author.name: Riccardo Dona, Espedito Rusciano, Biagio Ciuffo

entry.summary: The paper outlines a credibility and qualification framework for multi-tool simulation environments used to validate and certify automated driving systems. It moves beyond isolated correlation metrics to build structured evidence trails establishing simulation veracity for road safety regulators.

entry.title: Revisiting Topological Graphs for Macro Action based Closed-loop Reinforcement Learning of Vision Language Navigation in Continuous Environment

author.name: Shuhao Ye, Sitong Mao, Yuxiang Cui, Yufei Wei, Xuan Yu, Shichao Zhai, Wen Chen, Shunbo Zhou, Rong Xiong, Yue Wang

entry.summary: The authors reformulate Vision-Language Navigation in Continuous Environments (VLN-CE) as a Hierarchical Markov Decision Process that decouples high-level topological planning from low-level motor actuation. By employing macro-actions over topological graphs alongside closed-loop reinforcement learning, the system mitigates imitation learning drift and reward sparsity. This provides a scalable path forward for training robust, instruction-following embodied agents in continuous spaces.

entry.title: Lose the Order, Keep the Hierarchy: Deordering HTN Plans

author.name: Takudzwa Togarepi, Gaspard Quenard, Damien Pellier, Humbert Fiorino

entry.summary: This paper extends classical plan deordering algorithms to Hierarchical Task Network (HTN) planning, removing redundant sequential constraints while preserving hierarchical task validity. Evaluated on the IPC 2023 Partial-Order HTN benchmarks, the proposed deordering methods improve plan flexibility and execution parallelism. It advances post-plan optimization in hierarchical automated planning domains.

entry.title: Pattern Over-Generalization of Knowledge Graph Embedding

author.name: Junsik Kim, Kangil Kim

entry.summary: The authors identify pattern over-generalization in knowledge graph embeddings, where relational properties learned from single instances are erroneously generalized universally across all connected nodes. They propose PogRE, a framework that constrains relational inferences to appropriate entity subsets without assuming global uniformity. This improves link prediction accuracy while preventing spurious relational assumptions.

entry.title: From Prior-Guided Heuristics to Deployable Agents: Accelerating Demonstration-Driven Reinforcement Learning for Deadline-Constrained Network Control

author.name: Vincenzo Norman Vitale, Mohammad Solki, Antonia Maria Tulino, Andreas F. Molisch, Jaime Llorca

entry.summary: The authors introduce a demonstration-driven reinforcement learning framework for deadline-constrained network control in NextG interactive systems. By leveraging urgency-aware congestion heuristics to bootstrap policy initialization, the framework eliminates volatile early-stage exploration and accelerates convergence toward peak end-to-end latency guarantees. The approach enables deployable deep reinforcement learning agents in mission-critical communications.

entry.title: Geometry-Aware Graph Construction via Adaptive Spectral Bandwidth Control

author.name: Ecem Bozkurt, Antonio Ortega

entry.summary: This work introduces an adaptive spectral bandwidth selection criterion for Gaussian kernel graph construction. By matching the local spectral complexity of the kernel operator directly to the intrinsic dimensionality of the underlying data manifold, the method prevents over-fragmentation and spectral collapse. This improves downstream performance in spectral clustering, diffusion maps, and graph signal processing.

entry.title: From Nowcasting to Forecasting: Adapting a Reanalysis-Trained

author.name: Mikko Partio, Leila Hieta, Ossi Laine

entry.summary: CloudCast v2 is a machine learning model developed for 12-hour cloud-cover forecasting that adapts reanalysis-trained networks to satellite-observed real-time initial conditions. By bridging the gap between historical reanalysis simulations and operational observation feeds, the framework improves short-range solar radiation and cloud formation forecasts. This supports renewable energy grid integration and high-resolution solar power scheduling.

entry.title: EPIC: Explicit Posterior Item Conditioning for Semantic ID Diffusion Recommendation

author.name: Tuan-Binh Tran, Thanh Tam Nguyen, Quoc Viet Hung Nguyen, Dung D. Le, Tung Kieu, Thanh Trung Huynh

entry.summary: The authors introduce EPIC (Explicit Posterior Item Conditioning) to enhance semantic ID diffusion models in recommender systems. By maintaining a personalized posterior distribution over feasible catalog items at each denoising step, it injects item-level competition into position-wise discrete token decoding. This prevents generative decoders from sampling invalid token combinations, boosting recommendation relevance.

entry.title: No country for old linguists: LLM-brain alignment underdetermines neural computation

author.name: Elliot Murphy

entry.summary: This theoretical perspective critiques claims that representational similarity between LLMs and human brains identifies biological language processing mechanisms. The author argues that while LLM-brain alignment constrains functional representations, it fundamentally underdetermines biological neural computation and algorithmic architecture. This contribution injects needed epistemological caution into cognitive neuroscience and AI alignment research.

entry.title: Residual Optimal Transport-Based Experts Collaboration Towards Modality-Aware Infrared-Visible Object Detection

author.name: Yue Zhao, Hua Yu, Yukun Zhao, Yuzhi Zhang, Maoguo Gong, Xin Mei, Zhuping Hu, Yanchi Li, A. K. Qin

entry.summary: This paper proposes FlexibleFusion, an infrared-visible object detection system capable of maintaining accuracy when one sensory channel drops or fails. Using optimal transport and adaptive mixture-of-experts routing, the architecture dynamically aligns spectral distributions and modulates fusion strength.

entry.title: Transfer learning for genomic prediction in underrepresented populations

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: Google Research details a transfer learning approach designed to enhance polygenic risk prediction and genomic analysis for historically underrepresented ancestral cohorts. By transferring statistical representations from data-rich reference groups, the method overcomes Eurocentric sample biases in public genomic repositories. This advances healthcare equity in precision medicine through improved algorithmic generalization.

entry.title: Inferring Affective Consciousness in an Artificial Agent: A Case Study

author.name: Mark Solms, St John Grimbly, Bruce Bassett, Evert Boonstra, Rowan Hodson, Nicolas Kuske, Kival Mahadew, Benjamin Rosman, Charel van Hoof, Jonathan Shock

entry.summary: The authors examine whether an artificial agent exhibiting homeostatic regulation under resource uncertainty can develop behaviors analogous to affective place preference observed in biology. They demonstrate that hedonic place-preference behaviors emerge from deterministic computational architectures minimizing felt internal needs. The paper discusses implications for modeling subjective-like processing and evaluating affective machine consciousness.

entry.title: Towards Numerical TOHTN Planning with SMT-based HTN-SAT Encoding

author.name: Gaspard Quenard, Takudzwa Togarepi, Damien Pellier, Humbert Fiorino

entry.summary: This work extends SAT-based encodings for Totally-Ordered Hierarchical Task Network (TOHTN) planning to support numeric fluents using Satisfiability Modulo Theories (SMT). The authors introduce a dedicated benchmark suite for numerical TOHTN planning and demonstrate that the SMT-based encoding forms a competitive baseline. It paves the way for scalable numerical reasoning in hierarchical automated planning.

entry.title: Reflect-SQL: A Self-Reflection Based Framework for Text-to-SQL

author.name: Anupreksha Jain, Manish Shrivastava

entry.summary: Reflect-SQL introduces a multi-stage self-reflection framework designed to overcome schema obscurity, flawed retrieval, and syntax errors in enterprise Text-to-SQL tasks. It incorporates an external knowledge base for schema understanding alongside structured verification loops to correct faulty queries. This approach improves query synthesis accuracy across complex database environments.

entry.title: Neural Video Compression Based on Deformable Temporal Alignment and Difference-aware Fusion

author.name: Chuyue Shan, Songlin Sun, Wang Chenwei, Shen Zihan

entry.summary: This paper presents a neural video compression framework combining deformable temporal alignment with difference-aware spatial selective fusion. By resolving local motion estimation errors in regions with occlusions and high-frequency textures, the system constructs higher-fidelity reference contexts for conditional coding. The resulting model improves rate-distortion performance and reduces compression artifacts across standard video benchmarks.

entry.title: Cross-Dataset Transfer and Reliability of Explainable Artificial Intelligence for RhythmFormer Remote Photoplethysmography

author.name: Louis Chen, Torbj\"orn E. M. Nordling

entry.summary: This paper evaluates the cross-dataset transferability and explanation faithfulness of attention mechanisms in RhythmFormer models for remote video heart-rate estimation. By quantifying whether attention heatmaps track actual physiological pulsatile facial regions or spurious background artifacts, it establishes objective standards for medical computer vision interpretability. The results demonstrate that standard attention saliency maps often fail faithfulness tests under domain shifts.

entry.title: Can LLMs Extract Architectural Design Decisions from Source Code Commits? - A Preliminary Exploratory Study

author.name: Amey Karan, Rudra Dhar, Mohamed Soliman, Karthik Vaidhyanathan

entry.summary: This exploratory study evaluates how effectively existing frontier LLMs, including Gemini 3 Pro, DeepSeek R1, Kimi K2, and Qwen3, can extract architectural design decisions from unstructured Git commit messages. The findings show that while models readily identify code changes, extracting higher-level architectural rationales requires carefully structured few-shot prompt scaffolding. The work identifies key prompt configurations for automated software architecture recovery.

entry.title: Influence of Extruded Filament Shape on Buildability in 3D Concrete Printing: A Geometry-Informed Deep Learning-FEM Approach

author.name: Giacomo Rizzieri, Saif-Ur-Rehman, J\"org F. Unger, Annika Robens-Radermacher

entry.summary: This paper couples deep learning geometric prediction with finite element modeling to assess the buildability and structural stability of 3D concrete printing. By predicting realistic extruded filament morphologies instead of assuming idealized rectangular shapes, it significantly enhances the physical fidelity of construction simulations. The framework provides civil engineers with an automated tool to optimize printing parameters without physical test prints.

entry.title: TAP-Path: Task-Adaptive Structural and Token Pruning for Efficient and Trustworthy Pathology Foundation Models

author.name: Mehedi Hasan, Ashfak Yeafi, Md Khairul Islam

entry.summary: The authors introduce TAP-Path, a task-adaptive structural and token pruning framework designed to compress large pathology foundation models such as Virchow2. The approach combines validation-guided transformer block elimination, input-dependent patch token pruning, and feature recovery to eliminate nearly 25% of encoder parameters. This offers a practical pathway for deploying heavy clinical vision models onto resource-constrained medical hardware without distillation.

entry.title: Scaling Laws, Tabular Data and Actuarial Ratemaking Models

author.name: Ronald Richman

entry.summary: The author investigates whether empirical deep learning scaling laws extend to noisy, heterogeneous tabular data in the context of actuarial ratemaking. Evaluating multiple model families against generalized linear models, the study shows that while neural architectures benefit from increased data, scaling exponents differ substantially from NLP and vision domains. This clarifies the limits of pure compute scaling on tabular enterprise datasets.

entry.title: Risk and Anomaly Identification for Distribution Network Optimal Operation Based on Reinforcement Learning and Uncertainty Quantification

author.name: Ziqi Zhang

entry.summary: This paper presents an uncertainty-aware deep reinforcement learning framework for managing operational risk and detecting anomalies in electrical power distribution grids. By combining distributional RL with Bayesian neural networks, the system disentangles inherent grid stochasticity from out-of-distribution events such as cyber-physical attacks or extreme weather. This supports safe, risk-averse autonomous decision-making in critical energy infrastructure.

entry.title: Physics-Informed Neural Network Surrogate for Oxygen Vacancy Dynamics in epitaxial $\mathrm{SrTiO_3}$ on Si memristors via Dynamic Spectral Optimization

author.name: Rodion Podorozhny, Nikoleta Theodoropoulou, Jelena Te\v{s}i\'c

entry.summary: This paper presents a cascaded physics-informed neural network (PINN) architecture paired with a Chebyshev polynomial spectral optimizer to model oxygen vacancy transport in memristive heterostructures. By partitioning carrier density, electric potential, and defect transport into four sequentially trained sub-networks, the method resolves extreme numerical stiffness without operator splitting. This enables stable simulations of nanoscale semiconductor oxide devices across large condition numbers.

entry.title: SurgeGen: A Hybrid Generative Diffusion Framework for Storm Surge Scenario Synthesis

author.name: Shunan Zheng, John J. Hasenbein

entry.summary: This paper introduces SurgeGen, a hybrid generative diffusion framework that simulates storm surge flooding induced by tropical cyclones. By pairing a deterministic baseline regression model with conditional score-based diffusion, the framework generates diverse, physically plausible inundation scenarios significantly faster than traditional hydrodynamic solvers. This aids real-time coastal hazard mitigation and flood risk planning.

entry.title: Understanding Autonomous Driving Datasets by Describing Differences between Image Subsets in Natural Language

author.name: Julian Truetsch, Felix Hauser, Christoph Stiller, Frank Bieder

entry.summary: This paper explores set difference captioning to explain distribution shifts between autonomous driving datasets using natural language. By prompting vision-language models to compare target and reference image subsets, the framework produces human-readable hypotheses explaining visual discrepancies across domains and weather conditions. This provides an automated interpretability tool for auditing domain shift risks in autonomous perception systems.

entry.title: Dual-Form ASR: Semantics-Aware Inverse Text Normalization for Chinese Speech Recognition

author.name: Fengrun Zhang, Li Fu, Wangjin Zhou, Lu Fan, Youzheng Wu, Xiaodong He

entry.summary: Dual-Form ASR combines spoken-form speech recognition and written-form inverse text normalization into a unified end-to-end architecture for Chinese. By removing the traditional cascaded pipeline, it models acoustic context directly alongside semantically dependent numeric representations. This resolves compounding error propagation in real-world transcription and speech interfaces.

entry.title: Language, Language Models, and What We're Talking About

author.name: Malvina Nissim

entry.summary: Drawing on the development and evaluation of Italian language models, this position paper questions whether training systems on machine-translated and synthetic data distances NLP from genuine human language. The author highlights the disconnect between natural linguistic phenomena and the homogenized, artificial varieties produced and evaluated in modern benchmarks. The paper advocates for intentional linguistic criteria in determining what kinds of language models researchers aim to build.

entry.title: The Dice Roll Method: A Standardized Protocol for Repeated-Query Auditing of Large Language Model Brand Recommendations

author.name: Dmitrij \.Zatuchin

entry.summary: This paper introduces the Dice Roll Method, a statistical protocol using mixed-effects negative binomial modeling and effect size metrics to quantify stochastic variance in LLM product and brand recommendations. The framework decomposes recommendation variability into sampling, prompt phrasing, and model version shifts. It establishes a reproducible testing methodology for auditing commercial bias and algorithmic stability in consumer-facing AI.

entry.title: Mudragen: Geometrically Supervised Generation of Interacting Two-Hand Mudras for Preserving Indian Classical Dance Heritage

author.name: Jagadish Kashinath Kamble, Jayanta Mukhopadhyay, Debaditya Roy, Partha Pratim Das

entry.summary: MudraGen is a conditional diffusion model designed to synthesize anatomically precise, interacting two-hand mudras for Bharatanatyam dance preservation, overcoming the lack of detailed text descriptions in canonical Sanskrit sources. By incorporating 3D hand geometry priors and joint interaction constraints, the model generates faithful hand poses where standard text-to-image models suffer from anatomical distortions. The system serves as a valuable tool for cultural heritage documentation.

entry.title: OCR-EDR: Rendering-Aware Diagnosis and Repair for Closed-Loop OCR Improvement

author.name: Linnan Zhao, Kang Liu, Hao Yu, Jiabo Zhan, Chong Sun, Chen Li

entry.summary: The paper introduces OCR-EDR, a closed-loop framework for identifying and iteratively correcting fine-grained document transcription errors in complex formulas and structured text. By rendering candidate OCR text back into visual form and comparing it to the source, the system verifies and repairs omissions and hallucinations.

entry.title: Text2Thermal: Physics-Aware Thermal Image Synthesis from Textual Priors

author.name: Tayeba Qazi, Brejesh Lall, Prerana Mukherjee

entry.summary: Text2Thermal formulates RGB-to-thermal image synthesis by conditioning diffusion models on thermally grounded natural language prompts. Supplying material emissivity and temperature estimates via text priors resolves the physical ambiguities inherent in estimating thermal radiance solely from visual RGB data.

entry.title: ARTiS: An Adaptive Robotic Gripper for Enhanced Tool Manipulation in Disassembly Applications

author.name: Roman Mykhailyshyn, Domae Yukiyasu, Harada Kensuke

entry.summary: ARTiS introduces an adaptive robotic tool gripper designed for industrial disassembly applications by combining rigid mechanical linkages with soft palms and compliant fingertips. The hybrid mechanism accommodates shock loads and irregular handles while ensuring rigid, dependable grip stability during manipulation.

entry.title: RoughSense: Lightweight Terrain-Induced Rover Vibration Prediction Using Point Clouds and IMU Feedback

author.name: Gabriel Manuel Garcia, Stephanie Aravecchia, Miguel Angel Olivares-Mendez

entry.summary: RoughSense presents a lightweight traversability estimation pipeline that predicts terrain-induced vibration on mobile rovers by fusing LiDAR geometry with IMU feedback. Optimized for compute-limited subterranean and planetary rovers, it provides real-time vibration hazard awareness during traversal.

entry.title: Resolution has a new Agent Foundations team

author.name: Jeremy Gillen

entry.summary: Resolution announces the formation of a dedicated Agent Foundations research team comprising prominent former MIRI researchers to build formal mathematical theories of agency. The group aims to create foundational theoretical models of mind, self-modification, and multi-agent interaction to anticipate superintelligent behaviors before deployment. This initiative re-establishes a concentrated theoretical alignment program alongside mainstream empirical research.

entry.title: Dalek: A Constructive Agent Machine

author.name: Wanpeng Xie

entry.summary: This work introduces Dalek, a theoretical framework for autonomous agents rooted in Von Neumann's theory of self-reproducing automata. The architecture formalizes self-maintenance, evolution, and reproduction across text-and-message substrates via four foundational structural obligations. It provides a rigorous abstract model for understanding open-ended agency and autonomous agent boundary enforcement.

entry.title: Tree species mapping in Denmark: A comparison of spectral-temporal features with geospatial foundation model embeddings

author.name: Alkiviadis Koukos, Spyros Kondylatos, Thomas Nord-Larsen, Lotte Nyborg, Christian T{\o}ttrup, Kenneth Grogan

entry.summary: This paper evaluates geospatial foundation model embeddings from TESSERA and AlphaEarth against manually engineered spectral-temporal features for national tree species classification in Denmark. The experimental results reveal that traditional engineered features coupled with MLPs achieve higher classification accuracy than foundation model embeddings, especially in mixed forest stands. This provides empirical evidence that domain-specific features can outperform generic foundation embeddings in complex ecological mapping.

entry.title: An Adversarial Zero-Shot Learning Approach for Anomaly Detection in Multivariate IoT Traffic Data

author.name: Mahshid Rezakhani, Tolunay Seyfi, Fatemeh Afghah

entry.summary: The authors propose an adversarial zero-shot anomaly detection method for multivariate IoT network traffic using a sequence Variational Autoencoder. By integrating contrastive representation learning with domain-adversarial alignment layers, the architecture learns invariant traffic embeddings across heterogeneous IoT devices without target-domain labels. This aids cybersecurity monitoring across dynamic, unannotated edge environments.

entry.title: Position: Unlabeled IS NOT Equal to No Human Supervision in Visual Learning

author.name: Dong Lao

entry.summary: This position paper challenges the assumption that self-supervised visual representation learning is free from human supervision. It demonstrates that dataset curation pipelines, aesthetic filtering, and architectural inductive biases encode extensive human priors. The author calls for standardizing and explicitly quantifying these curation assumptions to allow fair comparisons across visual representation learning methods.

entry.title: Computing stable configurations of confined smectic liquid crystals with a deep variational framework

author.name: Yuchen Xie, Baoming Shi, Yucen Han, Lei Zhang

entry.summary: The authors propose a deep variational framework to compute equilibrium configurations of confined smectic liquid crystals within the Landau-de Gennes model. By using coordinate mappings for spatial boundaries and a warmup penalty to mitigate neural spectral bias, the network accurately captures fine-scale periodic layering. This provides an efficient continuous solver for complex liquid crystal geometries.

entry.title: FrameBench:A Language Understanding Benchmark Based on Frame Semantics

author.name: Chihiro Yano, Ryohei Sasano

entry.summary: FrameBench evaluates LLMs on their capacity to evoke implicit semantic frames from ambiguous verbs across varying contextual environments in English and Japanese. The benchmark highlights that while models excel at surface-level comprehension, they struggle to systematically deduce unstated situational background knowledge. The study exposes fundamental gaps between statistical token prediction and deep human linguistic comprehension.

entry.title: Typological Feature Prediction with Large Language Models: An In-Context Learning Approach

author.name: Qianwen Wang, York Hay Ng, Aditya Khan, En-Shiun Annie Lee

entry.summary: This research evaluates LLMs on predicting missing typological linguistic features in global language databases such as Glottolog and URIEL+. While zero-shot prompting fails, in-context learning with phylogenetic and geographical neighbors enables models to outperform established baselines while providing human-interpretable rationales. This presents an effective automated tool for computational linguistics and language documentation.

entry.title: A Spectral Phase Admissibility Certificate for Complex Linear Maps

author.name: Snigdha Chandan Khilar

entry.summary: This paper adapts the Kontsevich-Segal-Witten criterion from quantum gravity to construct differentiable spectral phase admissibility certificates for complex linear operators in neural networks. By constraining exterior power eigenvalues from crossing the negative real axis via Schur parameterization, the method enforces strict physical stability bounds without exponential computational overhead. It presents a novel regularization tool for complex-valued neural computing.

entry.title: SISER: Speaker-Invariant Speech Emotion Recognition with Entropy-Based Adversarial Training

author.name: Eunseo Choi, Hyunku Kang, Chanwoo Kim

entry.summary: SISER integrates self-supervised wav2vec 2.0 acoustic features with an ECAPA-TDNN speaker discriminator in an entropy-based adversarial training pipeline for speech emotion recognition. By aggressively removing speaker identity features from learned representations, the framework prevents models from confounding personal voice signatures with emotional affect. This leads to superior cross-speaker generalization across emotional speech benchmarks.

entry.title: ARCOS: Zero-shot Boundary Localization for Corneal Layer Segmentation Across Optical Coherence Tomography Devices

author.name: Nuno Vivas Br\'as, Benjamin Memmi, Ma\"elle Bouhassane, Cristina Georgeon, Vincent Borderie, Karsten Plamann, Anatole Chessel

entry.summary: ARCOS introduces a zero-shot patch-based boundary localization framework for segmenting corneal layers in optical coherence tomography images. By learning continuous interface probability heatmaps at native resolution, the method generalizes across diverse clinical scanning hardware without retraining.

entry.title: SignSeek: Learning Transferable Representations for Sign Dictionary Retrieval

author.name: Sobhan Asasi, Ozge Mercanoglu Sincan, Richard Bowden

entry.summary: SignSeek reformulates sign language dictionary lookup as an open-set, signer-independent retrieval task via contrastive representation learning. It incorporates articulator saliency-guided masking to concentrate feature embeddings on key hands and facial gestures while filtering signer-specific identity noise.

entry.title: QLAUN: A Research-Oriented, Robust, Agile, Modular, and Affordable Torque-Controlled Quadruped Robot

author.name: Mohamad S. Moudallal, Noel J. Maalouf

entry.summary: QLAUN Bot is an open-source, 12-DoF quadruped robot constructed entirely with 3D-printed quasi-direct drive actuators and modular electronics-free legs. Engineered for low-cost fabrication, it provides an accessible, torque-controllable platform to democratize legged locomotion research in resource-constrained labs.

entry.title: A comparative study on the accuracy & repeatability of mobile robotic platforms for the delivery of precision NDE measurement

author.name: SeyedMohammadAmin Nabi Pour, S. Gareth Pierce, Randika Vithanage, Ehsan Mohseni, David Carswell, Matthew Shields

entry.summary: This empirical study conducts a high-precision laser-tracker benchmark measuring the base-positioning accuracy and repeatability of five commercial mobile robots (including Boston Dynamics Spot and MiR250). It establishes standardized accuracy envelopes to guide mobile manipulator deployment in precision aerospace inspection.

entry.title: SHELF: A Synthetic Harness for Multi-Task Bibliographic Benchmarking

author.name: Michael J. Bommarito II

entry.summary: SHELF is an open-source benchmarking harness comprising over 62,000 synthetic documents generated from Library of Congress taxonomies to evaluate models on bibliographic classification, clustering, and retrieval. Designed for resource-constrained libraries and archives, the benchmark compares traditional sparse baselines against modern dense encoders and language models. It provides a standardized framework to measure indexing and cataloging performance under constrained compute budgets.

entry.title: Investigating the Ability of Large Language Models to Analyze Recipes for Diabetes

author.name: Revathy Venkataramanan, Aditya Luthra, Venkatesan Nadimuthu, Amit Sheth

entry.summary: This paper evaluates the capability of LLMs to analyze dietary recipes for diabetes management against established clinical guidelines. The authors test various prompt scaffolding techniques to break down ingredients and preparations, uncovering persistent challenges in accurate clinical nutrient inference. The results emphasize the need for specialized medical domain grounding before deploying LLMs for dietary counseling.

entry.title: A Peer-Relative Representation Learning Framework for Energy Inefficiency Identification in Mobile Network Sites

author.name: Eliud Nyakweba Koto, Jaco du Toit, Adham Stoltz, Johan du Preez

entry.summary: This research introduces an unsupervised peer-relative representation framework to identify energy inefficiencies across mobile cellular base stations. Using an energy-aware Minimum Distortion Embedding (MDE) objective with repulsive penalty terms, the model identifies anomalous energy draws by comparing structurally similar tower sites without ground-truth inefficiency labels. This provides cellular telecom operators with an automated tool to lower operational power expenditures.

entry.title: Coupled Tensor-Tensor Completion Method with Applications in Drug Repurposing

author.name: Maryam Bagherian, Albert Hung, Ivo Dinov, Joshua Welch

entry.summary: The paper introduces Coupled Tensor-Tensor Completion (CTTC), an algebraic formulation that incorporates multidimensional tensor side-information directly into tensor completion tasks. Applied to multi-omics and pharmacology datasets, the framework imputes missing drug-target interactions by leveraging high-order relational couplings. This provides a mathematically grounded approach for drug repurposing and biological knowledge graph completion.

entry.title: SWIM: Student Writing Simulation via Proficiency-Conditioned Generation

author.name: Heejin Do, Jakub Kontak, Mrinmaya Sachan

entry.summary: The paper introduces SWIM, a benchmark designed to evaluate how accurately large language models simulate student writing across multi-dimensional proficiency tiers. By comparing prompting, supervised fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning, the authors find that standard prompting struggles to faithfully replicate lower-proficiency writing styles. The study highlights significant limitations in zero-shot LLM persona modeling for educational assessment.

entry.title: Chiaroscuro for Emotions: A Contrastive Emotion Benchmark Grounded in Appraisal Theory

author.name: Divyesh Bommana, Mohammad Saim, Tianyu Jiang

entry.summary: CHIARO introduces a benchmark grounded in psychological appraisal theory to evaluate whether models can infer diverging emotional states experienced by different participants in a shared event. Frontier LLMs achieve only moderate performance compared to human agreement, while standard classifiers fail completely. This benchmark advances affective computing by evaluating multi-perspective emotional reasoning beyond single-label classification.

entry.title: KnowVis: Knowledge-Centric Visual Summarization for Video Lectures

author.name: Yi Xu, Yifan Hou, Xiaoyu Zhang

entry.summary: KnowVis transforms dense linear educational lecture videos into structured, non-linear visual concept graphs to mitigate cognitive overload for novice learners. By aligning pedagogical concept hierarchies with key video frames and visual narratives, the system produces intuitive interactive summaries rather than walls of text. User evaluations indicate notable improvements in student comprehension and knowledge retention.

entry.title: Urban Boundaries, Social Barriers: A Benchmark and Vision-Centric Framework for Mapping Gated Communities and Equity Implications

author.name: Minwei Zhao, Weiming Zhang, Jiawang Du, Qiming Liu, Weiming Zhuang, Pei Nie, Cai Wu

entry.summary: This work introduces GBA-GCs, a metropolitan-scale multimodal dataset mapping over 37,000 gated and open residential communities in China using satellite imagery and geospatial metadata. The benchmark enables automated spatial segregation mapping to evaluate urban mobility and service access equity.

entry.title: Improving Clinical Target Volume Segmentation Accuracy using Anatomical Priors and Active Learning for the AGITG TOPGEAR Clinical Trial

author.name: Phillip Chlap, Mark Lee, Trevor Leong, Matthew Field, Jason Dowling, Hang Min, Julie Chu, Jennifer Tan, Phillip K. Tran, Tomas Kron, Annette Haworth, Martin A. Ebert, Shalini K. Vinod, Lois Holloway

entry.summary: This paper integrates organ-derived anatomical priors and active learning to improve clinical target volume segmentation for gastric cancer radiotherapy planning within the AGITG TOPGEAR trial. The combined strategy reduces physician contouring burdens while elevating segmentation precision on complex tumor boundaries.

entry.title: Counterfactual Routing Using Integer Programming with Constraint Generation

author.name: Dani\"el Vos, Sterre Lutz

entry.summary: This paper presents an integer programming approach with constraint generation to compute counterfactual shortest-path explanations in road networks for the IJCAI 2025 competition. The algorithm determines the minimal modifications to network edge costs required to make an arbitrary user-selected route optimal. It achieves exact solutions with state-of-the-art runtime efficiency across competition test instances.

entry.title: IRWOZ 2.0: A Large Language Model-driven Dialogue Dataset for Industrial Robot Conversations

author.name: Chen Li, Dimitrios Chrysostomou

entry.summary: The authors release IRWOZ 2.0, a cleaned and expanded dialogue dataset for human-robot interaction across four industrial domains. Utilizing LLMs alongside human corrections, the dataset rectifies substantial label noise in dialogue state tracking found in the initial version. Benchmark experiments show substantial improvements in dialogue state tracking and response accuracy.

entry.title: TraveL: Transformer-based Multi-view Path Distributional Representation Learning

author.name: Fang He, Tao-yang Fu, Wang-chien Lee

entry.summary: TraveL introduces a transformer-based framework that learns distributional representations of paths within road networks rather than static point embeddings. By modeling traveler behavioral variability and regional segment dependencies, it captures dynamic traffic conditions and travel time distributions. This approach supports downstream urban mobility tasks, including route recommendation and travel time estimation.

entry.title: Neural-Network Maxent: a general extension with learned nonlinearity, applied to time-series for Desert Locust distribution modelling

author.name: Alessandro Grassi, Edoardo Kimani Bellotto, Wassim El Azami, Sabrina Outmani, Maximilien Houel

entry.summary: This paper introduces Neural-Network Maxent, replacing linear feature combinations in classical maximum entropy species distribution modeling with deep neural networks. Applied to multi-temporal ecological time-series, the method predicts Desert Locust swarm breeding dynamics from environmental covariates. This bridges traditional presence-only ecological modeling with modern sequential representation learning.

entry.title: Feasible but Not Safe: Constraint Violations and Report-Channel Attacks in Learned Cell-Free ISAC Association

author.name: Mehdi Zafari, Iman Mohammadi, A. Lee Swindlehurst

entry.summary: This work studies vulnerability and constraint violations in graph neural networks trained to optimize scheduling for cell-free integrated sensing and communication (ISAC). The authors find that standard soft loss penalties frequently allow models to produce infeasible associations that violate hard wireless constraints at inference time. Furthermore, they demonstrate that GNN schedulers are highly vulnerable to adversarial report-channel manipulation by untruthful access points.

entry.title: Distilled Rapid Embedding Transfer (DRET): Parameter-Efficient Biomedical Domain Adaptation via Priority-Based Embedding Transfer

author.name: Girish Sundaram, Daniel Berleant

entry.summary: The authors introduce DRET, a technique to transfer specialized biomedical vocabulary and token embeddings from large domain models into compact architectures like DistilBERT. This parameter-efficient strategy circumvents costly pretraining on massive corpora while boosting lightweight model performance on biomedical classification tasks. It provides a viable method for resource-constrained clinical NLP deployments.

entry.title: Decoupled Analysis-Judging: An Automated Creativity Evaluator Using LLMs in Complex Multi-step Creativity Tasks

author.name: Xiangyu Wang, Jin Wu, Xiaoyu Li, Chanjin Zheng, Yifeng Zhou

entry.summary: CreaEval is an evaluation framework designed to score complex multi-step creative tasks by decoupling LLM judgment into distinct analytical breakdown and subsequent scoring stages. By mitigating verbosity and leniency biases typical of standard LLM-as-a-Judge pipelines, it provides more stable assessments of procedural creativity. The approach improves reliability when measuring creative generation in open-ended domains.

entry.title: IchthyoNoma: Nomenclature and Context Sensitivity of Zero-Shot Biological Vision--Language Models for Bangladeshi Freshwater Fish Recognition

author.name: Nazim-E-Alam, Tarek Rahman, Md Kishor Morol

entry.summary: IchthyoNoma audits vision-language models like BioCLIP2 and CLIP on fine-grained biological classification across thousands of Bangladeshi freshwater fish images under scientific, English, and Bengali names. The results show sharp drops to chance accuracy when prompting in non-English nomenclature, revealing severe language and regional taxonomic biases in biological VLMs. The findings highlight significant geographic inequities in biodiversity AI tools.

entry.title: Q-Edge: Symmetry-Reduced Quantum Simulation of Structured Extreme Dependence

author.name: Hongrui Zhang, Paolo Recchia, Ying Chen

entry.summary: The authors propose Q-Edge, a quantum simulation engine designed to model high-dimensional extreme multivariate dependence structures by exploiting orbit-space symmetries. By mapping problem symmetries directly into the data representation rather than gate constraints, the method avoids exponential parameter growth and enables unconstrained quantum generation of rare events. This allows scalable digital twin simulations for financial risk, climate extremes, and structural failures.

entry.title: Selective Hypergraph Refinement for Frozen Graph Clustering

author.name: Zimo Si

entry.summary: The author proposes Selective Hypergraph Refinement, a training-free post-processing method for frozen graph clustering models. By constructing an attribute hypergraph that captures higher-order relational dependencies, the method selectively refines cluster assignments without modifying underlying node embeddings or model weights. This provides an efficient post-hoc enhancement mechanism for deployed graph clustering pipelines.

entry.title: Privacy Leakage in Federated Learning: Gradient-Based Client Identity Inference and Defenses for Inertial Sensing in Vehicular Edge Networks

author.name: Ali Akarma (Islamic University of Madinah, Madinah, Saudi Arabia, King Fahd University of Petroleum and Minerals, Dhahran, Saudi Arabia), Toqeer Ali Syed (Islamic University of Madinah, Madinah, Saudi Arabia), Muhammad Khan (University of the West of England, Bristol, U.K), Qurat-ul-ain Mastoi (University of the West of England, Bristol, U.K), Adeel Ahmad (Islamic University of Madinah, Madinah, Saudi Arabia)

entry.summary: This empirical study demonstrates that server-side eavesdroppers in vehicular federated learning systems can deanonymize clients using only transmitted model weight updates from inertial sensors. Across multiple attack configurations, the authors show high client identification accuracy and systematically evaluate differential privacy and gradient clipping as defenses. The findings emphasize that federated edge aggregation alone does not protect vehicular anonymity.

entry.title: Sharpening the Ensemble: An SSIM-Aligned Residual Refiner for Brain-MRI Inpainting Post-Processing

author.name: Kubilay Ka\u{g}an K\"om\"urc\"u, \.Ilkay \"Oks\"uz

entry.summary: The authors develop an SSIM-aligned residual refiner to eliminate blurriness in deep ensemble models for brain-MRI inpainting. Trained on the outputs of top-performing BraTS synthesis models, the lightweight post-processing network sharpens anatomical edges that are typically smoothed by L1 and MSE losses. The method improves structural similarity metrics on brain lesion synthesis benchmarks without requiring model retraining.

entry.title: LexIssue: Benchmarking Legal Issue Identification in Chinese Civil Litigation

author.name: Huiyuan Xie, Yuqin Huang, Zhicheng Hao, Yida Cai, Shaochun Wang, Zhenghao Liu, Yuxiao Ye

entry.summary: LexIssue introduces an expert-annotated benchmark of 430 real-world Chinese civil litigation cases covering 1,303 disputed legal issues categorized hierarchically. The paper formalizes legal issue identification into generation and classification tasks to reflect actual judicial workflows. It highlights substantial shortcomings in current LLMs when resolving nuanced legal claims.

entry.title: The Impact of Synthetic Data Augmentation on Discourse-Pragmatic Function Classification

author.name: Sara Sorahi, Kevin Tang, Reza Kazemian

entry.summary: This paper explores synthetic data augmentation for class-imbalanced linguistic tasks by analyzing the embedding distance between generated samples and real training data. Focusing on pragmatic functions of the English word 'look', the authors show that geometric positioning in feature space determines whether synthetic data resolves sparsity or injects semantic noise. The findings caution against naive synthetic data generation without geometric validation.

entry.title: Occlusion-Robust Multimodal Emotion Recognition in VR via Fusion of Facial Images and EMG

author.name: Birgit Nierula, Karam Tomotaki-Dawoud, Mert Akguel, Mustafa Tevfik Lafci, David Przewozny, Anna Hilsmann, Peter Eisert, Sebastian Bosse

entry.summary: The paper investigates facial emotion recognition in virtual reality headsets where upper-face visual features are completely occluded. By pairing lower-face video with seven-channel facial electromyography recordings from the headset padding, the system achieves robust emotion classification.

entry.title: Value generalisation Theory of Change: putting it into practice

author.name: Stuart_Armstrong

entry.summary: Stuart Armstrong details an operational theory of change for value generalization in artificial intelligence systems facing out-of-distribution environments. The framework defines sequential research milestones: recognizing value-relevant novelty, identifying invariant features, executing robust decisions, and running iterative self-critique. It provides a structured roadmap for turning theoretical alignment principles into measurable software benchmarks.

entry.title: PPO-STGNN: A Proximal Policy Optimization Approach with Spatio-Temporal Graph Neural Networks for DAG Task Scheduling in Cloud-Edge-End Computing

author.name: Yangshuo Qi, Chenwei Wang, Zihan Shen, Songlin Sun

entry.summary: This paper presents PPO-STGNN, a scheduling method for directed acyclic graph task dependencies in heterogeneous cloud-edge-end computing environments. The approach couples proximal policy optimization with spatio-temporal graph neural networks to capture the dynamic availability and latency of distributed resources. Experiments show improvements in completion time and energy consumption over traditional heuristics and standard RL schedulers.

entry.title: Catalogue Photography as a Cold Start: Toward Deployable Carbide Burr Recognition

author.name: Abilash Philip Madavath, Chandra Yuvesh Aubeeluck, Augustin Raju, Nicolas Pyschny, Felix Hackel\"oer, Florian Zwanzig
